# KB: Bug-fix invariants (incident essays)

## A MOUNT STILL REBUILDING ITS CACHE WAS CALLED FAILED AND LEFT WRITABLE (lane mount-cache-scan, 2.369.213 — the owner's OneDrive, 2026-10-04)

rclone `--vfs-cache-mode full` walks every cached file to rebuild its VFS cache index BEFORE it mounts — 164 788 files took 4.5 min (24 s CPU at 136 s). `_mountInner` judged the mount after a fixed 5 s, wrote the log tail as the error and called `unblockPath(mp)`: the bare directory was writable again while the daemon was alive and scanning; 26 s later an outside writer dropped `.restore` into it and rclone died `is not empty, use --allow-non-empty` (banned since 2.369.15). The owner's Connect clicks meanwhile hit "stale daemon still on … at mount time — killing it" ×3 — each click restarted the scan from zero. Earlier, the 60 s health sweep's hung branch (15:09:43, 16:41:43 — its :43 phase) lazily unmounted the MOUNTED OneDrive while its daemon was busy (`ls` over 6 s) and killed it ("daemon survived lazy unmount").

**Invariant:** a starting daemon is a STATE — spawned, alive, no fuse mount yet; the mount point stays blocked (`blockPath`) and shadowed until the fuse mount exists. A connect JOINS it (one daemon per mount point; a restarted server ADOPTS it). Killing is only for a daemon with no CPU progress (utime+stime, /proc/<pid>/stat) for 60 s and no mount, or past the 15 min ceiling; the health sweep never tears down a daemon that made CPU progress during its probe. A "not empty" death → the stranded move + ONE retry, said on the row. The cache count runs in a child process, bounded at 200 000.

**Proof:** scripts/test-mount-starting.mjs — a fake rclone (bash re-exec'd so argv[0] reads …/rclone, as the /proc scan needs) drives the real MountManager; patched-copy controls: the 5 s verdict restored ⇒ red, unblock before mount ⇒ red.

## THE NEWEST CHANGE CHIP'S × SAT PAST THE STRIP'S EDGE IN DEJAVU SANS (lane mirror-green-ui, 2026-10-03 — test-design-window 9–10 ✗ on the 2.369.203 / .204 Actions heavy job)

Eight of the nine reds were one cascade from A⑧ "removing that chip (its × in the strip) UNDOES its preview" ({"x2":{"x":817.25,"y":237},"undone":null}); reproduced exactly (9 ✗, 153 ✓) with the runner's fonts alone (a fontconfig of DejaVu + Liberation + Noto CJK), green with this box's fonts. In DejaVu Sans two text chips (181 + 166 px + the gap) overflowed the 339 px chips list of a 502 px strip by 14 px; the list scrolls sideways (`overflow-x: auto`) but a new chip lands at its END and the list never moved, so the newest chip's × lay past the edge — `elementFromPoint` there was the strip itself, and a real click removed nothing. A real product bug on any wide-font desktop (and on every desktop once the chips outnumber the strip): the change just made was out of sight.

FIX = src/lib/design-changes.js `draw(show)` → `reveal(key)`: after every add / update (a frame's edit report, a composer "Add") the list scrolls — the list only, never an ancestor — so that chip lies whole inside it (client-rect overflow converted back to the list's own px for a zoomed window). Runner fonts: 162 ✓; runner fonts + PATH: 162 ✓ (both fixes in). The 10th red (.203, once: "Skip — decide everything for me", a global info toast still over the Skip tap point after the leg's 10 s wait) came only with the A⑧ cascade here (1 of 2 cascade runs; 0 of 5 runs after the fix) — not explained further.

不变量=a list that scrolls must bring what the user just added into view — a fixed width that "fits two chips" holds only in the font it was tried in.

## A CENSUS THAT MATCHED "16" ALSO MATCHED THE CLOCK (lane mirror-green-ui, 2026-10-03 — test-design-window B③, red once here at load 37)

B③ judged the two windows refused a watch (16 designs per window set) by `/watch|live|16/` over each window's stamp + chip + title — and a GRANTED window's title is "Last read from /tmp/vs-dwin-<pid>/…/wNN at <date>, hh:mm:ss". A read at second or minute 16 (17 windows open over several seconds under load), or a scratch pid holding "16", made a third "refused" window. FIX = the refusal is judged by its own words on exactly the refused windows (the stamp "Live repaint off · read …", the title "This window is not watching its folder: one window set watches at most 16 designs. Press Reload…"), no granted window says them, and the census waits for the stamp (a window's first read can land after its ack).

不变量=match a census on the product's own sentence, never on a digit that a clock, a pid or a path can also print.

## THE BUILD SECTION SAID "COULD NOT BE READ" BEFORE IT HAD ASKED (lane mirror-green-ui, 2026-10-03 — test-browser-profiles-ui ① red on the .203 / .204 Actions runs, and locally once in a while)

The New-profile dialog draws its provider rows, THEN asks /api/browser/builds; leg ① judged the build list the moment the provider rows existed and read ["default","path"]. Meanwhile the dialog's first draw passed `st.builds = null` to buildRows, which words null as "The list of Chrome builds could not be read." — a false failure for as long as the answer takes (a paired machine answers through its agent: seconds), and on a machine switch the previous machine's builds stayed on show until the new answer. A real product bug the race exposed.

FIX = `st.builds = { pending: true }` from the open and on every machine switch; buildRows says a pending list as "Reading the list of Chrome builds…" (zh/ja), the section carries `aria-busy`. Leg ① holds the page's first builds answer until it releases it (a deterministic race): the waiting section is aria-busy with the reading sentence and no build rows, then the answered one lists the builds. test-browser-builds pins the pending rows.

不变量=a list not yet answered is said as waiting; a gate judges what it asserts only after the answer it depends on — hold that answer to judge both sides.

## THE CLEANUP KILLED CHROME'S BROWSER PROCESS AND LEFT ITS NETWORK SERVICE WRITING (lane mirror-green-ui, 2026-10-03 — test-phone-chip-ui ENOTEMPTY on every .203 / .204 Actions run)

`done()` did `chrome.kill('SIGKILL')` then `fs.rmSync(ROOT)` at once. Measured: after a SIGKILL of the browser pid alone, 10–11 Chrome processes live on for ~40 ms and the network service writes `Default/.com.google.Chrome.*` temp files AFTER the kill; Node 22's JS rimraf meets a directory that gained an entry ⇒ ENOTEMPTY. The runner adds three things: a disk-backed /tmp, Node 22.23.3, and a depth-1 checkout that skips the CONTROL leg (so the cleanup runs seconds sooner after the last page work). Under that shape here (depth-1 clone, Node 22.23.3, TMPDIR on ext4, 4 CPUs): 6 of 10 runs ENOTEMPTY, and 15 of 16 pre-fix runs left a scratch dir behind.

FIX = Chrome is spawned in its own process group; cleanup kills the GROUP, reaps the browser, waits until the group is empty (ESRCH), then removes the folder: 10 of 10 green, no scratch left.

不变量=to delete what a process tree writes, stop the whole tree and wait for it to be gone — killing its parent is not the same instant.

## "IMMEDIATELY" WAS SAMPLED 60 MS AFTER A WHEEL THE PAGE HAD NOT SEEN YET (lane mirror-green-ui, 2026-10-03 — test-desktop-resume-paging TRUSTED WHEEL red on the 2.369.204 Actions heavy job)

The leg dispatched a trusted mouseWheel over CDP, slept 60 ms and read `view._pinned`: true on the runner, while the SAME leg's trace shows `userPos/wheel`, `extendTop:done` and the window paged and unpinned. A trusted wheel travels browser → compositor → the renderer's main thread asynchronously (the message list's listeners are passive); the CDP call's answer is not the page's dispatch. Here it reached the page 29 ms after the listener was armed at load 37 on 4 CPUs (the old sample: ~60 ms + one evaluate) — half the margin; the 4-CPU runner overran it. Not reproduced locally (the unchanged leg 2 of 2 green).

FIX = a one-shot `wheel` listener on window (bubble phase — after the list's own listeners) records the pin state AT the event's own dispatch, and the suite waits for that record (it prints the measured arrival lag); "immediately" now means in the same dispatch, on any machine.

不变量=judge "at once" from inside the event it is about — a wall-clock sleep after an asynchronous input call measures the machine, not the handler.

## A WINDOW THE APP SIZED ITSELF SAT IN A BLANK PANE (WECHAT) OR WAS CUT AT THE BOTTOM (INKSCAPE) (lane app-fit-fixed, 2026-10-03 — the owner on 2.369.202 at "2× · 自动": 「目前微信和inkscape的窗口尺寸匹配都有点问题」, then 「对于自己定死尺寸的窗口我们应该遵循他们的尺寸并且禁止缩放」)

- **What happened (MEASURED by the lane's reproducer — a scratch-tree server, headless Chrome 1920×963 at DPR 2 with the sidebar at 470, REAL xpra 6.5.4, the real apps on a scratch display, xprop beside xpra's metadata).** Both windows state WM_NORMAL_HINTS minimum = maximum: WeChat 4.1's login 560×760 device px (a NORMAL, client-side-decorated main), Inkscape 1.4.3's welcome 1420×1356 (typed DIALOG, `_NET_WM_STATE_MODAL`, NO `WM_TRANSIENT_FOR`, the app's only window); a GTK 3 `set_resizable(False)` window writes the same. Of the four candidates the brief named: **(a) our fit ignored what the hints meant** — `fitGeometry` honoured the maximum (correct), but the VibeSpace window learnt only a MINIMUM, so WeChat's 280×380 CSS picture sat at 0,0 of an 898×618 pane: 81 % of the window blank (a 400×300 fixture: 76 %). **(b) the dialog** — Inkscape's welcome was not the main (`windowKind` ⇒ dialog) and there WAS no main: never fitted, never named (no constraints, no minimum), mapped where X centred it on the display (188,0 device ⇒ 94 CSS px bands either side) and its 678 CSS px height cut by the default window's 555 px pane. **(c) the scale** made it larger than the pane, not than this workspace (710×678 CSS fits 1450×878); a 1000×900 fixture at 2× (2000×1800) WAS larger than the workspace and was scaled to fit with the badge (stage 0.903). **(d) the app's title area under our revealed bar** is expected — the bars auto-hide (the owner's correction); unchanged.
- **FIX (the owner's rule, not the brief's "scaled-down, the chip says 75 %").** FRAME = PICTURE for a window whose app fixes its size: the xpra client names the FIXED window (the main, else a lone dialog — no main, no transient-for) through `on.fixed`, maps a lone fixed dialog at 0,0 and grows the display to contain it; the view hands it to the window in CSS px (`onFixedSize`) and never scales it while the window adopts it; `WindowManager.setFixedSize` makes the window exactly that pane + its chrome, min = max inline (the .window 320 px floor overruled — WeChat's window is 282 px wide), NOT resizable (no handles, no maximize button, no resize drag or header-bar resize, no maximize by double-click / command / app, no snap or grid zone on a drag, programmatic zones move it without sizing it), NEVER capped at the workspace; null (WeChat's login replaced by its resizable main, Inkscape's welcome closed) gives the window back its size before the lock, resizable. After, the same reproducer: pane = picture to 0.0 CSS px for WeChat (282×382 window), Inkscape (712×743 window round its 710×678 welcome, X at 0,0), both fixtures; stage 1, no badge.
- **Named, not fixed.** A fixed window larger than the workspace keeps the app's size and hangs past the bottom / right edge, and #workspace clips that part (the 1000×900 fixture at 2× on 878 px: 86 CSS px of the picture); the window cannot be dragged above the workspace top, so that bottom strip is reached only through the window's Scale ▸ (1×) — the owner chose this over scaling. The ≤ 768 px phone layout keeps today's scale-to-fit (the window IS the screen). A fixed dialog OF a resizable main keeps the dialog rule (nudged inside, never adopted). An app that ignores configure-window WITHOUT stating min = max is not detected (none measured on this machine).
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) The app's size hints are a contract: minimum = maximum means the APP decided its size — the frame follows the picture, never the picture the frame (no blank pane, no scale). (2) "The main window" is not the only window that can be the picture: an app whose only top-level is a dialog still has a subject. (3) Read the hints X carries (xprop WM_NORMAL_HINTS) beside what xpra relays before blaming the fit — the two agreed here, so the fault was ours. (4) A lock that the session sets is released by the session (a reconnect never unlocks; the next window that says otherwise does).
- **Gates.** test-xpra-client §8 (fixedSizeOf on the measured hints; WeChat's fixed main named and the swap to a resizable main ⇒ null; Inkscape's lone dialog at 0,0, the display containing it, the belt holding it; a fixed dialog of a resizable main never adopted; CONTROLS: the lone-dialog levers ⇒ mapped at X's 188,0 and unnamed; the view's no-scale lever ⇒ scaled with the badge), test-window-minsize §5 (the REAL WindowManager: lock, no drag, no maximize, a zone moves without sizing, uncapped above the workspace, release; CONTROL = the lock's levers pulled back), heavy test-desktop-app-fixed (real xpra + a GTK 3 fixture at DPR 2 zh / 1 en, frame = picture on a decoded screenshot, every resize path refused by trusted input, release, the lone dialog, the oversized window; CONTROL tree: 76 % blank, the dialog cut at the pane's bottom, the badge); test-desktop-app-snap unchanged.
- 不变量=an app that fixes its window's size fixes ours: the frame follows the picture, never the picture the frame.

## AN AGENT'S `tab new` OF A LOOPING PAGE SAT 25 S AND FAILED WITH ITS TAB OPEN (lane site-reset-windows — the 2.369.202 integration's site-reset reds, 2026-10-02 23:08 PDT)

- **What happened.** On the integration head 269b7c21 (green on 2.369.200 = 0e7dc5b4) test-browser-site-reset-chrome stayed red in 7 rows after lane browser-windows-fix: on a shared profile an agent's `tab new <url>` of userW's looping sign-in page answered only after 25 s with `Operation timed out … [tab_failed]` (⑥ ⑧ ⑨ ⑪). Its tab was open and bound, but no loop was told. Before windows-per-holder that `tab new` answered at once (0.38.1's `tab new` waits for nothing).
- **Why.** With a window per holder the keeper opens the tab (`openOwnTab`: CDP create in the holder's window, `--pin-tab tab <id>`), then navigated it with the binary's `open <url>`. That `open` waits for the page's load, and a page that never settles never loads. The dialog watch only cuts a VERB in flight, and the keeper's own `open` is not one.
- **The fix.** `openOwnTab` navigates with `Page.navigate` on the new tab's own socket (`browser-viewport.navigateTarget`). That answers at the commit; a slower server is `pending`, and the socket stays open so the navigation is never cut. The binary's `open` stays only as the fallback where no page socket answers. Separately, the ladder's `windowOf` read `Number(w)`, so a dead tab was window 0 (a false stray, a lease stamped window 0); it now reads through `WIN.windowIdOf`.
- **Semantic changes, not regressions** (the suites now assert them): each holder's session is bound to its own window at attach, so (1) a looping tab with the holder's own-window tab beside it is not the browser's only page — `tab close` opens no blank tab; (2) the browser's first tab is nobody's, and the tab fence refuses an agent's `tab t1` by name (`not_your_tab`). An orphan tab's loop is still told as a kind (`[navigation_loop_shared]`) and `stop` still refuses by name.
- **不变量** = a verb VibeSpace runs FOR an agent never waits longer than the agent's own verb would have. The keeper's helper steps never wait on the page's load where the binary's verb did not.

## A SHARED PROFILE'S SITE-RESET FOUND NO TAB OF ITS OWN; A POD ROLL'S FIRST COMMAND LOST ITS TAB UNSAID (lane browser-windows-fix — the 2.369.202 integration's two reds, 2026-10-02 22:38 PDT)

- **What happened.** On the integration head 2666de5a the heavy test-browser-site-reset-chrome ⑤ and test-browser-share ⑩ went red (green on 2.369.200 = 0e7dc5b4, red on lane browser-windows' own 652523ad). ⑤: on a shared profile a bare `site-reset 127.0.0.1` answered "VibeSpace could not read your current tab's address … [host_not_current]". ⑩: after the keeper took over a previous pod's SingletonLock, the first `get title` printed no `[tab_rebound]` note — the agent lost its page and was not told.
- **Why.** With a window per holder the KEEPER opens each holder's first tab, in a window of its own (`ownWindowAtAttach` → `openOwnTab`), at attach — no verb in flight, so the dialog watch's creation witness never names it. The keeper recorded that tab only as the lease's tab-fence root (`l.tabRoots`); `holderTabs`, the watch's `tabsOf` in production, read `l.targetId` + the witnessed `l.tabs` and not the roots. Two readers of "whose tab", and the new tab was in only one of them, so `ownTabs` came back empty. Separately, `ownWindowAtAttach` runs before L2's rebind block and deleted L2's `tabClosed` / `tabLostWhy` mark when it bound the new window, so L2's block — the only writer of the rebound note — never ran.
- **The fix** (src/server/browser-keeper.js, two places): `holderTabs` adds the holder's roots through `tabHoldersOf` (the tab fence's own reader — one whose-tab answer, no second rule); `ownWindowAtAttach`, when it takes a lost-tab mark (or binds a lease whose window was in a previous browser run), keeps L2's note on the lease (`keepRebound`: how `new`, why `life` | `closed`), so the attach answer prints `[tab_rebound]` once.
- **Gate.** test-browser-windows bwf ① / ② on the fake window model, each with a keeper-copy control holding 2666de5a's text (red); the two heavy legs on the real 0.38.1.
- **不变量** = a tab the keeper opens for a holder is that holder's in EVERY reader (the tab fence, the dialog watch, site-reset, `stop`): it is recorded in one place and every reader reads that place. A bind that consumes a "your tab is gone" mark says so, whoever performs the bind.

## A LEAKED SCRATCH DAEMON GREW TO 45.7 GB IN TWO MINUTES AND ITS OOM KILL STOPPED THE PRODUCTION SERVICE (lane runaway-daemon, B-442c — 2026-10-02 16:23 PDT)

- **What happened.** test-restore-liveness §4 (lane stdin-liveness ran it 16:20–16:23) SIGKILLs each worktree server right as it reports "upgrading". A self-upgrade spawns the NEW daemon before that one writes `state/agentd.pid`, so `installStale()`'s kill (the pid file only) ended the old pid and its `rm -rf` deleted the new one's root — pid 3859144, born next to the e2e dtach session. One fs worker of that orphan died; every respawn then failed to load the deleted bundle (MODULE_NOT_FOUND), and a failed Worker emits `'error'` AND `'exit'`: the pool ran `die()` on both, decremented `live` twice and scheduled two respawns, the size cap stopped binding, and the pool doubled every ~0.5 s (pids jumped ~19k in 43 s — worker threads; 5.7 TB virtual). Lane commands still ran inside vibespace.service's cgroup (env.sh's MemoryMax scope came at 16:27); the kernel killed it at 45.7 GB anon and systemd's default `OOMPolicy=stop` stopped the service. Afterwards `ci.mjs --reap --dry-run` spared hour-old orphans as "young: 42 s": it aged a process by its /proc/<pid> dir's mtime, which procfs stamps when it instantiates the inode — the OOM's dentry eviction re-instantiated every one at 16:23:10.
- **Why.** Three unbounded beliefs: an event PAIR is two deaths and every death respawns at once; the pid file names the daemon (not during a re-exec handoff); a /proc dir's mtime is the process's start.
- **The fix.** src/agentd/worker-pool.js (extracted from agentd.js): a worker dies once, `live` never exceeds the size, a death with an `'error'` is a crash and consecutive crashes back off (500 ms doubling to 60 s; only a respawn's own answer ends it), each said in agentd.log; a deadline's terminate keeps the R2 pace. scratch.mjs `endDaemonsOf(root)` ends every daemon whose own VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT / VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT lies in the root (title or agentd-bundle argv, two passes) and `endRootedProcesses` matches that env too; test-restore-liveness uses both. scripts/scratch-run.mjs `procBornMs` (btime + starttime / USER_HZ) is the reaper's age and the lock holder's. install-service.sh writes `OOMPolicy=continue` (the owner's ruling).
- **Gates.** test-agentd-worker-pool (heavy since lane fast-budget — 11 s of real wedged Workers: bounded and backing off; the pre-fix shape in a patched copy storms past 24 spawns of a size-2 pool in ~0.2 s); test-scratch-reaper (25: a starttime-old row under a fresh dir is convicted, the dir-mtime copy spares it "young: 0 s", the kernel's birth equals node's timeOrigin; 26: the pid-file kill leaves a re-exec child, endDaemonsOf ends it, a session-shaped sibling and another root's daemon live); test-architecture §57b (a server-booting suite ends what it started — the 80 that predate it named as shrink-only debt); test-fd-limit (OOMPolicy=continue + control). Real bundle: 94 MB → 4.2 GB and 978 threads 10 s after one death; the fixed bundle stays at ~83 MB over 45 s.
- **Verify r1.** A bounded pool can still wedge: a thread blocked in a syscall cannot be terminated, so its slot never came back, queued ops had no deadline, and `process.exit` (which joins every thread) never returned on SIGTERM or the re-exec. The pool abandons such a worker after a 2 s grace (bounded, said), queued ops fail by name at their deadline, and the daemon exits through `pool.exit` (exit handlers, then SIGKILL).
- **不变量** = a respawn loop has a ceiling and counts one death once; a kill finds a daemon by what it is, not by a file it may not have written yet; a process's age is the kernel's birth time.

Moved VERBATIM out of CLAUDE.md (tier-2 pass).

## TWO GATE JUDGES MEASURED THE WRONG THING — OUR OWN TOAST OVER THE PICTURE, A SAMPLED PROCESS TOTAL (lane test-judges, 2026-10-03 — found by mirror-green-ui and exit-transfer verify r2)

- **What happened.** Two heavy gates were red with no product cause, the base included. test-desktop-app-snap: 4–7 ✗ "bottom strip N % of pixels found on screen", a different act each run, more with the box's load (4 ✗ on a git-archive copy of the base at load 22). test-agentd-transfer: "the hub's memory ≤ two windows" red 3/10 at load 21 (6/10 at load 5 in exit-transfer verify r2) — the same 100 MiB pull read 0.1–16.4 MiB on its probe, the push 0.1–27.1 MiB.
- **Why — app-snap (the cause handed over was wrong; measured before fixing).** The proposal (mirror-green-ui): a repaint lands between the screenshot and the separate backing read. Built first — the backing strips read BEFORE and AFTER the shot, a moving picture re-taken — a full run: 0 of 105 states moved, and 9 ✗ with the base's very numbers (`grid13 23.9 % of 8255`, `10.8 % of 13356`): no race. The SNAP_SHOTS pictures showed the cause: OUR toast — `New port on "This machine": 9538 (chrome), 26824 (python3) — 🔌 on its machine row forwards it` — over the bottom of a window snapped to the right. The server's port sweep (src/port-forward.js, every 30 s) announces every new listener ≤ 32767 of ANY process on the host; on a shared, loaded box other runs keep opening ports, and the 3 s toast (anchored by the inbox button, bottom right) lands over whichever state is being shot. The old ≤ 2 re-takes 700 ms apart sometimes outlasted it — a best-of-3 that hid the cause.
- **Why — transfer.** The probe sampled the TEST process's gc'd `arrayBuffers` every 20 ms: mux / socket chunks, decode and hash buffers all counted, and whether a live window was caught depended on the instant — it could not measure "the file held by the hub".
- **The fix (the judges only; no product change).** app-snap: a verdict only on a CLEAN shot — none of our toasts over the picture (waited out first, ≤ 10 s) and the backing strips + rects + toasts equal before and after the shot; anything else is no measurement, taken again (≤ 6); a clean shot's verdict is final, never a best-of. THE TOAST LEG makes the cause on purpose: the suite listens on a port, the real sweep's toast lands over a Calculator in the bottom-right cell — a single read finds 23.6 % (the CONTROL: the old ✗ with the window where it belongs), the judge waits 6.1 s and reads 99.2 %. transfer: THE MEMORY JUDGE counts the file inside the hub at its two edges — IN = the socket's own `bytesRead` (a push: the source stream's own pushes off the disk), OUT = the target + any part of it on disk — at EVERY arrival, the only moments a hold can grow: the exact maximum, not a sample. Its first cut stat'ed `<target>.vs-part` while the hub's part is `<target>.<8 hex>.vs-part`: 100.0 MiB 10/10 — the judge's bug (OUT read 0), caught by its own number, fixed by listing the folder.
- **Measured.** pull hold 0.26–0.27 MiB (= the mux's 256 KiB credit window), push 1.6–2.5 MiB (the link and the device's queue counted too): no real hold. Both controls — the whole-range read, and a sink that keeps every piece (credited at once, written at the end) — 100.0 MiB.
- **What it does not change.** The port toast itself: VibeSpace announces every new port on the host (other users' and other runs' processes included) and the toast sits over windows at the bottom right — product behaviour, reported, not changed by this lane.
- **不变量** = a judge reads its subject on a clean line: the moving side read before AND after (unequal ⇒ re-measure, bounded), anything of OURS that can cover the subject waited out, a clean reading's verdict final — never a best-of; a memory claim is bytes in minus bytes out at the edges at every arrival, never a sampled process total; a cause handed over is measured before it is fixed (the proposed race: 0 of 105).
- Gates: test-desktop-app-snap 3/3 green (load 19→6, 6→60, 60→50; 1–7 states a run waited a toast out) (base copy 4 ✗ at load 22; the race-only judge 9 ✗), test-agentd-transfer 10/10 at load 24–27 + 5/5 beside a 32-loop CPU burner (load to 44) (base 3/10 red at load 21), test-ci-gate 299, test-architecture 428, test-fixture-isolation 109, test-changelog-style 40, test-harness-honesty 182 (all green).

## THE FIX LIVED ON THE DEVICE, AND THE HUB SAID "EXIT 1" FOR A REFUSAL IT COULD PREDICT (lane device-upgrade-stuck, 2026-10-03 — the owner: "怎么还是exit 1啊，不是说修好了吗？而且我还是看不到指令结果")

- **What happened.** lane exit-run-output (2.369.200) moved the choice of shell into the DEVICE agent (`run-shell`). The owner's Windows machine WIN-DESK1 kept agent 2.369.199: the hub tried to upgrade it 3× at 19:08 (to 2.369.200) and 3× at 22:11 (to 2.369.201), every attempt exactly 31 s after the last (the hub's 30 s `upgrade timeout` + the redial), then logged "GIVING UP … capability-gated" — a journal line and an event; `_onUpgradeStuck` was called but never assigned. Every `vibespace-exit run` then went to a daemon whose hello said `win32` with no `run-shell` as `sh -lc <cmd>`: ENOENT folded into `code 1` in 8 ms, no output — the card read "exit 1 · 0.0 s · 没有输出", the pre-fix symptom, while the hub knew from the hello that it could not work.
- **Why the upgrade never landed (code read + a model of Windows' rules; no Windows box ran this lane).** The installer makes `<root>\current` a JUNCTION (`mklink /J`, "no admin needed, unlike symlinks"); the daemon's self-upgrade repointed it the POSIX way — `fs.symlinkSync(dir, tmp)` (a directory symlink: EPERM without SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) then `fs.renameSync(tmp, current)` (a rename cannot replace a directory: EPERM even in Developer Mode). The throw happened inside src/agentd/ws-min.js's `emit`, which swallows listener exceptions: no device log line, no `upgrade-done`, so the hub waited out its 30 s. Decided on the device by `%USERPROFILE%\.vibespace\device@<host>\state\agentd.log`: "upgrade to 2.369.201 (N bytes) begins" ×3 with no "landed — re-exec" after them. The "two daemon versions at once" were two DEVICES: the 2.369.200 lines at 22:11:42 were host-b-0d1e2f3a's (it dialed in that second) — `[device-dial]` lines did not name the device; WIN-DESK1 never self-upgraded since its install on 10-01 11:37.
- **The fix.** (1) `XS.canRunLine(platform, caps)` (src/exit-shell.js): a Windows agent without run-shell is refused BEFORE anything is sent — `device_agent_outdated`, whose sentence names the machine, the agent's version, 2.369.200 (`RUN_SHELL_SINCE`, the first with run-shell) and the one step (rerun the device's install command: Remote → <machine> → Pairing command); the card, the audit line, the row's last run (`agent_outdated`), the history row and the CLI all say it. Every other old agent keeps the `sh -lc` it always ran. (2) DeviceManager `onUpgradeStuck` / `onVersionMatch` hooks, bound at all three construction sites (dial, ssh, local) to ONE door, `hosts.onAgentUpgrade` → src/server/device-upgrade-watch.js: ONE For-you item per (machine, expected version) under `machines` (what no longer works when known; the one step), the row's `agentUpgrade` line, re-armed for a newer version, retracted when the device reports it. (3) src/agentd/reexec.js `repointCurrent`: junction + unlink + rename on Windows; a failed landing is logged and answered `upgrade-failed` (the hub ends the attempt with the device's reason); the re-exec is `windowsHide`. The dial log names the device.
- **What it cannot fix.** The broken repoint is the OLD agent's code: 2.369.199 on WIN-DESK1 can never upgrade itself. The install command must run on it once; from the agent it installs on, upgrades land.
- **不变量** = a fix that lives on the device is not shipped until the device runs it: the hub reads each device's version and capabilities, refuses BY NAME what that agent cannot do, and an upgrade it gave up on is the user's news, never a journal line. A step that can throw inside a swallowing emitter says its own failure.
- Gates: test-exit-run (+DUS-1..4, controls dus / dus2), test-agentd-reexec-argv (+the Windows-shaped repoint: the cause ×2, the fix ×4, POSIX on the real fs, a control), test-agentd-upgrade-loop (+DUS-H1..3, the wiring, a control), test-device-upgrade-watch (new, fast, 24, 2 controls).

## THE HUB ASSUMED `sh` FOR FILES TOO — A WINDOWS MACHINE'S FILES ARE THE AGENT'S OWN FS (lane windows-device-fs, B-c484, 2026-10-03 — the coordinator's read: GET /api/files?host=host-dial-WIN-DESK1 → 400 "command failed (127)")

- **What happened.** The Files view on the owner's Windows machine WIN-DESK1 answered 400 "command failed (127)" to its first listing. Same class as THE HUB CHOSE THE SHELL (exit-run-output, 2.369.200): there the hub picked `sh -lc` for commands; here src/remote-fs.js picked `sh -c` for EVERY device file operation — the home (`echo "$HOME"`), the listing's fallback rung, du, the folder zip, the download streams (`cat`), the archive verbs, rename / copy / move (`mv -n`, `cp -rn`). A Windows machine has no `sh`.
- **Why the 127, step by step (reproduced on a real agent whose hello says win32 and that has no `sh`).** `list('~')` → `_devAbs` → `_devHome` = `sh -c 'echo "$HOME"'` → the agent's spawn failure (127, empty stdout) → home `''` → `fsList('')` → "absolute path required" → the catch fell to the legacy rung → `_run('printf %s "$HOME"')` → over the device link as `sh -c` again → `command failed (127)`. Every fallback was another shell.
- **The census.** 35 hub→device shell sites outside the Files view too (src/hosts.js path completion / probes / home, ctx-sync, writer-sweep, sysinfo's fallback script, machine-mounts, port-forward, mounts-plugins, desktop installs, the session spawn specs in ws-create, a token sweep in ws-handler). Each is now judged in scripts/test-windows-device-fs.mjs §1: works on win32 via X | refused by name | n/a; a new site is red until it has a row.
- **The fix.** (1) A Windows agent's files go through ITS OWN fs ops (`fs-portable` in the hello-ack): list / stat / read-range / write / mkdir / rm as before, plus `home`, `copy` (= cp -rn), `move` (no clobber, said; another volume ⇒ copy + remove), `du` (a bounded lstat walk); the fs-op handler expands `~` with the device's own path module, so `C:\Users\…` is never parsed on the hub; downloads and the local-parser previews read over read-range in 4 MB chunks. (2) What still needs a shell there is refused BY NAME (`WIN_REFUSED`: "folder download as .zip is not available on Windows machines yet", archive list / entry / extract / make) — never a 127. (3) A Windows agent older than `fs-portable` is told so once, in lane device-upgrade-stuck's words: "this machine's agent is X, too old to browse files on Windows — rerun the device's install command (Remote → <machine> → Pairing command)"; nothing is asked of it. (4) THE DOOR (src/agentd/client.js `posixShellRefusal`): runCmd / runStream / openSession / openPipeSession refuse a `sh` / `bash` argv asked of a win32 agent by name (`windows_no_shell`) before anything is sent — every remaining shell site on a Windows machine is a sentence, not a number. Every other machine's path is unchanged (the head and the base RemoteFs answer byte-identically over a real Linux agent).
- **What it cannot fix.** The owner's agent must carry `fs-portable` — an agent from before this lane gets the sentence (3), and WIN-DESK1's 2.369.199 cannot self-upgrade (device-upgrade-stuck): its install command must run once. Path completion, port scans, mounts and sessions on a Windows machine remain refused by name (the door), not working.
- **verify-r1 F1 — THE SHELL IS THE DEVICE'S FACT, NOT THE PLATFORM'S.** The first door refused `sh` to every win32 agent. Git for Windows / MSYS2 / Cygwin put `sh.exe` on PATH (libuv resolves `sh` ⇒ sh.exe), and on those machines the 28 refused sites (sessions, ctx-sync, sweeps, mounts, port-forward, sysinfo) RAN before this lane — reproduced: a real agent whose hello says win32 and whose `sh` starts, the base client answered `printf %s "$HOME"`, the head said windows_no_shell; an old agent with `sh` lost its Files view to the outdated sentence. FIX: the agent STARTS each POSIX shell once (the first hello, run-cmd's own env) and says which did (`posixShells`); the door refuses only a shell that list leaves out; an agent too old to say is ASKED (the Files route asks `sh -c 'exit 0'` once per link) and a spawn that failed there is named (`windows_no_shell`, or the outdated sentence / WIN_REFUSED on the Files route) — never refused by OS, never a bare 127.
- **verify-r2 — A SHELL COUNTS ONLY IF IT RAN, AND THE PROBE NEVER HOLDS THE AGENT.** r1 measured with `spawnSync` (5 s per shell, the agent's loop blocked) and counted any shell that STARTED — a hung `sh` (WSL's bash.exe booting a distro, a first-run prompt), one that exits 3, one that is not POSIX were "here", and the hub sent them its lines. Now: all five in parallel, async, killed at 3 s; present only when `echo vs-$((40+2))` answered `vs-42`; re-measured at every hello (a shell installed later counts at the next link). The hub's old-agent probe likewise counts only exit 0. The Files refusals travel as codes the client words (zh / ja); du's 10^6 bound and a failed cross-drive move are said in words.
- **不变量** = the hub never assumes a shell on a machine it does not run on — what the device can do with its own facilities (its fs, its own path rules, its own `~`) it does there; what needs a shell the DEVICE SAYS it lacks is refused by name BEFORE it is sent (the device's fact, never its OS); an agent too old to say is asked and its failure named; a census holds every hub→device shell site with its Windows verdict, and a new one is red until judged.
- Gates: test-windows-device-fs (new, fast, 134 at verify-r2; 107: the census + 2 controls, the door table, a REAL win32-hello agent with no `sh` through every Files op, the base hub over it = "command failed (127)", the base tree's agent as the old one, POSIX head ≡ base, controls c1 no door / c2 no gate / c3 no route / c4 no outdated words / c5 no `~` expansion / c6 the door keyed on the platform / c7 the Files route without the `sh` question; §4b Windows WITH `sh` and an old agent with `sh`; POSIX errors ≡ base), test-exit-run, test-sysinfo-op, test-raw-filename, test-agentd-switchover, test-architecture, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`.

## A DESKTOP APP OPENED ON THE MACHINE'S OWN SCREEN — DELETING WAYLAND_DISPLAY IS NOT ENOUGH (lane desktop-wayland, 2026-10-02 21:36 PDT — the owner's Blender)

- **What happened.** The owner opened Blender (5.x, ~/.local/bin/blender) as a desktop app; the keeper started it on xpra display :4. Its window opened on the machine's physical GNOME screen, and the VibeSpace window sat on "Waiting for the app window…" for ever.
- **Why.** Read-only on the live process: DISPLAY=:4, XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11, GDK_BACKEND=x11, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb and NO WAYLAND_DISPLAY — yet its fd 3 was connected to /run/user/1000/wayland-0 (gnome-shell). `x11Env` did `delete env.WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; libwayland's `wl_display_connect(NULL)` then defaults to `wayland-0` under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and Blender's GHOST prefers Wayland whenever a connect succeeds (its log: libdecor-gtk "Failed to initialize GTK … falling back on no decorations"). GDK_BACKEND / QT_QPA_PLATFORM steer two toolkits; a program that calls libwayland itself (Blender's GHOST, SDL3) reads none of them.
- **The fix** (src/desktop-display.js, one place): `x11Env` sets `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=vibespace-x11-only` (`NO_WAYLAND_DISPLAY` — relative, so libwayland looks for $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/vibespace-x11-only and finds nothing; never "", which some toolkits read as unset) and `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11` (SDL3 prefers Wayland; SDL3 still reads the SDL2 name). Every caller inherits it: desktop apps on this machine and a paired machine's `desktop-serve` op run the same src/desktop-serve.js (the app spawn, the relaunch hand-over, `x11EnvFor` → window targets / tier 3). The keeper's OWN X parts get the variable dropped (`withoutWayland` in `startXServer` / `startX11vnc` / `startXpra`): x11vnc 0.9.17 exits on ANY WAYLAND_DISPLAY — re-measured with the new name ("Wayland display server detected … Exiting", rc 1; unset ⇒ still serving at 4 s) — and xpra 6.5.3's `is_Wayland()` reads any value as a Wayland session (its source); none of them is a Wayland client, so their env is what it was. The X server is in the set because test-desktop-app-keeper §7's stand-in Xvnc (Xvfb + a real x11vnc inheriting its env) went red without it — an Xvnc that wraps x11vnc would lose its picture server the same way.
- **Not touched: the agent browser's hidden-window rung** (src/browser-display.js `launchPlan`) does not go through x11Env. It runs only when no Wayland socket is live in the runtime dir (the default has nothing to reach), pins `--ozone-platform=x11`, and its `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=''` is what makes agent-browser 0.38.1 start its own Xvfb (measured there: a non-empty WAYLAND_DISPLAY beside DISPLAY='' ⇒ "Missing X server") — the name that cannot exist would break it.
- **Gate** (scripts/test-desktop-display.mjs §9): the env table (the name non-empty, relative, not a wayland-N; an unset or empty base gets it; SDL pinned); shim Xvnc / x11vnc / xpra binaries record an env without WAYLAND_DISPLAY; THE REAL LEG — python3 ctypes on libwayland-client.so.0 against a scratch XDG_RUNTIME_DIR whose wayland-0 is a plain listening socket: the pre-fix env CONNECTS (1 accepted — the incident reproduced), x11Env's env is REFUSED (0 accepted), and the same client with WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 connects (the refusal is the name, not the client). It SKIPs by name without python3 or libwayland. §2's real x11vnc and §5's real xpra bring-up run on the new env.
- **不变量** = an X11-only child NAMES a Wayland display that cannot exist; deleting the variable is not enough — unset means `wayland-0`, the user's own screen. A program that reads the variable as a session signal (x11vnc, xpra) is the keeper's own part and gets it dropped, never a user's app.

## THE WORK METER LOST A HOT FUNCTION'S CALLS TO THE OPTIMIZER (lane mirror-green, 2026-10-03 — the Actions mirror's fast red on 2.369.199 / .200)

test-channel-reactions' determinism leg read compactSide over 2 000 deltas as 48363, then 46363 ops on the runner (setup-node 22 = Node 22.23.3) and equal here (Node 24.12.0); reproduced exactly under `npx node@22.23.3`. A per-function diff of the takes named the 2 000: `isReactionKey`'s own count (it has no inner block, one call per delta). ROOT CAUSE: precise block coverage does NOT stop V8 from optimizing, and a function's own count is its invocation counter, which an optimized (TurboFan or Maglev) frame never bumps — `--no-turbofan` (Node 22) / `--no-turbofan --no-maglev` (Node 24) made every take equal, `--jitless` too. WHEN the callee tiers up depends on the Node version and on what ran before: Node 22 between the second and third take, Node 24 earlier. lane-mirror-198's "the first measured take reads a constant more" (steady()'s comment) was the same loss read backwards — the FIRST take was the true count.

FIX = `startWorkMeter` pins `--no-turbofan` + `--no-maglev` for the process (`v8.setFlagsFromString`, before the measured modules load; the interpreter and Sparkplug keep every counter). The determinism leg pins the warm take equal too; a HOT leg (200 000 warm calls, then 1 000 calls read 1 000 blocks on each of six takes); CONTROL (f) runs a meter copy without the pin in a child process (the flags are process-wide) and reads the calls lost (Node 22: 1000 ×4 then 0; Node 24: 1000 then 0). Cost: a meter suite runs un-optimized once the meter starts — reactions 3.5 → ~7 s, thread 2.9 → 3.8 s, usage-ledger-perf 1.8 → 4.7 s, index-scale (heavy) 21 → 30 s; all seven meter suites green on Node 22.23.3 and 24.12.0. No wall-clock complexity leg was left in test-channel-reactions (control (d)'s 2 s hang kill and the one informational timing line are not complexity pins).

不变量=a counter read off the runtime is exact only in the tier that maintains it — pin the tier, prove it on a HOT callee, and run it under the runner's Node before calling it deterministic.

## A SCHEDULED JOB'S COMMAND SKIPPED THE VENDOR/CREDENTIAL BAN (B-f8c7, lane job-vendor-ban — found by lane agent-cli-fixes 2026-10-02)

- **What happened.** `vetSpec` (src/job-model.js) judged `spec.cmd.argv`, `spec.cmd.env` and `spec.health.value` only. `vibespace-job run … --every / --cron / --at` puts the command ONLY in `action.task.cmd` (a cron's child is `{ ...action.task }`), so `curl api.anthropic.com` on a timer was created and FIRED — reproduced over the real engine on b924041f with an offline marker command — while the same plain task was refused: the §ban-safety class (a vendor call on a timer is what got a subscription banned). The vet also ran only at create: a keep-up restart, a boot replay, a `start` and a record persisted earlier were never judged, and `cmd.cwd` and `--env-from` secret names were outside it.
- **The fix.** `jobCommandParts(spec)` is THE census of what a job can run: cmd whole (argv, env, cwd), the health probe, the `envFrom` names, and `action.task` as a spec of its own (recursive). The one vet runs at every door: `create` (an agent and the owner alike), `start`, and the first act of `_spawn` — the only place src/jobs.js starts a process. A refused run never starts: the record (and a cron child's parent, else the timer re-fires every tick) parks — failed, desiredUp off — with a `refused to run (<trigger>)` event.
- **Gates.** test-job-model: 13 shapes × (planted ⇒ refused, clean twin ⇒ passes) + the one-door source census (one process start in jobs.js, behind the vet; create and start vet first). test-jobs-engine §10: an agent and the owner scheduling it (cron / at / every) refused; a pre-census cron's fire, an edited job's start, a keep-up restart and a boot replay never run; a clean twin fires (the harness sees a run). CONTROL on b924041f: 12 + 11 red; mutant without the run-time door: 5 red.
- **不变量** = a guardrail judges what RUNS, where it runs — every field a command can come from and every path that starts one; a vet at the create door alone is passed by every shape that door did not list.
- **Verify r1 — the pattern list had the same hole.** The census was whole but the LIST was the API host only: an agent's `--every` POSTing to `platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` (claude 2.1.288's token endpoint) or running `claude -p` was CREATED and FIRED on 03935d92 (real engine, offline marker). Added: `console.anthropic.com`, `platform.claude.com` (docs open), `claude.ai` (installer open), `claude.com/cai`, `sk-ant-oat`, and `claude -p` / `--print` on a timer (cron, cron child, keep-up service; a one-shot task passes); the refusal names the host in words. Read-only impact: 0 of 914 production records match. The vet stays a text guard — a script file, a secret's value or a run-time-assembled command is not read, and the manual says so.
- **Verify r2 — the list is derived, not hand-grown.** r1's list still missed what the CLIs themselves use: 31 shapes were CREATED and FIRED on 2f06a2f5 (real engine, offline marker) — the connector proxy `mcp-proxy.anthropic.com` and `*.mcp.claude.com`, `api-staging.`, ChatGPT's backend and `auth.openai.com` (codex's ChatGPT login), codex's `auth.json` / `data/codex-subs`, the macOS keychain item, a refresh token `sk-ant-ort…`, the whitelist's own `anthropic-beta` header; on a timer `claude -p` spelled `-cp` / `--output-format` / by its versioned binary / `@latest` / as an argv list, the Agent SDK inline and `codex exec`; and an open path carried a dot-segment into a closed one (`platform.claude.com/docs/../v1/oauth/token` — curl folds it). FIX = a vendor DOMAIN closed by default (`vendorHost`: only public docs/status/support/download pages and installers open, never with `..` / `%2e`; `downloads.claude.ai` is open now, r1 refused it); the credential list from the harness descriptors (`creds.subsDirName` / `authFile` / `spawnEnvVar`); `PROGRAM_USE` on a timer. Gate = test-job-model's census reads test-vendor-whitelist's VENDOR, its allowlisted files' URLs and every harness descriptor's creds — a host the whitelist gains and the ban lacks reds it (control: the whitelist + `api.claude-vendor.io` ⇒ 6 red); test-jobs-engine (g). 不变量 = a deny list is derived from facts the repo already keeps (the whitelist, the descriptors, the CLIs' own hosts) and censused against them, never grown by hand from the last incident.
- **Verify r3 — the owner narrowed it to credential reads (2026-10-03).** r3 found r2's list still grown (opencode's login, the CLI's FedStart / staging OAuth hosts, `$(which claude) -p` created and fired; a planted descriptor binary or CLI host left every census green). The owner's decision: a text check cannot tell which login a CLI will use nor stop an agent set on bypassing it, and an API call with the job's own key is ordinary pay-as-you-go use — so the vendor-host, whole-domain and `claude -p`-on-a-timer rules (and the `api.anthropic.com` refusal of .200) are gone. `VENDOR_PATTERNS` is a short list of subscription sign-in paths and variables; test-job-model's census derives the facts from every harness descriptor (`creds.subsDirName`, `creds.authFile`, `creds.spawnEnvVar`) and reds when a descriptor gains one the list misses (a planted codex `tokens.json` + `gem-subs` ⇒ 18 red), and a pass leg keeps API-key calls, `claude -p` / `codex exec` on a timer and ordinary jobs running in every form (test-jobs-engine §10 (f): created AND fired). **不变量** = a guardrail the owner cannot make complete stays small and says what it is: the credential reads it catches are derived from the descriptors, everything else runs.

## A HUNG TAB WAS A BLANK CANVAS WITH NO WORDS; A VNC DESKTOP WAS "NO DESKTOP SESSION" (B-d635, userW's inc-murizo36-ecri, lane browser-reliability)
(a) .201's background check asks a silent tab `document.visibilityState` and RETURNED SILENTLY when the page did not answer (`!r || !r.ok`), so a tab that never answers (userW's t4: "did not recover after activation", set viewport failed 3×) kept a blank canvas with its loading dots for good. ## A POLL THAT BROUGHT NOTHING REWROTE THE WHOLE CHANNELS INDEX (design 011 lane 2, userW, lane channels-quiet-index)

- **Symptom.** userW's 87 MB `data/channels/index.json` was rewritten whole about every 2.3 s with nothing arriving.
- **Cause.** Every pass stamped `lastPollAt` / `lastScanAt` / `walkStartedAt` into the conversation's row, so the index was dirty after every poll, and every flush wrote every chunk.
- **The fix.** The stamps live in `data/channels/poll-stamps.json` (≤ 120 s, close; still persisted — a row is due at `lastPollAt + cadence`) and every set in between is appended to `poll-stamps.log`, replayed at the start (a kill -9 before the 120 s write once lost them: a restored window fetched the "never polled" row ahead of discovery, test-channels-e2e ⑰); the serializer omits them; a flush whose bytes equal the last write is skipped; a legacy row is read and healed.
- **Invariant.** A quiet pass writes no index byte (test-channels-index-scale ⑩, test-channel-store ⑭), and a restart — clean or a kill -9 — never makes a conversation due early (test-channels-engine, test-channel-drain ②c, test-channel-store ⑭'s SIGKILLed child).

## THE CHANNELS PANEL'S FIRST READ SENT EVERY CONVERSATION (B-3cf8, userW, lane channels-first-read, design 008)

- **What happened.** After the 2.369.201 hotfix userW still waited seconds on the first Channels open (later ones were fine). `GET /api/channels` answered `digest()` — a `rowView` of every live conversation: 77.5 MB, 1.49 s to first byte at ≈ 50 000 rows; every account-level change pushed the same list to every tab.
- **Why.** One read served two jobs: the first screen (a few hundred rows) and "every conversation" (the All list, the filter, the counts, the account menu) — so the client needed all of them and the server built all of them.

The attention rows are found by `candidateOf` (raw facts, over-includes) and decided by the SAME `statusTag` the panel draws by (PURE src/channel-focus.js). The client keeps a keyed store (src/lib/channel-rows.js) with one rule for a row it never loaded.
- **Invariant.** A read costs what it shows: no surface reads the first read's `conversations` as "every conversation" (test-channel-rows ④), and the candidate test may over-include, NEVER miss — a quiet conversation handed to an agent at position 49 000 is on the first screen after a first read, a reconnect and a non-partial broadcast (test-channel-rows ① property, test-channels-index-scale ⑨ V1).
- **Gates.** test-channel-rows, test-channels-index-scale ⑨, test-channels-engine § design 008, test-channels-panel-redraw, test-channels-groups-e2e.

## THE ⚠ MODEL CHIP BLAMED "CAPACITY/OVERLOAD" FOR A SAFETY-CLASSIFIER REROUTE (B-c643, lane chat-residuals, 2026-10-03)

- **What happened.** When Fable's safeguards flagged a message (2026-09-08: twice in one session, both `cyber` — code reading credentials / tokens / process identity) the CLI retried on Opus 4.8 and the session stayed there. The chat showed ONE notice card ("⚠ Safety-classifier fallback: …"); the status bar's model chip turned into "⚠ claude-opus-4-8" with the tooltip "Auto-fallback: the harness is serving … (capacity/overload)" — the wrong cause, for as long as the reroute lasted. Not an account or quota problem; the control is `claude.disableModelFallback` (off by default; on = the turn stops instead of switching).
- **Cause.** The chip is purely client-side (served model of the last assistant turn vs the commanded one) and had one wording for every mismatch. The reroute's facts (from / to / category) reached the client only on the notice card; the server's `_servedViaFallback` stamp carries no cause and is not part of the chat status.
- **FIX.** The notice's renderer returns a side effect `{refusalFallback: {from, to, category}}` (live AND on a rebuild — the renderer runs for both); chat-view applies it with `ChatStatusBar.setRefusalFallback`. While the served model IS that `to` (the same alias-tolerant `sameModel` the mismatch uses), the chip reads "⚠ <served> · refusal (<category>)" and its tooltip "Safety-classifier fallback: <from> flagged a message (<category>), so <served> is answering instead of <model>. Your model setting is unchanged." A reroute to another model keeps the capacity wording; back on the commanded model the chip is plain. zh / ja words added. Limit: a notice paged out of the rendered window is not seen, so the chip falls back to the capacity wording until it is.
- **Gates.** test-model-fallback-notice (the REAL ChatStatusBar over a fake DOM: names it, keeps naming it on the next turn, a capacity reroute is not claimed, back to plain; the renderer → view wiring; the zh / ja words; NEGATIVE CONTROL = the pre-fix rule copy blames "capacity/overload", label "⚠ claude-opus-4-8"); test-status-bar-chips, test-billing-chip green (the chip is written once when nothing changes).
- 不变量=a chip that explains a state names the cause the records state, or says nothing about the cause — never a guessed one.

- **What happened.** Lane S1 found that a background Agent card reloaded from the transcript did not record which helper it launched (its helper asks were found by the call id instead) and that the suite's launch ack was a plain string while real records carry a text-block list. All five builders call it (the JSONL scan states the record's provenance: `promptSource` ⇒ typed, `origin.kind` peer / auto-resume ⇒ a card, codex `webui_peer` ⇒ a peer); chat-minimap says `t(noteSentence(note))` in the drag label and the outline row and filters on that. chat-run-summary imports the rule (assistantNoteOf / messageKind unchanged in behaviour; its two "imports nothing" pins now read "nothing but src/assistant-note.js"). ② `hookPayloadText` (src/message-manager.js): ONE unwrap for the stream's hook_response and the transcript's hook attachments — `additionalContext`, else `decision: reason`, else '' for a success / the raw text for a failure.

## GMAIL "REPLY" ANSWERED THE SENDER ALONE — AN AGENT ON A TICKET THREAD COMPOSED A NEW, UNTHREADED MAIL TO REACH THE CC (B-a085, lane gmail-reply-all, 2026-10-02 — 设备运维大师 for the owner's datacenter tickets)

`replyHeaders` (src/channels/gmail.js) took To = the anchor's Reply-To / From (ours ⇒ its To) and `cc: null`; there was no other way to answer a thread. An agent replying to a support ticket that had the desk, an ops list and people on Cc could only `compose` a NEW message with `--cc` — its own Message-ID, no In-Reply-To / References, no threadId: a second conversation the humans had to stitch together (the owner: "a new thread is unfriendly to humans").

FIX = REPLY ALL, resolved when proposed (the r6 F3 rule: the send re-derives nothing). `replyHeaders(anchor, self, { all })`: To = Reply-To (else From) + the anchor's To (ours ⇒ its To alone), Cc = its Cc; the account's own address and every duplicate dropped, case-blind, To winning over Cc (`addressList` splits a header on commas outside quotes / `<…>` — `"Lee, Sam" <s@x>` stays whole; a group label is no address); nobody left in To ⇒ the Cc moves up; nobody at all ⇒ the plain reply's To; a header over 16 KB is REFUSED (`reply-all-too-long`), never clipped into another list (test-peer-parsers row: cap + linear). ON THE WIRE `buildMime` writes To / Cc through `encodeAddressHeader`: a non-ASCII display name is encoded on its own and the address stays bare — `encodeHeader` over the whole value hid every address of a reply-all with one CJK name in it (RFC 2047 §5). `replyEnvelope(conv, { anchorId, all })` ECHOES `all`; `P.envelopeVerdict(env, anchor, { all })` refuses an answer without it (an adapter deaf to `all` never turns "reply all" into "the sender alone" silently). `reply --cc <addr>` = addresses the drafter ADDS: validated by the ONE address rule (`P.addressesOf`, which `validateCompose` now calls too), merged by PURE `P.withAddedCc` (an address already on the mail not repeated; a quoted display name is no address), listed apart as `added`. Item (3) of the ask — `compose --in-reply-to` vs `reply --all --cc` — took the second: it reuses the reply path whole (the stored anchor in the agent's own conversation, reach, the two-phase draft in the thread, reconcile by draft); `compose --in-reply-to` would need a cross-conversation anchor lookup, its own reach judgement and a threaded reconcile for `messages.send`.

Surfaces: `vibespace-channels reply … --all [--cc …]` (prints `reply all — to: … · cc: … (you added: …)`); `/api/agent/channels/reply` + the owner's `/propose` and `/send` carry `replyAll`; the window composer of an adapter with `replyAll` (the adapter view: `caps.replyEnvelope`) shows a "Reply all" box; the card's To row says "To (reply all)", the Cc row is whole, "Cc added by the drafter" is its own row. The AGENT's view of the envelope passes the belt (`agentEnvelope` — the anchor's display names and subject are a PEER's words, each a line piece; test-peer-text-census pins the door and rows `e.to` / `e.cc`).

不变量: a reply-all is a REPLY (same thread, same In-Reply-To / References, same propose-time envelope) — never a compose; every recipient is on the card before Approve; reply-all / an added Cc on a chat channel is refused by name (`replyAll` / `cc`), never dropped; a reply-all (the thread's own people) follows the reply's policy; an agent's ADDED Cc is composing — compose's reach (the whole account) and compose's verdict (verify r1 F1, below). Gates: test-channels-gmail-shape (PURE + the recorded thread + the draft's MIME in the thread), test-channel-outbox (engine legs + the echo CONTROL), test-channels-agent-cli, test-peer-text-census, test-channel-window-render ⑩i (zh card, chrome).

VERIFY r1 (2026-10-03). F1 HIGH — `reply --cc` was compose without compose's gates: an agent reaching ONE conversation (a send assignment, the conversation's policy direct) sent the owner's mail to any address at once, no card, while `compose` to the same address answers not-found (it needs the whole account). FIX (channels-engine propose): an agent's added Cc needs the account reached (`ACL.effective` at key '' + the account-scope grants — compose's own check; else `bad-proposal` / `cc` by name, nothing asked or created), and it goes direct only when compose's verdict would (the account's policy, the account rows' authority). F2 MEDIUM — the address grammar: `encodeAddressHeader` split a non-ASCII item at its LAST `<`, which can sit inside a comment — `j@x (张 <evil@x>)` reads as j on the card and went to evil on the wire (a plain reply's From too); `z@x (张三)` was hidden whole inside an encoded-word; `addressList` split on a comment's comma (`j@x (Doe, John), k@x` became an unclosed comment that swallowed k) and kept a group's label, so we were not filtered out of `Team: b@x, us;`. FIX: `addressList` tracks quotes, comments, `<…>`, domain literals and groups (label dropped, `;` ends a member; an unclosed item is no address); `addressParts` names ONE item's address (its `<…>` outside quotes and comments, else the bare addr-spec) and its words; the self / duplicate filter and the wire rebuild read it — an address never sits inside an encoded-word. Repro: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/gmail-reply-all/r1-repro/ (table.cjs: 34 peer header shapes, card vs a strict RFC 5322 reading of the MIME; cc-reach.mjs).

## A KEY LEFT HELD AFTER A KILL NOBODY HERE SENT, A TEXT ECHOED INTO A REFUSAL, A LOCALE NEVER LISTED (B-f18a, lane window-targets-residuals, 2026-10-03)

- **What happened** (lane E verify r4 O1–O4). ① `runInject` called an injection "killed" only when `err.killed` — node's own kill (the cancel, the timeout). An xdotool killed by anything else (`kill <pid>`, the OOM killer, a crash) skipped the release pass, so a key it held kept autorepeating on the display, and the refusal read `exit null: no message`. ② The UTF-8 rule tried `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, then the env's own locale only when its name said UTF-8; a machine without C.UTF-8 whose env names no locale was refused even with `en_US.utf8` generated. ③ A failed type quoted xdotool's stderr verbatim — a tracing wrapper or a binary posing as xdotool prints its argv, i.e. the typed text, back into the refusal. ④ A hanging `locale` cost 3 s per candidate before the verdict (the NO was already remembered 60 s).
- **FIX.** ① `outside` = a signal death node did not cause ⇒ `killed`, and `afterKill` names the signal. ② `locale -a` as the third tier (UTF-8 names, en_US first, at most `LOCALE_A_MAX` 4, each verified with `locale charmap`, the list memoized 60 s). ③ `xdoStderr` + `XDO_STDERR_KNOWN`: only measured xdotool lines are quoted, the rest counted "withheld". ④ The candidate walk stops at the first timeout.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A release pass keys on "the child died before it finished", never on WHO killed it. (2) A refusal never quotes a child's free-form output when the child was handed user text — quote a closed set, count the rest. (3) A capability probe that hangs is asked once per verdict and remembered like a NO; a fallback tier never multiplies a hang.
- Gates: test-window-targets §2 (four legs, four patched-copy controls; ④ on a time-scaled copy pinned to differ only in `LOCALE_PROBE_MS`).

## AFTER A RESTART, `type` WITH NO REF ASKED THE TREE AND ANSWERED THE MACHINE (B-a38d, lane window-targets-residuals, 2026-10-03)

- **What happened.** A window shared `auto` resolves its mode at attach (and at every snapshot); the resolution lives in the engine's memory, the share and the lease on disk. After a VibeSpace restart the lease was still the agent's ("your next verb just works") but nothing was resolved, and `act()`'s `type` branch read "no resolution" as "not pixels": with no ref it asked the tree for the focused node and threw the helper's own code. Same window, same call: `no_injection_backend` (keys, no xdotool) before the restart; `python3_missing` / `a11y_unavailable` / `helper_error` / `helper_missing` after it, by machine. Named as a residual in the 2.369.181 mirror-red entry below.
- **Reproduced (b924041f):** the runner's shape (PATH empty, buses unset) four ways, `attachWithMode` ⇒ pixels, a second engine over the same data dir, `type "hi"` ⇒ the machine's code, `modeInfo` still unresolved.
- **FIX.** A no-ref `type` under an unresolved `auto` share runs the attach probe first (`ensureResolved`), re-checks (`held()`) and re-reads the share, then takes the resolved mode's road (pixels ⇒ keys). The focused-node read is followed by a re-check as well. Not a `mode_pixels` refusal: pixel mode allows `type` without a ref, and the refusal would name the call just made as the remedy.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A verb's ROAD is a function of the share's mode as resolved — "not resolved yet" is resolved, never read as one of the modes. (2) Anything an engine keeps only in memory (a resolution) is re-derived at the first verb that needs it after a restart; the persisted half (the lease) must not answer differently because the memory half is gone. (3) Every await inside a verb is followed by the reach/lease re-check before its result can shape the answer — a refusal included.
- Gates: test-window-targets §4r (before/after a restart in four shapes ⇒ one code; CONTROL = no pre-road probe ⇒ the machine's code) + §5 (two race legs; the per-site census pins both new re-checks).

## A PAGE LINK IN CHAT COULD NOT BE OPENED: THE PATH PASS RE-WRAPPED ITS TEXT (B-2dbc, lane page-link, 2.369.202 — userW inc-murolahg-3rtv)

- **What happened.** An agent wrote "私有页 /p/pg5vex1gylcn（文件 …）". A click copied the bare "/p/pg5vex1gylcn"; Cmd+click flashed "Not found" and opened nothing (2.369.199, unchanged in .200 / .201).
- **Why.** `linkifySegment` = URLs → `/p/<id>` pages → paths. The path pass split at tags and linkified every text run, including the text INSIDE the spans the earlier passes made: `/p/pg…` matches PATH_SRC, and so does a URL's `//host/…` (the lookbehind stops at `:`). The click handler's `closest('.chat-link')` found the inner path span (copy = data-path; Cmd+click = /api/file/info → "Not found"). The page pass ran over raw HTML and could write a span into a URL's `data-href`. Prose URLs hid it (marked autolinks them to `<a>`); code spans and tool output did not. The suite pinned the CALL ORDER as the guarantee and never ran the renderer.
- **The fix.** `_linkifyBareText(html, fn)` skips every tag and every whole `.chat-link` span; the page and path passes both run through it. Cells without a nested link are byte-identical.
- **不变量** = a linkifier pass never wraps text an earlier pass already made a link — no link inside a link, no markup inside an attribute; an ordering guarantee is proven by running the renderer over a corpus (test-path-linkify ④⑤ census + patched-copy control; test-page-link-ui clicks it in chrome).

## A SECOND MESSAGE TYPED INTO A BRIDGE THAT NEVER SPOKE WAS NEVER RE-SENT; A HEALED TERMINAL KEPT ITS HOLE UNTIL A RELOAD (lane stdin-liveness, B-c20d — held by lane-dead-bridge verify r2; pre-existing since 09-09)

- **What happened.** The broken-stdin detector (src/server/user-input.js) re-sent only ITS OWN input through the heal. A second message typed inside the first one's 5 s went into the same dead bridge; the first detector's heal re-sent message one, its `_stdin_ack` (or the new attach's bytes) ended the second detector, and message two was gone. A heal by the attach probe (4.6 s) or the dead-bridge watch re-sent nothing at all. On a terminal session the heal never repainted the `.buf` tail, so the clients kept the output the dead client swallowed out of view until a reload (the onExit ladder's re-attach does repaint).
- **Why.** The re-send was a property of one detector's timer, not of the bridge: what a bridge that never spoke was handed is that bridge's backlog, and every heal of it owes all of it.
- **The fix.** `writeSessionInput` (src/server/session-stdout.js) is the one write of a typed input: while the current bridge has never spoken, each input is held on it (`session._bridgeHeldInputs`), in order; the bridge's first byte ends the hold (a client that spoke forwards what it got — verify r1). THE ONE HEALER takes the held inputs before the new pty re-stamps `_ptyOpenedAt` and replays them, in order, 500 ms after the new attach (an input typed inside those 500 ms queues behind them); they stay held on the new bridge until it speaks, so a second heal replays them again. The healer repaints a terminal's `.buf` tail through `repaintFromBuf`, the function the onExit ladder's re-attach now shares. Verify r1: a never-spoke pty that EXITS on its own (a device link that died before its preamble) forwarded nothing either, and the ladder's re-attach dropped what it held — the onExit branch takes the held inputs and hands them to the next `setupSessionPty` (`pty: null` = carried), which replays them. And the detector judged in the TIMERS phase: after an event-loop stall of 5 s or more it ran ahead of a preamble and an ack that had long since arrived, so the heal replayed inputs the bridge had already forwarded (twice to the CLI — b924041f's single re-send did the same); it now confirms after a poll phase (600 ms), as the attach probe does.
- **Gates.** test-dead-bridge §5 ⑧ (raw dtach + the real session-stdout + user-input: both messages land once, in order; copies with b924041f's rule lose the second) and ⑨ (the repaint; a copy without it keeps the hole); test-bridge-liveness §F (the healer's order: take, wire, repaint, replay); test-restore-liveness §5 (a held input replays through a real attach); test-dead-bridge §5 ⑩ (verify r1: the exit ladder carries the held input; a copy without the carry loses it) and ⑪ (a 6 s stall: one delivery; a copy that judges at once delivers twice).
- **不变量** = what a bridge that never spoke was handed is that bridge's backlog — every heal replays all of it, in order; a re-attach repaints what the clients missed, whichever path re-attached.

## A LATE ACK KILLED A HEALTHY R6 PIPE SESSION (lane stdin-liveness, B-b675 — R6 local pipe sessions, `agentd.localPipeSessions`, default off)

- **What happened.** ws-create kept the `cw-*` socketPath on an R6 session although no dtach socket is ever created for a daemon pipe. The broken-stdin detector armed on every input: a `_stdin_ack` later than 5 s plus 5 s of quiet sent it to the healer, whose first act is `session.pty.kill()` (the daemon's kill-pipe-session) and whose `dtach -a` then pointed at a file that never existed. The dead-bridge watch read the same field.
- **Why.** A field that names a transport the session does not have arms every path written for that transport. The ocPty branch nulled it; the R6 branch did not (the R6 boot re-open never set one).
- **The fix.** The r6Handle branch nulls `socketPath` as the ocPty branch does; `pipePtyShim` marks its duck `_pipe` and the healer refuses it (the belt). A `daemonPtyShim` is still healed: it relays a real `dtach -a` (the attach probe's case). The frame-file bypass keeps a local R6 pipe (`agentdSession`), as before.
- **Gates.** test-pty-duck §4 (the healer refuses the pipe duck; a copy without the refusal kills it — the old §4 pinned that kill as the reproduction; the r6 branch's null is pinned); test-chat-frame-guard (the bypass condition).
- **不变量** = a session carries only the transport it has; a healer refuses a bridge it cannot re-attach.

## A SEND FROM A VIEW THAT WAS NOT THE LIVE TAIL DID NOT SHOW THE SENT MESSAGE (B-172e, inc-mt1zrvj3-wsr4, owner on 2.361.6 — lane chat-scroll, 2.369.202)

- **What happened.** After scrolling up the owner sent a message: the transcript had it, the view did not. The frozen bundle was no longer in data/incidents (the oldest bundle there is from 2026-09-21; the item was filed 2026-08-20), so the cause was reproduced on current code — scripts/test-chat-send-landing.mjs: one live session behind the real chat-wrapper and a stub CLI, real wheel gestures, the message typed and sent with a real Enter.
- **Why — three mechanisms, each reproduced before its fix.** ① A window paged out of the tail sends through `jumpToBottom()`, which fetched `[start, total)` with the total read BEFORE the await. The server feeds the user's message live in the same breath (src/server/user-input.js → feedLive), so its `create` arrived during the fetch on a view still reading history — deferred (`_total++`, no card) — and the slab that replaced the DOM ended one record short of it: the view landed on the live tail without the message it was sent for. ② A teleported seek slab keeps the window accounting it had before the jump, so with nothing new since, `windowEnd < total` read "at the live tail": onSend pinned the SLAB and scrolled to its bottom, while teleport mode defers every live op — the view stayed in the slab, the message nowhere. ③ An extend still in flight when the send rebuilt the window wrote its old slab into the new one: older history appended below the sent message (extendBottom; the base run ended at `window 776..377`) or a page prepended above the tail with the old bounds (extendTop: bounds 3399..3801 over 102 cards).
- **The fix.** ① `jumpToBottom` holds every live op from its request to its landing (`_tailHold`, checked in `_onOp` right after the `_resetPending` hold) and replays them in arrival order once the slab is the pinned view — a create the slab already holds dedups by id, an edit is a field assign, so a replay is idempotent; overlapping calls share one hold, and only the NEWEST call lands or fails for the view — an older call answered later drops its slab (verify r1 ④, below); the window ends where the slab ends (`_windowEnd = _total = start + msgs.length`) so every replayed create is counted once as it renders (and the read-only poller, which reads from `_windowEnd`, no longer skips what lay past the slab). ② onSend sends a teleported view through `jumpToBottom` like any window that does not end at the tail (`_teleported || windowEnd < total`, the resume re-tail's own test). ③ Every full-window rebuild (jumpToBottom, jumpToIndex, `_seekTeleport`) bumps `_windowGen`; an extend whose fetch returns into a newer generation drops its slab (`_windowMoved`, traced `extendStale`).
- **Gate.** test-chat-send-landing (heavy): four rows on the fix — a window paged out of the tail, a teleported seek slab (40 MB fixture: a slab exists only past the 34 MB gap threshold), an extendBottom and an extendTop held in flight with CDP Fetch across the send — each must end with the sent card on screen at the pinned live tail, the stub's answer below it, nothing older below it, and bounds that describe the window. Three scratch copies revert ONE fix each by a string-exact marker (asserted in the source and in the built bundle); each fails its own row. test-desktop-resume-paging's source-level control now strips this layer too (its patch (6)): its ungated sentinel page was still in flight when the resume re-tail's jumpToBottom rebuilt the window (`gapUp:tail` → `gapReset` → `extendStale`), so the `extendTop:done` that control read was exactly a stale page landing on a rebuilt window.
- **Not done.** A view's `_total` can trail the server's: a live create that renders nothing returns before it is counted (`if (!el) return`), so a slab sized by `_total` ends before the newest records. A read-to-the-server's-end loop was tried and dropped — it is not this incident's cause, and it made ①'s control pass.
- **Verify r1 ④ — a hung tail fetch held the whole view.** As built, the hold was released by the LAST overlapping `jumpToBottom` to finish. A tail fetch that never answered (CDP-held in the gate; measured: headless Chrome keeps a fetch to a server that accepted it and never answers pending past 330 s — nothing in the product bounds it) kept every live op held: the reader's ↓ landed a fresh tail slab sized by the `_total` read before the echo, pinned, without the sent message or the answer, and the next send did not show either (8 ops held) — until the hung fetch answered and its OLDER slab replaced the view. Fix: each call takes `_tailCall`; only the newest lands or fails (shows the error, releases the hold); an older call answered later drops its slab (`tailStale` in the ring). Gate: test-chat-send-landing row `hang-return` (the send's tail request held; a real ↓ click; a second send; then the release), control `ctl-newest` (the last-to-finish release restored by four string-exact replacements) red on its row.
- **不变量** = a send lands on the sent message: a view that is not the live tail leaves for it, nothing that arrives while the tail is fetched is dropped, a page answered after the window moved is discarded, and only the newest tail fetch lands — one that hangs never holds the view past the reader's next ↓ or send.

## THE PAGING GATE'S MIRROR FLAKE WAS A NOTCH THE LOAD LOCK SWALLOWED, NOT A FOLD (B-8c25 — test-chat-paging ① red once on the 2.369.195 Actions mirror, passed on retry — lane chat-scroll, 2.369.202)

- **What the item said, and why it was wrong.** The ring the item cited (`scroll 870→390 by:runsRestore`, later `390→849`) was read as the run-fold restore moving the reader inside the judged window. It is the §4d PRE-FIX CONTROL's `up-mid-1` evidence — an `[evidence]` block is printed BEFORE its row, and the control's rows are expected to violate. And a coarse `scroll` sample is no write: its `from` is the previous SAMPLE (they are ≥ 400 px apart) and `by` is only the last writer (`writeAgo 2687` — that write was 2.7 s earlier). Neither the fold restore nor the judge was involved.
- **What was red.** The job log (Actions run 36409457863, job 108885956231): `up-fast-3: landed at scrollTop 31 (inside the 100 px pageUp band) with 2472 messages and the gap still above (before: st 1516)`.
- **Why.** An extend holds `_loading` for 300 ms after its landing (`_liftLoadLock`). A notch in that window scrolls natively; when it lands inside the scroll handler's 100 px pageUp band, the handler's decision for that scroll is taken under the lock and pages nothing. The lift re-checked only the very edge — `_wheelPending === 'up' && scrollTop < 10` — and armed `_wheelPending` only for a notch the wheel handler read as an edge notch (Chrome's compositor may already have applied the scroll when the passive handler reads `scrollTop`; the probe saw both orders). The reader parked at the top of the slab with history above until the next notch. A fling's last notch falling into that window is timing: 240 unconstructed upward gestures here (three drivers on two pinned cores each) hit it 0 times; the runner's starved cores hit it once.
- **The fix.** The lift re-takes the decision the lock skipped (`_lockSkippedPageUp`): unpinned, history above the window, `scrollTop < 100`, a REAL wheel-up within the scroll handler's own `goingUp` horizon (1200 ms), no down-lockout, no input resize → `_extendTop()`, traced `lockBand`. A view that only drifted into the band still pages nothing (displacement is not intent).
- **Gate.** test-chat-paging §4g, constructed: one real notch from the top edge starts an extendTop; the page catches its landing while the lock holds and puts the view at 170 px (a write, no input); one real 120 px notch lands it at ~50, off the edge. On the fix the lift pages on (`lockBand`); the control — `_lockSkippedPageUp` neutered on the instance, which is the pre-fix lift exactly — parks inside the band with history above. Before the fix a scratch probe parked 3 of 3; after it paged on 4 of 4.
- **不变量** = a decision a lock skipped is re-taken when the lock lifts, on the same positive evidence; and an `[evidence]` block belongs to the row printed AFTER it — read the verdict line before the nearest ring.

"⣿ 全部 → Beta Ma": `.chat-status-billing` (the phone's status-bar stand-in for the title-bar badge) had `max-width: 90px; text-overflow: ellipsis` (the switcher row's `.mobile-win-billing` 96 px) — lane G made the desktop badge fold (full → compact → icon) and the phone's two pills kept the cut. FIX = the same three forms on the phone, chosen by measured width (`pillMode` / `chipMode`), the cut removed from the CSS. 不变量=a pill is whole or it folds — a CSS cap with an ellipsis on a pill is the bug, on every surface that draws one.
