## THE DESKTOP STREAM WAS CUT "NO PONG" WHILE THE BROWSER WAS READING, AND A PASTE PRESS SAID NOTHING (lane desktop-keepalive, userW inc-muoshmqn-dect, 2026-10-02)

**What was seen.** His pod's journal: `desktop-singleton: closed (no pong for 40000 ms) after 40–80 s` six times in 12 h; then two presses on the Desktop window's Paste — nothing visible, no toast in the ring.

**Measured.** The keepalive was already a PROTOCOL ping (the browser answers it; the "background tab" guess was wrong). The ping frame waits BEHIND the send buffer (up to 8 MiB before the RFB side pauses): a live browser reading at 512 KiB/s never saw one ping and was cut (test-desktop-stream-keepalive §6; the pong-only rule as the control). And on the .199 shell two Paste paths said nothing: the box opened without a toast, and a clipboard read that never settles did nothing at all (test-vnc-view §9, the retired file).

**The fix.** ONE keepalive (`livenessVerdict`): a pong OR bytes from the browser OR kernel-accepted bytes through a backlog keep the stream; two silent rounds cut it, named. Every Paste press is said; the read has a 3 s deadline; a press while the stream is down reconnects, queues and pastes when it is back (or says it was not pasted after 30 s); a watching pane says so; the bar counts the ladder and words the bridge's own close reason.

**Invariant.** A liveness probe that can be QUEUED behind the data it guards is no evidence of death while that data is still moving; and a user's press ends in words — a box opening, a wait, a refusal — never in a state the eye must find by itself.

## THE WORD A RESTART LOSES — A PRESS THAT STRADDLED A RESTART LONGER THAN THE WRAPPER'S WAIT ENDED `unknown` ON A FLOOR, CHARGED AND UNSAID WHILE ITS OWN WORDS SAT IN ITS BUFFER FILE (lane reset-path verify r10 ⑧, availability + a false floor, 2026-10-02)

Reproduced on the REAL wrapper file against the stub app-server (r10-repro/r10-08-lost-word.mjs). r9 ② takes the wrapper's push / `skipped` when it reaches the new engine LIVE — which needs the restart to be shorter than the wrapper's wait (its push ≤ 20 s after the press, its go-wait 25 s). A longer restart — most real ones (`systemctl restart` + boot + restore) — and the wrapper's `rate_limits_updated {beforeReset}` and `reset_credit_result {skipped, no-verdict}` went to stdout with no server attached (dtach replays nothing; the re-attach repaint goes to CLIENTS and skips chat; the daemon's early-data buffer is delivered once) and into its OWN buffer file (`data/session-buffers/<id>.buf`: every record the wrapper emits, a 1-s debounce). Nothing read that file back: the boot revived the press unknown + charged on a 10-min cooldown and nobody was told — the r9 incident shape for every restart over ~25 s. The same for a consume that went out and was ANSWERED during the downtime (sent, the post-reset read, `reset`, all in the file): unknown until some later reading, the person never told it landed. **Fix:** `catchUpResetCreditFromBuffer(session, id)` in the engine, called by the codex stdout consumer AT the attach before its first live byte (test-stdout-registry pins the call): when THIS session has an attempt open or revived unknown, the file's tail (512 KiB, a local file only) is scanned for that key's `reset_credit_sent` / `reset_credit_result` / `rate_limits_updated` records and each is fed through the ONE entry (`recordCodexQuotaSignal`) at ITS OWN instant (`asOf` — a pre-consume read stamped at the attach would "settle" the consume that followed it); a `beforeReset` push that a send / result of its key FOLLOWS is dropped (answered before the restart: re-fed, it would re-open the guessed record and write a go to nobody); a reading older than LATE_MS is dropped; a keyed sent / result is always taken. Net on the real file: (A) skipped, free, said, the boot's charge the one ledger line; (B) landed, said. **Invariant:** what a wrapper wrote while nobody listened is read back from where it wrote it, at the moment somebody listens again, stamped when it happened. The window left: a record inside the file's 1-s debounce right before the attach is in neither the file nor the live stream — the orphan path (the floor, then a reading settles it; ⑤ pinned) covers it. Gates: test-reset-credit-ui §4e ⑧ (the real wrapper file, both shapes, the no-catch-up control = the incident shape), scenarios S71 / S72, test-stdout-registry (the wiring, before any live byte).

## A RECORD SENT BEFORE A RESTART WAS RE-OPENED BY A REPLAYED PUSH — A GO TO NOBODY, "NOTHING SPENT", A SECOND KEY OVER A CONSUME THAT WENT OUT (lane reset-path verify r10 ②, money — latent until the catch-up above re-fed old pushes, 2026-10-02)

Reproduced on the real engine (r10-repro/r10-02-sent-revived.mjs; r10-01 (b) = the same through a second restart). The boot erased WHICH half it guessed: `t.sentAt = sentAt || at` made a record SENT before the restart indistinguishable from one merely written, and r9's `revivedReadFirstWaiting` keyed on `revivedAt` alone. A replayed copy of the press's original `beforeReset` push (no product path produced one before r10 — dtach replays nothing — but the buffer-file catch-up re-feeds exactly such pushes) re-opened the SENT record: sentAt 0, a go written to a wrapper holding no waiter, the ack window ended it `not-sent` ("never sent the request — nothing spent"), the floor gone, and a second press was ADMITTED — a second key over a consume that went out (its late `reset` then landed as "an earlier request no longer tracked"). **Fix:** the boot marks `sentGuessed` (persisted) only on a record with NO send on file; the predicate requires it; a real `reset_credit_sent` RECORD (live, or from the file at its own instant) ends the guess and carries the send instant; an ANSWER that proves a send ends the guess but keeps the earliest-known instant (the parity walk under a short floor caught a re-stamp to the answer's arrival — `proof: 'answer'`); the PURE table mirrors it (boot / sent / reading / answer). **Invariant:** a boot guesses only what it cannot know; a fact on file (the send) is never re-guessed. Gates: test-reset-credit-verdict §9 r10 ② (+ the "guess every send" control), test-reset-credit-ui §4e ② (+ the r9-predicate control: re-opened, a second press admitted), scenario S70.

## A PRESS SENT AND UNANSWERED AT A RESTART WAS CHARGED TWICE (lane reset-path verify r10, money — the owner's ledger and the hour cap, 2026-10-02)

Reproduced (r10-repro/r10-09-double-charge.mjs): `noteResetCreditSent` persisted the record and THEN set `charged = true`, with no persist after — the file said `charged:false` for every sent-and-unanswered press (the consume's round trip, up to the whole floor), so the boot's "open at the stop, charged now" charged the same consume a second time: two spend-ledger lines, the per-identity hour cap eaten twice. **Fix:** one persist, after the charge. **Invariant:** the charge is on disk with the send (a flag that only lives in memory is not a fact a restart can read). ## A PRESS THAT STRADDLED A SERVER RESTART ENDED `unknown` ON A TEN-MINUTE FLOOR, CHARGED, THE WRAPPER'S OWN WORD IGNORED AND THE PERSON TOLD NOTHING (lane reset-path verify r9 T1 ②, availability + a false floor, 2026-10-02)

Reproduced on the real engine (r9-repro/r9-02-restart-mid-read.mjs; the pre-fix block in r9-repro/OUTPUTS.txt): a person pressed Use…, the 2.369.202 wrapper took its read before the consume (r8 T0), and the server restarted in between. The boot revived the open record `unknown` + charged (right in itself: a failed read consumes at once, so it MAY have gone out). Then the wrapper's own words reached the NEW engine and were thrown away: its `rate_limits_updated {beforeReset, idempotencyKey}` met "a read before the consume for an attempt that is sent already — no verdict written" (the wrapper waited its 25 s for nothing and skipped), and its keyed `reset_credit_result {skipped, no-verdict, sent:false}` met "the attempt is unknown already". Net: nothing spent, the ledger charged, the dialog on a 10-min cooldown, no notice — and when the push DID reach the new engine in time the wrapper could have consumed once, but nobody answered it. **Fix (engine + the PURE table):** `revivedAt` marks the boot's guess (persisted on the record). A `beforeReset` push for a revived press proves nothing went out (the consume follows the verdict) ⇒ `reopenRevivedReadFirst` runs BEFORE the reading settles it: outcome / sentAt / settled cleared, the press instant re-stamped to NOW (`pressedAt` keeps the original — a restart longer than the ack window would else admit a SECOND press over a consume about to go out: reproduced, its own control), the ack timer re-armed, the boot's charge kept (the ledger never under-counts; a later send charges nothing twice); then the one table judges it (go ⇒ ONE consume ⇒ reset; a second press ⇒ cooldown). A keyed `skipped` (sent:false) for a revived press is the wrapper's word over the boot's guess: settled skipped, the floor gone, the person told by the RECORD's origin (the restarted session's origin slot is empty), the restart's charge said to stand. A `skipped` for an attempt that was SENT is ignored by name (the real wrapper never emits one; a stub could). The own-reply lateness gate admits a revived press's push within the same bound from the press. `attemptStep` mirrors it (boot ⇒ `revivedAt`; `reading {beforeReset, idemKey}` ⇒ re-open; `answer skipped` on a revived unknown ⇒ sentAt 0) so the three judges agree (S68 / S69). **Invariant:** a boot's guess about an open record is overturned by the carrier's own keyed word; a press re-opened after a restart is as in-flight as a fresh one. Gates: test-reset-credit-ui §4d (+ scenarios S68 / S69; three patched-copy controls: no re-open ⇒ no go, no acceptance ⇒ the incident shape, no re-stamp ⇒ a second verb), test-reset-credit-verdict §9 (the boot control re-anchored).

## A HELD WALL AND READING WERE REPLAYED OVER A NEWER READING OF THE ACCOUNT — THE CACHE REGRESSED AND AUTO-RESUME ARMED FOR A WALL ALREADY ANSWERED (lane reset-path verify r8 T2 ②, availability, 2026-10-02)

## A THREAD BORN AFTER ITS ROOT WAS STORED WAS INVISIBLE FOR EVER; NOBODY COULD SAY WHO AN AUTHOR WAS (lane lark-threads, 2026-10-01 — the owner: "这个帖子应该是有个thread的，但显然你这里没展示出来" and "你有可能读取我在lark里看到的人的名字吗")

**The symptom.** A post in a Lark group grew a topic after VibeSpace had read it; the window showed a plain message, no chip, nothing to open. 432 other Lark records carried a thread key — every one a topic whose root was LISTED after the topic already existed. And 9.5 % of person-authored records had an empty author (a bare `ou_…`), 43 bots still read "app".

**The cause — four holes, one shape.** The vendor names a topic on its root only once the topic exists (`thread_id`: "不返回说明该消息不是话题形式的消息"), and nothing ever read that root again: (H1) the change feed dropped a hit on a STORED message before its thread mark (`stored++; continue` came first); (H2) the append-only log's dedup kept the FIRST copy — a later copy naming the thread was thrown away, with no path to patch a place; (H3) the chat walk stops at its anchor, so a stored root is never re-listed; (H4) the thread walk needs an `omt_` key nobody could learn. Names: `namesFor` read only the chat's member list (a person who left / an external contact is not in it) and the contact fallback was gated to single chats — and, MEASURED by an owner-approved probe, it could never have worked: `contact/v3/users/:id` of another person under the consent's `contact:user.base:readonly` answers 99991679 naming `contact:contact.base:readonly`.

**The fix.** A1 the store's ONE place door widens a stored record's place (null → the vendor's key / root, never the reverse, never another field) by a side line folded on every read and into the log at its trim; every append path offers its duplicates; a widened key is owed its walk and the root's row grows its chip in place. A2 drain rule 22: the newest page of each active separately-listed chat re-listed once per `channels.threadRecheckSec` (the lowest priority, bounded per pass) and at once on the owner's Refresh. A3 a stored hit's thread is still owed. A4 a feed hit the chat read did not find is read by id (≤ 5 per tick, every non-reply answer remembered 6 h). A5 the card says what the search carries. B: the consent asks the measured scope (and the card says "re-authorize to read people's profiles" while it is missing); profiles once per 6 h, the unnamed first; the organization's nickname + department as Lark renders them; external by tenant; the owner's own names for authors (aliases.json) on every surface; a bot never "app" at the view door.

**The invariants.** (1) A stored record is the FIRST copy, not the truth about its place: a later vendor copy that knows more must be able to widen it — widen-only, through one door. (2) A mark derived from a hit is judged before the hit is dropped as known. (3) A metered re-read is decided by a PURE rule (rule 22), never by an engine loop; the owner's press is the only free trigger, agents never. (4) A vendor call a product depends on is MEASURED before a fallback is trusted — a fallback that is refused for everyone is a silent failure, said on the card. Gates: test-channel-feed ③, test-channel-store ⑬, test-channel-thread ⑫, test-channel-drain (rule 22 + ④d + 4 mutants), test-channels-lark-shape ⑮⑯, test-channels-engine ㉓㉔, test-vendor-whitelist §8, test-architecture §65b, test-channel-authors, test-channel-lark-threads-ui (heavy).

## A JOB'S BROWSER SAID "NO PROFILE", COULD NOT SAVE IN ITS FOLDER, SHOWED AS "HELPER 1" AND LEFT ITS WINDOW OPEN (lane accept-fixes-jobs, 2.369.204 — the owner's acceptance of 2.369.202, F5/F6/F10/F11)

**What was seen.** Inside job jb-77df5327 `status` said "no profile attached / pin: none" and the next `open` landed on office-devices; `screenshot <lane dir>/x.png` was refused with "a session started before this version … restarted"; the live view's browsers row read "帮手 1"; after `vibespace-job stop` the job's window stayed open.

**Causes.** status read the job's bare child handle; the jobs engine exported no directory; `attachmentsFor` dropped the child's `job` tag (so the route's `jobNames` was empty); the release's detach keeps a conversation's page for its return — a job never returns.

**Invariant.** A derived principal (a job's child handle) is reported by what its verbs WILL do (the same verdict function, read only), carries its tags through every rebuilt view of the registry, and its END closes what only it held — a "kept for your return" rule never applies to a holder that cannot return. scripts/test-jobs-browser.mjs ④/⑥ hold each, with a patched-copy control per fix.

## A SCHEDULED JOB COULD NOT USE THE AGENT BROWSER, SO A DAILY RECONCILIATION STAYED ON THE OLD DESKTOP CHROMIUM (B-dbc1, lane jobs-browser, 2026-10-02)

The agent-browser profile holding the login was unreachable from the one place the work ran unattended.

**The fix (src/browser-job-principal.js + routes + keeper + jobs).** A job browses AS ITS OWNER CONVERSATION, the rule every other agent route already applied to `jbt_`: its lease key is a child handle of the owner's browser key (admission = the owner's who-may-use, by construction), its profile = the owner's pin / default attachment, its own window; nothing that changes the conversation's browsers is open to it (`job_token`, fail closed, a census of every route); a running job carries its handle (a job whose conversation stopped keeps browsing until it ends); its run's finalize releases it, and the reconcile releases any job handle whose job is not running. **Invariant.** A new principal on an agent surface inherits its OWNER's admission through the existing key shapes — never a parallel admission rule; its lifetime is bound to evidence of its own liveness, never to its owner's; and a surface it may not change is refused by a census-checked list that fails closed. ## ONE TAKEOVER FROZE EVERY CONVERSATION ON A PROFILE, AND A TAB BEHIND ANOTHER WAS A FROZEN PICTURE NOBODY SAID (lane browser-windows, userW's pod 2026-10-01 — D-payments 18:21, inc-muqdohf0-hkjc 20:02)

- **What happened.** ① userW took over jarvis-work from Majordomo's live view; every command of D-payments (another conversation on the same profile) answered "the user took over the jarvis-work browser — your command did NOT run" until the handback; it fell back to its ephemeral browser (no logins). Ten Jarvis conversations on one profile also serialized at a 90 s grain (`driveVerdict`, `browser_busy` by agent). ② D-payments' tab sat behind another tab of the profile's one window (a neighbour activated when sess-31's tab closed): its live view showed a stale frame, userW's clicks went nowhere visible, his chip clicks were a no-op (the active chip) or unexplained, and nothing was journaled.
- **Why.** Every conversation's tabs were tabs of ONE Chrome window; only a window's foreground tab paints (measured 0 fps / rAF 0 behind; a click 4.6–5 s; a CDP press lands but nothing repaints). The lane's takeover was of the BROWSER (verify S2 r6 took every sibling WITH the view) precisely because one conversation's tab switch could hide another's page under the user's hands — the shared window was the root; the 90 s claim protected nothing the daemons serialize (measured: one daemon per conversation, 3–5 ms beside another's `wait 5000`).
- **The fix.** A window per holder (every VibeSpace-opened tab opens in its own unfocused window; the mediator rewrites a lease's creates the same way; measured: Chrome cannot place a tab into a chosen window, a page's popups land in its opener's window); the drive claim deleted; a takeover of ONE window (`windowMates`: only an old run's shared-window leases still couple); the live view says a tab that paints nothing within ~2 s of silence and polls its picture; a driving click on the agent's current tab brings it forward; every chip act journaled and said.
- **不变量** = a pause is of the thing the user's hands are on — never wider; a view never shows a frozen picture in silence; a user's click that runs is recorded and said.

## ONE CHANNEL WINDOW COPIED THE WHOLE CHANNELS INDEX, UP TO FIVE TIMES (B-f32b, userW inc-muro2wt1-e8lu, lane channel-index-copy — hotfix 2.369.201)

- **What happened.** userW's pod held 49,977 Gmail threads + 207 Lark chats + 90 agent groups (index.json 45 MB). He opened 19 windows from the channel list in ~20 s: eight logged "who touched this conversation could not be read" 11–20 s later, and the 9th still read "Channel" 55 s after its click.
- **Why.** `known()` — the gate of watch, refresh, messages, mark-read and the broadcast's re-read — looked up ONE key through `store.index.snapshot()` = `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(ix))`: 0.51–0.55 s of the server's one thread per copy on his index, up to five per window. Three more costs on the same path grew with the index: the index write stringified all of it (0.40–0.52 s, every 2 s while anything changed — a mark-read included), every partial broadcast summed `unread` over every row, and mark-read broadcast a bare id, which makes `notify` scan every key. And every broadcast walked every row of every account for the card's census (`schedulerView`, each row's cadence by the clock — ~90 ms at 50,274 rows). Reproduced on a generated 50,274-row index (62 MB, never his data): nine windows clicked over 4.4 s finished at 3.0 … 24.4 s, the event loop stalled 14.1 s.
- **The fix.** (1) One-row reads: `has(key)` (no copy) for `known()`, `peek(key)` (that row) for `convFor` / `pointerSync` / the grant answers / `setFilter`, `table()` for one filter or one rotation cursor; whole-index scans read `live()` read-only or copy only the rows they keep — the engine calls `snapshot()` nowhere. (2) THE INCREMENTAL WRITE: index.json is written from cached chunks of 256 rows, byte-identical to `JSON.stringify(ix, RUNTIME_KEYS, 1)`. `entry()` marks its row; an update that reaches `ix.conversations` or calls `live()` marks EVERY row (a whole write — the conservative default); `rows()` + `touch(key)` = a scan inside an update that marks only what it changes (discovery's unlisting; discovery pages and change-feed births ask `has()`); close() writes the whole serialization; every 2 s tick re-checks two chunks, so a row changed outside `update()` reaches the disk within chunks / 2 ticks and is said with its key. (3) THE KEPT ROW FACTS: what the clock does not move — listed, unread, unlisted, paused, overridden, being read, walked — is kept per account (`index.onTouch` names the touched rows, a partial digest re-reads only those; a full digest, a whole-map touch or a minute without one re-sums); the digest's unread total and the card's counts read it. (4) THE PACED CENSUS (r2, the coordinator's ruling 2026-10-03): the CLOCK counts (hot / warm / cold / due) are walked at most once per 5 s per account; a broadcast inside the window reads the last walk and arms ONE trailing walk + broadcast at its end (never from a trailing broadcast), so the card settles exact; what a user's action moves stays exact on every broadcast. (5) Mark-read broadcasts its key.
- **Measured** (the same storm, head vs base): each of the nine windows done ≤ 8 ms after its click (base 3.0–24.4 s); the write after one row changed 30 ms (579 ms); the event loop's longest stall 30 ms (14.1 s). Work meter, one whole open at 50,286 vs 100,560 rows: 120,905 vs 120,807 (base 358 M → 716 M).
- **不变量** = a read of one conversation costs that conversation, never the index; a write re-serializes what changed, and "every row changed" is a write tracker's conservative default — never its assumption.
- **Verify r1.** The persistence attack held (SIGKILL at every write step, ENOSPC, two racing writers, the loader's set-aside: always the old file or the new one); a proxy census on every read surface over 33 channel suites saw no write outside an update. Three latent tracker gaps closed: an update's rows are marked again at its END (a write inside an async fn's await had cleared them), the sweep's cycle end counts the map against the chunks (a row born past `entry()`), a re-born row or a touch of a missing one is a whole-map write (the map's order). Rule: a dirty-row tracker re-marks at the END of the unit of work, never only where a row is first reached.
- Gates: test-channels-census-pace (new, fast, 10: a 21 s burst over 50,274 rows walks ≤ ceil(21/5)+1, the user-moved numbers exact on every broadcast, the trailing census = the full walk; controls pace 0 / a timer that never fires). test-channels-index-scale (new, heavy, 39: ① the whole open bounded, 0 census walks inside it + controls base known() / whole-map re-sum / bare-id broadcast; ② the write bounded + the whole-file control; ③ the bytes through a walk; ④ the sweep; ⑤ VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_INDEX_VERIFY's own control; ⑥ the kept total = the old sum; ⑦ no `snapshot()` in the engine; ⑧ every engine writer incremental + control). The census: 32 channel suites run with VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_INDEX_VERIFY = 0 drift. test-channels-engine's two controls re-modelled (mark-read's broadcast names the key; the r3-first gate's `convFor` as it was — a whole-index clone).

## AN AGENT COPIED A FILE THROUGH `run` — pull / push through the agent's own file ops (lane exit-transfer, 2026-10-03, design 013 B)

- **What happened.** The owner's screenshot: a conversation moved a big file off a paired Windows machine with dozens of `vibespace-exit run` calls (8 MiB base64 chunks, a PowerShell receiver on the machine's own loopback reached through `use`) — 30 s per call, the output cap, no integrity, a shell. The hub already streamed device files for the user (`read-range`); agents had no door to it.
- **The fix.** `vibespace-exit pull` / `push` (src/exit-proxy.js `_transfer`, PURE verdicts + words in src/exit-reach.js): the `run` verdict + its ask, judged again between windows; pull = `read-range` in 8 MiB windows through the NEW sink form of `fsReadRange` (nothing kept beyond the window's writes) with the NEW `sha256: true` flag (fs-done carries the hash of the bytes sent; an old agent ignores it ⇒ "size verified"); push = the NEW device op `write-stream` (capability `fs-write-stream`, the three touches: FS_ACTIONS `part-open/part-write/part-commit` + the fs-op handler, `client.fsWriteStream`, the hello-ack string) — `<path>.vs-part` made new with 'wx', worker writes in 1 MiB steps credited as the disk takes them, a COUNT-GATED `end` (the read-range contract inverted: the end can overtake queued data) that renames only when the count and the sha256 match; abort / 60 s idle / the link's death remove the part.
- **不变量** = a transfer never starts a process on either side (test-agentd-transfer ⑥: a child_process census on the real agent); every byte that lands was counted AND hashed on both ends; a failure keeps nothing on the receiving side; the hub holds at most one window of a file (gc'd probe ≤ 2 windows over a 100 MiB run; the whole-read control measures ≥ 90 MiB); a pull writes only inside the browser CLI's write fence, judged physically.
- Gates: test-exit-reach (the verdict table, path shapes, bound, words, row + 5 controls), test-exit-run §8 (the real manager over a fake agent: windows, hash / stall / revoke / growth / bound / fence / ask / remote_session / push gate + 5 controls; the routes + the real CLI), test-agentd-transfer (heavy: a REAL agent, 100 MiB both ways), test-dial-facts (three content-hash exemptions + the fence's two reads declared).

## A PULL WROTE WHERE IT WAS JUDGED A MINUTE AGO — the local write judged when it writes, one pull per target (lane exit-transfer fix r1, 2026-10-03)

- **What the review found** (verify r1 of B-ab7e, read from the code; reproduced by test-exit-run §8 (n) / (o) on 7e634160): ① `_localTarget` judged a pull's local path ONCE, before the ask (up to 60 s) and the stat; the part was then made by path after `mkdirSync(recursive)` — a destination folder moved away during the ask was silently re-made and the file landed in it; a folder swapped for a link had the part written THROUGH the link (into VibeSpace's data) before the realpath check at the rename removed it. ② every pull into one target shared `<target>.vs-part`: a second pull removed the first one's part and made its own; the first then renamed the second's part and answered "sha256 verified" for bytes that were not the file on disk.
- **The fix.** src/exit-proxy.js `_transferHeld` (pull): the folder's dev + inode pinned at the verdict; `inPlace(fd)` = `_localTarget` again on the physical target (the same path, still allowed) + the folder's identity + the part's (its fstat = its name's lstat, one link) — before the part is made, after every window, right before the rename. The part is the transfer's OWN fresh name (`<target>.<8 hex>.vs-part`, O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW), removed only while its name still holds the handle's file (else its bytes are cut through the handle and its current name, /proc/self/fd, removed when it is the same file); its size = the counted bytes before the rename. `_pullTargets` (the physical target) refuses a second pull `target_busy` (409); `_transfer`'s finally gives it back — never the refused pull.
- **不变量** = a pull's bytes go only into a folder judged allowed at the moment they are written and renamed — the verdict's folder by identity, never re-made; a part is made by exactly one transfer and removed only by it; "verified" is said only of the file that is at the target.
- Gates: test-exit-run §8 (n) a folder moved during the ask, (n2) a folder swapped for a link into data, (o) two pulls into one target by two spellings; §8c controls x6 (no write-time judge ⇒ lands in the re-made folder), x7 (no busy check ⇒ the second pull runs), x3 now patches the judge itself; test-agentd-transfer ⑤ (a real agent: two pulls into one target).

## THE HUB CHOSE THE SHELL — THE SHELL IS THE DEVICE'S FACT (lane-exit-run-output, 2026-10-01 — the owner's screenshot of a paired Windows box: "这里执行了指令怎么看不到回复。侧边栏也看不到指令和结果历史")

- **What happened.** Four `vibespace-exit run` commands on WINDOWS-PC (a Windows machine — the agent even tried `cmd /d /c ver`): `nvidia-smi …`, `cmd /d /c ver`, `hostname`, `echo NOMAD_READONLY_PING`. The audit held four lines `code 1, ms 7–8, ok true` with no output; the chat showed four cards "ran `…` on WINDOWS-PC — exit 1 · 0.0 s"; the Machines row showed `lastRun` only; the agent spent a turn guessing "远端缺少或无法启动 sh".
- **Why, three layers.** (R1) src/exit-proxy.js ran EVERY command as `dm.runCmd('sh', ['-lc', cmd])` — the HUB chose the interpreter for a machine it never runs on; a Windows daemon has no `sh`, so execFile failed with ENOENT in ~8 ms. (R2) agentd's `run-cmd` folded that spawn failure into `code: Number.isInteger(err.code) ? err.code : 1` with empty streams and dropped `err.message` — a child that never started was indistinguishable from one that ran and exited 1. (R3) the card printed head + exit + seconds, the audit line kept no output, and no surface listed a machine's runs although `auditTail` existed server-side.
- **The fix.** PURE src/exit-shell.js: the DAEMON plans the shell where it runs (`shellPlan(process.platform, line)`: win32 ⇒ `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<line>"` + `windowsVerbatimArguments`, a CR/LF line refused by name; else `sh -lc`); the `run-cmd` op accepts `{shell}`, `run-shell` in the hello-ack, the hub sends the LINE to a capable daemon and `sh -lc` to an older one (never an op it lacks). `spawnFailure(err)` names a child that never started — `cmd-result.spawnError {code, message}` beside the shell's own 127 / 126 an older hub reads; the hub refuses `spawn_failed` with one sentence (why, nothing ran, what the machine runs commands under, that an `sh` failure on a Windows box means an older agent), the audit line / the row / the card say it, the CLI exits by the shell's code. `outputHeads` keeps 4 KiB per stream (URL secrets cut, the peer-text belt) on the audit line, the card draws the first lines + "Show output", the ONE audit writer broadcasts `exit-audit`, `GET /api/hosts/:id/exit-runs` (owner) / `GET /api/agent/exit/runs` (own) + the keyed "Commands…" dialog + `vibespace-exit runs`; the row states the device's platform.
- **不变量** = the interpreter of a command is a fact of the machine that runs it — the hub names a LINE, never a shell (`hostId` is a parameter: the device decides what only the device knows); a child that never started is named as such, never folded into an exit code; a command's output is kept where the user looks (bounded, redacted, belted) — "exit 1 · 0.0 s" with nothing to read is a silent failure.
- **Gates:** test-exit-run (heavy since lane fast-budget, a SERIAL clock witness; 106: PURE tables over node's REAL execFile errors, fake daemons with and without the capability, the routes, the CLI, a REAL daemon + a control daemon built from a copy that never consults the judge), test-exit-reach (the card rows + control), test-peer-text-census (the new door), test-architecture §65 (D) (the exit CLI), test-exit-access-ui ⑤ (heavy).

## A FLEET USER'S AGENTS NEVER LEARNED THE TOOLS (lane hooks-create, 2026-10-01 — read-only forensics on a fleet pod, VibeSpace 2.369.199)

- **What happened.** Every boot logged `Hook registration (claude) skipped: ~/.claude/settings.json not found (start the CLI once to create it)`. The user had ~/.claude (projects/, plugins/, skills/) since the pod's first day and no settings.json: the CLI writes that file only when somebody changes a setting. So VibeSpace never registered SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / Stop — 0 `vibespace-reminder` in her 11 transcripts — and an agent asked to use the browser spent four minutes probing DISPLAY, installing gcloud and listing MCP servers before stumbling on `vibespace-browser`. Four more pods in the same state.
- **Why.** claude's descriptor declared the file `createIfMissing: false` with the comment "the CLI writes its own on first run" — a belief never measured; the chip told the user to "start the CLI once", which she had done many times.
- **The fix.** `createIfMissing` is a closed set `false | 'dir-exists'` (src/harness-config.js): the FILE is created when its directory exists (0600, linked into place exclusively, never the directory); claude's settings.json declares 'dir-exists'; the chips say "will be created at the next start — or press Apply" beside a working Apply; the conversations already running get one free next-turn note (dropped unread in a resumed process) and the owner one For-you line.
- **不变量** = a file we depend on is created by us when its directory proves the tool is in use — never the directory, never on a guess; and a file another program "will write" is a measured fact or it is ours.

## ONE 5-SECOND ATTEMPT DECIDED FOR EVER (lane notify-retry, 2.369.200 — the owner: "以前这个是自动唤醒的啊 怎么现在开始排队要我手动发了？")

- **What happened.** The cron job dc-discussion-watch woke its owner conversation seven times over two days (`lane: message, ok: true`); at 14:17:13 PDT one local peer post answered `timeout` (postToPeer's 5 s) while the CLI's pid lived ⇒ `[jobs] notify → stashed (timeout)` ⇒ two seconds later the stash "waits for the next prompt — the 900 B digest does not fit the 0 B left under the inline cap" (39 skills + task context first) ⇒ nothing until the owner typed at 14:53, and the hand-over card said "These completed while this conversation was closed". It never was.
- **Why.** (H1) ONE attempt decided: a transient miss on a live pid was stashed at once and the stash is drained only at a prompt — never, for a conversation nobody types into. (H2) the inline cap is the wrong door for a 900 B message a live session can receive as its own frame. (H3) the words were a fixed sentence. And the `timeout` itself: on Linux a unix-socket connect completes at the syscall or fails at once (MEASURED with a non-accepting python listener: a full backlog answers EAGAIN at 0 ms, never a hang), and libuv hands the connect callback to the next loop iteration's pending phase, which runs AFTER the timers phase — so a stall of OUR loop longer than the timer, right after `net.connect()`, called a completed connect a timeout (reproduced: 160 ms stall over a 40 ms timer on the pre-fix copy).
- **The fix.** `postToPeer` judges by the socket's phases (connect → write → written → closed) and defers the timer's verdict one loop turn; it classifies `transient` and measures `late` (a stalled loop) — both ride the journal line and the job's Delivery log with `target mid-turn`. The ladder PARKS a transient miss on a live pid (`data/msg-retry.json`) and posts the same text at the conversation's turn end (server.js's hooked `noteTurnEnd`) and on a backoff bounded to 60 min, under the SAME authorization (held, converted when it lands, released on its own TTL and re-judged after), then falls to the stash as `not-reachable`; a dead pid stashes at once as `not-running`. A prompt that cannot carry the stash arms a hand-over its turn end posts as ONE frame (`stash-retry`). The words come from the entries' `held` kinds.
- **不变量** = one attempt is never a verdict about a live process — a transient miss on a live pid is retried at the next moment the process can take it (its turn end), under the authorization already taken; a timer alone never judges an I/O whose completion may be queued (defer one loop turn, measure the lateness); "wait for the next prompt" is never said of a live conversation; a held notice says why it was held, from its own record, never from a fixed sentence. Gate: test-notify-retry (150) + the re-pinned test-job-model / test-jobs-triage / test-spend-paths §5 / test-stash-strip.
- **Verify r3 (2026-10-01).** Three more, each reproduced: ① a may-have-landed copy (a `ho` / `inflight` stamp at boot) handed to a FULL stash made the cap evict the oldest REAL waiting entry — at both caps a possible repeat gives way before a certain miss, said; ② a floor witness (`lastPostAt`, the jobs' `_notifyRate.ts`) stamped in the future by a backward clock step held the floor for the whole step and the notice expired unposted — a witness ahead of now is DROPPED (never re-based to now: that would hold the next frame 30 s for a post that never happened); ③ the floor is read off the last LANDED post, so a turn end during a frame's flight posted a second frame 5 ms behind it — one attempt in flight per conversation. And the rule itself, stated once: PURE `src/park-step.js` (9 states × 19 events = 171 cells) with test-park-step's seeded walk (every sequence ≤ 4) and the engine driven through all 95 drivable cells (95 agree). 不变量 = a possible repeat never displaces a certain miss; a witness from the future is no witness; a frame on the wire is the conversation's only frame; the park's rule lives in ONE table the engine is measured against, and a new state or event goes into the table first.
- THE OWNER'S OUTCOMES, THE THIRD JUDGEMENT (notify-retry verify r4, 2026-10-01; 34 scenarios drawn from r1–r3's findings and the original incident, each driven through the REAL ladder + REAL jobs engine + REAL hand-over view + REAL drains; the table's verdict, the engine's record and what the owner sees compared — 34 / 34 agree on the final head). Three findings, each reproduced before its fix: ① (LOW, words) the jobs engine's fell listener carried maybeDelivered / evicted but DROPPED `expired` — the digest tail's "The hour of retries passed…" (r2 ⑦) could never fire for a jobs notification, and the parked Delivery-log line stayed one retry short of the attempts the stash line named (the last attempt's failure IS the fall; no `attempt` event follows it) — FIX = `expired` carried, the parked line closed at the fall with the attempts as counted; ② (LOW, spec) the table lacked two doors the engine has — the hand-over's CLAIM of a waiting entry and a prompt's inline TAKE (S10 / S12 / S13 read "table lacks handover-claim / prompt-take") — FIX = 9 × 21, test-park-step's DOOR CENSUS (every engine door names its event, every event has a door, every `via` is an event, a terminal record is never written again), the I5b hold-conversion invariant (a cell mutant converting a forgotten hold was green under every rule), three cell-level controls; ③ (LOW, money bounded by the spend ceiling) a clock that KEEPS stepping back (two time daemons fighting) found the floor witness in the future at every attempt and dropped it (r3 ②) — seven frames in one millisecond, seven billed wakes, the 30 s floor gone — FIX = the first drop stands, a second future witness within the hour is RE-BASED to now (one floor held — the lesser harm while the clock misbehaves), said once an hour; both twins (the park's `lastPostAt`, the jobs' `_notifyRate`). Refuted with evidence: T2① a hit during a 5 s flight is not lost — the waiting turn end re-asks the floor and the TIMER posts it at the landing + 30 s (no second turn end needed); a crash mid-flight leaves each entry's own `inflight` stamp (identity, not the conversation). Held (LOW): a stash eviction — a may-have-landed copy's or a real entry's — is journaled only, never a For-you line (pre-existing shape: the evicted job's record keeps its last stash line; the owner's panel shows the 30 waiting); the park id `rt-<ms36>-<seq>` is unique by construction here — the fleet deploys with `strategy: Recreate` (deploy/helm/vibespace-user/templates/main.yaml) and the service restarts with `RestartSec=5` (scripts/install-service.sh), so two engines over one file in the same millisecond is unreachable outside a frozen test clock. 不变量 = a producer's held record carries EVERY detail the words can name (a sentence nobody can reach is a lie in waiting); every door of an engine is a cell of its table; a witness dropped twice in an hour is a clock, not a fact — bound it; the third judgement is what the owner sees, and it is measured, never assumed.
- **Verify r1 (2026-10-01) 不变量, each reproduced first:** an entry whose post is IN FLIGHT is nobody's to take (the hand-over took it and posted its own frame: the notice twice, two turns); ONE wake carries EVERY parked entry of a conversation (five notices were five billed wakes); a sweep that moves nothing must not re-arm at once (a failed frame's rest beyond the bound spun the timer at 0 ms); a park is bounded and names its drop (STASH_CAP, `evicted`); an in-flight entry at boot MAY HAVE LANDED — the stash, never a re-post (the CLI's dedup is per sender; a restarted hub is a new sender), and a graceful stop waits for the posts in flight; a schedule bound holds at every attempt, a boot's included (a two-hour-old entry was posted and billed); a torn store is set aside with its bytes, never read as empty; unknown is said as unknown (a restore's default read as "no"); a TTL release never touches an in-flight entry's hold.
- **Verify r2 (2026-10-01) 不变量, each reproduced first:** a claim stamp is released by the process that minted it or by the next boot — never by nobody (a `ho`-claimed park entry across a crash was invisible to every door for ever); a bounded delivery queue rides in the order the producers spoke, oldest first, because the bound expires the oldest (a newest-first cut dropped the one that waited longest); a wall-clock instant stored for the future is the clock's fact, not the record's — re-base at every read and judge by a monotonic count too (a two-hour step back = three hours of unbounded attempts); a card drawn for a frame that landed draws the words as they stand and dedups by the frame as written (a mid-flight clear left two cards); a cap counts what WAITS — an entry spoken for (on the wire, claimed) is neither counted nor evicted; a wait for an I/O in flight is at least the I/O's own bound (a 5 s exit settle under a 6.15 s post); a held record says HOW it got there, not only that it waited (thirty may-have-landed notices read as refused).

## A LONG PRESS ON CHAT TEXT OPENED THE MESSAGE MENU OVER THE WORDS (lane mobile-select, 2026-10-02 — a tester's phone, via the owner)

- **The report.** "手机模式下想要复制一段chatview里的内容会触发右键菜单导致选择了右键菜单的内容，无法正确选择要复制的内容" — on a phone, pressing and holding chat text to copy it opened the message menu, and the selection landed on the menu.
- **Measured** (Chrome's own touch gesture path, 390×844 DPR 3, Android UA): +0 touchstart on the paragraph → +501 ms our synthetic contextmenu → the chat opened its menu with its corner at the finger → +680 ms the native long press: selectstart (the word selected) → a TRUSTED touch contextmenu → the chat cancelled it and built the menu again → the selection sat under the menu. iOS has no contextmenu: our 500 ms timer was the only menu, racing iOS's selection. The cause was a 2026-09-20 rule (design-mobile-gaps #5): on touch a long press ANYWHERE on a message opened its menu, because the hover buttons were hidden ≤ 768 px.
- **Fix.** ONE door judges every touch press (utils.js installLongPressContextMenu + PURE src/lib/press-select.js): selectable text under the finger ⇒ no timer, and the trusted contextmenu is stopped before any handler WITHOUT preventDefault; a menu press (chrome, gutter, a toggle, a none label) that an app handler took cancels `selectstart` while the finger is down, and when the platform's long press comes first our menu fires at its `selectstart` (measured second order: a press on the role strip opened our menu, then Chrome selected "Answer" and that selection closed it); a press no handler takes (the file viewer) keeps the platform's behaviour. The menu moved to a … button per message, floated so it is never drawn over the words. An open menu closes when a touch selection starts outside it; menus, popovers, toasts, the chooser and tab chips say user-select none themselves. Copy text names what it copied.
- **Verify r1 (2026-10-02; three findings reproduced on the real build, fixed in one commit).** F1 a code-first message: the toolbar's "Wrap" was the element under the … (a tap toggled wrap), the `pre` 38 px narrower to its last line (a formatting context beside a float is narrowed for its whole height) ⇒ code blocks / tables `clear: right` in a message with the button. F2 bubble mode: a short message's words sat UNDER the button (a shrink-to-fit bubble measures max(float, words), never their sum) ⇒ the float lives in the first paragraph. F3 a touch tablet (1024 px, isTouch not isMobile): an invisible hover "Open in editor" covered the … and a tap opened the editor ⇒ the hover buttons hide by app.isTouch's media query, never by width. 不变量=a floated control is judged beside every block kind its host can hold, in every layout mode, on every device class the gate's media query admits — "drawn over no words" is not "the element under its own centre".
- **The finger's point, not the event's target (channel-touch-menu verify r1, 2026-10-03).** Chrome's touch adjustment retargets a touchstart to a control NEAR the finger: a long press on a channel message's first word, 11 px under its author's name (role=button), arrived with clientX/Y on the word and target = the name, while the platform's long press selected the word — the door judged the target ⇒ its 500 ms menu held the selection off (heavy test-channel-threads-ui (p), the chat's Android method). `pressFacts` now judges `document.elementFromPoint(x, y)`; the target only when nothing is there. A harness press is read where it LANDED (the touch's point), never by its target.
- **不变量 = a long press on selectable text is a selection, never a menu.** A touch surface whose menu lives on text gets a visible affordance; a handler never re-derives the rule — it asks the door. Gates: test-press-select (fast) + test-mobile-select (heavy).

REFUTED with evidence: the 9222 port collision (the image's chromium.d prefix, last-wins → port 0, DevToolsActivePort 41607 on userW's pod); the CLI's 30 s give-up on a queued /resolve (`call()` has no timeout — only the harness's tool timeout cuts it, hence F4). 不变量=a ladder is ONE ordered function and a swapped order is a RED control; a removal is keyed on the thing judged, never on the shape found; what a refused attempt learned (the lineage, the mark) rides the record it leaves; a note is said in an answer that was DELIVERED.

- **What happened.** His fleet pod rolled (`vibespace-pod-a-5d6f7c8b9a-x1y2z` → `…-7e8f9a0b1c-p3q4r`, the same RWO home). His pinned profile "jarvis-work" then refused every start — `profile_locked … is held by another browser process (pid 452500 on vibespace-pod-a-5d6f7c8b9a-x1y2z) — the lock (…/SingletonLock) names another machine … if this machine was renamed … remove …` — until his agent removed `Singleton{Lock,Socket,Cookie}` by hand, exactly as the sentence suggested (W1). - **Why.** (W1) Chromium's `SingletonLock` is a symlink `<hostname>-<pid>` INSIDE the profile directory on the persistent volume; the dead pod left it there, and Chromium — like lane H r4's verdict — judges a lock by hostname and refuses a foreign one for ever. The verdict had the remedy in words ("if this machine was renamed … remove …") and no way to KNOW the machine was renamed. (W2) The binary keeps each session's bound tab by CDP target id across a daemon restart and, pinned, answers `tab_gone` once it is gone; every tab of a replaced browser is gone. `stop()` marks every lease so its next attach binds a tab first — but a browser life the keeper did not end (a daemon found dead, a boot that could not adopt it, an in-place relaunch) marked nothing.
- **The fix.** (L1) The witness is the keeper's OWN registry: every launch stamps the record with the machine's hostname (the lineage `hosts`), the registry file is stamped with its writer; `profileLockVerdict({…, launchHosts})` answers `stale-previous-host` for a lock whose hostname is not ours but IS one this keeper launched on — the three Singleton SYMLINKS are removed, the launch goes on, the journal says "the lock named this machine's previous name <old> — taken over", the profile says "renamed from <old>" for a day. A foreign hostname never launched on stays refused by name, with the two hostnames and the one command (`rm -f '<dir>/SingletonLock'`). A legacy record inherits the file's writer, else nothing. (L2) `tabsLost` marks every lease of a replaced NAMED browser (`life`) from the dead-daemon path, the boot and the in-place relaunch; the attach binds the browser's ONE unowned page (`tab <targetId>`, no second blank tab) else a new tab of its own, and the answer says so once (`[tab_rebound]`).

## THE MAC REPAIR COMMAND DIED ON ONE BYTE: `bash: line 253: DHOST?: unbound variable` (lane install-ellipsis, 2026-10-02, the owner's Macbook re-pairing on 2.369.199)

- **What happened.** The owner pasted the pairing dialog's repair command on a Mac. The installer fetched the daemon bundle and then died at the new dial-check line (2.369.197, lane-pairing ⑤) before the check ran: `bash: line 253: DHOST?: unbound variable`. Nothing was installed, nothing said why.
- **Why.** macOS ships `/bin/bash` 3.2 (2007). Under it a byte ≥ 0x80 right after `$NAME` is taken as part of the NAME: `"… dial $DHOST…"` read the variable `DHOST\xe2` (the terminal prints the byte as `?`), unset under `set -u`. bash 4/5 on Linux stops the name at the first non-identifier byte, so every Linux run and every gate was green; the line had never run on a Mac. The ellipsis was the only such site in the tree (the `→` / `✗` glyphs open their lines, never follow an expansion).
- **The fix.** `${DHOST}…` — a braced expansion. The gate: test-dial-facts' macOS bash 3.2 census runs `/\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[^\x00-\x7F]/` over every shell script a device may run from an instance (the device installer, install.sh, scripts/*.sh) and names the offending line; the pre-fix line is the control. **Workaround on an instance before the fix:** pipe the script through `perl -pe 's/\xE2\x80\xA6/.../g'` before `bash -s`, or run it with Homebrew's bash.
- **不变量** = a shell script a user's machine runs is written for the OLDEST shell it may meet (macOS bash 3.2): an expansion followed by a non-ASCII byte is braced; a glyph never directly follows `$NAME`; a Linux-only green on a Mac-facing script is no evidence.

## A WINDOW OPENED IN THE FIRST SECONDS AFTER A LOAD WAS CLOSED BY A RECORD OLDER THAN IT (2.369.199 integration — found by test-channels-i18n's phone pass and test-desktop-xpra-window §10 (5) on the composed tree)

- **What happened.** A phone page opened a Channels window during the boot's 5 s `_restoring`; 12 ms after the next window opened, `_applyRemoteState` (via `_handleRemoteSync`) closed it — traced with a wrapper on `wm.closeWindow`. In the xpra suite a desktop-app window re-opened right after a peer's close never reached the layout.
- **Why.** Since lane desktop-move (r1+) a remote record of the desktop on show is DEFERRED under `_restoring` (the boot's 5 s, an apply's 1 s cooldown), never dropped; master applied it at once. Drained at the gate's end, it closed every local window it did not list — including the windows this page opened after the record had arrived.
- **The fix.** `WindowManager.createWindow` stamps `_bornAt`; the apply's close loop passes over a window born after the record's `receivedAt` (beside the held move, the remote move-out and the wired-only re-read).
- **不变量** = a record undoes only what happened before it arrived — a window's BIRTH is an act like a move; a deferred record is judged by its arrival, never by its drain.
