## THREE GATE JUDGES READ THE RUNNER, NOT THE CHANGE — A COMPLEXITY PIN ON THE CLOCK, A CARD'S TRANSIENT, A BUTTON'S PRE-FOLD RECT (lane-mirror-198, 2026-09-29 — the Actions mirror of 2.369.198: test-channel-reactions red on the fast job, test-new-session-dialog red on both heavy attempts, test-browser-identity red once)

- **What happened (a shared 4-vCPU runner at nice 15).** ① `linear: quickSet(n keys) — 2× the input ⇒ ≤ 2.5× the time (… ×2.50)` and `measurable: whoList / chipPlan × n reached the floor … (1.1 ms)` — a wall-clock ratio at its own boundary and a floor the runner's calibration never reached (the .197 rebuild had only moved the coin flip from the median to the minimums); ② `C3 the card shows it resolved, its buttons gone` — both attempts; ③ `a REAL click on Reconnect RE-RESOLVED the target` — `{"target":null,"error":{"code":"not_attached"…}}`, green on the retry. All three green on this box, every run.
- **Why (each reproduced under the runner's conditions — `taskset -c 0-3 nice -n 15`, a DejaVu-only fontconfig — or by construction).** ① Time is the machine's, not the parser's. ② The click renders "✓ Allowed" AT ONCE (the optimistic overlay in the click handler), then the stub's tool_result COMPLETES the card and `renderToolMsg` drops the overlay BY RULE (resolved + complete ⇒ no overlay: the ✓ label and the output say it ran) — taking `data-request-id` with it; the judge asserted that transient through `data-request-id` and lost the race to the round trip click → stdin → tool_result → edit → swap. Two orders: (A) the judge's first sample before the completion edit (this box), (B) after it (the runner; a control now shows the old expression FALSE on the completed card). ③ Reconnect's appearance schedules the bar's fold (bar-fold.js: MutationObserver → rAF → layoutNow); under DejaVu's widths eight lower-priority items fold and the button moves 126 px left ONE FRAME later (measured: x 774.8 → 648.8); the judge read the rect the moment the refusal appeared and clicked it three CDP round trips later — (A) both before that frame: hit; (B) the frame between them: the click lands on the bar, "Reconnect does nothing".
- **The fix.** ① `scripts/work-meter.mjs` — a complexity gate COUNTS WORK: V8 precise block coverage (exact per-block execution counts of the measured modules, taken and reset around each call) + the element work of the natives a parser leans on (the array / string / collection / iterator prototypes patched only while a call is measured: `includes` adds the elements it scanned, `filter` the callbacks it ran, a string walker its receiver's length) — never the clock: a linear parser reads ×2.00 on any machine, the pre-fix quadratic `compactSide` ×3.90, and the meter proves itself first (the same call measured twice agrees to the op; 20 runs under the runner's conditions, 20 × 107 green). Counted now: the reactions census, test-channel-thread's index / first page / placeOf claims, test-dial-facts' O(1) per hit, test-usage-ledger-perf's per-pair and memo claims (the suite's own brute-force reference is the control: 22 121 ops per pair against 64 072 for a full scan), test-channels-lark-shape's 4 KiB cut; test-channel-outbox's "refused BEFORE any lookup" is proven by a spy set (0 reads of its keys; 2 for a good key) — a fact about the set, never the clock. ONE informational timing line stays, never asserted. ② The judge keys the MESSAGE (`<sid>:t:<toolUseId>` rides the swap) and waits on the card's own settled evidence — buttons gone AND (the overlay says Allowed OR the card is complete) — then on the completed card, each with a deadline. ③ The judge reads the button's rect only once it has SETTLED (the same rect across two animation frames and elementFromPoint at its centre IS the button — the fold's own evidence) and waits on the re-resolve's own evidence (`followed` incremented + the new target id) with a deadline scaled to this machine's measured follow (5×, ≥ 10 s).
- **不变量** = a complexity gate counts WORK (block executions + the natives' element work), never the clock — a count is the same on every machine, and a ratio at its own boundary on a shared runner is a coin flip whichever statistic it takes; a chrome judge waits on the CHANGE'S OWN EVIDENCE with a deadline — a keyed element that survives the re-render, a rect that has settled across frames, a counter the act increments — never on a transient the product replaces by rule, never on a rect read before the frame that moves it. Held, by name: the regex-backtracking controls of test-channel-blocks / test-mail-frame (the meter counts a regex by its receiver's length — a step counter would be needed), the I/O-timeout legs (a mechanism's constant × a stated slack, the .189 lesson) and test-codex-zst's tick gap (an event-loop property).

## A DRAG ONTO A DESKTOP THE PAGE HAD NOT OPENED WIPED THAT DESKTOP'S WINDOWS — A CACHE OF A RECORD THE PAGE HAD NOT BUILT WAS REBUILT FROM THE PAGE (userW inc-mun7qjmw-iksh, userW 2026-09-29, 2.369.196 — present through 2.369.198; lane desktop-move)

- **What happened.** 13 desktops, the page on Fin; HR never opened since the page loaded (its 3 windows lived only in the desktop manager's cache — a desktop's windows are built on its first visit). A title-bar drag of a Fin window onto HR's taskbar preview, a click on HR: only the moved window was there, and the autosave 5.5 s later wrote `HR = [the moved window]` over the server's record — HR 3 → 1, recoverable only through a layout rollback point (the pre-drag one survived; the ring keeps 10 oldest + 30 newest).
- **Why.** `_updateCachedDesktop` (the move's target update) rebuilt the target's cached record FROM THE WINDOWS BUILT IN THE PAGE (`cached.windows = wins`) — for a never-visited desktop that is only the moved window; `switchTo` replays what the cache holds (nothing else), and ws-handler's layout-sync REPLACES a desktop's record whole. Every door reached it: the drop, the "Move to Desktop" menu, command mode d/D, and resume placement (resume-all of a desktop never opened — no gesture at all). The preview drew 1 rect at the drop (its cache fallback ran only when no live window was there). The move's target was also never SENT: a reload before visiting HR lost the moved window too.
- **The fix.** PURE `src/lib/desktop-record.js`: `mergeDesktopRecord({record, built, add, remove})` is the ONE rule for a held record (the record kept, the page's capture in its place, adds appended, removes dropped); `DesktopManager._setRecord` is its ONE writer (census in scripts/test-desktop-record.mjs); a move adds the moved windows to the target and removes them from the source; every record that leaves the page is `recordFor(desk)` = held ∪ built − (windows the page TRIED to build and could not, after a 20 s grace) − (windows the page holds on another desktop); the autosave sends a changed desktop it does not show from its held record; the preview draws the record's unbuilt windows beside the live ones; resume placement `replaces` its old never-opened entry. The server belt (ws-handler, PURE `shrinkVerdict`) refuses a sync that loses ≥ 2 windows nothing explains (the client's evidence: closed / moved / replaced / unbuilt; or the window's session gone) and hands its record back (`layout-sync-refused`); the page reconciles (view = that record + what it built, missing windows opened, a toast, re-sent). A rollback point now names the change that followed it ("Then: HR 3 → 1").
- **不变量** = a cache of a record the page has not built IS the record: a write merges, never replaces; an autosave never shrinks what it did not build; a window leaves a record only by a close, a move, a replace or a failed build — each named to the server, which refuses a shrink nobody explains. Gates: test-desktop-record (heavy since verify r5 — 162 s on the real timers, THE TIER RULE; fast until then) + test-desktop-move (heavy: the incident's gesture on a real page, the belt on a forged sync and on the pre-fix writer re-installed live).

## A DRAG ON THE DESKTOP ON SHOW WAS SNAPPED BACK BY THE RECORD DEFERRED UNDER IT (lane desktop-move verify r2 ⑩, 2026-09-30; pre-existing since §6b guard 3, reproduced on two real pages)

- **What happened.** B drags hr-2 across HR; A's autosave of HR (hr-2 where A last saw it) lands on B and is deferred under the pointer; B releases 360 px away. 300 ms later guard 3 applied the deferred record: hr-2's box was "changed" against the record and `_applyGridBounds` put it back where A last saw it; the apply's dirty clear swallowed the drag's own save. 4 s later the box was back at its old place on B, the server held the old place, A never saw the drag, no toast. The held close and the held ratio already had the rule ("a local act the record could not know is kept and re-sent"); a drag and a resize did not.
- **Fix — THE HELD GEOMETRY (the held move's twin).** window.js stamps `win._boundsAt` at the drag's and the resize's pointerup; the apply keeps the user's box, maximize and minimize over a record received before it (`heldGeom`), applies the rest of the record, and `_resendHeldMove` sends the act once as the user's own (`_movesSentAt` marks acts a save already carried).
- **不变量**: the same as ①'s, for geometry — a record undoes only what happened before it arrived; every kind of local act (close, divider, move, drag, resize) is held over an older record and re-sent. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 v + control no-held-geometry + the §6 pin; test-desktop-move M (two real pages).

## A MOVE WHOSE WINDOW A PEER HAD CLOSED SAT ON THE PAGE, UNSENT, UNTIL THE NEXT ACT (lane desktop-move verify r5 ⑥, 2026-09-30; LOW, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** The held re-send (`_resendHeldMove`) is armed by the apply's loops when the record TOUCHES a held window. A peer's record of the desktop on show that never names the moved window (the peer closed it, captured before the move) touched nothing: the apply's dirty clear dropped the move's pending save, no loop re-armed it, and the window lived on its new desktop on the page only — its dirty desk waited for the user's next act; a reload in between lost it (the server had it nowhere once the peer's close was written). The move wins over a concurrent close by design (a close can be redone, a lost window cannot) — the gap was the save.
- **Fix.** The owed desk is the witness: at the end of `_applyRemoteState`, a dirty desk no owed save names re-arms the held re-send (which sends only what a held witness justifies). 不变量: a desktop this page owes the server is re-sent after any apply, whatever the record named. Gates: test-desktop-record a5 + control owed-desk-unarmed.

## THE STALE RELEASE COUNTED THE SAME EXPIRED ACT AGAIN AT THE NEXT RELEASE (lane desktop-move verify r5 ④, 2026-09-30; LOW, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** r4 ④'s `_expiredHeldActs` counted the witnesses past their hold and toasted "not kept (n)" — and left the stamps on the windows. An expired witness holds nothing (actHeld's bound), but a SECOND stale episode (another outage, the same page) counted it again and toasted "not kept (1)" for nothing new.
- **Fix.** What the count counts it retires: the expired `_movedAt` / `_boundsAt` / `_chainAt` zeroed, the expired held closes deleted. 不变量: a thing said once about a past act is not said again — a count that reports is a take. Gates: test-desktop-record st2's second episode (nothing new ⇒ no toast) + control expired-not-retired.

## A MERGE, A SPLIT OR A TEAR-OFF WAS UNDONE BY THE RECORD DEFERRED UNDER IT (lane desktop-move verify r5 ②, 2026-09-30; the r2 ⑩ class for the group itself, the merge reproduced on two real pages)

- **What happened.** The held witnesses covered a window's place (`_movedAt`), its box (`_boundsAt`) and a divider's ratio (`holdRatio`) — never the GROUP. The apply's chain loop breaks a local chain the record does not carry and applies a record's layout in place over a chain with the same members (`applyChainRecord`), and its create loop rebuilds a record's chain around any member not in a local chain. So a record of the desktop on show captured before the act and received after it (deferred under the drag, or under the cooldown where r3 ③ defers the act's save) dissolved a merge 300 ms after the drop (test-desktop-move R), put the tabs layout back over a side-by-side, pulled a torn-out tab back into its group — and the apply's dirty clear swallowed the act's save, so the server never saw the group.
- **Fix.** tab-group.js `witnessChain(chain, extra)` — THE ONE stamp, `win._chainAt` on every member (and the member that LEFT, the tear-off's `[winId]`), called by every structural verb this page runs (createTabChain, addToTabChain, bindSplit, unbindSplit, swapSplit, moveTabInChain when the key moved, the Undo's `_restoreChainLayout`, the tear-off's detach site) and by none of the apply's or the restore's paths (applyChainRecord, restoreTabChain, _detachFromChain, _ungroupLast, removeFromTabChain). layout.js's chain loop asks `actHeld(w._chainAt, receivedAt, w)`: a held host's chain is kept as it is (`heldKept`, re-sent once through `_resendHeldRatio`'s path), and a record's chain is never rebuilt around a held member; the stamp is counted at a stale release and re-armed after a sleep like every witness.
- **不变量**: every kind of local act — a close, a move, a box, a ratio, and now a GROUP's structure — is held over a record that cannot know it and re-sent as the user's own. Gates: test-desktop-record ch1 (merge) / ch2 (split) / ch3 (tear-off: the two-group stands, the 3-group is not rebuilt) + the chain witness pin + controls chain-unheld (the two hold lines gone: all three RED) / verb-unstamped; test-desktop-move R (two real pages: a real icon drag merges hr-3 into hr-1 150 ms into a cooldown, a record deferred under it, the group stands, the server carries it).

## THE DOORS r4 ③ MISSED — A PRESET, THE DIGIT SNAP, THE TEAR-OFF'S DROP, AN APP'S OWN □ — AND THE CENSUS THAT FINDS THE NEXT ONE (lane desktop-move verify r5 ③, 2026-09-30; the preset reproduced on two real pages)

- **What happened.** r4 ③ stamped the geometry witness at the doors it LISTED (the title-bar buttons, snapToHalf, revealWindow, move mode, the taskbar row + menu, command mode m + cycle) and the pin was that list. A layout preset (`applyLayout` — the toolbar's buttons, a custom grid, command mode's freeform), command mode's digit snap (`snapActiveToCell`), the drop that ends a tab torn out of its group (`_setupTabDrag`'s onUp → `_snapToGrid` / `_applySnap` / a free place), a desktop app's own □ / ▁ mirrored onto its frame (`onAppState`) and a named preset (`loadPreset`'s restore / minimize per window) stamped nothing: another page's record deferred under the second after them (the apply's cooldown, where r3 ③ defers the act's save) applied its older boxes over the act and the deferred save then wrote them back as the user's (test-desktop-move P: B's two-column preset 150 ms into a cooldown; a second record under it put all three windows back, nothing reached the server).
- **Fix.** Every one stamps `witnessGeometry` (applyLayout / snapActiveToCell / loadPreset on each window they place or minimize; the tear-off's drop before its snap; the app's state only when it IS an act — the app's state is the machine's truth, never undone by an older record). THE CENSUS (test-desktop-record §6): every call of a geometry primitive in src/lib (`wm.X(` / `this.X(` for toggleMaximize / minimize / restore / snapToHalf / snapActiveToCell / applyLayout / _snapToGrid / _snapToGridRange / _applySnap / _positionToCell) is grep-derived and must be one of: a call INTO a self-stamping verb (its body pinned to stamp), a site stamping within the four lines above, a primitive's own body, or a MACHINE path named with its reason (the apply, the boot restore, a replay's placement, the Stage's borrow / return, the refused drop's put-back, the title-bar drag's own drop) — anything else is RED by file:line (control planted-door), and a dead machine row is RED too.
- **不变量**: a list of doors is a snapshot; the doors are a census over every caller of the primitives, and a new caller is a door until it names itself a machine path. Gates: test-desktop-record §6 (the census + the doors pin + the self-stamp pin) + controls planted-door / 5 door-unwitnessed / self-stamp; test-desktop-move P (two real pages).

## A SLEEP IN THE SECOND AFTER A DRAG LOST IT AT THE WAKE, IN SILENCE (lane desktop-move verify r5 ①, 2026-09-30; the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** Every hold (ACT_HOLD_MS, CLOSE_HOLD_MS, RATIO_HOLD_MS, §6b guard 2's 60 s dirty expiry) is a wall-clock age. A laptop that sleeps in the ~2 s after a drag (the 500 ms debounce, or the apply's cooldown + the r3 ③ deferred save) wakes with `Date.now()` 20 min ahead while the page ran for none of it: the pending save timer fires at the wake and guard 2 drops it (`_lastUserInputAt` 20 min old), the witness is past its hold, the dead socket reconnects, the re-read answers from before the act and reverses it — no toast (not a stale episode). `performance.now()` is no cure: it stops during a sleep on Linux and macOS but not on Windows.
- **Fix.** THE CLOCK WATCH (layout.js): `_clockTick` every CLOCK_TICK_MS (5 s) and at every wake path (`scheduleAutoSave`, `_doAutoSave`, `_handleRemoteSync`, `_resyncFromServer`, the reconnect); a tick that arrives CLOCK_JUMP_MS (20 s) past its interval is a sleep and `_rearmAfterSuspend(gap, before)` moves forward by `gap` what was HELD at `before` (within its hold then, and not carried by an acked save): `_movedAt` / `_boundsAt`, held closes, held ratios, `_lastUserInputAt` while a save is pending, the owed answers' clocks. A run minute (the page ticking through it) expires as ever; `document.hidden` re-arms nothing (a throttled background tab's late tick is not a sleep, and nothing fresh can be held in a tab nobody drives).
- **不变量**: a hold measures how long the page RAN past the act, never how far the wall clock moved. Gates: test-desktop-record cj (a drag, a 20 min leap, the dead socket, the re-read: kept + saved) + control clock-unwatched (RED); st2 is the run-minute control (a minute the watch saw tick still expires); r5-fake A3/A3b/A3c.

## A SAVE THE SERVER NEVER READ COUNTED AS SENT — THE RE-READ REVERSED THE ACT FOR GOOD (lane desktop-move verify r5 ⑤, 2026-09-30; r4's held (a), reproduced on two real pages)

- **What happened.** The unsaved-act witness (r4 ①) was released at the SEND: `_movesSentAt = Date.now()` whenever `ws.connected`. A socket that looks open but the server never reads — a restart under it, a wifi drop the browser notices late — swallowed the save; at the reconnect the re-read answered from before the act, `actHeld` said "carried", the drop / drag was reversed and nothing re-sent it (test-desktop-move Q: B's dragged window back where A last saw it). And `takeDirty()` had taken the move's target desk out of the dirty set at that dead send, so even a re-send carried the desktop on show alone. On the real page a third gap: the re-send's text equalled `_lastSentJson` — the swallowed save's own — and the no-op guard silenced it.
- **Fix.** THE ACK: every `layout-sync` carries `sentAt`; ws-handler answers each write it made with `layout-sync-ack {desktopId, sentAt, seq}` (after the write + broadcast; a refusal carries `sentAt` back too). layout.js keeps the owed answers (`_unacked`: one entry per save, one answer per desktop record) and releases only at the answer: `_carried` per desktop (`_carriedAt`, read by `actHeld(t, receivedAt, win)`, `_resendHeldMove`, `_expiredHeldActs`), the held closes up to the save's time, the divider ratios, the dirty desks (`DesktopManager.noteCarried`; `takeDirty` no longer clears — a desk sent twice before its ack is an idempotent duplicate). A refused desktop is released by nothing (its reconcile + re-send carries it). A dead socket is owed nothing: at the close the owed saves that had left are dropped (their acts stay held, the re-read keeps them, the re-send carries them) and `_lastSentJson` is reset; a text identical to the last sent is a no-op only when nothing is owed for that desktop. An older server that never acks: ACK_WAIT_MS (2 s) after the save left on an OPEN socket, then today's rule — only until the first ack ever seen on this page; the horizon `_movesSentAt` is the time an acked save LEFT (`s.at`, the open for a queued one).
- **不变量**: a client releases a held act only on the server's own receipt; "sent" is a fact about a socket, never about the server. A refusal, a dead socket and an identical text are three ways a save carried nothing. Gates: test-desktop-record ak (the dead socket, a dirty desk) / ak2 (the desktop on show, the identical text) / ar (the refusal) + controls queued-as-sent (released at the send: RED by ak) / noop-unread (both no-op guards neutered: RED by ak2) / refusal-carries (RED by ar); the §6 ack pin; test-desktop-move Q (two real pages: the real server's ack proven, the swallowed socket, the re-send; CONTROL acks ignored ⇒ the fallback, the loss, no hang).

## A STALE HOLD THAT OUTLIVED THE MINUTE DROPPED ITS ACTS IN SILENCE (lane desktop-move verify r4 ④, 2026-09-30; LOW, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** r3 ④ holds every save while the reconnect's re-read fails and tells the user "held until it can be". Past §6b guard 2's 60 s the hold cannot be kept — `_doAutoSave`'s expiry sends nothing older — yet on the r3 tree the held move's witness still held the re-read's records off (`_movedAt >= receivedAt`, unbounded): the window stayed on HR on the page while the server had it on Fin, nothing ever sent it, and a reload lost it; a held close past CLOSE_HOLD_MS came back through the re-read. Neither was said.
- **Fix.** ①'s `actHeld` bounds every witness at ACT_HOLD_MS, so at the release the page FOLLOWS the server (the expired move is re-adopted home, the expired close rebuilt — no fork); `_expiredHeldActs()` counts the held acts past their hold BEFORE the applies prune them, and one toast names the count ("The layout was re-read — window changes made on this page more than a minute ago were not kept ({n})"). Gates: test-desktop-record st2 + control stale-release-untold; the i18n key pin.
- **不变量:** a promise to hold is kept, or its breaking is said — a page never shows an act the server will never hear of.

## A MAXIMIZE, MINIMIZE, RESTORE OR KEYBOARD SNAP WAS UNDONE BY A RECORD DEFERRED UNDER IT (lane desktop-move verify r4 ③, 2026-09-30; the r2 ⑩ class for non-pointer geometry — the fake-app repro, then two real pages)

- **What happened.** r2 ⑩'s geometry witness (`win._boundsAt`) was stamped by the drag's and the resize's pointerup only. A maximize by the □ button or a title-bar double-click, a minimize / restore from the taskbar or the window menu, a snap by command mode's ← → ↑ ↓ (`snapToHalf`), a Tab-cycle's restore and a move-mode placement changed the geometry with no witness — so another page's record deferred under the second after them (the apply's cooldown, where r3 ③ defers the act's save) applied its older box / maximize / minimize over the act, and the deferred save then wrote that back as the user's. Reproduced on two real pages: B's □ click 150 ms after A's record landed, A's second record deferred ⇒ B un-maximized; the same for Ctrl+\ ←.
- **Fix.** `WindowManager.witnessGeometry(id)` — the ONE stamp, called at every USER door of a geometry act (the two buttons, the double-click, `snapToHalf`, a named window's restore in `revealWindow`, move mode's restore + placement click, the taskbar row and its Restore / Minimize command, command mode's m and its cycle's restore; a grouped guest's act is its host's) and at NO primitive: the apply, the boot restore, a replay, a preset and the Stage call `toggleMaximize` / `minimize` / `restore` themselves, and a witness stamped there would hold another client's un-maximize for a minute and re-send the old state over it (r3 ①'s class). The held geometry (`actHeld`, r4 ①) then keeps the act and re-sends it. Gates: test-desktop-move O (two real pages: the □ and Ctrl+\ ← under the cooldown, the server ends with the user's state); test-desktop-record's §6 doors pin (every door, no machine path) + 5 controls (a door without its stamp, the helper without its stamp).
- **不变量:** a witness is stamped at the user's door of the act — by every door, by no machine path; a primitive shared with the apply never stamps.

## A WINDOW LISTED BY THE DESKTOP ON SHOW WAS MOVED OFF IT BY A STALE HELD RECORD (lane desktop-move verify r4 ②, 2026-09-30; pre-existing since r1, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** `adoptRemoteMove(win, from, {to, rec})` computed `dest = to !== from ? to : null` and, on null, SEARCHED the held records for one listing the window. The apply's update loop calls it with `to` = the desktop on show for every window the record lists; for a window already ON that desktop `to === from`, so the search ran — and a stale held record of another desktop listing the same window (this page's own move that no save carried, a racing double from a peer) moved the window OUT of the desktop whose record had just listed it. Under ①'s chatty-peer repro the window bounced Fin ⇄ HR on every record; the page's next save then dropped it from the shown desktop with `moved` evidence.
- **Fix.** Told a destination, `adoptRemoteMove` answers it or nothing (`to === from` ⇒ null, no search); the search stays the close loop's and the cached sweep's, which do not know. Gates: test-desktop-record ue + control adopt-falls-through + the §6 pin.
- **不变量:** a caller that knows the answer never asks the search; the record of the desktop on show is the freshest fact about what is on it.

## A RECORD THAT LANDED RIGHT AFTER A DROP OR A DRAG UNDID IT (lane desktop-move verify r4 ①, 2026-09-30; an r2 ①/⑩ class one phase later, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** r2's held move / held geometry compared the act's witness (`_movedAt` / `_boundsAt`) to the record's RECEIPT (`receivedAt`): a record received before the act cannot know it. But a record received AFTER the act cannot know it either while the act's save has not left — the autosave's 500 ms debounce, or the apply's 1 s cooldown where r3 ③ defers the save. A peer's record of Fin (captured before the drop) landing 100 ms after a drop on HR re-adopted the window onto Fin (`adoptRemoteMove` in the update loop) and the apply's dirty clear swallowed the move's save; the same record after a drag snapped the box back; under the cooldown the deferred save then wrote the peer's box back to the server as the user's own; a page saving every 400 ms undid every act made here, and the window bounced Fin ⇄ HR on each record (verify r4 ②'s fallthrough).
- **Fix.** `LayoutManager.actHeld(t, receivedAt)` — the ONE question for a witness: held when the record landed before the act, OR while no save has carried the act (`t > _movesSentAt`, stamped by every save that leaves on an open socket); bounded by `ACT_HOLD_MS` (60 s) like the close hold and the divider's, so an idle page holds nothing over the server and no input time is fabricated. Asked at the apply's update loop, its close loop, the held geometry and the cached sweep; `_resendHeldMove` re-arms only a fresh witness. Gates: test-desktop-record ua (the drop) / ub (the drag; the drag under the cooldown and its deferred save) / uc (the chatty peer) + control unsaved-act-reverted; leg w's answer now lands after the save left (the horizon's own case).
- **不变量:** a record cannot know an act no save has carried — whenever it landed. Receipt order is not knowledge order; the save that left is the witness of what a peer could have seen.

## A FAILED RECONNECT RE-READ LEFT THE PAGE SAVING ITS STALE BASE, TOLD TO THE CONSOLE ONLY (lane desktop-move verify r3 ④, 2026-09-30; the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** r2 ⑥ retried the re-read three times (≈ 9 s) and then `console.warn`ed. A server restart's 5xx outlasts that; the page then kept the records it last saw and its next save (a drop on HR) wrote HR from a base that had never heard of the window another page added during the outage — one window, below the belt, and after a restart the arrivals ledger is empty. The user saw nothing.
- **Fix.** After the last retry the page is STALE (`_resyncStale`): `_doAutoSave` saves nothing from it (the dirty desks stay dirty) and asks the read again (single-flight `_resyncing`); a successful read clears the flag and releases the held save on the fresh base (the move's window is merged back by `recordFor`); one toast per episode names it. Gates: test-desktop-record st + controls stale-base-saved / stale-untold.
- **不变量:** a base the page knows is older than the server's is never written; a failure the product cannot repair by itself is said to the user once, never only to the console.

## A DROP, A CLOSE OR A DRAG IN THE SECOND AFTER ANOTHER CLIENT'S RECORD LANDED WAITED FOR THE NEXT ACT (lane desktop-move verify r3 ③, 2026-09-30; pre-existing, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** `_restoring` meant two things: the synchronous span of a remote apply AND its 1 s cooldown (the anti-echo gate for the apply's own timers). `scheduleAutoSave` / `_doAutoSave` returned under it, `noteClosed` refused every close under it and `purgeClosedWindow` marked no desktop dirty under it — so a window dropped on a preview, closed from the taskbar or dragged 200 ms after another client's record applied had no save of its own: the page showed the act, the server never heard of it until the user's next click; a reload in between undid it (a closed window came back, a moved one went home). With two active users the cooldown is up a lot.
- **Fix.** `_applying` (+ `_booting`) is the record's own span: `noteClosed` and the dirty desks refuse only inside it (the cached sweep's closes raise it too); a user-caused save under a gate is DEFERRED past it (`_deferSave`, 1.1 s, once) and, when an apply cleared the dirty bit meanwhile and no save left since (`_savedAt`), re-armed at the act's real time — the held move's / close's / ratio's rule. Guard 1 holds: the apply's own churn schedules nothing (inside `_applying`, or not user-dirty). Gates: test-desktop-record y/z + controls close-under-cooldown / save-dropped-under-gate.
- **不变量:** a gate that protects a record from the apply's own timers never swallows the user's act — the act is deferred past the gate, never dropped; "made by the apply" is the apply's synchronous span, not the second after it.

## A RECONNECT'S RE-READ REVERSED A MOVE MADE WHILE IT WAS IN FLIGHT (lane desktop-move verify r3 ②, 2026-09-30; r2 ① one layer up, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** r1's reconnect re-read (§6b guard 9) took r2's held-move stamp at its ANSWER. A drop on a preview made after the read was asked but before it answered (a 50–500 ms window on every reconnect), or made while disconnected with its save queued in ws.js and flushed 250 ms before the read (the server may read the GET first), had `_movedAt < receivedAt`: the answer's source record re-adopted the window, the apply's dirty clear swallowed the move's save, nothing re-sent it — the drop silently undone, and the target's dirty record later written without it.
- **Fix.** The re-read's horizon is `min(the ask, the last save sent on an OPEN socket)` (`_movesSentAt`, stamped only when `ws.connected`): a move newer than either is held over the answer and re-sent as the user's own act (the held move's rule; `recordFor` merges the built window back into the cached stale record). `msg.receivedAt ?? Date.now()` — a horizon of 0 (a page that never saved) is a value. Gates: test-desktop-record w/x + controls resync-horizon / queued-as-sent.
- **不变量:** a read's knowledge horizon is when it was ASKED, and never later than the last thing the reader is sure the server received.

## A CLICK ON A TITLE BAR HELD ANOTHER CLIENT'S MOVE OFF THIS PAGE (lane desktop-move verify r3 ①, 2026-09-30; an r2 ⑩ regression, reproduced on two real pages)

- **What happened.** B presses hr-2's title bar and releases in place (a click-to-focus); A drags hr-2 360 px away meanwhile and its save of HR lands on B under the press, deferred. r2 ⑩'s witness `win._boundsAt` was stamped at EVERY title-bar release — before `if (!dragging) return;` — and at every resize-handle release, so B's click was "newer than the record": the apply skipped hr-2's box, B kept it where it was while A and the server had it moved, and B's next save of HR (the merge takes the page's geometry for a built window) wrote the old box over A's move.
- **Fix.** The stamp sits AFTER the drag threshold gate (`dragging`), and the resize's behind a `resized` flag set by the handle's first move — a press that moved nothing holds nothing. Gates: test-desktop-move N (two real pages: the click, A's move applied on B, the server kept), test-desktop-record §6 pin + control.
- **不变量:** a witness is stamped by the act it witnesses, never by the press that could have made it — a hold is the age of a real change, not of a click.

## A WRITE FOR A DESKTOP DELETED MEANWHILE RE-CREATED IT AS AN ORPHAN RECORD (lane desktop-move verify r2 ⑦, 2026-09-30; pre-existing, reproduced with two raw sockets on a scratch server)

- **What happened.** `desktop-delete` removes the meta and `desktops[<id>]`; the next per-desktop `layout-sync` for that id — from a page still on the deleted desktop (its switch off it broadcast the record, before ④), an old bundle, or the deleter itself when another client deleted its target in the same second — went through `if (!layoutData.desktops[desktopId]) layoutData.desktops[desktopId] = {}` and wrote a record no meta names. The orphan sat on disk for good, `loadFromServer` cached it as a ghost held record on every boot, and the windows in it were reachable by nobody (the deleter's own retag rescued them only if that page was still there).
- **Fix.** ws-handler's layout-sync refuses a per-desktop write for a desktop the meta does not name (when a meta exists): a journal line, telemetry, and `layout-sync-refused {reason:'no-such-desktop', desktops: <the meta>}` to the sender; `DesktopManager.onSyncRefused` treats it as the `desktop-updated` it missed (the windows follow the record that lists them, else the first desktop — ④). Nothing written, nothing broadcast.
- **不变量**: the server writes a record only for a desktop it names; a writer that names a desktop the server no longer has is told, with the truth. Gates: test-desktop-move E⑦ (two raw sockets: the write lands nowhere, the sender told with the meta); test-desktop-record §6 pin.

## A FAILED RE-READ LEFT THE PAGE ON THE STALE BASE THE RE-READ EXISTS TO END (lane desktop-move verify r2 ⑥, 2026-09-30; the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** r1's reconnect re-read (`_resyncFromServer`) tried `/api/layouts` once and returned on any failure — a 5xx on a loaded fleet server, a socket cut inside the request. The page then kept the records it last saw before the outage, and its next save wrote that base over whatever another page had written meanwhile: two windows are the belt's, an arrival older than 10 min is nobody's — one window lost, the r1 D2 class again.
- **Fix.** The read is retried, bounded (3 more tries, 1.5 s × the attempt apart; a non-OK status counts as a failure); when every try fails the page says so (`[layout-sync] the reconnect re-read … failed` + the `layout-resync-failed` breadcrumb) instead of nothing.
- **不变量**: a read that ends a known-stale state is retried before the stale state is allowed to write again; a silent single try is the stale state kept. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 s (a cut, a 503, then the answer) + control resync-no-retry.

## A RECORD STILL DEFERRED WHEN THE RECONNECT'S RE-READ LANDED DRAINED OVER IT (lane desktop-move verify r2 ⑤, 2026-09-30; r1's re-read vs r1's per-desktop deferral, the fake-app repro)

- **What happened.** A record deferred under a gate (the boot's 5 s, the apply's 1 s) is drained 200 ms at a time once the gate opens; r1's re-read runs 250 ms after a reconnect and feeds its records through the same path. When the gate opened and the read answered before the drain's next tick, the read cached the fresh record (HR with hr-4) and the OLDER deferred record then drained over it (HR without hr-4) — this page's next save of HR dropped hr-4, the belt refused it as an arrival, the window reopened with a "were kept" toast. The reverse order was wrong too: a broadcast that landed while the read was in flight can be NEWER than what the read saw, and the read's record replaced it in the per-desktop map.
- **Fix.** `_resyncFromServer` remembers when it asked: a deferred record received before that instant is older than the read — dropped (or replaced when the read's record is deferred too); one received while the read was in flight stays and supersedes the read's record for that desktop (a per-desktop record is whole).
- **不变量**: two records of one desktop land newest-last by the time they were RECEIVED, whichever path brought them; a read answers for everything received before it was asked and for nothing after. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 r (both orders) + control resync-keeps-stale.

## A DELETED DESKTOP'S WINDOWS WENT TO DESKTOP #1 ON EVERY OTHER PAGE, AND THE PAGE ON THE DELETED DESKTOP WROTE AN ORPHAN RECORD (lane desktop-move verify r2 ④, 2026-09-30; pre-existing, surfaced by r1's handover)

- **What happened.** A, on X (of Fin, HR, X), deletes X: `deleteDesktop` switches to the NEIGHBOUR (HR), merges X's entries into HR's held record and broadcasts it before `desktop-delete` (r1 ④). Every other page's `_onRemoteDesktopUpdated` retagged X's windows to `_desktops[0]` (Fin) — and showed them there when Fin was on show — so B's next save of Fin wrote them under Fin too (a second record of the same windows on the server), B's later save of HR dropped them from HR ('moved' evidence, explained), and on the deleter's page they then jumped from HR to Fin. A page ON the deleted desktop ran `switchTo(_desktops[0])`, whose capture + step-8 broadcast wrote a record for the deleted id — an orphan `desktops[<id>]` the server keeps with no meta naming it (`loadFromServer` then caches it as a ghost held record on every boot). A deferred record for the deleted desktop, and its held record / wire base, lingered as ghosts too.
- **Fix.** `_onRemoteDesktopUpdated` sends a deleted desktop's windows where the DELETER's record put them: the desktop whose held record — or whose record still deferred under a gate — lists the window (the target's record always arrives first, r1 ④); the first desktop only when nothing lists it; hidden unless that desktop is on show; the page on the deleted desktop switches to where its windows went. The deleted desktops' held records, wire bases and deferred records are dropped. `_setRecord`, `noteWire` and `_broadcastDesktopState` refuse a desktop this page does not know — a deleted desktop's record is nobody's to hold or write.
- **不变量**: a deleted desktop's windows follow the record that carried them, never a positional default; a desktop the page no longer knows is never written, held or broadcast. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 q (both gates; the page on the deleted desktop) + control delete-to-first; test-desktop-move L (two real pages).

## EVERY SAVE OF THE DESKTOP ON SHOW BY ANOTHER CLIENT BROKE EVERY TAB GROUP THIS PAGE HELD ON ITS OTHER DESKTOPS (lane desktop-move verify r2 ③, 2026-09-30; pre-existing, reproduced on two real pages)

- **What happened.** B groups hr-1 + hr-2 on HR (the server's HR record carries the chain), switches to Fin; A nudges a window on Fin. B applies A's Fin record: `_applyRemoteState`'s "break local chains not in remote" loop walked EVERY chain host on the page — HR's hidden host included — and, its key absent from Fin's record, detached the guest and ungrouped it. B's group was gone on the page at once (`_tabChain` null on both), and B's next save of HR (a visit + any input) wrote HR without the chain — the group gone on the server for everyone. No move, no race: one save of any desktop by any other client.
- **Fix.** The loop skips a host whose `_desktopId` is not the desktop on show (`activeDesk`): a record judges only the chains of the desktop it describes. A chain on the shown desktop the record lacks is still broken, as before.
- **不变量**: a desktop's record judges that desktop's windows only — a window (or a chain) hidden on another desktop is never touched by it. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 p + control chain-any-desktop; test-desktop-move K (two real pages).

## A DROP ON A DESKTOP PREVIEW WAS PUT BACK BY THE RECORD DEFERRED UNDER THAT VERY DRAG (lane desktop-move verify r2, 2026-09-30; reproduced on two real pages over the r1 head 900e0a73)

- **What happened.** Two pages of one workspace. B presses on fin-2's title bar and drags it toward HR's preview; while B's pointer is down, A nudges a window on Fin and A's autosave of Fin — which still lists fin-2 — lands on B and is deferred under §6b guard 3. B releases on HR's preview: `moveWindowToDesktop` retags fin-2 to HR (hidden) and arms the autosave; 300 ms later the deferred Fin record is applied — r1's move-in (`adoptRemoteMove`: "the record of the desktop on show lists a window this page holds elsewhere ⇒ another client moved it here") put fin-2 BACK on Fin, and the apply's `_userDirty = false` swallowed the move's own save. 4.5 s later fin-2 was on Fin on both pages, the server had never heard of the move, no toast, no refusal. Before r1 the apply could not retag, so the move survived on the page and its record went out with the next input; r1's move-in made the record older than the move win.
- **Fix — THE HELD MOVE (the held close's twin).** Every inbound record is stamped when it lands (`msg.receivedAt`, before any gate; the reconnect's re-read stamps at the answer); `moveWindowToDesktop` stamps every member `_movedAt`. The apply's update loop and close loop, and `cacheRemoteState`'s gone sweep, skip a window whose `_movedAt >= receivedAt` — the record cannot know a move made after it arrived — and the apply then re-sends the move once as the user's own act (`_resendHeldMove`: dirty at the move's REAL time, §6b guard 2's expiry kept; `_movesSentAt` marks moves a save already carried). A record received AFTER the move is a real remote move and applies as before.
- **不变量**: a record can undo only what happened before it arrived — a page's own act made after a record landed (a close, a divider drag, a MOVE) is held over that record and re-sent, never reverted by it. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 o + control no-held-move + the §6 pin; test-desktop-move J (two real pages).

## THE MOVED WINDOW STILL VANISHED UNDER A SECOND CLIENT — AN INBOUND RECORD DROPPED UNDER A GATE, A REMOTE MOVE APPLIED AS A CLOSE, A STALE BASE AFTER A RECONNECT (lane desktop-move verify r1, 2026-09-29; each reproduced on two real pages over the lane's head ef70b8fe)

- **What happened.** Two pages of one workspace. (a) B holds a drag on HR while A drops fin-1 from Fin onto HR: the lane's autosave now sends HR, Fin, Fin in one burst; §6b guard 3 kept ONE deferred record (the last — Fin), so B never learned of HR's new member; B's release saved HR from its stale base (3), the belt admitted a 1-window drop, A's cached-record sweep closed its own copy: fin-1 gone from the server and both pages in 4 s, no refusal, no toast. (b) B booting while A moved: the record under B's 5 s `_restoring` gate was dropped outright — same end. (c) NO race, both pages with HR built: B applied A's Fin record as "fin-1 is gone" and CLOSED it; `purgeClosedWindow` turned that close into 'closed' evidence; B's next save of HR dropped fin-1 with evidence — accepted. (d) B's socket cut for 2 s while A opened one window on HR: B reconnected with its pre-outage base and its next save wiped A's window (two windows are the belt's; one is not), A watched its window close.
- **Why.** Four assumptions from the single-record era: a deferred inbound record has one slot (all broadcasts were for the active desktop); a record under `_restoring` may be dropped (the next one will do); a window absent from the record of the desktop on show was closed (moves arrived only at a switch); a reconnect needs no re-read (broadcasts carry everything). The lane's held-record sends made per-desktop bursts routine and a move an immediate two-record event.
- **The fix.** layout.js: `_pendingRemote` is a Map per desktop, filled under the pointer AND under `_restoring`, drained lowest-seq-first when both gates are down (never dropped). `DesktopManager.adoptRemoteMove`: a record that lists a window this page holds elsewhere moves it here (shown); a record that drops a window another held record lists (the target's record is sent first) moves it there (hidden); the cached record's gone sweep asks the same; only a drop nobody lists is a close. ws-handler: the belt REMEMBERS ARRIVALS — per desktop, what a write added and which socket (10 min); an unexplained drop of ANOTHER socket's arrival is refused at any count (PURE `shrinkVerdict`'s `recent` → `arrived`). Every reconnect but the first re-reads `/api/layouts` through the ordinary inbound path, closing only what the wire base listed. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 i/j/k + four controls; test-desktop-move G / H / E+ (two chromes).
- **Also found by the round (D1, pre-existing since 2.90.0): deleting the desktop ON SHOW held its windows in no record until the next input.** `deleteDesktop` switches to the neighbour, retags the windows there and calls `scheduleAutoSave` — which the switch's 1 s gate drops; `desktop-delete` then removed the only record that listed them (a reload in between: gone, the rollback point the only way back). Fixed: the deleted desktop's entries are merged into the target's held record and the target's record is broadcast BEFORE `desktop-delete` (test-desktop-record §4 l + control delete-no-send; test-desktop-move I).
- **Also found (⑥, by the neighbouring test-split-close-resurrect going red on ②): a record entry nobody could build lingered 20 s and the belt held it against every other client.** `_replayMissing` replayed an `attachSession` entry of a conversation already open on the page under another window id; attachSession's "already open" shortcut focused that window and built nothing, the entry stayed a build attempt for the grace, `recordFor` kept sending it, and ②'s arrivals rule then refused another socket's record for lacking it. Fixed: the same-session entry is settled at once (the Stage's leave rule), evidence 'unbuilt' (test-desktop-record §4 f + control dup-lingers; test-split-close-resurrect green again). **Verify r2 ②: the key was the CONVERSATION id and it over-settled** — a fork's window keeps its parent's `backendSessionId` in its openSpec (`createSession({fork:true, backendSessionId: resumeId})`, never re-pointed), so with a fork open the parent's own never-opened window entry on another desktop was settled as a duplicate and dropped from that desktop's record with 'unbuilt' evidence (the server accepts an explained drop: the parent's window placement gone for every client), while attachSession's shortcut keys on `serverId` and would have built it. Now `_replayMissing` keys on `openSpec.serverId` — the shortcut's own key. 不变量=a "cannot be built" verdict uses exactly the key the builder's own shortcut uses, never a broader one.
- **不变量** = an inbound record is deferred, never dropped, and one slot per DESKTOP; a window that leaves one record and enters another has MOVED — a close is only a drop no record explains, and a close the page did not make is never its evidence; a belt that admits N−1 must at least refuse the window that just arrived from somebody else; a broadcast-only mirror is re-read on reconnect.

## THE PHONE'S BILLING CHIP KEPT THE MEMBER A CONVERSATION STARTED ON — ITS KEY NAMED THE POOL, THE CHIP PRINTED THE MEMBER (lane billing-chip, 2026-09-30 — the owner: conversations still showing the member they started on after the pool moved their links to another member)

- **Why.** A phone has no title bars; its billing identity is the chat status bar's chip (chat-status-bar.js `setBilling`, fed by app.syncSessionIdentity on EVERY active-sessions merge). `setBilling` skips a repaint while its key is unchanged, and that key was `${auth.source}:${auth.name}` — the POOL's name — while the chip prints `⣿ <pool> → <member>`. A per-session switch, a pin or a gather changes `poolTarget` and not the pool, so every broadcast arrived, matched the old key and was dropped: the chip showed the old member for the life of the page. The title-bar chip (window.js `setAuthBadge`) repainted — it had its own, longer key. Two keys for one identity, each hand-picked, one short; the sidebar digest was never involved (the card prints no pool member; `auth` stays carried-only in LIVE_SESSION_FACTS).
- **The fix.** ONE PURE `billingAuthKey(auth, t)` beside `placementNote` (src/lib/pool-priority-model.js) = source, name, the member by name AND id, host, the estimated mark, an API key's tail / detail, the placement note — the census of what the keyed chips print (a moved pool DEFAULT, which no chip prints, buys nothing); both setters call it; a pooled phone chip's tooltip now carries the placement words the title chip prints. Gates: test-billing-chip (fast: the REAL bar, A → B on the same node; the pre-fix key as a mutant-copy control stays on A; both renderers hold the PURE key after every step; a src/lib census catches any file spelling its own billing key) + test-mobile-gaps' phone leg (a stub active-sessions frame through the page's own socket at 390 px, DOM text + a screenshot).
- **不变量** = a keyed chip's key is a CENSUS of what the chip prints (the MEMO SIGNATURE lesson, channel-render verify r5), and ONE identity has ONE key function every keyed renderer calls — a surface that repaints from the poll must repaint when what it PRINTS moves, not when some hand-picked subset does.

## LARK SINGLE CHATS NEVER APPEARED — THE SEARCH FEED READ EVERY HIT AS MALFORMED AND NOTHING SAID SO (lane-lark-p2p, 2026-09-30 — the owner: "我怎么在频道里还是看不到lark私聊？"; production 2.369.198)

- **What production showed.** The Lark account's `feed`: `mode: measuring`, `counters: {malformed: 241260, births: 0, pages: 8043}`, `catchUp: {pages: 0, done: false}`, `strikes: 7`, `backoffWhy: failed`, `lastOkAt` the previous afternoon. The adapter's own shape probe had printed the real fields at boot — `display_info, id, meta_data; meta_data: chat_id, create_time, from_id, is_p2p_chat, message_id, position, type` — and the names were exactly what the parser read. The card said "behind" / "not answering", never why.
- **Why (two faults, each hiding the other).** ① The hit's `create_time` is an ISO 8601 STRING (`2026-03-21T16:15:30+08:00` — the vendor's doc and its answer); the .197 lane declared the unit `ms` from an invented fixture (the design had it as unverified U5), so every hit was `no-time` ⇒ malformed. ② The request put `time_range` / `chat_type` at the body's TOP level; the vendor reads them only inside `filter` — every page answered the whole searchable history, has_more for ever (8 043 pages at the feed's 10/min). Every guard of the page (the ignored-window check, `total`, the repeated-page check) judges READABLE hits only, so ② was invisible behind ①. The 504s the search answers in bursts kept one strike count across the never-ending window (reset only on window completion) — strikes 7, each new 504 a 15-min wait.
- **The fix.** The request's `filter`; `timeUnit: 'iso'` (a declared FORM, read by a bounded ISO reader — never `Date.parse`, never a magnitude guess); THE ONE hit reader `readSearchHit` (tolerant of `meta_data.message_id` / `id`; malformed BY NAME with the fields); PURE `shapeVerdict` — a run of pages ≥ 90 % unreadable parks the feed `shape` by name, the card: "Lark's search answers, but its hits have a shape this version does not read (missing or unreadable: meta_data.create_time) — the single-chat feed is off until an update"; an answered page ends a 504 run, the card says "did not answer 3× in a row — … until 03:28"; `caps.changeFeed.reader: 2` restarts the old reader's feed row as a first run at boot (the 7-day single-chat catch-up, born read); a gap while a catch-up is pending widens it. The fixture is now the probe's field list verbatim (the probe line over it reproduces the production line), with the .197 shape and the .197 request as controls.
- **不变量** = a vendor shape is READ from the vendor's own answer — the probe that printed the fields must feed the parser's fixture (and name the FORM of the field whose form decides everything), never an invented fixture alone; a guard that refuses everything must say so on the card, by name; a guard that judges only readable items must itself refuse a page it cannot read (otherwise the unreadable page disables every other guard); a failure count "in a row" ends at the first answer.
- **Verify r1 (2026-09-30) — THE COUNT'S CEILING.** Reproduced on the real engine with a fake vendor: `has_more` for ever with a fresh token, 30 fresh in-window ids a page and no `total` (or `total: 0` — a finite number the claim rule trusts) paged ONE steady window 300 times in 30 minutes, the card "behind", no park: the only bound on a window's size was the vendor's CLAIM (`total`), and production's 8 043 pages had already proved the claim never stops it. FIX = `pageVerdict` takes the window's page count and parks `time-range-ignored` once the PAGED count passes the same S × 50/s rule (a 90 s window: page 151, 15 minutes at 10/min), then 24 h by name; the catch-up keeps its own 20-page bound. 不变量 = a bound on a vendor's claim is not a bound on the vendor; the count the feed itself paid for is judged by the same rule.
- **Verify r1 (2026-09-30) — THE SHAPE RUN OUTLIVED ITS WINDOW.** Reproduced: a quiet account whose only two messages in a minute are of a shape the reader cannot read (`malformed: 2`, nothing else) — the 60 s overlap on a 30 s tick re-reads them on three windows, the run counted 2, 4, 6 and the feed PARKED `shape` for 24 h at the third tick (the brief's coin flip on a tiny page, made worse by the overlap). FIX = the run is keyed by the window and dropped at every page 1; a full unreadable page still parks at once. 不变量 = a threshold over a RUN of pages is judged per window — the overlap re-reads, so a run across windows counts one item as many.
- **Verify r2 (2026-09-30) — A 200 THAT IS NOT A SEARCH PAGE COMPLETED THE WINDOW.** Reproduced on the real adapter with a stub fetch: `{}`, `{code:0}`, `data:{}`, `items:null`, and — the worst — `has_more:true` with NO `page_token` (30 of 500 hits) all RETURNED `more:false`; the engine then completed the window and moved its cursor past everything it still held (470 hits never asked for; a single chat among them born only with its next message, nothing said). The doc marks `has_more` REQUIRED and a token rides every `has_more:true`; the adapter read the absent field as its false value. FIX = the envelope is judged before the page is trusted: no data object / no boolean `has_more` / `has_more:true` without a token / `items` not a list ⇒ the search's own retryable `vendor-error` (`detail.envelope`, the feed's 30 s → 15 min ladder, the card "failed N× in a row", the cursor held), never the 24-h contract park; `has_more:false` with no items is the quiet window's empty page. 不变量 = a REQUIRED field's absence is never read as its false value; "the window is complete" is only ever the vendor's own `has_more:false`.
- **Verify r2 (2026-09-30) — THE UNREADABLE LINE NEVER CLEARED.** Reproduced on the real engine: two stray unreadable items in ONE minute on a quiet account put "4 search hits could not be read (missing or unreadable: meta_data.chat_id)" on the account card (the overlap read each twice) — and the same line was there a day and 2 884 clean pages later. r1 had made that line visible (it was a tooltip) but it read the CUMULATIVE counter, reset only by a reader revision: a one-off became a permanent "something is wrong now". FIX = a PURE ring (`recentUnreadable` / `recentUnreadableCount`, src/channel-feed.js): the pages of the last hour that held an unreadable hit; the view's `counters.malformedRecent` / `malformedAt` read it, the words say "in the last hour" and fall silent when the hour holds none (the cumulative `malformed` stays for diagnostics). 不变量 = a card line about the present reads a bounded recent count, never a counter that only ever grows.
- **Verify r3 (2026-09-30) — THE ENVELOPE FAILURE WAS LADDERED IN SILENCE.** Reproduced on the real engine: a vendor answering r2's non-page on EVERY call (a changed API, a proxy page, a captive portal) climbed the feed's vendor-error ladder for three hours — 15 searches (bounded), the card "Lark's search failed 15× in a row — … until HH:MM" (the first strike "is not answering", though it answers), and NOT ONE journal line: the r2 judge's own reason ("carries no has_more — not a search page") was thrown into a branch that logged nothing, and `detail.envelope` had no reader. Fix: the vendor-error branch strikes a kind of its own, `envelope`, when the error names the field; `feedText` reads it ("{vendor}'s search answered {n}× in a row with something that is not a search page — each chat is checked on its own until {time}"); the vendor-error and the continuation ladders write ONE loud line at `FAILURES_BEFORE_LOUD` (the outage line's count) with the missing field and the error's words. Gates: ㉒ (p2p-h) + two controls (the unkinded copy reads "failed 3× in a row"; the copy without the line writes nothing), caps `envelope3` / `envelope1`. 不变量 = a typed reason a judge produces is READ somewhere the owner or the journal can see — a refusal's `detail` nobody reads is a diagnosis thrown away; every failure ladder has its loud line.
- **Verify r3 (2026-09-30) — THE HOUR'S COUNT WAS A FLOOR PAST 200 PAGES.** Reproduced on the real engine: a busy vendor whose every page held 26 unreadable of 30 (below the 90 % park), six pages a window at the feed's 10 pages a minute — 600 pages an hour — filled r2's per-page ring (200 entries) in 20 minutes; the card then said "5200 search hits could not be read in the last hour" for 15 600 dropped, as a count, for as long as the pages kept coming (and across a restart: the ring is persisted). Fix: `recentUnreadable` keeps ONE entry per MINUTE (`[the minute's newest instant, its sum]`) — ≤ 61 entries an hour, the count exact at any page rate; the 200 bound still holds a ring read from disk. Gates: feed ⑨ (two pages in a minute = one entry; 600 busy pages ⇒ 60 entries and 15 600) + the per-page copy as the control. 不变量 = a bounded ring that backs a COUNT is keyed so that its bound cannot be reached by the rate it counts — else the count must be said as a floor.
- **Verify r3 (2026-09-30) — A LOOP OF PERIOD TWO WAS PARKED UNDER THE WRONG NAME AFTER 161 PAGES.** Reproduced on the real engine: a vendor whose continuation pages loop A → B → A → B … with fresh tokens and `has_more` for ever. The r1 token guard (e) judged a continuation against the token it SENT and the PREVIOUS page only, so a period of two repeated nothing it looked at: 161 pages in 77 minutes (every DM born, nothing lost — the dedup) until the count's ceiling parked it as `time-range-ignored` ("Lark ignored its time window"). A period of one was parked at page 2 (r1's rule). Fix: `pageVerdict`'s `prevSig` takes a LIST — the engine keeps every page's signature of the window in flight (`e.feedPrevSig.sigs`, ≤ `PAGE_SIGS_MAX` 256, restarted at every page 1 because a restart re-reads the same pages legitimately) — parked `contract` at the third page. Gates: feed ② (the A → B → A row; a string is still the previous page alone), ㉒ (p2p-i) + the last-signature copy (pages on, 100 in ten minutes). 不变量 = a pagination-loop guard remembers the whole walk, not its last step; a park names the fault it found, never the ceiling that happened to stop it.

## A STALE LOGIN LOOPED THE PAGE AND EVERY VERB TIMED OUT — NOW A NAMED FACT WITH WAYS OUT, AND ONE SITE'S LOGIN CAN BE CLEARED (lane site-reset, userW's pod 2.369.196, 2026-09-30)

- **What happened.** The shared browser was restarted; a bank's login page read "Log In | …" for a few seconds, then the app's own title, then EVERY verb timed out and screenshots failed. Plausibly (unverified by us) an expired login cookie: the sign-in page sends a signed-in-looking visitor to the app, the app fails auth and sends it back — the tab never settles. The product could neither name that state (the agent saw 30 s timeouts) nor clear one site's storage.
- **Measured on a LOCAL fixture before anything was built** (scripts/measure-navigation-loop.mjs, 0.38.1 + its Chrome — never a vendor site): a loop whose every page moves on BEFORE its load event is exactly the incident — `open` ends after 25 s "Operation timed out", `snapshot` "(empty page)" after 2–8 s, and on the never-painting shape the CLI's screenshot AND a raw `Page.captureScreenshot` both time out (there is no frame). Every page hop is renderer-initiated (`frameRequestedNavigation` scriptInitiated / metaTagRefresh / reload); the agent's own `open` is not. `Page.stopLoading` ends every loop in ms; `tab close/new/<ref>/list` never wait on the page. And THE QUEUE: a verb whose client is killed keeps its session's daemon waiting until its own 25 s timeout — every later verb queues behind it; stop / close do not shorten it.
- **Fixed.** The dialog watch records each tab's main-frame navigations and PURE `navigationLoopVerdict` judges ≥ 6 page hops in 30 s over ≤ 3 addresses (query/fragment dropped; the agent's own and an acting command's page turns excluded): the verb in flight is answered AT ONCE with `[navigation_loop]`, the cycle and the ways out; page-waiting verbs are answered with it while it stands; the chip, the live view (the cycle, keyed) and the panel row show it. The ways out go DIRECT through the watch's own socket (`stop`, a bare `tab close`, a bounded `screenshot` / `[no_picture]`), and say how long the session still finishes the cut verb. `vibespace-browser site-reset <host>` clears the cookies that reach the host + its origins' storage (on a page's session — the browser endpoint answers "Internal error") in the conversation's OWN browser; on a SHARED profile it is ONE proposal (lane browser-propose's card / For-you item / routes, kind `site-reset`) whose Approve clears exactly the frozen (profile, host) and tells the agent for free.
- **不变量** = a page that will not settle is a NAMED fact returned at once — a timeout is never the report; a stored login is cleared per site, per profile, by its holder or by the owner's Approve (never `clearBrowserCookies`, never every site); a way out never waits in the queue it is the way out of.
- **verify r1 (2026-09-30).** ① A FOUR-STATION SIGN-IN CYCLE WAS NEVER JUDGED: the hard "≤ 3 addresses" rule read sign-in → authorize → callback → app → … as no loop and the agent sat out the 25 s timeout again. FIX = a loop is a REPEAT (distinct addresses × 2 ≤ hops); `LOOP_MAX_URLS` bounds only what is SHOWN (`more`), `hosts` names every host of the cycle and the sentence says `site-reset` for each. 不变量 = the fact is the hops; a display bound is never a judgement. ② ON A SHARED BROWSER NOBODY'S LIVE VIEW SHOWED, `stop` STOPPED A STRANGER'S PAGE: the watch's `tabsOf` was only the stream bridge's active target, so an unattended conversation's scope was the empty set — and `pickTab` / `ownTabs` admitted EVERY tab to it: B's `stop` stopped A's looping page and then the user's own loading one, the `site-reset` current-tab check read strangers' addresses. FIX = an unattributed scope admits NOTHING (`stop` refuses by name: `not_watched` / `why: unattributed` + the `tab close` way), and the keeper attributes what it knows (`holderTabs`: the lease's pinned tab, a mediated lease's grant targets, the user's own + adopted tabs — unioned with the bridge's). 不变量 = a direct act on a shared browser needs a PROVEN tab; "cannot tell" is said, never guessed. ③ THE SAME UNATTRIBUTED CONVERSATION'S TIMED-OUT VERB WAS THE SILENT INCIDENT AGAIN (the builder's HELD "no live view ⇒ no report"): its only word was the binary's timeout line while the panel digest already said `loop`. FIX = `loopShared` (a KIND, never an address — another conversation's page, maybe the user's own) on the fact and the audit answer; the CLI prints PURE `loopSharedText()` with the way out (`tab close`, `tab new`, `site-reset --host`) on a failed or timed-out verb `[navigation_loop_shared]`. 不变量 = what the product knows about a verb's failure reaches the verb's result, in the words it may say. ④ (LOW) THE USER'S OWN CLICKS DURING A TAKEOVER READ AS THE PAGE'S LOOP: seven clicks between an inbox and a message in 10 s (anchorClick hops, no agent command on record) ⇒ the chip said "page keeps reloading" under their hands, the agent's first verb after a quick handback was refused. FIX = the watch stamps a hop made while `userDrives` the browser `user`; the PURE verdict resets the run on it. 不变量 = a hop is the page's own only when neither the agent nor the user made it. ⑤ (gates) THE REVERT TABLE (ten lane parts each reverted alone against the fast gates) left nine green: the busy memory (`noteCut` / `busyFor` — the heavy suite's ③ catches it), the boot drop of a gone conversation's site-reset proposal, the direct route's refusal while the user drives, `loop-cleared` on a tab close, the quiet-timer re-judge, the waiter wake's `movedOn` (needle-pinned only), the audit's `loop ? 'loop'` branch (unreachable: the shipped CLI never sends `timedOut` beside `loop: 'cut'`), the CLI's mid-flight screenshot bound (needs a hanging binary). FIX = test-browser-site-reset ⑤c (takeover refusal, three cuts are no timeouts, loop-cleared on close, the boot drop, the quiet clock through the watch's new `quietMs` option) + C7; held: the mid-flight screenshot bound and the waiter's `movedOn` have no behavioural row.

## A REFUSED SIGN-IN WAS PROSE THE USER COULD NOT PRESS — NOW ONE PROPOSAL WITH ONE APPROVE (lane browser-propose, userW's fleet pod 2.369.196, 2026-09-30)

- **What happened.** Google refused a FRESH sign-in in the agent's browser ("This browser or app may not be secure"). The pod had no display (headless ⇒ `HeadlessChrome/154`) and the generated config carried no `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` (`navigator.webdriver` true). The agent explained the refusal in prose and proposed copying a desktop session; CloakBrowser was not installed, so the live view had no "Switch to CloakBrowser…" to offer; nothing in the chat was a button.
- **The owner's ruling.** The agent PROPOSES the switch, the user APPROVES with one click; D31 stands — nothing escalates by itself.
- **The fix.** (1) the chromium launch carries the flag by default (`browser.automationFlag`; the user's own value wins; CloakBrowser untouched) — measured on 0.38.1: `navigator.webdriver` true ⇒ false, headed AND headless; (2) a navigation whose FINAL url + title are a known vendor's sign-in refusal page carries a HINT (never a detection — SIGNIN_REFUSAL_ROWS, dated and sourced); (3) a tier-2 `blocked` claim files ONE proposal: ONE chat card at the claim's position + ONE For-you item carrying the card's words line for line; the user's Approve names the digest of the card pressed and runs EXACTLY its frozen fields — the install if needed (its progress on the card), ONLY the claim's host on the CloakBrowser site list, the in-place switch or a new CloakBrowser profile (never a downgrade of a directory a newer Chromium wrote), the page reopened, the agent told for free (`noWake`: a steer into a running turn, else the next-turn stash — never a wake); Reject is told once at the agent's next navigation to the host; a second claim is the same card; (4) the manual: file the claim at once and say one sentence — no workaround, no copied session, no other browser.
- **不变量** = a refusal the agent meets becomes ONE proposal with ONE Approve that runs exactly what it shows; nothing escalates by itself. An Approve names the card it was pressed on (a digest over the frozen fields); an agent can never decide its own proposal (403 at the route, `agent_forbidden` in the PURE step); telling the agent what the user decided is free (never a wake).
- **Verify r1 V1 — the one-host allowlist broke the sign-in it was approved for.** Reproduced on a local fixture through the keeper's own CloakBrowser proxy: after Approve the list held `accounts.google.com` alone, so every part of Google's sign-in page from its other hosts (gstatic, apis, googleusercontent, youtube's cookie hop…) was refused 403 — and the refusal reached nobody (the verb answered `{ok:true}`, the card said "a page that needs another site says so in the live view"; nothing did). FIX: the PURE dated `SIGNIN_DEPENDENCIES` (four vendors, not a measurement) frozen on the proposal, NAMED on the card, added with the host; one egress proxy per cloak profile so the verb answer carries `egressRefused` (its own browser only) and the agent's claim for that site is a `site`-plan card. 不变量 = what an Approve adds to an allowlist is every host the approved page needs that the card NAMES; a refusal the boundary makes reaches the one whose request it refused, by name.
- **Verify r1 V2 — an Approve outlived the conversation that proposed it.** Reproduced: the claimant ended, another conversation took up the profile, Approve switched it to CloakBrowser under that other conversation; a new-profile card downloaded 217 MB and added its site before saying "nothing was created". FIX: the runner's pre-flight (before the install and again before the site / switch). 不变量 = an Approve acts only for the conversation whose card it is, and checks it is still there before the first thing it runs. And (V2 b, reproduced) a card that said CloakBrowser IS installed downloaded 217 MB on Approve when the program had gone since — the download was never on the card; now `install_gone`, nothing fetched. And (V2 c, reproduced) a switch card that said no other conversation used "Portal" switched it under one that attached before the press — now `proposal_stale`, nothing ran, the next claim a new card.
- **Verify r1 V3 — "Approve again" could never succeed after a bad download.** The vendor's CLI returns a cached `chrome` as is and unpacks in place, so an install's own rejected download (wrong SHA-256) failed every retry identically, and an unpack cut after `chrome` (a full disk) was stamped installed with its other files missing — both reproduced over a vendor-shaped fake. FIX: the install removes its own unpack on failure, and a marker finds one a dead process left; a pre-seeded build is never removed (its refusal names it). 不变量 = a retry that a cache can short-circuit starts from a cache the failed try cleaned — what one run wrote and rejected, it removes.
- **Verify r1 — another conversation's claims evicted an open proposal.** The claim store's `slice(-50)` counted every claim alike, and a proposal rides its claim entry: 50 tier-1 claims from one conversation removed another conversation's OPEN proposal (its For-you Approve → 404, the card gone at the next rebuild — reproduced). FIX: PURE `blockedKeep` ranks what nobody waits on first; a drop that must still happen dismisses the item and is journalled. 不变量 = a bound drops the undecided last and names what it drops.
- **Verify r1 — the chat card's Approve took a press the instant it appeared.** The lane's card had no press-arm (its own heavy suite noted "the card has none"): reproduced in chrome, a press the moment the card appeared under the pointer ran the install, the site and a new CloakBrowser profile to done. FIX: the card arms its Approve like every approval surface (appear / move / new words ⇒ ARM_MS). 不变量 = every surface that shows the same Approve carries the same arm — a census pin per surface.
- **Verify r1 — the For-you popup refused the first press after every open.** Its row pass sampled each Allow / Approve's position before the anchor moved the popup into place, so a press on a button that had sat still for seconds read as "moved under the pointer" (reproduced in chrome, 696 → 709 px). FIX: sample again after the anchor. 不变量 = an arm samples where the control IS, after every move the code itself makes.

## "HAND BACK AND CONTINUE" PRESSED AGAIN FILED A SECOND FRAME — THE ONE CARRIER HAD NO ONCE (lane browser-resume verify r2, 2026-09-30)

- **What the verifier saw.** The real keeper + announcer over the kept suite's fake: a takeover, "Hand back and continue" pressed, then pressed again with nothing new (no takeover between), then again mid-turn, then again after the agent's command had consumed the restore — every press answered `ok` and filed ONE MORE stash entry (`bres-…`, kind notification) and one more card: four frames for the agent's one next turn, each "The user drove your browser and handed it back…". A double press, a second owner tab inside the fact's broadcast window (its button folds only after `kept.handedBack` arrives), a retried POST — each is a second frame. Money: none (the stash is free; `delivered: 0` in every arm) — but the injection's budget is fit-or-wait, so the copies push other waiting entries a turn out, and the agent reads the same hand-back N times.
- **Why.** `continueFor` minted a fresh `bres-` id per call and asked nothing about the previous one; the client's guard (`contBtn.disabled` during the POST, `st.handedBack` after it) is per VIEW, and the server had no idempotence at all.
- **The fix.** `continueFor` asks the stash (`deliver.stashPeek(cid)`) for a waiting `bres-` entry of this conversation and — when no takeover ended in this very call — refuses `already_handed_back` by name (the waiting id in the answer; 409). A takeover that ends here is a NEW hand-back (its tab acts and re-run list are this press's own) and files beside a waiting one. The stash is asked at the act, never remembered (a drain, a restart, an eviction move the truth); a deliver with no `stashPeek` leaves the press alone (a dedupe, not a money gate). The live view folds its button on the code and says "Already handed back — the agent reads it with its next turn". Gate: test-browser-kept ⑨ (refused with one waiting; files again once drained; a takeover files beside a waiting one) + ⑬ the copy without the guard files two.
- **不变量** = a "one carrier" claim is a claim about the STORE, not about the press: the producer of a next-turn entry asks the store what already waits before it writes, and "nothing new" is refused by name.

## WHOSE-TAB WAS QUADRATIC ON THE BROWSER'S OWN PAGE LIST — 8 000 POPUPS = 1.2 s ON THE LOOP PER `tabs` RECORD (lane browser-resume verify r2 / r1 F4, 2026-09-30)

- **What the verifier measured.** `tabOwners` (PURE src/browser-tabs.js — asked by the bridge after EVERY `tabs` record of a shared profile's view, by every tab act and by the hand-back) spread ownership by a fixpoint that re-scanned every page per pass and resolved ONE tab per pass on a chain of popups (each page opened by the next one listed): 2 000 tabs 63 ms, 4 000 275 ms, 8 000 1 201 ms — ×4 per doubling, on the event loop, per record. `cleanRoots` deduped with `includes` per item (8 000 ids = 60 ms, ×4 too) over `own` sets as long as the page list. The list is Chrome's own (`Target.getTargets`, uncapped in browser-viewport) — a page's popups and the agent's own `window.open`s grow it. r1's F4 (the client's `chipTitle` walking a 512 KiB page title whole per row per record, 438 ms) was the same class, held LOW.
- **The fix.** The opener forest is built ONCE (a tab has one opener) and walked breadth-first from every owned tab — linear, the same answers (a tab takes its nearest OWNED ancestor's owner; a root claimed below another holder's root keeps its claim); `cleanRoots` dedupes with a Set; `chipTitle` cuts a title to TITLE_CHIP × 4 code units before the code-point walk; `tabRowModel` bounds a row's tip (300) and url (2048) like the kept store's rows. Gate: test-browser-tabs ① perf pins (8 000-chain < 100 ms and t(2n) ≤ 2.6 × t(n); a 1 MiB title < 5 ms) + the peer-parser census rows (test-peer-parsers) that judge every export of the two modules for a cap and linearity.
- **不变量** = a reader of a list the browser (or a page) sizes is judged for linearity at 8 000 and 16 000 before it ships, and a string a page chose is cut before it is walked — "bound before parse" holds for tab lists and titles exactly as for mail bodies.

- **The hand-back frame said "The user drove your browser" when nobody drove.** "Hand back and continue…" is offered while THIS view drives OR after the user's Resume; the frame's head (and the resolve note after it) said "drove" in both legs. - **The two browser modules that read page-chosen bytes were not rows of the peer-parser census (r1's F5).** FIX = every export of src/browser-kept.js and src/browser-tabs.js is a census row (cap + linearity) or excluded with a reason; the census's first run found `targetIdOf` JSON-parsing every `{` line of the binary's stdout (32 K throws = 88 ms) — it parses only a line that can carry an id now. 不变量 = a reader of bytes a page chose is MEASURED by the census before it is trusted, never walked by hand once.

## THE USER'S ✕ ON THE AGENT'S TAB RAN AFTER CONTROL RETURNED TO THE AGENT, TOLD TO NOBODY (lane browser-resume verify F3, 2026-09-30)

- **What the verifier saw.** The real keeper + route over the tabs suite's fake 0.38.1: the user took over A's view (viewer 7) and pressed ✕ on A's current tab; while the keeper was inside its CDP read, `handback({cause:'explicit'})` answered ok with `userActs: []`; the read released ⇒ the keeper ran `--pin-tab tab <neighbour>` and `tab close <id>` under A's own session, the act answered ok and the tab was gone.
