## THE TOTAL BOUND REMOVED A RUNNING CONVERSATION'S KEPT LOGINS — "LIVE" WAS READ AS THE BROWSER, NOT THE CONVERSATION (lane browser-resume verify F2, 2026-09-30)

- **What the verifier saw.** 100 kept conversations over a 256 MB total; the victim's session RUNS (a live session carries its key), its browser stopped after the turn (the turn-idle release — restore `auto`: the resolve answer had promised "reopened at its next start"), its `lastUsedAt` the oldest. The sweep removed 75 entries, the victim first — its entry AND its directory. Its next command started a fresh browser and said nothing (no entry ⇒ no `kept` / `restored` note): the "same logins" promise silently broken.
- **Why.** `keptRetentionPlan` knew one liveness: `live` = the browser runs. The sweep read `liveKeys()` for D1's end verdict (where `carried` already protected an entry) but never handed it to the plan, so a carried key whose browser was stopped was an ordinary LRU candidate.
- **The fix.** The plan's rows carry `carried`; a carried entry is passed over by the total bound (its caches may still go — it is not running — its logins and tabs never) and REPORTED by key in `kept[]`. The sweep reads the live sessions AFTER the measure's await (fail closed: unreadable ⇒ every entry carried), and `removeEntry(bk, why, {unlessCarried})` re-asks `carriedNow(bk)` AT THE ACT for the sweep's two rules (D1's end and the bound) — a session that takes the key up between the plan and the removal keeps it. The user's own Forget is unchanged. Gate: test-browser-kept ① p7/p8 + the 100 × 60 walk with carried rows, ④ the verifier's repro on real scratch directories + the 100-directory leg with carried keys + the act-time leg; ⑦ two patched-copy controls (the plan without the carried guard; the store without the act-time re-ask).
- **不变量** = "never a live X" names WHICH liveness: a retention that protects a running process but not a running conversation deletes what that conversation was promised. A list read before an await is re-asked at the act.

- **What the owner saw.** Every message of the coordinator's conversation answered "You've hit your session limit · resets 3:50pm" while the member the pool had just linked it to had quota; restarting the conversation fixed it.
- **What it was NOT (refuted by measurement).** The first reading of the evidence was "a running claude process holds its birth member for its whole life — the pool's link moves never reach it" (the OTel rows named one member for 3.5 days through ~25 link moves). scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs ran the real claude 2.1.281 in a loopback-only netns with fake credentials and a mock that recorded the Authorization header of every request: every turn the CLI statx()es the creds file THROUGH the per-session link and re-reads it when the mtime differs — a re-point is billed to the new member on the next turn (an equal-mtime replacement is the one blind spot; the utimes bump is load-bearing). The OTel `organization.id` was the same value for both tokens: `~/.claude.json`'s oauthAccount, rewritten machine-wide by whichever claude process last refetched its own profile (every 24 h) — a LABEL. Production agreed without circularity: 47 of 47 fingerprinted rejections ("resets H:MM" = the answering account's 5 h window, matched against the identity-verified panel readings only) were answered by the member each link named, and four different resets inside five hours on 09-29 cannot come from one account.
- **What it was.** The server crashed at 12:03 (EMFILE) and re-attached its sessions; one conversation's stdout bridge came back DEAD in both directions for three hours while the CLI kept working. At 15:05:14 the owner's first message since the crash tripped the broken-stdin detector, and the local re-attach released the whole backlog in three seconds (4.4 MB + 6.8 MB queued to the two tabs). Every stdout consumer took every record as NOW: hours-old readings were re-filed as current (the SPENT member U's 5 h read 95 % again); a 12:15 Fable rejection another member had answered was archived at the record ("contradicts the member's own unexpired window but the ledger names that same member") — and its window-less BANNER then marked the linked member S's Fable spent anyway, the turn end excluded S from the conversation ("nowhere to go — 2 member(s) already rejected"), and the pool moved ten conversations onto U. Every message after that hit U's real wall. The restart made a new process with a new link placed on S.
- **The fix.** ① A LATE RECORD IS NOT A LIVE FACT (src/record-lateness.js + the engine's `gateLiveFact`): claude stamps assistant records at emission; a record whose own stamp is > 2 min old (30 min remote), or an unstamped one inheriting such a stamp (or looking ahead in the same chunk), never runs the reading / wall / banner / turn-end / odometer consumers — counted and journalled per backlog. ② A REFUTATION IS PROOF TOO: `_turnWallRefuted` — the banner, the turn-end fold, the session-wall exclusion and the ≥2-walls ring all follow a record that refuted the pin, exactly as they followed a re-file. ③ The switching verdict carries its measurement (`hotSwitchEvidence`, test-architecture §67) and a heavy gate re-measures the installed CLI. ④ The OTel org is retired as an identity everywhere (corroboration stamps and lines, the witness veto, the ⟳ skip, the observed-org wall rung). Repair: none needed — the two false marks were overwritten by live readings within minutes, the exclusions were in memory; no ledger row re-keyed.
- **不变量** = (1) a record's age is its OWN stamp, never its arrival: a stalled bridge's backlog is history, and history never moves a pool; (2) a wall whose own window refutes the member it is pinned to never marks, demotes or excludes that member — not through the window-less banner of the same wall, not at the turn end; (3) which member a process billed is proved by the RESPONSE (the windows a rejection or reading states), never by a telemetry label — and a label that disagrees with the link 90 % of the time is a machine-wide constant before it is evidence; (4) a capability verdict is a dated measurement with its record and a gate that re-measures it; (5) a hypothesis that inverts a law gets measured before the law is inverted.
- **Held.** The three-hour dead bridge went unnoticed (a heal trigger needs a stdin probe old wrappers cannot answer without a billed turn); the 12:03 EMFILE crash; B-f69c ②'s premise "a no-pool session's observed org is its slot" is refuted as well — rows of no-pool sessions baked by `truthLookup` between 2.361.0 and 2026-09-07 were not re-keyed and are not quantified.

## A RESTORED SESSION'S BRIDGE STAYED DEAD FOR THREE HOURS AFTER THE 12:03 CRASH — THE CRASH LEFT ITS ATTACH CLIENTS ALIVE, AND ONE STUCK CLIENT KEEPS dtach FROM EVER ATTACHING THE NEXT (lane-dead-bridge, 2026-09-30)

**THE SHAPE.** 12:03:17 `EMFILE … open '…/data/session-status.json.tmp'` from session-status's debounce timer ⇒ uncaughtException ⇒ exit(1); systemd restarted the server at 12:03:23 and it "✓ Reconnected" all 13 sessions. The coordinator's session (sess-4, busy at the moment of the crash) then delivered NOTHING until 15:05:14 while its CLI kept calling the API (OTel rows every minute); the owner's message tripped "Broken pty stdin detected — re-attaching dtach locally" and the three-hour backlog arrived at once (lane-hot-switch's incident).

**WHO RAN OUT (the first reading was wrong).** `systemctl show` said `LimitNOFILESoft=1024`, read as "node runs at 1024". MEASURED: node raises its OWN soft limit to the hard one at startup — the server and every child ran at 524288 and held ~75. The workspace is `fuse.bindfs` at the default soft 1024, sitting at 947 at 12:05 (~700 mmapped `.so` of another group's venv; lane-lark-p2p r3 raised it by prlimit at 12:05:12); a FUSE daemon's EMFILE is relayed to the caller. The product's share: a background write that could not fail softly.

**WHY THE BRIDGE STAYED DEAD (reproduced, raw dtach + a worktree server, 4/4).** node-pty's forkpty master has no FD_CLOEXEC, so every process the server spawned after an attach (rclone mounts, a Background Work job, agent browsers, the next dtach clients) held every attach's pty master; the crash path, unlike the clean shutdown, killed no attach pty — so the kernel never hung the old clients up and they survived, reparented, blocked writing to a pty nobody reads (still alive in production hours later). dtach's master waits in pty_activity() for ANY attached client to become writable; the new server's client is accepted and — the pty being readable in the same pass — pty_activity runs before its attach packet is read: never attached. The client's own clear-screen preamble satisfied the 09-09 attach probe. The wrapper's synchronous TTY write blocked it whole (its buffer file froze); claude's async pipe writes queued in memory. Any second connect (the broken-stdin re-attach) breaks the loop once — hence "the owner's message released it".

**THE FIX.** ① ONE attach-pty teardown for the clean shutdown AND the crash path (`bridgeWatch.endAttachPtys`). ② The boot sweep: after the restore's attaches connected, SIGKILL every orphaned attach client of our sockets (a dtach with a controlling terminal whose parent died — a master has none and is never touched; a person's attach has a live parent). ATTACH FIRST, THEN KILL: dtach discards what it reads while no client is attached (kill-first measured 81 records lost; attach-first lost none). ③ The watch: silent ≥ N min (`session.deadBridgeMinutes`, default 3) AND a witness — the wrapper's buffer file or an OTel api_request — newer than the last byte ⇒ re-attach through the one healer, then end that socket's orphans; ≤ 3 an hour; an empty heal doubles the silence. ④ What a heal releases is counted through lane-hot-switch's late rule (the engine never takes it as live) and ONE card says when the output was lost and restored and how many records caught up — shown, never re-run. ⑤ The debounced writes (session-status, user-todos, the channels index — the third measured by holding a server at a full table for a minute) retry and NAME who ran out (this server / the mount's FUSE daemon / the machine); the unit states the limit the process really runs at.

**INVARIANTS.**
- **A crash tears down what a shutdown tears down.** The clean path's `s.pty.kill()` was the only thing that ended the attach clients; a crash path without it leaves processes that hold the sessions' output hostage for as long as anything inherited their masters.
- **A file descriptor inherited is a lifetime extended.** A pty master without FD_CLOEXEC lives in every later child; "the server died, so its ptys hung up" is false whenever the server spawned anything after the attach.
- **A probe must read what only the far end writes.** dtach's attach preamble is written by the CLIENT to itself — it proves the client started, not that the master relays. Liveness is judged against the CLI's own witnesses (its API requests, its wrapper's file), never against our side of the pipe.
- **Silence is not death; silence plus a witness is.** An idle CLI is quiet and is never healed; a CLI that worked after our last byte proves the bridge lost it.
- **Order the cure by what the transport discards.** Ending a stuck client before the new one is attached hands its backlog to a master that drops reads with no client: attach first, then end it.
- **A backlog is caught up through the late gate, never replayed as live** — and said so in the conversation, once.
- **A background write fails softly and names the owner of the failure.** "too many open files" on a FUSE path is the file system's daemon, not this process — the next EMFILE says which.
- **A bridge that has spoken holds its input; re-send only through one that never spoke (verify r1).** A dtach client that connected (its preamble) forwards every input into the master's socket queue, and the master reads that queue — the attach, then the pushes — after the client is killed. The broken-stdin detector's re-send through the new attach therefore delivered the owner's message TWICE in exactly the stuck-master shape (raw dtach: 2×; the detector's sequence verbatim). `_ptyOpenedAt` (stamped beside the liveness stamp) answers "has THIS bridge spoken"; only a bridge that never spoke — the device channel never opened, a stale socket, the 09-09 shapes — is re-sent. Gate: test-dead-bridge §1 ⑥ (once; the old re-send = twice as the control), test-bridge-liveness §F.

**Production hazard at the time of the fix:** the 13 orphaned clients of the 09-29 20:49 server (ppid 3604) were still attached; the next restart during a busy turn would have reproduced it until the boot sweep shipped. **Held:** node-pty's missing FD_CLOEXEC itself (a native change; harmless to the bridge once crashes tear down and boots sweep); bindfs's durable limit (a `[Mount] LimitNOFILE=` drop-in, the machine owner's). **Gates:** test-dead-bridge (heavy), test-bridge-liveness + test-fd-limit (fast), test-restore-liveness ⑤ (the EMFILE-shaped restart).

## EVERY CODEX RESET CREDIT FAILED — THE CONSUME SENT `{}` TO A CLI THAT REQUIRES AN IDEMPOTENCY KEY, AND NOTHING COMPARED THE TWO (lane-codex-0159, production telemetry 2026-09-30 20:27 PDT)

- **What happened.** `codex-reset-credit-user` → `codex-reset-credit-failed "Invalid request: missing field `idempotencyKey`"` right after the owner's codex-cli went to 0.159.3; the 7-day window stayed at 100 % and the credit never landed.
- **Why.** The wrapper's `account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume` carried `{}` since 2026-08-24. Measured: 0.153.4 ALREADY requires the key (same words on `{}`), so the credit was broken before the update — the update only made somebody press it. No gate read the CLI's own protocol.
- **The fix.** The engine's one writer mints `crypto.randomUUID()` per press (kept on the identity's try record) and hands it down in the verb; the wrapper sends it (its own UUID under an older server), retries ONCE with the SAME key only on a timeout; a keyed `alreadyRedeemed` (the schema: "the same idempotency key already completed a reset") is the press's own reset; an old wrapper's local refusal names Terminate + Resume. THE DRIFT GATE (scripts/test-codex-protocol-drift.mjs) judges every wrapper request against tables measured from the CLI itself and FAILS when the installed version was never measured.
- **不变量** = a request to a vendor CLI is judged against that CLI's OWN schema, measured per version; an installed version nobody measured is a red gate, never a silent assumption. A money action that may be retried carries one idempotency key per human press, minted where the press is counted.

## A PHONE'S HEADLESS PAGE WAS RE-FITTED AT 500 PX — THE BRIDGE JUDGED AN EARLIER FIT'S LATE FRAME AS THIS FIT'S ANSWER (lane-heavy-197, the .197 heavy red on test-browser-live-fit ④, 2026-09-29)

- **What the gate saw.** Run 1: the phone pane 390×737, the page 500×945, the fit record `why: "headed-floor", floor: 500` — on a browser whose config is `headed: false` (the daemon applies `set viewport` through `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` alone, no window bounds, so a 390-wide page IS possible: the same leg is green alone). Run 2: the desktop pane's census 35.66 % dark, the picture ending at row 576 of 897 — the same shape one leg earlier. The integrator's "green" on this suite was a SKIP (its scratch HOME had no `~/.agent-browser/browsers`).
- **Why.** `checkFit` handed EVERY frame to `fitHonored` against the NEWEST fit. The pane reports twice as it settles (390×700, then 390×737); on the loaded 4-lane gate machine the daemon's frame of the FIRST set arrived after the second CLI call had returned — same width, smaller height, below 500 — which is exactly the measured shape of a HEADED window that cannot be that narrow (390×760 ⇒ 390×593 on 0.38.1). The floor was raised to 500 and the phone's page re-fitted at 500×945. Chrome 154's new headless refuses a WINDOW narrower than 500 (`--window-size=390,844` ⇒ a 500×701 viewport, measured), but that is not what fired: the emulated viewport is honoured.
- **The fix.** PURE `frameJudgeVerdict` (src/browser-fit.js): a picture AT the fit's size is always judged; a picture at a size we asked for within the last 10 s (`fs.asked`, kept at `beginOwn`) is that earlier ask's frame arriving late — `stale-own`, not judged; a picture read before the daemon's echo of THIS set (`own.doneSeq`, stamped when the result mirror lands — the stream is ONE ordered channel, every frame before the echo shows the page before the set) waits — `unmirrored`, at most 3 s so a daemon that never mirrors is still judged. The headed floor is unchanged and still fires on a real headed browser (test-browser-fit's headed leg). Gate: test-browser-fit ② the late-frame leg + two patched-copy controls (each fence removed ⇒ `500,945` / `500,1026`), the ① table; test-browser-live-fit ④ prints the bridge's fit lines on a failure.
- **不变量** = a measurement is judged only against the request it answers: a frame is this fit's answer only when it is not an earlier ask's size and only after the daemon has echoed this set. A gate suite that SKIPS in the integrator's env and RUNS in the gate's is a blind gate — read the "ALL PASS (0, 1 skipped)" line, never the ✓.

## A FORMATTED MAIL THAT SLID INTO VIEW STAYED A BLANK BOX — THE LIVE SET WAS RE-JUDGED ON TWO TRIGGERS, AN APPLIED HEIGHT WAS THE THIRD (lane-mirror-197, 2026-09-29 — found by the Actions mirror of 2.369.197)

- **What happened (the runner, attempt 2 of test-channels-aggregate-ui: `{"maxOnScreen":7,"blank":["svg-onload:table-background"]}`).** In the attack room of short formatted mails the judge centred a row and, 3.7 s later, counted 7 formatted rows on screen — one of them a placeholder with no frame. On this box the same leg was green every run.
- **Why.** `createMailFrames` (src/lib/channel-mail-frame.js) re-judged the live set (PURE `liveFrames`: every visible row live, the keep zone pre-warmed nearest first under `LIVE_FRAME_CAP`) on exactly two triggers: the list's `scroll` and an IntersectionObserver crossing of the keep-zone margin. A frame is born as a 140 px placeholder and posts its measured height a moment later; six frames above the reader shrinking by 80 px each move every row below UP by ~480 px. A row that was already inside the keep zone (in `near`, not visible, no warm slot — the cap was spent on the six) slides into the visible band this way and crosses NO threshold and fires NO scroll — nothing re-judged it. Fast CPU: the heights landed before the judge's last `scrollIntoView` (a scroll — a reconcile). Throttled runner: they landed after it.
- **The fix.** `applyHeight` calls `later()` (the rAF-coalesced reconcile) after every APPLIED height — the third trigger, named: the live set follows the geometry it was judged on, and an applied height IS a geometry change. Pinned in test-channels-aggregate-ui (WIRING PIN: `later()` follows the apply inside `applyHeight`, spelled once) beside the chrome leg that now waits on the frames' own evidence (live + measured + a stable rect) with a deadline.
- **不变量** = a lazy set derived from geometry is re-judged on EVERY writer of that geometry — a scroll, a crossing, and every applied size — never only the two a fast machine happens to need; and a judge of a settling picture waits on the picture's own evidence with a deadline, never on a nap sized to the machine it was written on.

## THE SCRATCH REAPER CONVICTED BY A NAME — ONE FAST TIER KILLED ANOTHER RUN'S STRAY AND A COORDINATOR'S SHELL (B-1d08, 2026-09-29)

- **What happened (three incidents, one day).** ① Two lanes ran `ci.mjs` fast tiers at once; the per-suite sweep of one reaped the stray the other run's suite had just planted under a scratch dir that suite had already removed (exit 144, "a planted stray reaped"). ② The coordinator's `node scripts/ci.mjs --check-heavy > /tmp/vs-checkheavy.txt` was killed by a lane's fast tier: a `/tmp/vs-*` NAME whose path is a FILE was read as a root, "gone" ⇒ orphan. ③ The reaper's actual target, which had to stay in reach: a finished verifier's scratch server left 15 `vibespace-device` daemons re-parented to systemd for an hour (the reaper only runs inside a tier).
- **Why.** The sweep convicted a process by the `/tmp/vs-*` path its cmdline / environ NAMED. A gone root convicted at once, with no age — so a seconds-old stray from a run in flight was litter to every other run; any string with the scratch shape was a root, whatever it was on disk (a file, a lookalike); and nothing said who OWNED a root, so "no live suite owns it" was inferred from the process tree alone. Two fast tiers (which by design take no machine lock) also swept concurrently.
- **The fix.** A root has an OWNER on record: `<root>/.vs-run.json` (scripts/scratch-run.mjs — pid + starttime + boot id + run), written by scratch.mjs `scratchDir` / `scratchHome`, mutant-copy's dirs and ci.mjs's isolated worktrees. `judgeScratch` convicts only on (a) a DIRECTORY root (an existing real dir of ours, or a gone one its naming proves was a directory — cwd, a directory-typed env name, `--user-data-dir`, a path going on beneath it), (b) an owner that is GONE (pid gone / reused / zombie / another boot, or the dir gone with its record) and (c) an age past the 10-min stale floor, on every rule; a process naming ANY root whose owner is alive is never a candidate. A record-less existing dir keeps the pre-record rule. The sweep takes a machine-wide `flock(1)` held by one child (the kernel releases it when that child dies); a sweep that cannot get it in 5 s skips and says so. `--reap --dry-run` prints every verdict with its evidence (root, owner state, age, what named the root). A victim is signalled only while its pid still carries the judged starttime.
- **不变量** = a reaper convicts by the root's OWNERSHIP EVIDENCE (a directory, its record's owner gone, old), never by a name; one sweep at a time, and a skipped sweep is printed; a suite plants a stray only under a root whose owner record is live (never under a root it removed — any sweep on the box, on this code or older, may take it). Gate: test-scratch-reaper (fast, 70: the fake-proc table incl. the three incidents' shapes, the lock with two real node sweeps started together, real planted orphans judged DRY over the real /proc, five patched-copy controls — name-only, lock removed, file-as-root, no age rule, starttime ignored) + test-ci-gate §9/§9b/§9c + test-ci-heavy-launch §6 (heavy: the lanes reap, over a fake table the stub suite writes — `VIBESPACE_CI_REAP_PROCFS` / `VIBESPACE_CI_REAPER_LOCK`; verify r1 K7: a seam is REFUSED unless its table is a directory under a `/tmp/vs-*` scratch root, and an accepted one is announced on every sweep — a real `--reap` had judged a table under a lane HOME and SIGKILLed the real, owned process behind a pid it named; verify r1 K1: the scratch shape ends at a segment boundary, so an existing `/tmp/vs-a+b/sub` never claims a gone `/tmp/vs-a`; K4: the holder touches the lock file it holds; K5: `--reap`'s closing count reads a zombie as reaped, and a victim is signalled only while its pid carries the judged starttime — gated by §5b; **verify r2** (attacking r1's additions): a seam LISTS and never signals — a table under an ACCEPTED scratch root naming a real, owned sleep with a made-up starttime had it SIGKILLed by the real `--reap`, since the re-check reads the same table; the seam is judged by its real path (a symlink into the lane HOME was accepted) and its scratch root must have a live owner (a finished run's stale table was accepted); the kernel's `<root> (deleted)` cwd marker — r1's boundary rule read it as "not the shape" and the reaper's own target, a stray whose cwd was a removed root, named nothing; paths are normalized before the shape is read (`<gone>/../<live>` named the gone root); the skip line names the holder. Gate: test-scratch-reaper 104 + the revert table over every product part of r1 + r2, one part per patched copy). **verify r3** (2026-09-30, attacking r2's additions): the SIGNAL SITE is the choke point — r2's "a seam lists, never signals" lived in each caller's early return, and a third caller that forgot it (planted on a copy: judge, then signal) SIGKILLed a real child off a fake row because the identity re-check read the seam's own table; `signalVictims` now refuses while `VIBESPACE_CI_REAP_PROCFS` is set with no in-process table, and re-checks identity against the KERNEL's /proc. The kernel's ` (deleted)` cwd marker is read with the kernel's STAT (nlink 0 = gone; ENOENT under a fake table): stripped as a string it convicted a live reparented process in a directory a person literally named `… (deleted)` (linked, nlink 2 — real /proc), and it spared, by a NEW run's record at the recreated path (the dbg-*.mjs fixed names, `/tmp/vs-fixtest` twice over), the OLD run's stray in the deleted inode — that cwd is now a gone root `<root> (deleted)` whatever the path holds, never the live claim that spares. The table announced is the table judged (the judge re-resolved the seam; a symlink re-pointed between the announce line and the judge listed another table's rows under the first name). A run record's owner is a process of THIS uid (`procUid` off /proc/<pid>/status): a forged record naming pid 1 (init, root's, alive for the boot) was an owner for ever — the seam under it accepted, a reparented stray under it spared an hour later. The skip line's holder facts: `command exec` (a lock file this user cannot open says `cannot open`, not "the lock holder exited 2"), a pid that no longer runs `cat` is said to be `not a holder`. Held (sparing direction, no producer): `<gone>/../<live>` groups under the live sibling (the kernel resolves no path through a gone dir); an env root that is a symlink is a lookalike while the cwd resolves to its target; a REMOVED symlink root named by HOME reads dir-gone (scratch.mjs mints no symlinked root). Gate: test-scratch-reaper 123 (fixture 574 flips to a victim, the literal name 577 listed nowhere, 578 — a gone cwd whose path now holds a FILE — the revert table's one uncaught part pinned, two real legs by nlink, the seam-swap leg, the forged-owner refusal, the two lock lines, controls (12b) (17)–(22)) + the revert table over every r2 + r3 product part (26/26 red after the pin). **VERIFY r4 (2026-09-30, attacking r3's additions on the real kernel):** ① (MEDIUM, an r3 regression of the never-block law) the kernel's stat through `/proc/<pid>/cwd` reaches the cwd's OWN filesystem — on a FUSE/NFS mount whose daemon hangs it blocks in D state, SIGTERM does not end the wait (a frozen bindfs held the judge until SIGKILL, 8 s bound), and r3 asked it for EVERY (deleted) cwd on the box: a shell left in a removed worktree on a hung workspace mount would have held every fast tier's sweep under the reaper lock (every other sweep skipping) and `--reap` with it. FIX: the stat is asked only for a scratch-shaped cwd (the only one whose answer is used); a hung mount a suite itself put under its own /tmp/vs-* root is the residual, stated. ② (LOW, kill shape, constructed with root) a process of this uid in another MOUNT namespace prints its cwd as a plain scratch-shaped path this namespace does not have (no marker, no `(unreachable)`): ENOENT ⇒ `scratch dir gone`, the live process convicted an hour later; unprivileged user namespaces are off on this box and a container's processes are owned through its live init, so no producer at this uid — fixed anyway: the kernel's stat answers for the directory ITSELF, and a LINKED one is never a gone root. ③ (LOW) the signal site's env-seam refusal was a silent `return 0` — a forgetful caller closed with `reaped 0 of 1 — 1 still alive after SIGKILL` for a signal never sent; it is said now. ④ (LOW, dry) a seam table that vanished after acceptance read as an EMPTY sweep (the announce line, then silence); the judge throws naming the table, the tiers print `scratch reaper skipped: …`, `--reap` refuses with exit 2. PROVED on the real kernel, no finding: a victim whose pid is REUSED by a live process of this uid inside the grace (steered with `ns_last_pid`, 1 try, 1 ms) is NOT SIGKILLed — the starttime is compared at the signal (the control that compares the pid alone kills the new process); the inode number of a held deleted cwd is never handed out (ext4 + tmpfs, 5 000 tries) so the stat reads the held inode's nlink 0; `procUid` reads the REAL uid (a setuid-root `su` of mine: `Uid: 1000 0 0 0` ⇒ mine; an unreadable status ⇒ unknown ⇒ alive, never foreign); a record naming another run's live process (the box's running tier) is alive; `--reap --dry-run` signalled nothing (the whole box, 30 spared); two invocations under a re-pointed seam each announce their own table. Held: an in-process table IS its caller's kernel (a fake row with a fake starttime for a real pid is signalled — a test's own call, unreachable from any environment, stated). ## PEER TEXT REACHED AN AGENT THROUGH MANY DOORS, EACH WITH ITS OWN RULE — ONE CENSUS, ONE BELT (lane peer-census, B-00ef, 2026-09-29)

- **What happened.** Three lanes learned the same rules one door at a time — channel-render (bounded before parse, linear), lark r2/r3 (the frame check looks THROUGH invisible characters; the line rule per line and per inline piece — a quoting block's `> ` completed a dangling opener), browser-stuck (a page's words folded, JSON-quoted, frames inert), pairing r6 (src/hidden-chars.js is the ONE hidden set) — and every door composed its own rule. The held LOW of the .197 integration: src/inbox-reply.js quoted a For-you item line by line with NO rule (an item ending in `<system-reminder` + the `> detail:` line = a live frame in the reply; reproduced by the suite's pre-lane copy). Found by the census on the way: src/job-model.js's four renderers put a job's OWN stdout line (`announced: <system-reminder>…`), its name and its context into the owner conversation and the hook's injection with a length clip only; src/channel-groups.js neutered complete tags but a member's message ending in an opener was completed by the NEXT report line when it began with `>`; agent-routes' legacy direct `vibespace-msg` lane handed a peer session's text on raw and the stash rendered a PEER entry as stored (a legacy entry never re-judged); the engine's agent copy ran the whole-text rule, not the per-line one.
- **Fix.** ONE belt, PURE src/peer-text.js `toAgentText(raw, {max, kind})` = bound → fold (hidden-chars' set, joiners kept) → the frame rule PER LINE (never a whole-text pass first: it matched `<system-reminder⏎> …` across the break and merged the next line, quote mark and all). Six callers (channel-filter, channel-groups, inbox-reply, job-model, agent-routes, channels-engine); browser-stuck keeps its byte-equal copy (it ships alone). The census (scripts/test-peer-text-census.mjs): every (file, door) site over `git ls-files` is a TABLE row with its rule and a wiring pin; a derived renderer fence beside it; attack legs over the real modules; mutant-copy controls.
- **Gates.** test-peer-text-census (fast, 102) + test-channel-filter (203) + test-channel-groups (300) + test-inbox-reply (137) + test-job-model (156) + test-stash-strip (275) + test-architecture (395: the PURE row).

## THE TITLE CHIP KEPT THE MEMBER THE POOL HAD MOVED THE CONVERSATION OFF — THE ONE PER-SESSION WRITER NOTIFIED NOBODY (lane badge-stale, 2026-09-30 — the owner, live: "你的最新消息显示的是走的 UCI Max，但是右上角写的是 Mat Max")

- **What production showed (read-only).** The pool engine moved its default AND every per-session link Mat Max → UCI Max at 10:49–10:52 PDT (`per-session-switch` rows in data/slot-transitions.jsonl); the CLI's `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` resolved to UCI; the message-meta popup said UCI; a fresh `active-sessions` frame said `auth.poolTarget: "UCI Max"`. The window's title chip on the owner's open page said Mat Max 30+ minutes later. `/api/sessions` (the 5 s poll) carries `auth: null` — the ws frame is the page's ONLY source of `auth`.
- **Reproduced on a real page first** (a scratch server, a pool of two FAKE members, a pooled stub-CLI session, its window in headless chrome, the engine's writer driven in-process): after `accounts.ensureSessionPoolLink(pool, sid, B, {why:'per-session-switch'})` the page received **0 `active-sessions` frames in 16 s**; `syncSessionIdentity` ran on every poll, FOUND the window's row (the brief's candidate (a) — a missed `byWebui` match — was not it), and re-applied the row's auth — the LAST frame's, i.e. the old member (candidate (b)). The pool DEFAULT's move repainted at once: `setPoolTarget` → `_notify` → `broadcastActiveSessions`.
- **Why.** `ensureSessionPoolLink` is THE one writer of a per-session link (the engine's per-session switch, a pin, a partial gather, an auth-failure move, a removed-member eviction, a spawn) and the link's target is a fact every client caches (server.js poolAuth → poolMemberOfSession → poolCurrentFor → readlink). It re-pointed, recorded the slot row and told nobody; its twin `setPoolTarget` notified. So the chip moved only when an unrelated broadcast happened to go out — and a conversation in one long RUNNING turn (the owner's orchestrator) publishes none (the 1 s turn digest moves only on a flip). The pin route had patched its own call site with a hand-written broadcast; the engine's paths never did.
- **The fix.** accounts.js `_notifyLinks()` — ONE notification per burst (an armed `setImmediate` after the synchronous pass; a pool pass re-pointing N conversations sends one frame) — at the end of `ensureSessionPoolLink`, a new constructor hook `onSessionLinks` wired in server.js to `broadcastActiveSessions()`; `noteDeviceRepoint` (the daemon's sealed-orders re-point, recorded late) notifies too (a per-session row ⇒ the links hook, a default row ⇒ `_notify`). The billing key is untouched (lane billing-chip's `billingAuthKey` applies on top). Gates: test-pool-link-notify (fast: the real store, once per burst, the pre-fix copy as a mutant-copy control, the writer census over every pool-link re-point + the wiring pin).
- **The second finding, on the same page (the gate's same-node legs).** With the frame fixed, a tab-group guest's / a split pane's / a layout-restored grouped window's chip named the new member — on a NEW node every time. `app.syncSessionIdentity` writes every window's title meta on EVERY merge (the 5 s poll + every frame) and `WindowManager.setTitleMeta` had no no-op guard (its twin `setTitle` does — "called per 5s identity sync for every window"): each call re-built the icon slots, re-rendered the WHOLE tab strip of a grouped window (every tab's billing chip destroyed and re-made from `_authBadge`) and re-notified the manager (taskbar, autosave) per window per merge. The staleness was not this (the re-made chip read the freshest `_authBadge`), the churn was: a hover / a press on a tab lost every 5 s, the keyed-chip law broken. FIX: setTitleMeta returns before the store when the merged meta equals the current one; desktop-app-window.js (which forced a strip re-draw with an EMPTY patch for its app icon) calls `_renderTabBar` + `_notify` itself; the identity sync asks the autosave where the openSpec it keeps changed (that save used to ride the per-merge notify). Gates: test-title-meta-guard (fast: the real setTitleMeta, the unguarded copy as the control) + test-billing-badge-live's quiet leg (every chip on the page the same node across ≥ 3 merges and a frame).
- **不变量** = a billing identity shown on a window is the LIVE frame's, re-judged every merge for every window kind — so every writer of a fact the frame carries notifies at its ONE entry point (the 2.309.0 "cache invalidation must NOTIFY" law), never by a call site remembering to; and a fake-DOM test that feeds the frame itself never proves a real page: the missing frame is exactly what it cannot see.

## AN APPROVED QUOTE REPLY CAME BACK TAGGED "IN THREAD" — TWO RULES FOR ONE QUESTION (lane channel-threads, the QUOTE-vs-TOPIC round — owner rulings 2026-09-28 21:55 PDT, both "是")

- **What the owner saw (the naive-user pass, shots 03 / 12 / 35).** Lark has two things: a TOPIC (话题 — a topic group's message, a reply made with `reply_in_thread`; the vendor's `thread_id`) and a QUOTE REPLY (引用回复 — a plain group message pointing at another one: `parent_id` + `root_id`, no thread id). The window tagged both "在线程中" and opened a "线程" pane for both; the message a quote chain answered grew a "3 条回复" chip. So an approval card that promised "引用回复 (stays in the chat)" was followed, once the vendor listed the sent reply, by the same message tagged "in thread".
- **Why.** The model's thread index keys a reply chain as a thread of kind `chain` (T1 — right for grouping) and the placement rules already judged "is the parent inside a thread" by the kind (`vendor` only — a chain is not a thread). But `placeOf` handed the window a thread fact for EVERY index entry but a mail thread, the chain included — the chip, the tag and the pane read that. One question ("is this message in a topic?"), two answers.
- **The fix.** ONE PURE classifier, `placeKindOf(recOrId, ix)` in src/channel-thread.js → `{kind: plain | quote | topic-root | topic-reply | topic-quote, topic, quotes}` (a TOPIC = an index entry of kind `vendor`; a chain is never one). Its readers: `placeOf` (a thread fact ONLY for a topic, the kind carried in the read shape), the window (`threadChip` / `inThreadTag` draw only for a topic kind — `isTopicPlace`; `quoteLine` says "quoting …" for a quote), the agent's words (`↳ quotes <author>: "…" (id …)` — never "in thread" for a quote), the engine's placement parent fact (PL3 / PL5), its thread read (`not-a-thread`, no records, the agent's note) and its thread WALK (`not-a-thread`, ZERO vendor calls — a Lark thread listing asked with a message id was a wasted metered call). A message a topic's members name as their root sits under that topic even when it also sits in a reply chain (a quote later answered with `reply_in_thread` heads a topic — the vendor mints the thread on it); the window grows its chip in place from the `threads` broadcast's `root`. The fake adapter's `fake-poll` rooms hold BOTH shapes and its thread send mints a topic on a parent outside one. zh: 话题, never 线程 (ja keeps スレッド; the pane title is `tc('channel', 'Thread')` — collab-row's Codex "Thread" keeps its own word).
- **不变量** = one question, one rule: every surface that decides or draws "is this in a thread" reads `placeKindOf`; a derived fact never gets a second spelling in a reader. Gate: test-channel-quote-topic (the table over the naive pass's shapes through the REAL Lark normalizer + the fake-poll rooms, the render over a fake DOM, the real engine; the zh census; controls: a chain-is-topic classifier, the pre-fix render pair reproducing the shot with each layer alone holding, the engine's own parent rule, the walk without its refusal, planted 线程 / トピック) + test-channel-threads-ui (the quote leg in chrome).

## A 429 ON A REACTION LIST STARTED NO WAIT — THE NEXT BATCH WENT STRAIGHT INTO THE VENDOR'S RETRY-AFTER (lane channel-threads verify r2 — MONEY, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (reproduced over the real engine + store with a scripted list that answers 429 once, Retry-After 30 s).** The trickle stopped its OWN batch at the first 429 (the rest refused `rate-limited`), but nothing remembered it: the next viewport settle — other rows, a second later — sent its batch straight into the vendor's Retry-After (3 calls in the control), and so did an unreact's list-first and a reaction reconcile; every doomed call is charged to the minute's budget the timer's message passes need (the ceiling allows 20 a minute, a third of Lark's default 60). Beside it, a refusal by the ACCOUNT's back-off came AFTER the rule-20 verdict, so a refused batch still reserved slots of the minute's ceiling and floored its rows for 5 minutes.
- **The fix.** A 429 answered to a reaction LIST call sets `e.rxBackoffUntil` (the vendor's Retry-After, else the picture path's transient wait); `rxBackedOff(e)` (that or the account's back-off) refuses the trickle's whole batch `backoff` BEFORE the verdict (no call, no slot, no row floored), the per-call cut, an unreact's list-first and a reaction reconcile. The window already holds itself quiet on `backoff` for the stated wait.
- **不变量** = a vendor's rate refusal is remembered where the next call is decided — "stop this batch" is not "wait"; a refusal that did not ask the vendor spends nothing (no slot, no floor). Gate: test-channels-engine (the rate-limit block: the account's back-off refuses the trickle / react / unreact / the walk with 0 calls and 0 slots; a list 429 ⇒ the next batch `backoff`, 0 calls; after the wait the rows are asked) + the copy where a 429 starts no wait as control.

## THE ACCESS GATE CENSUS — A PRODUCER THAT NEVER ASKED REACH RETURNED IN BOTH ROUNDS (lane channel-threads verify r2 — IDENTITY census, 2026-09-28)

- **The class.** Round 1 found the reaction digest handing a revoked agent its counts; round 2 found the agent verbs answering after a revoke that landed inside their await, drafts created for an agent without access, and the proposal views (receipt, `status`, `withdraw`) carrying facts minted after the revoke. (B) every function that calls `deliver.stashFor` / `deliverToConversation` carries a gate (`mayHear`, `stillInEffect` / `stillWatched`, `drafterSees`). (C) every function that calls `broadcast(` / `userTodos.add(` is on the CLOSED owner list with its reason. (D) every API path the CLI names is an agent route. - **The runtime leg (test-channels-engine ⑲).** One agent, one conversation, the owner's revoke landed INSIDE each await (gated vendor calls, a gated store search) and after it: the walk, the refresh, the two drafts, the search, the receipts, `status`, `withdraw`, `read`, `read --thread`, `list`, a peer's reply to what it sent (no wake, no stash — with access the same reply wakes it once: the positive control), the reaction digest — nothing; the owner's Outbox stays whole. - **不变量** = a recurring identity class gets a census over every producer and a runtime leg over every channel, never a fourth example.

## A PROPOSAL DECIDED AFTER THE AGENT'S ACCESS WAS REMOVED HANDED IT WHAT THE CONVERSATION PRODUCED SINCE (lane channel-threads verify r2 — IDENTITY, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (reproduced over the real engine + store).** An agent drafted a reply-in-thread and a reaction with access; the owner removed its access and then approved both. The owner's Outbox card stays whole (the card is the owner's).

## A REVOKE THAT LANDED INSIDE AN AGENT VERB'S AWAIT WAS ANSWERED ANYWAY, AND DRAFTS WERE CREATED FOR AN AGENT WITHOUT ACCESS (lane channel-threads verify r2 — IDENTITY, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (reproduced over the real engine + store; the revoke landed inside each await through a gated vendor call).** Every agent verb asked reach first and never again: `refresh <conv> --thread` awaited the vendor walk and then answered with the walk's count and the conversation's title; `react` and `reply --in-thread` awaited a convCaps lookup (a stale cache is re-asked) and then CREATED the draft — an approval card for an agent the owner had just cut off, its answer quoting the target message; `search` awaited the store and returned the revoked conversation's messages; `refresh <conv>` answered with the title. The window is one vendor round-trip — small, but it is the named invariant this codebase already paid for twice (R4 verify r2's stash, the browser lanes).
- **The fix.** `stillSees(ctx, adapterId, convId)` — reach re-asked after the last await, before the answer or the write: the walk / refresh answer the uniform not-found (what the walk fetched stays in the owner's log), the two drafts and compose create nothing (propose asks before its wake gate, so no slot is taken), search drops the conversations whose reach went.

Gate: test-channels-engine ⑲ (five channels, the revoke inside each await) + the copy with every re-ask disabled as control (the walk and the refresh answer with the title, two drafts created, the search returns the revoked messages).

## A THREAD PAST 500 REPLIES WAS WALKED BACK TO ITS 500TH REPLY ON EVERY OPEN, AND ITS NEWEST REPLIES WERE NEVER SHOWN (lane channel-threads verify r2 — MONEY, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (reproduced over the real engine + store with a Lark-shaped walk).** The thread index kept `replies: replies.slice(0, THREAD_REPLIES_MAX)` — the OLDEST 500 reply ids. The engine's thread walk anchors on `replies[last]` (the newest reply the log holds — the walk stops there), so for a thread of more than 500 replies the anchor was the 500th-oldest reply and every walk paged from the newest back down to it: 600 replies ⇒ 3 vendor calls for a walk with nothing new (1600 ⇒ 11), and a real Lark walk runs to its 200-record bound (4 calls instead of 1) on every pane open and every 60 s pane beat of a big topic — a pane left open on one busy thread spent ~4 of the account's 60 calls a minute. The same list fed the pane (`threadView` paged over it): the first page of a 600-reply thread ended at reply 500 — the newest 100 replies were never drawn, and an agent's `read --thread` never saw them either.
- **The fix.** `threadIndex` lists the NEWEST `THREAD_REPLIES_MAX` in `replies` (oldest-first order — `replies[last]` is the newest reply, the walk's true anchor) and carries the whole list as the non-enumerable `all` (never in a JSON answer); `threadView` pages over `all` (the first page = the newest replies, paging back reaches the first reply, `exhausted` only at the true start); the `in-thread-with-me` place rule reads `all` too (an agent's early message in a big thread still counts). Measured after: 600 replies ⇒ a re-walk is 1 call; 50 000 replies in one thread index in 24 ms, page in 17 ms.
- **不变量** = a bounded list that also serves as a cursor keeps the end the cursor needs — "≤ N, oldest first" is an ORDER, not a choice of which N; a view that pages must page over the whole set, never over a display bound. Gates: test-channel-thread ⑤b (600 replies: the newest 500, the newest page, paging to reply 1; 50 000 in one thread) + control (e) (the oldest-500 copy); test-channels-engine ⑱ (a') (a Lark-shaped 600-reply walk: 1 call on the re-walk, the newest on the first page) + an engine bound to the pre-fix index as control (3 calls, "newest" = reply 500).

## THE REACTION DIGEST KEPT TELLING AN AGENT WHOSE ACCESS WAS REMOVED (lane channel-threads verify r1, continued — IDENTITY, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (reproduced over the real engine + store).** Reactions on a message an agent SENT from a conversation become one line in that agent's next-turn stash (`👍 ×2 · 🎉 ×1 on your reply in <title> — message <id>`). The digest found its agent through the conversation's `sentBy` ledger alone — it never asked REACH. After the owner removed the agent's access (the agent's `read` answered the uniform not-found), every new reaction on its old message still handed it the counts, the conversation's title and the message id, hour after hour: information from a conversation it may no longer see.
- **The fix.** `reactionDigest` asks reach first, like every agent-facing path (`reachFor` over the agent's own grants and its groups' — `groupsOfSession`), once per agent per flush; no reach ⇒ no line.
- **不变量** = every channel of information from a conversation to an agent passes the reach door at the moment it is delivered — "the agent sent this message" is a fact about the past, never an authorization for the future. Gate: test-channels-engine ⑱ (c) (with reach a line per hour; reach removed ⇒ none) + the gate-less copy as control.

## A COMPACTED SIDE LOG PAST THE TRIGGER WAS RE-WRITTEN WHOLE ON EVERY REACTION EVENT, AND OLD MESSAGES' REACTIONS FELL OUT OF THE READ WINDOW (lane channel-threads verify r1, continued — MONEY / the event loop, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (measured over the real store).** The first r1 fix compacted the side log in place past `SIDE_COMPACT_BYTES` (1 MiB) and read only its newest `SIDE_READ_BYTES` (2 MiB). But a log that is ALREADY compact — one list snapshot per message, the steady state of a busy room whose rows were viewed: 5 000 messages × 3 keys × 4 reactors = 5.4 MiB — stays past the trigger after its compaction, so EVERY append compacted again: the whole file read (twice — the dedup set is dropped by the rewrite and rebuilt on the next append), parsed and re-written: **43 ms per reaction event on the event loop, 10.8 MiB read + 5.4 MiB written per event** (100 events: 4.3 s, 1 GiB read). And the compaction kept each message's lines at its FIRST appearance, so a new reaction on an old message folded into a line at the file's head — outside the 2 MiB window every read takes: invisible for good (the pre-fix copy loses it; the suite reads it).
- **The fix.** A compaction's OUTPUT is bounded and ordered: `trimSide` orders the messages by their LAST line (the most recently changed last — the read window is the tail) and keeps them newest-first until `SIDE_KEEP_BYTES` (half the trigger, 512 KiB); the least recently changed messages' folds are FORGOTTEN (`forgotten`, logged by count) — a list adapter re-reads them when a window shows them (rule 20). So a compacted log never outgrows the read window, and the next compaction is ≥ 512 KiB of appends away (amortized O(1) per event). Measured after: the same 5 000 snapshots stay at 511 KiB; 2 000 events cost 23 ms in all, 1 whole-file read, 0 rewrites.
- **不变量** = a compaction whose output can exceed its own trigger is a loop, not a bound — the output bound sits BELOW the trigger (hysteresis), and a bounded read window is only exact if the log it reads is bounded by it. Gate: test-channel-store (the thrash leg: bounded size, ≤ 3 whole-file reads for 300 events, the oldest message's new reaction visible) + the pre-fix compaction (unbounded, first-appearance order) as control.

## A REACTION STORM ON ONE MESSAGE GREW ITS SIDE LOG FOR EVER, AND EVERY PAGE READ THEN READ IT WHOLE, TWICE, ON THE EVENT LOOP (lane channel-threads verify r1, MONEY / the event loop, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (measured over the real engine + store).** 20 000 reaction events on ONE stored message (300 members toggling a reaction in a loop — a vendor-consistent stream) wrote 20 000 side lines (2.8 MiB); no trim ever ran, because the side log's compaction lived only inside the MESSAGE trim, which runs after a message append — a reaction storm appends no message. Every `messages()` page then did TWO synchronous whole-file reads of the side log (`reactionsFor` and the thread-stat pass each called `readSide`, which read the file whole): 30 ms per page on the event loop at 2.8 MiB, growing with the storm; every broadcast fold (`flushSide`, every 250 ms while events land) read it again. The spec (§3.2) had said "the readTail 2 MiB backward walk"; the shipped reader read the file whole.
- **The fix.** `readSide` is the newest `SIDE_READ_BYTES` (2 MiB) of the file (a partial first line dropped), never the whole file; `appendSide` compacts the log in place past `SIDE_COMPACT_BYTES` (1 MiB) with the trim's own `compactSide` (one snapshot per message + its newest thread stat — the fold is exact: the 300-member toggle stream folds to the same 200 as the whole stream), so the newest window always holds every message's whole state; `withView` reads the side lines ONCE per page; and an event that NAMES its conversation (the fake's shape, a future adapter's) still needs the message to be one that conversation holds — `not-in-conversation`, dropped by name — so a line about nothing is never written (compaction can only fold what is about a message). Measured after: 0.8 MiB file after the same 20 000 events (2 compactions), 6 ms per page.
- **不变量** = an append-only log a peer can grow has its bound WHERE IT GROWS (the append compacts), never only in a sweep some other event triggers; a reader of such a log reads a bounded window, never the file. Gates: test-channel-store (the growth leg + the window leg, with the no-compaction and the whole-read copies as controls), test-channels-engine ⑰ (the named-conversation drop).

## EVERY REACTION EVENT ON AN UNKNOWN MESSAGE SCANNED THE WHOLE ACCOUNT STORE, AND A MISS WAS NEVER REMEMBERED (lane channel-threads verify r1, MONEY / the event loop, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (measured over the real engine + store).** A Lark reaction event names its message and no chat (L10), so the engine's `convOfMessage` asked the store's `locateMessage`, which reads every message log of the account into memory and scans it — per event, with only a POSITIVE memo. On a 12-conversation account (14.3 MiB of logs): 14.3 MiB read per event, 11.6 ms each mostly on the event loop (the `indexOf` over the read strings is synchronous), 2.8 GiB for 200 events, 717 MiB for 50 events on ONE already-missed id. Lark delivers a reaction event for every message of every chat the bot is in — chats never listed here included — and any member can toggle a reaction in a loop.
- **The fix.** A miss is remembered (`msgMiss`, 20 000 entries, 10 min TTL; cleared by the write hook's positive memo when the message is stored later, so a late message is placed on its next event), and the store search has a per-account budget (`LOCATE_PER_MIN` 30); past it an unplaceable event is dropped `message-unknown` with `why:'locate-budget'`, still acked (fence 11 is about durability of what is placed; a reaction folded onto nothing has nothing to make durable), and the next list snapshot of that message is the truth for its counts anyway. Measured after: 2.1 MiB per event over a 200-event flood (30 searches, 170 dropped by name), 0 bytes for a remembered miss.
- **不变量** = a lookup a peer can trigger per event carries a NEGATIVE memo beside its positive one and a per-account budget; "no vendor fetch per event" is not enough when the local fallback reads the whole store. Gate: test-channels-engine ⑰ (the th-poll block: the same id again = 0 searches; 60 distinct ids ≤ 30; the late message placed) + the memo-less copy as control (40 events = 40 searches).

## A THREAD ID OF ANOTHER CHAT WALKED THAT CHAT'S REPLIES INTO A CONVERSATION THE AGENT MAY READ (lane channel-threads verify r1, IDENTITY, 2026-09-28)

- **What happened (reproduced over the real engine + store with a Lark-shaped scripted adapter).** `threadRefresh(adapterId, convId, msg)` resolved its walk key as `ix.byRecord.get(id) || (ix.threads.has(id) ? id : null) || id` — the third rung handed the CALLER's raw id to the vendor as the thread to list. Lark's `GET im/v1/messages?container_id_type=thread&container_id=<omt_>` answers by the thread id whatever chat the caller named, and `toRecord(adapterId, convId, item)` stamps the caller's `convId` on every item. So an agent with reach on conversation X alone ran `vibespace-channels refresh X --thread <omt_ of chat Y>`: one vendor walk, three of Y's replies appended to X's log, `read X` printed them. The owner's route had the same rung (Y's replies under X's log, wrong by construction).
- **The fix.** The walk key is one THIS conversation's index names — a record's thread or a thread its members declare (a root not loaded is still named by its replies); an unknown id is `thread-not-loaded` (404) on the owner's route and the uniform not-found on the agent's door (no existence oracle for another chat's ids), with no vendor call. The ONE internal exception is the post-send walk (`vendorNamed:true` — the thread id the vendor itself answered for a reply sent INTO this conversation; the routes never pass it). Two belts under it: Lark's `threadHistory` drops every listed item whose `chat_id` is another chat's (counted as `foreign`, carried through the registry's `threadHistory` shape), and the engine drops any walk record stamped with another conversation.
- **不变量** = a vendor id the caller supplies is never the key of a vendor call; the key is resolved from what THIS scope already holds, and the vendor's own word on where a message lives (`chat_id`) is judged before a record is stamped. A reach check on the scope is not enough when the call's argument can name another scope. Gates: test-channels-engine ⑱ (a) (+ the raw-id-fallback copy as control), test-channels-lark-shape ⑩ (+ the filter-less copy).

## A MEMBER TAKEN OUT OF THE POOL KEPT SERVING UNTIL IT WAS SPENT (lane-pool-pin, 2026-09-28 — the owner: "如果用到一半把账号从池里排除，不会第一时间触发切走，比如现在我把martinmax排除池子了你却还在用")

- **What happened (production, read-only).** 16:56 the owner removed Martin Max from the pool's members (11 left); `data/pool-links/<pool>/` still held six conversations → Martin Max and they kept billing it; the journal shows only a member wake re-deciding the pool, nothing moved. Two causes, one missing fact: the STORE (`updatePool`) re-pointed only the pool DEFAULT, to `list[0]` (the first member, not a decision), never a per-session link; the VERDICT (`decidePoolSwitch`) judged the current member by its cache and login alone — membership was never a fact (`exclude` only removes CANDIDATES) — so a removed member with quota left read "healthy", the proactive tier's warm hold kept a warm conversation on it, and it served until exhausted. Reproduced as a patched-copy control on the real engine (test-pool-auto: the pass without the membership fact leaves all three conversations on the removed member).
- **Fix.** `accounts.poolMembership` (the CONFIGURED list, login-blind — a signed-out member keeps its login verdict and its re-login words) is handed to the verdict as `membership`; a `currentId` outside it answers `not-a-member`, the HARD band (moves now, warm or mid-turn, past the no-data hold and the gain floor; nobody left ⇒ `notMember` in the blocked sentence). ONE engine entry point `memberRemoved` (the members route — Members… and Exclude both PATCH it — and the stale-link sweep every pool tick runs first) moves the default by decision (`updatePool`'s `chooseMember`; `list[0]` only as the store's no-engine fallback), re-points each linked conversation through `ensureSessionPoolLink`, restarts cold pools / held processes through `sendColdRestart`, tells each conversation in words (i18n), and starts no turn. Membership unchanged ⇒ 900 seeded verdicts byte-identical to master.
- **不变量 = membership is a placement FACT judged by the verdict, never a candidate filter.** A filter on the candidate list can only stop the pool from moving ONTO a member; it can never move anything OFF one. Any fact that says "this account may not serve" (removed, excluded, dead login) must reach the verdict about the CURRENT member, or the conversations already on it are exactly the ones it never applies to.

### lane-pool-pin verify r2 (2026-09-28, closure) — census adequacy: each r1 fix reverted one part at a time on a scratch copy; a revert nothing noticed is a finding

- **THE OWNER'S DECISION ON "A REMOVED MEMBER WITH NOBODY TO TAKE OVER" (2026-09-28 21:50 PDT, 全B — built in verify r2).** Until then such a conversation kept running on the removed member ("nothing is cut off", an hourly notice) — for a pay-per-use credits member that was real money the owner had just tried to stop, and its notice even told him to "exclude it from the pool", the thing he had done. Now: PURE `decidePoolSwitch` answers `removed-hold` (`to` null — nobody can serve it; `holdTo` = the listed member usable soonest; `blockedWhy` keeps the sentence's reason) for every member kind; the engine's ONE act `holdRemoved` lets a running turn finish (never cut), then parks the link on `holdTo` (the removed member serves nothing after that turn) and arms auto-resume with cause `removed-member` if the conversation was running (a normally-completed turn never disarms that arm — it is the turn the hold let finish); an idle one is parked, not armed (its next message meets the parking member's own wall like any quota wall); a held codex process is restarted onto the parked default; the member wake delivers ONE continue through the pre-fire gate + the breaker + the spend ceiling; a new conversation is never placed on the removed member (nobody signed in ⇒ refused by name); ONE For-you notice per (pool, member). - **F4'S JUDGEMENT WAS ONE server.js LITERAL AWAY FROM OFF (money, the UNSTAGED-WIRING class).** Reverting `gatherPlan` out of the `engine: {…}` literal server.js hands the account routes turned NOTHING red: every suite builds the routes over the WHOLE engine, and the route fell through to the unjudged move when the engine offered no plan (`plan` null ⇒ `wholeOk` true) — r1's money bug back with every gate green. The census found a PRE-EXISTING gap on master: `onMemberLoginSuccess` (the login-edge member wake, 2026-09-08) is read by the routes and never passed — dead in production since it shipped. The owner chose to wire it (2026-09-29, "好" = A: one usage read + one pool re-decision per login); the exemption is gone, test-new-member-wake §6b drives a login through server.js's own literal (kb-file-structure, THE NEW-MEMBER WAKE). 不变量 = a fallback for a missing collaborator on a money path fails closed; what a test injects whole, production passes by name — census the name.

- **THE CHOOSER RE-DERIVED THE POOL THE STORE HAD ALREADY RESOLVED (authority, census adequacy).** ws-create's `chooseMember` computed its own pool (`_poolPinPool || accountId || <claude default>`) beside `resolveForSpawn`, which resolves the pool per backend. Reverting r1's F13 there (the claude default for every backend) left every suite green — r1's gate drove `resumePoolPin` only — and a codex pin on the default pool was asked of the CLAUDE pool and dropped at the spawn. - **WHEN NOBODY COULD TAKE THE DEFAULT OVER, THE TWO WAYS A REMOVAL REACHES IT DISAGREED (identity, r1's held residual).** The members route landed the default on the store's `list[0]` (not a decision — the addendum's own word); the stale-link sweep (a removal the store could not act on: every other member signed out at that moment) left it ON THE REMOVED MEMBER, and the spawn chooser then started every NEW conversation there — F14's invariant broken in exactly the no-candidate case. Each leg reddens on its revert (verify r2's revert table). 不变量 = a control anchor proves a patch hit; it never proves the behaviour is gated.
