## THE SAME CLASS RETURNED THREE ROUNDS, SO THE THIRD ROUND SHIPPED A CENSUS AND A BELT (identity verify round 3, lane-browser-dialog, 2026-09-28)

- **THE SAME CLASS RETURNED THREE ROUNDS, SO THE THIRD ROUND SHIPPED A CENSUS AND A BELT (identity verify round 3, lane-browser-dialog, 2026-09-28).** Round 1 refused a remote session's key on the PATCH; round 2 found the same session admitted at `use`, the user's attach and the user's pin. Round 1 stripped `profile` from one agent route; round 2 found the digest, the `backend` GET's lease rows and the `use` / `resolve` records still naming other conversations. Round 3 found (a) the digest's `browsers` map still WHOLE — every browser record's pid, daemon namespace (`vs-bk-…`, a conversation's bs-session id), socket dir, directory, launch env and `startedBy: "attach bk-…"`, another conversation's ephemeral records included — and (b) an agent the list keeps OUT switching a kept profile's backend DIRECTLY (its browser stopped and relaunched under another backend, a fingerprint seed minted) because the switch's "not the owner ⇒ a proposal" rule read the retired single-owner shape `owner.kind === 'session'` and a list is never that shape. FIX = (1) `agentBrowserView` + `agentDigestView` over `browsers` (the view decides SHAPE); (2) `switchVerdict({admitted})` fed by the keeper's `mayAttach` over the conversation's live groups (not admitted / not judged ⇒ a proposal); (3) THE SERVER BELT — `router.use(AGENT_PREFIX, agentBelt)` registered before every agent route, wrapping `res.json` with the PURE `agentAnswerView`: any foreign browser key in any string masked, foreign session ids masked, foreign pids nulled, the asker's own echoes kept, `$.drivers` the one exception, a throw answered `belt_failed`; (4) THE CENSUS (test-browser-identity-census): the keeper's TEXT — every lease / pin / owner write inside a known function with the fence needles before it; every caller of a fenced primitive known; the belt's line before every route; and a RUNTIME WALK of every agent route's answer for a not-admitted and a remote conversation against every identifier of the admitted one, with eleven patched-copy controls (including the routes WITHOUT the belt + a raw route ⇒ 49 hits, and the REAL belt over the same raw route ⇒ masked). 不变量 = when a class returns round after round, the next deliverable is a census that names every site of the class and a belt at the ONE choke point every answer passes; a view decides shape, a belt guarantees the identifier class; a new guard layer is peeled out of the older layer's controls (test-browser-share-model's route-copy controls now strip the belt line first) and gets its own; an authorization RULE that reads a stored SHAPE is re-based on the ONE admission the moment the shape migrates (the switch's rule outlived the who-list migration by a day).
- **THE ONE ID EVERY BROWSER AUTHORITY HANGS ON WAS THE ONLY ONE MINTED WITHOUT A UNIQUENESS CHECK (identity verify round 4, lane-browser-dialog, 2026-09-28).** Round 4 asked what lies OUTSIDE round 3's census and belt. The browser key is `bk-` + 8 hex digits — 32 bits — and "Who can use it" rows, leases, pins, caps, the `told` memory, child handles, blocked claims, the bindings, the trace and the env directory all hang on it; ws-create minted it as `mintBrowserKey(randomBytes(4))` with no check, while the profile id (`keeper.mintId`), the mediator's grant token and the blocked-claim id each loop for uniqueness. Reproduced on the real keeper + routes: a conversation attached to a kept profile with an alias and a pin, then stopped; a NEW conversation handed the same 8 digits answered `status` with the old conversation's attachments and alias and resolved `open` on the kept profile — it WAS the old conversation to the keeper, and its first bare command would have landed in the stranger's logged-in browser. There was no reuse rule at all: the bindings prune past MAX_BINDINGS (4096) and a stopped conversation's list row is kept for good, so the space of keys a fresh mint must avoid only grows. FIX = THE FRESH-KEY RULE: PURE `browser-profiles.freshBrowserKey({mint, named, tries})` loops until `named(key)` is false and returns `exhausted: true` (never a refused create) if it cannot; `keeper.keyNamed(bk)` scans the WHOLE serialized registry (every field, present and future — not a hand-written list) plus the drivers and input maps and the ephemerals; `browserEnv.keyNamed(bk)` asks the bindings, every env-directory entry named by the key (a child's `<key>.N.json` too), the scratch profile dir and the session-meta files; THE ONE mint site (`rawMint` inside src/server/browser-key.js `mintKey` — the .197 integration moved it there from ws-create so the spawn AND the late key `ensureBrowserKey` go through it) runs the rule over the live sessions + both stores, a check that throws is said by name and the mint proceeds unchecked. Gate: test-browser-identity-census ⑥ (each named place on both sides, the PURE loop incl. the exhausted case, the ONE mint site census over the callers + controls (l) the loop without its rule mints the named key, (l′) browser-key.js with the raw mint restored fails the pin). 不变量 = an identifier that CARRIES authority is minted against every store that names it, whatever its entropy; a store that never forgets a row (a list) is a store the minter must read. **Second r4 finding — AUTHORITY WITHDRAWN BY A TASK GROUP CHANGE OUTLIVED THE CHANGE ON THE CHANNEL THE DESIGN HANDS THE AGENT.** The documented rule was "at the next browser command" (the verb-time re-judge) — true for the CLI rung, false for a mediated lease whose grant (and the raw CDP url in the daemon's env) stood until that verb: reproduced, a `Runtime.evaluate` through the mediated url kept answering after the conversation left the group. FIX = the task store's one change hook → `keeper.rejudgeAll` (every lease admitted through a Task Group, judged like a narrowing: detach, grant revoked 1008 `lease_gone`; a stopped member undecided and kept). 不变量 = a withdrawal of authority is applied where the authority is HELD (the lease + its grant), at the withdrawal, never at the holder's next act; "at its next command" is a rule for a channel that has commands. **Third r4 finding — THE MEDIATOR'S SCOPING DOES NOT SEE A SIDE EFFECT CHROME APPLIES BROWSER-WIDE:** a browser-level `Target.setAutoAttach {waitForDebuggerOnStart:true}` (class `session`, forwarded) froze every OTHER client's new tab at its first navigation (measured on Chrome 153) and the proxy dropped the `attachedToTarget` that could resume it — refused by name now (`auto_attach_pause_refused`; the page-level form the 0.38.1 daemon sends passes). 不变量 = a scoping rule judges what a call NAMES; a call whose effect is browser-wide is judged by its effect.

## A PASTE AND AN IME COMMIT OF FOUR CHARACTERS NEVER REACHED THE AGENT'S PAGE, AND THE BAR SAID "SENT"; ⌘A TYPED "a"; NOTHING COULD BE COPIED OUT (lane live-input, 2026-09-27 — the owner on a Mac, Chrome 152, plain http, the NAMED profile "shopping", agent-browser 0.38.1 + chromium 151)

- **What happened.** "我似乎无法从外面复制文本进入那个浏览器" + "中文输入法也不 work" during a 176 s takeover on a checkout page; plain typing and clicks worked. The fit chip ("按另一个窗口的大小") was unreadable; the journal showed a second `record start` 106 ms after the first, "already holds" on every agent command and the page's full query string in the handback line.
- **Reproduced first.** Two independent diagnoses on the owner's binaries, then this lane's own measurements (standalone Chromium 151 over CDP, the scratch world with the real daemon). Every hop of a failing paste: the viewer's `paste` fired on the keyboard sink (plain http, Ctrl+V and ⌘V, a clipboard filled by another X app — H3 refuted), ONE `char` record `"hello world"` left the page, the bridge wrote it and answered `ok via:'stream'` (a direct lease's receipt is only the write), the daemon issued `Input.dispatchKeyEvent {type:'char'}`, and Chromium answered **-32602 Invalid 'text' parameter** — swallowed. The cap: a key event's text of **4+ UTF-16 units** is refused ("abc", "你好世", "😀a" insert; "abcd", "你好世界", "😀😀" never). A real composition ran in the sink (focus held after a click on the picture — H4 refuted) and died the same way at ≥ 4 units. A mediated lease said it (`browser_refused`); the owner's direct lease could not (H2 refuted as the cause). Lane J r2's "a multi-character char inserts all of it" had been measured with `'abc'`; its gates only ever crossed the wire with 2- and 3-unit strings.
- **Cause 2 (H5, worse than stated).** A ⌘ chord reached Linux Chromium as Meta + the letter WITH its text — Linux gives Meta no editing meaning, so ⌘A / ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘Z TYPED "a" "c" "x" "z". **Cause 3 (found by the copy legs).** A drag's moves were sent `button:'none'` and a double click as two single presses — no text could be selected in the page by the mouse (measured: nothing selected through the view, a whole paragraph through the stream with `button:'left'`). **Cause 4.** Nothing carried a copy OUT: the outer keydown was `preventDefault`ed and nothing read the page's selection. **Cause 5.** `maybeStartRecording` checked `recordings.has(key)` before two awaits and set it after — the agent command's `attach` and the panel's record-on fan-out both started, the loser's failure overwrote the refusal slot after the winner cleared it.
- **THE DECISION, SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT (the two diagnoses disagreed).** Diagnosis 1: cut the text into ≤ 3-unit `char` records on the stream. Diagnosis 2: a new `input_text` record the bridge answers with ONE `Input.insertText` over the page's own CDP socket. Measured: insertText types any length in 2 ms and keeps line breaks exactly — but beside the serial daemon it is not ORDERED: 20 keys queued before it on a page whose keydown takes 30 ms, then an insertText at once ⇒ `"xTEXTxxxx…"` (the text landed after the FIRST key). Text in the wrong place (a password pasted into the username field of a slow login page) is worse than a slow paste. The chunks stay on the ONE ordered channel; the viewer still sends ONE `input_text` per act and the bridge cuts it. The chunker's control-character rules come from the same build: a `char` that STARTS with a tab drops the rest, one that is only "\n" inserts nothing, "\r" drops what follows — a naive 3-unit chunker loses "z" in "ab\tz"; the rules were then fuzzed on the real textarea (393 + 300 seeded texts, 0 wrong). Cost: 20 000 characters = 6 667 records in 3.6 s on a quiet page. A MEDIATED lease needs a window: the mediator keeps 256 credits for 1.2 s, and a paste sent at once evicts its own first credits.
- **FIX.** src/browser-stream.js `CHAR_TEXT_MAX_UNITS` / `textChunks` / `textRecords` / `inputTextRecord`, `text_too_long` for any key record past the cap, per-record receipt waits; src/server/browser-stream.js ONE ordered input pipeline per relay (a text act = one item, one receipt with `landed` / `dropped`, `INPUT_WINDOW` 16 on a mediated lease); src/browser-takeover.js `macChord` (a PURE table; identity for a non-Mac viewer or a Mac browser); the view's pressed-key set (a keyup only after its keydown — an IME commit key's keyup never arrives alone), the sink's focus kept after a click elsewhere in the view, `clickCountNext` + the held button on moves; COPY OUT = the page's own copy / cut event read in an ISOLATED WORLD through a per-arm binding (src/server/browser-viewport.js `watchCopies`, armed per takeover, following the tab) → `clipboard` to the holder → picture-shell's rule (the API on a secure page, the gesture copy on plain http, else the chip); the fit chip CLAIMS ("Fit here") and says where the size comes from; the recording start is single-flight and a refusal is written only when real; the keeper logs a lease when the holder changes and prints `urlForLog` in the handback line.
- **Gates (measured).** test-live-input (fast, in-process 8.4 s, 165 asserts, 10 patched-copy controls). test-browser-live-input (heavy, 47–58 s, 95 asserts): the cap re-measured on the real Chromium, three kinds of browser under trusted input from a non-secure origin, a Mac-emulated viewer, the fit chip in en + zh, and a patched control tree where the pre-fix paste lands "", ⌘A types "a", the commit key's keyup reaches the page, a drag selects nothing and Ctrl+C leaves the clipboard untouched.
- 不变量 = a key event's text is ≤ 3 UTF-16 units — anything longer is text, cut on code points by the measured rules, or refused BY NAME before it is sent (a receipt that only proves a write can never be the whole truth); text the user types rides the SAME ordered channel as their keys and clicks; a Mac viewer's ⌘ is translated for a browser that is not a Mac, and a translated chord carries no text; a keyup reaches the page only after its keydown did; a copy is read at the page's own copy event, never beside the stream; a start that may be asked twice is single-flight and a loser never writes a refusal.

## A PAGE'S OWN SCRIPT WROTE THE DRIVING USER'S CLIPBOARD (lane live-input security verify, 2026-09-27 — the S2 law on the copy-out door; CONFIRMED on the real stack, MAJOR)

- **What the verifier did.** The lane's copy-out path (the page's copy/cut event read in an isolated world → `clipboard` to the holder → the viewer writes the clipboard) was driven adversarially on the real agent-browser 0.38.1 + chromium 151: a page whose script selects a hidden `<div>` ("HIJACK-n") and dispatches a synthetic `copy` every 400 ms — the page's own, and then the SAME script planted by the AGENT with `vibespace-browser eval` before the takeover.
- **Reproduced.** The bridge delivered EVERY copy the page fired (nothing bound it to an act of the holder's), and the viewer wrote it: on a SECURE page (the fleet's https; here 127.0.0.1) through `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with **nothing pressed** — "HIJACK-19" on the viewer's clipboard right after the takeover; on plain http inside the 5 s window a plain CLICK on the picture had opened (`st.gestureAt` was stamped on every pointerdown — picture-shell's rule says the user's OWN copy chord) — "HIJACK-11" after one click, the bar's only sign a small "copied to your clipboard". The agent-planted variant: "HIJACK-8". A classic paste-swap: the party the takeover fences OUT reached the user's device.
- **FIX = the S2 shape on the copy path.** PURE src/browser-takeover.js `copyGestureOfRecord` (a forwarded copy/cut chord keyDown ⇒ 'chord'; a mousePressed ⇒ 'click'; anything else nothing), `armCopyGesture` (the latest gesture replaces the arm), `copyDeliverVerdict` (a copy is delivered ONLY on a live arm — `COPY_GESTURE_MS` 2 s — which it CONSUMES: single-use; none / stale ⇒ dropped), `copyWriteVerdict` (the viewer writes a copy by itself ONLY when it answers the user's own CHORD inside its window — the API on a secure page, else the gesture copy; a click's copy, the page's own Copy button, is the CHIP: one explicit click, never a silent write). The bridge stamps `relay.copyArm` in `forwardInput` (every forwarded record), judges in `deliverCopy` (dropped copies counted `copiesDropped`, nothing leaves the server), names the `gesture` on the record; the viewer's `onPageCopied` reads `m.gesture` + `st.copyAt` (a press stamps nothing any more), spends the chord on the copy it answers.
- **Refuted on the same stack** (the rest of the verifier's brief): the agent's raw CDP through its mediated url during the user's paste — `Input.insertText`, a `char` of its own, a `char` mirroring a chunk, `Runtime.evaluate`, `Input.imeSetComposition` — all `browser_interrupted`, the 1 752-character paste landed whole; the copy world's NAME leaks through `Runtime.executionContextCreated` and `Page.createIsolatedWorld` (harmless class) lets the agent create a world of that name, but the binding can only be called by script, refused while the user drives, and gone with the watch at the handback; a pasted card number and a copied marker are on no file under data/, in no journal line, not in /api/browser/actions, not in telemetry; a 20 000-character paste landed in full before a handback could be pressed (no post-handback typing observed); every new bar string is textContent (`place` tags are regex-validated, `platform` is the server's).
- **Gates.** test-live-input §3 (the door's tables: 14 gesture rows, the arm, 6 verdict rows, 8 write rows) + §6 (the real bridge: a copy with no gesture dropped and counted; a chord delivers ONE `gesture: chord` to the holder only; single-use; a press delivers `gesture: click`; stale after COPY_GESTURE_MS; the door removed in a patched copy delivers the timer's copy) + §9 (wiring: `copyWriteVerdict`, the chord spent, no `gestureAt`); test-browser-live-input "the copy-out door" (the hostile page: nothing pressed ⇒ untouched, no chip; one click ⇒ untouched, the chip; a SECURE viewer with nothing pressed ⇒ untouched) + ⑤ the control tree with BOTH halves of the door removed ⇒ "HIJACK-n" on the clipboard after one click.
- 不变量 = a capability toward the USER'S DEVICE (its clipboard) is bound to the user's own act the server itself forwarded — single-use, short-lived, fail closed — exactly like an input credit; the Clipboard API needing no browser gesture is not a licence to write without one of OURS; a click is not a copy; a copy nobody asked for never leaves the server.

## A SHARED BROWSER'S OWN FIT WAS REFUSED AS THE AGENT'S AND READ BACK AS "AGENT'S SIZE"; A TAKEOVER'S RESIZE LANDED UNDER THE FIRST DRAG (lane live-input reality verify → builder r2, 2026-09-27 — both pre-existing on master 371642a4, LOW; the chip's words fixed with them)

- **What the verifier saw (real agent-browser 0.38.1 + chromium 151, a viewer on plain http).** (A) On a SHARED (`--sharing instance`, mediated) profile, once the user drove, the bridge's own `set viewport` was refused by the mediator as an agent act (`browser_interrupted`): the chip read "Page 698×435 · could not resize" with the agent's English refusal ("CDP error (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride): browser_interrupted: … Wait for the handback, then ") in its tooltip, stayed so AFTER the handback, and in a longer session the chip said "Agent's size 1398×835" — a size the agent never set. (B) After "Take over" while the page was sized for another viewer, the re-fit landed 250–400 ms later; a drag begun in that window was mapped in the old page and the page re-laid out under it (moves jumped y=232 → y=361, 3 of 3; the selection came back empty 2 of 3).
- **Reproduced first (builder r2).** (A) the verifier's `vr-fit` on the lane's HEAD: `unavailable` while driving, the raw error, still `unavailable` 1.5 s after the handback (the failed size sat in `fs.failed` for FIT_RETRY_MS). The "Agent's size" half did not reproduce in four real-stack runs — the debug trace showed why it can: the refused set's `command` mirror normally arrives BEFORE the CLI returns (recognised as ours), but the failure path dropped `fs.pending`, so a mirror arriving after the return (a busy stream) had no pending to match and `agentViewportOf` claimed it; a fast in-process leg that delivers the mirror 40 ms after the return reproduces it every time. (B) `vr-drag` without its 1.5 s settle: 3 of 3 on the lane's HEAD (the moves jumped y=232 → y=361, two selections empty) — the takeover's `scheduleFit('mode')` (250 ms debounce) was RESTARTED by the second tab's close (`viewer-left`), so the resize ran during the person's next clicks; 0 of 3 after the fix, the resize at 44 ms after the takeover instead of ~295 ms.
- **FIX.** (A) the keeper answers `held_while_driving` for a mediated profile somebody drives (the mediator's own paused read) BEFORE spawning a CLI the fence would refuse, and maps an in-flight set the takeover interrupted to the same code; the bridge never remembers it as a failure (the handback re-fits at once), says it once per takeover in the journal, and every failed set is set aside as OURS (`prevOwn`) so its late mirror is never the agent's. The chip is worded by the code: "Page {w}×{h} · resized after the handback" / "A shared browser cannot change its size while you drive it …" (a watcher: "while someone drives it"); any other failure says "The page could not be resized to this window, so it is shown scaled." — the raw error stays in the journal. (B) a mode change fits AT ONCE (no debounce: the resize lands while the hand is still on the button), and the page is never resized under the driver's HELD button (PURE `buttonStep` / `fitHoldVerdict` over the records the bridge forwards; the release runs the held fit; a buttonless move ends a release the view could not map; 15 s cap).
- **Left, by decision.** The page is NOT fitted to the driver's window while a shared browser is driven — the product's own viewport call would need a credit past `Input.*` through the S2 fence (a wider capability surface for a cosmetic gain: the picture is scaled, clicks map by the page's own size). A set already in flight when a press begins (~100–300 ms) can still land under it.
- **Gates.** test-live-input §6 A1 (a failed set's late mirror stays ours; control = the pre-fix `fs.pending = null` reads it as the agent's), A2 (`held_while_driving` re-fits at the handback; control = remembered as a failure ⇒ stuck), B (the takeover fits in ≤ a few ms, no resize under a held button, the release runs it, a lost release ends at the next buttonless move; control = no hold + the 250 ms debounce ⇒ resized mid-drag); §4 the words in zh / ja with a patched copy (old join + raw error). test-browser-live-input (heavy): the shared browser driven on the real mediator — the plain chip, no "agent set" line, one journal line, fitted again at the handback.
- 不变量 = a refusal the product earns by design (a fence it built) is a STATE with its own words, never a failure to remember or an error to print; a mirror of our own act stays ours after the act failed; the page is never re-laid out under a held button, and a mode change's resize runs at once, not under the first press.

## GMAIL'S `stripHtml` AND `parseAddress` WERE QUADRATIC AND UNCAPPED — THE TWO PARSERS ROUND 1'S CENSUS NEVER LISTED (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, 2026-09-28)

Round 1 timed the mail sanitizer and the Lark reader, the two readers the lane ADDED; the peer-byte parsers the lane INHERITED stayed unmeasured. `stripHtml` (src/channels/gmail.js — the record's `text` for an HTML-only mail, i.e. the words an agent reads, run at INGEST on the server) was a regex chain: `<[^>]+>` re-tried to the end of the part for every `<` with no `>`, `<style[\s\S]*?<\/style>` for every `<style` with no closer — measured 64 KB of `<` = 1.2 s, 128 KB = 4.7 s, and NO cap on the part (Gmail hands over megabytes: minutes of event loop per mail, on every ingest pass). `parseAddress` (the From header) was `^(.*?)\s*<([^>]+)>\s*$` — lazy, every prefix re-tried per `<`: 64 KB = 1.4 s, 128 KB = 5.8 s, uncapped.
- **FIX:** `stripHtml` = ONE walk cut at `STRIP_HTML_MAX` (512 KiB — the record's text is bounded to MAX_TEXT after it anyway): a tag's `>` looked for once (none ⇒ the rest is words, a browser's rule), a raw-text element's closer looked for once (none ⇒ the rest is dropped), block closers a newline; `parseAddress` = the LAST `<…>` pair, found once, the header cut at `ADDRESS_MAX` (2 KiB). Both still read every real shape (pinned).
- **THE CENSUS (scripts/test-peer-parsers.mjs, fast):** DERIVED — every exported function of src/mail-frame.js, src/channel-blocks.js, src/channel-record.js, src/channels/gmail.js and src/channels/lark.js is a ROW (a size cap proven by an input over it; linearity t(2n) ≤ 2.5 × t(n) on the row's own adversarial shapes at 64 / 128 KB, or under 15 ms at 2n — min of 5 runs, the base repeated to ≥ 25 ms) or in EXCLUDED with a reason (a number, a lookup, our own string, a validated tree); a new export goes red until placed. CONTROLS: round 1's per-quote newline scan in `sanitizeCss`, round 2's regex-chain `stripHtml` and lazy `parseAddress` restored in patched copies — ×4 under the same judge.
- **不变量.** A census of "every parser over peer bytes" is derived from the modules' exports, never hand-written from the diff — the parsers a lane INHERITS are peer-byte parsers too.

## THE INLINE MARKUP READER RE-READ ITS OWN RUN ON EVERY `<li>` — QUADRATIC AT INGEST, AND THE POST ELEMENT HAD NO BOUND (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, 2026-09-28)

Round 1 made `markupRead` linear in BLOCKS mode and bounded `larkPlainText` / `larkMdBlocks`; a Lark POST's text element takes the INLINE mode (`larkPostBlocks` → `markupRead(t, {mode:'inline'})`, one run list for the line) and that mode's `brk()` and cell rule asked `/\n$/.test(last.text)` on the text run every `<li>` / `<br>` / `<td>` had just been appended to — V8 flattens the rope for each regex, so n items cost n × (the text so far): 32 KB of `<li>` 10 ms, 64 KB 37 ms, 128 KB 433 ms, on the server's event loop at ingest; and `const t = String(el.text || '')` never went through `bounded()`, so a 1 MB element was half a minute. Measured through `larkToBlocks` on the real post shape.
- **FIX:** the last text run's TAIL CHARACTER is tracked beside the run (`tail`, set in `pushRun`, cleared in `flush`) and `brk()` / the cell rule read it in O(1); the post element's text goes through `bounded()` like every other body. The inline shape is unchanged (one break, a bullet per item, two spaces between cells).
- **Gate:** test-channel-blocks ⑱ — inline `markupRead` linear from 32 to 64 KB on `<li>` / `<br>` / `<td>` / `<p>`; a 1 MB post element through `larkToBlocks` in a few ms; the wiring pin (bounded + the tracked tail); CONTROL = a copy re-reading the run is ×3.2. test-peer-parsers rows `larkToBlocks` / `textOf` / `toRecord` hold the same at the census level.
- **不变量.** Never ask a regex a question about a string that is being appended to in a loop — a rope flattened per iteration is quadratic; keep the fact (the tail character) beside the string.

## AN UNCLOSED `<title>` IN A LARK MESSAGE DELETED THE REST OF THE MESSAGE (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, 2026-09-28)

The markup reader (src/channel-blocks.js `markupTokens` / `markupRead`) opens a DROP at every tag in `MK_DROP` (`script`, `style`, `iframe`, `title`, `select`, `video`, `svg`, `canvas`, `textarea`, `math`, `template`, …) and reads to its closer — and a plain chat sentence has no closer: "please set the <title> of the page to Foo" → `rec.text` "please set the", the blocks the same; "the <select> is broken, use a <video> instead" → "the". Every word after the tag was gone from the agent's `read`, the search, the window and the attention list, silently — a data loss any sender causes by writing an HTML word in angle brackets, and a way to hide a message's tail from an agent while Lark's own client shows it whole. The lone-tag rule already protected UNKNOWN tags (`<country>` stays a word); the known drop tags had no such rule.
- **FIX:** in `markupTokens`, a drop tag the message never CLOSES is not a drop — with no attributes it is the word the person typed (the wall words it `‹title›`), with attributes it is that one tag alone (`self`, dropped by itself); the words after it stay either way. A closed `<script>…</script>` is still dropped whole.
- **Gate:** test-channel-blocks ⑰ — a 12-row table (unclosed words kept and walled, closed pairs dropped with their contents, attributed unclosed tags dropped alone) judged on `rec.text` AND the blocks through `lark.toRecord`; CONTROL = a copy without the rule reads the sentence as "please set the".
- **不变量.** A reader of peer prose never drops to the END of the input on a token that may be a word; a drop needs its closer in the same text.

## THE LAZY-FRAME CAP BLANKED MAILS ON SCREEN — THE NEWEST REPLIES OF A SHORT THREAD WERE EMPTY BOXES (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, continued, 2026-09-28)

`liveFrames` sorted the candidate rows by their distance to the view and SLICED to `LIVE_FRAME_CAP` (6) — every row inside the view has distance 0, so with more than six formatted rows on screen the kept six were the first six in the IntersectionObserver's Set order and the rest stayed `chanmail-ph` placeholders; the row's `chanmail-formatted` class hides its text body, so a visible mail showed NOTHING. Short HTML replies ("Thanks!" + a signature) shrink their rows to ~70 px once live, which pulls more rows into view. Measured in chrome (probe `scen-blank-visible.mjs`): 16 short replies, an 812 px list at the tail — 9 on screen, 6 live, the NEWEST three blank, still blank 8 s later. The chrome leg had seen it twice as a flake (`custom-elements: timeout`, `dom-clobber: timeout` — the row never went live while centred). The suite's own table pinned it: 7 rows on screen, 6 live, "the visible ones first".
- **FIX:** every row inside the view is live; the cap bounds only the keep zone's PRE-WARMED rows (nearest first while the total is under the cap). The visible rows are bounded by the view itself (a row is never shorter than HEIGHT_MIN + its header).
- **Measured after:** the same thread — 9 on screen, 9 live.
- **Gate:** test-mail-frame ⑦ (7 on screen ⇒ 7 live; 3 on screen ⇒ 3 + the 3 nearest pre-warmed; the measured tail shape; cap 0 ⇒ only the rows on screen; CONTROL = the round-1 verdict keeps 6 of 7) + test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑩ⓗ (every formatted row on screen live at every stop, frames ≤ max(cap, on screen)) + ⑩x (around five short corpus mails, > the cap on screen, all live).
- **不变量.** A resource cap on lazily-rendered rows bounds what is OFF screen; what the person is looking at is never traded away — a tie at distance 0 is not a ranking.

## THE HEIGHT BUDGET DROPPED THE LAST HEIGHT OF EVERY BURST — A RESIZED WINDOW CUT THE MAIL'S LAST LINE (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, continued, 2026-09-28)

Round 2's belt against the animated mail (the entry below) applied one height change per `HEIGHT_MIN_GAP_MS` 250 after the settle and answered `hold` for the rest — a hold KEPT NOTHING. The frame's resizer posts a height only when its own measure CHANGES (`if (v !== last)`), so a held height is never sent again: the LAST height of any burst was lost for the frame's life. Measured in chrome on the scratch server (probe `scen-height-trailing.mjs`): the channel window narrowed 520 → 480 px in 12 steps 25 ms apart ⇒ the frame posted 677 then 696 (30 ms apart), the row stayed 677, and the mail's last line ("LAST LINE OF THE MAIL", 19 px) was hidden — the frame's overflow is hidden, so nothing scrolls to it. The same drop hits two pictures landing within 250 ms of each other after the settle (Show pictures over a slow network), a phone rotation, a sidebar toggle. The suite's own table had pinned the false premise ("the same height asked again past the gap applies") — the frame never asks again.
- **FIX:** the TRAILING EDGE in the PURE verdict — a gap hold stores the height as the budget's `pending` and answers `retryAt` (= the last apply + the gap); a later message supersedes it, an apply / a height equal to the applied one / a freeze clears it; `heightPending(b)` reads it. The DOM half's `applyHeight(s, h)` arms ONE timer per live frame on a hold with `retryAt` and re-judges `heightPending` of THAT budget (a rebuilt frame's new budget is never fed an old height); `drop()` clears the timer. The flip cap still freezes a pulse (nothing waits on a frozen budget).
- **Measured after:** the same drag — the row at 696, the last line shown.
- **Gate:** test-mail-frame ⑬ (the pending / retryAt / supersede / clear table, a burst walked on a fake clock through the DOM half's rule — a drag ends at 696, three pictures at 610 —, two wiring pins; CONTROL = the round-2 budget as shipped ends the drag at 677 and the pictures at 420) + test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑩x (`height-burst`: the window narrowed in 12 quick steps, the row at the frame's LAST posted height).
- **不变量.** A rate limit over a stream whose producer sends only CHANGES must keep the latest value and deliver it at the window's end — a throttle without a trailing edge turns "fewer updates" into "the wrong final state".

## ONE MAIL MADE THE WHOLE CONVERSATION JUMP 60 TIMES A SECOND (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, 2026-09-28)

`<style>@keyframes g{from{height:100px}to{height:19000px}} body{animation:g .2s linear infinite alternate}</style>` — no script, no network, every wall held — and the conversation window was unusable: the frame's OWN resizer (a ResizeObserver) posted each new height, the parent's verdict clamped each one and APPLIED it. Measured in chrome on the scratch server: 181 height messages and 44 scrollTop changes in 3 s, the row between 100 and 19 000 px, for as long as the mail sat inside the keep zone — a stored, fleet-wide denial of the conversation (every client that opens it), by anyone who can send a mail.
- **FIX, two walls:** ① the ROOT — a mail does not animate: `sanitizeCss` takes out every `@keyframes` block (`cssKeyframes`: brace-balanced, every vendor prefix, ONE walk — an unclosed block takes the rest) and every `animation-*` / `transition-*` declaration (a mail client's rule); ② the BELT — the parent's PURE `heightBudget` / `heightVerdict`: while the frame settles (`HEIGHT_SETTLE_MS` 1 500 after it went live) every change applies, then one change per `HEIGHT_MIN_GAP_MS` 250, and a height that flips direction `HEIGHT_FLIP_CAP` 8 times inside `HEIGHT_FLIP_WINDOW_MS` 10 s FREEZES the row at its last size for the frame's life (`data-frozen` on the box); a person's quote toggle (a flip every few seconds) and a row that only grows never freeze.
- **Measured after:** the same mail — 0 height messages, 1 row height, 1 scrollTop in 3 s.
- **Gate:** test-mail-frame ⑬ (the CSS table incl. nested braces / prefixes / an unclosed block / an inline style, the budget's tables, the wiring pin, the `@keyframes x{` shape at the 2 MB bound in 76 ms; CONTROLS = a copy that keeps animations, a copy whose budget never freezes) + the chrome leg's corpus mail `height-animation`.
- **不变量.** A number a peer's content can change CONTINUOUSLY is budgeted over TIME by the side that acts on it — clamping each value bounds the size of one step, never the number of steps.

## THE MAIL BODY'S "BOUND BEFORE THE DOWNLOAD" NEVER ENGAGED — THE ROUTE SENDS NO CONTENT-LENGTH (lane channel-rich security verify round 2, 2026-09-28)

Round 1 rated "the mail view downloads the whole body before checking its size" LOW and fixed it by reading `Content-Length` before `res.arrayBuffer()`. Measured on the scratch server: `GET /api/channels/…/attachment/<body>` answers `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and NO `Content-Length` — the route pipes `fs.createReadStream` straight into the response — so the guard compared `Number(null) = 0` with the 2 MB bound, passed, and `arrayBuffer()` pulled the WHOLE body (the route's `ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` = 100 MB; Gmail's part limit ~25 MB) into the page before `byteLength` was judged: on every open of the conversation, in every client, with the string then held in the frame cache. A LOW whose fix was dead is a MEDIUM (a mail costs every reader of the conversation 25 MB per open).
- **FIX:** `src/lib/bounded-read.js` `readBounded(res, max)` — imports nothing: a `Content-Length` over the bound is refused before the first byte (the cheap rung kept, never trusted UNDER the bound), then the body is read chunk by chunk and the read STOPS the moment the bound is passed (`reader.cancel()` — the socket released, at most one chunk past the bound ever held); the DOM half (`channel-mail-frame.js` `load`) reads through it and never `arrayBuffer()`; the attachment route stats the cached file (async) and answers `Content-Length` before piping.
- **Gate:** test-mail-frame ⑫ — a 3 MB chunked body with no length refused after ≤ bound + one 64 KiB chunk with the stream cancelled; a 1 MB body read whole; a header over the bound refused at 0 bytes; a header UNDER the bound with a bigger body still refused at the bound; wiring pins (readBounded at MAX_HTML_BYTES, no arrayBuffer, the route's Content-Length before the pipe); CONTROL = a copy without the running bound reads the 3 MB whole.
- **不变量.** A size guard is judged at the BYTES it actually reads, never at a header a route may omit or a peer may forge; a round-1 fix on a LOW is re-measured on the real answer before it counts.

## A PEER'S MAIL FROZE THE TAB, A PEER'S LARK MESSAGE STALLED THE SERVER OR THREW OUT OF THE NORMALIZER (lane channel-rich security verify, 2026-09-28 — every shape reproduced with a timer before the fix)

The lane's two new readers of PEER-CONTROLLED markup were correct on every hostile corpus the builder wrote and QUADRATIC (or unbounded in depth) on shapes nobody wrote: the mail sanitizer runs on the browser's main thread when a conversation opens (formatted is the default), the Lark markup reader on the server at ingest AND at every read (`recordView` — the window's page, an agent's `read`, both searches).
- **The mail sanitizer (src/mail-frame.js), measured:** a tag with no `>` to the end (`<a ` × n) — `readAttrs` walked to the end, the loop wrote `&lt;` and advanced ONE character, and the next `<` walked to the end again: 64 KB = 15 s, the 2 MB bound = hours; the same for an unterminated attribute quote and `<b<b<b…`. A dropped element's skip (`<svg>` then `<svg ` with no `>`) re-walked `[^>]*>` per candidate; CSS: `cssStrings` re-scanned for the next newline at every quote (2 MB of `''` = 15 s), the `url(` regex re-scanned to the end for every `url(` with no `)`, the `@font-face` block regex per `{` with no `}`. FIX: a tag walk that reached the end makes the rest TEXT in one piece (a browser reads it as one unfinished tag), the drop skip / newline / next `)` are found once and reused until passed (`cssUrls`), an unclosed `{` takes the rest. Every shape at 2 MB now ≤ 165 ms. The DOM half also refuses a body whose Content-Length is over the bound BEFORE downloading it.
- **The Lark reader (src/channel-blocks.js), measured:** `MK_TAG_RE`'s lazy attribute run followed by `\s*` backtracked quadratically over a whitespace run inside a tag (`<a` + 64 KB of spaces = 1.7 s of the event loop per record; 3.5 s through `toRecord`, which reads it twice); `larkMdBlocks` re-introduced the fence walk the email rung had fixed in verify round 4 (10 000 `\`\`\`js` lines = 0.6–1.3 s); `<blockquote>` × 5 000 and `> ` × 20 000 built trees as deep as the input — the text path's `blocksToPlain` overflowed the stack and `toRecord` THREW (a poison message that fails every pass of its conversation). FIX: one greedy attribute run (the trailing `/` peeled in `markupTokens`), `noCloserFrom` in `larkMdBlocks`, a nesting bound in both readers counted from where the output lands (`opts.depth`: a card's inner blocks start at 1) — a quote past the record's depth is a paragraph break / its words unquoted — and `textOf` guarded (a throw inside is the raw words behind the wall).
- **Gates:** test-mail-frame ⑪ (8 shapes at MAX_HTML_BYTES under 1 500 ms; 5 patched copies restoring each old loop run under the SAME judge in a child cut at the budget — all OVER; the harness on the real module under), test-channel-blocks ⑯ (4 shapes at BLOCK_LIMITS.text under 250 ms, the depth table incl. a card holding both, 4 child controls OVER + 2 unbounded-nesting copies THROW), test-channels-lark-shape ⑩ (the guard; its removal throws).
- **不变量.** A reader of peer-controlled markup is judged at its OWN size bound with adversarial shapes — a tag / quote / block that never closes, a whitespace run inside a tag, nesting as deep as the input — never only on a hostile corpus of well-formed attacks: every walk that can reach the end of the input either consumes what it walked or remembers that nothing follows, and every recursion or nested structure has a depth bound. A fix once made in one rung (the fence walk) is a census over every rung that walks the same syntax.

## THE STASH TWO LANES BUILT ON — ONE QUEUE, ONE MERGED DOOR; ONE WRITER IN THE CONVERSATION WINDOW (integration 2.369.195, 2026-09-28)

Two lanes built on one store from the same base (4c5f9146) and never saw each other's code: lane channel-withdraw made the conversation stash tell a producer the FATE of an entry it tracks (`ref` = a receipt's proposal id; events `stashed` / `drained` / `evicted` / `unwritten`; every write synchronous with a `{stored, why}` verdict), lane channel-jump made the same stash VISIBLE and HANDABLE (the `stash` session fact, the Hand over now press, the `ho` claim stamped on disk, drains by identity, a frame that came back restored as its original entries, a cap that never evicts a claimed entry). Their verifiers wrote the merge rules ahead (withdraw r5–r7's checklist ①–⑬, channel-jump r3/r4's integration note); this is what the merged `src/server/conversation-deliver.js` DOES — the one statement the two lanes' essays below now point at.

- **The entry and its write.** `stashFor(cid, envelope)` builds withdraw's entry (`ref` kept — channel-jump's literal dropped it and every receipt would have lost its fate), snapshots the queue, pushes, applies THE CAP, then writes synchronously (`flush()` → boolean). A write that FAILS for a ref'd entry restores the queue EXACTLY as it was (`q.splice(0, q.length, ...before)` — the cap may drop from anywhere between claimed entries, so the lane's splice-then-unshift would have re-ordered it), tells `onStashChange`, and throws (the engine records the receipt `undelivered`, `stash-failed`); an entry without a ref stays in memory and its producer hears `{stored:false, why}` + an `unwritten` event. Every mutation says BOTH hooks: `emitStash` (withdraw's listeners, ref'd entries only) and `stashChanged` (channel-jump's strip / session fact).
- **THE CAP is channel-jump's `capUnclaimed(q)`, now RETURNING the entries it dropped.** It counts the UNCLAIMED entries and drops the oldest unclaimed beyond STASH_CAP; a claimed (`ho`) entry is never evicted (the store may exceed 30 by the claimed count while a hand-over is in flight). The dropped entries are logged by name ("never delivered") and carried by withdraw's `evicted` event — the ONLY place `evicted` is said, so an entry a hand-over carries can never read "Not delivered". src/jobs.js's twin `capUnclaimedNotifs` only logs: a job notification carries no `ref`, nothing tracks its fate.
- **Drains.** `drainStash(cid, only)` = channel-jump's body (a Set drains exactly those entries — the hand-over's "what I delivered" — and keeps what arrived meanwhile; a full drain keeps every claimed entry; EVERY drain writes at once) + withdraw's `drained` event naming what was TAKEN, never the whole queue (a receipt still waiting must not read "handed").
- **Restores and claims.** `restoreStash` (a frame that came back undelivered) puts the originals back by ts, trims NOTHING (they are the oldest; the next arrival's cap applies), writes at once, and says `stashed` for its ref'd entries (+ `unwritten` if that write failed) — a receipt back in the queue reads waiting again. `claimStash` stamps `ho:<hand-over id>` and writes through; a claim write that fails is LOGGED by name (the stamp lives in memory — a crash before the 30 s retry re-delivers: a duplicate, never a loss). An entry with both `ref` and `ho` is an ordinary receipt being handed over: it leaves by the hand-over's drain (`drained`) or is released unclaimed.
- **Boot order.** The ladder is created at server.js's deliver construction; its loader releases every `ho` stamp a dead process left (`releasedAtBoot`, logged with the hand-over id) BEFORE the channels engine starts and runs `reconcileReceiptFates` — a released receipt reads as still waiting, never handed.
- **Exports** are the union: `stashPeek` (copies, the engine's reconcile), `stashEntries` (the same objects, the hand-over's identity drain), `stashHealth`, `onStash`, `claimStash` / `claimedCount` / `restoreStash` / `registerFrameRestorer` / `restoreFrame` / `releasedAtBoot` / `flush` / `capUnclaimed`.
- **The conversation window's list has ONE writer (the same merge, src/lib/channel-window.js).** mirror-193 (2.369.194) had fixed the thrice-drawn list with a render GENERATION (`renderGen` / `pageFor` / `upInFlight`); lane channel-render, from the older base, with a SERIAL QUEUE (every render, patch and upward page runs one after another). The merge keeps ONE mechanism — the queue — plus mirror-193's other rule, the list-ready flag (a scroll event the rebuild's own clear causes never asks for the page above the boundary the clear reset), which PURE `pageUpVerdict` reads beside its scroll-evidence clauses. Since channel-render a broadcast PATCHES the list in place, so test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑨b builds its rebuild from a reconnect's re-read; its CONTROL neuters the queue ("run now") and removes the ready rule together with the three scroll-evidence clauses (each alone refuses the clear's event — a control that removed one layer would stay green for the wrong reason).
- **Gates (the merged tree).** test-channel-outbox merge-a (a claimed receipt is never evicted; control: the whole-store cap reads "evicted" for a carried notice), merge-b (a drain by identity names what it took; control: the whole queue), merge-c (a restore says waiting; control: a quiet restore), merge-d (the boot release before the reconcile), merge-e (the exact take-back + the change hook; control: the lane's splice-then-unshift re-orders); test-stash-strip ②c's .195 leg (`evicted` names only the oldest unclaimed; control: the whole-store cap names claimed entries); test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑨ / ⑨b + the one control bundle; the lanes' own spelling pins re-pointed to the merged lines (outbox take-back, stash-strip anchors 7 / 15 / the eviction log / the claim + drain pins, channel-touch's head-column call).
- **The heavy tier's three reds (root-caused, none a flake — each red on both attempts, green after its fix).** ① test-desktop-app-window §E shared a window with a CLIENT-ONLY roster entry: withdraw verify r6 made the Share dialog send a session by its LIVE webui id (pinned by test-window-reach §10 — never the client-spelled key) and the engine refuses an id no session answers to (`bad_principal`), so the fixture was the stale part: the share legs now use a stub agent the server RUNS (dtach socket + meta restored at boot as `w-lane-e`, test-channels-aggregate-ui's recipe; SKIP by name without dtach) and the ask leg's `not_live` refusal keeps a page-only ghost. ② test-channel-jump's phone leg still expected `.chat-stash-cost` hidden — the lane's own verify r4 keeps the money word on the button on every width; the leg now asserts it stays. ③ test-queue-steer's layout pin read the queue strip as the input area's FIRST child; channel-jump put the stash strip above it (what waits FOR the agent over what YOU sent) — the pin reads that order.
- **不变量.** Two lanes that write to one store merge into ONE statement of its rules, never two doors: an entry leaves undelivered in exactly one place and that place says so; an event names exactly the entries the act touched; a take-back restores the state it found; a view rebuilt by fetches has ONE writer, and a control neuters the whole guard, not one of its layers.

## A CLICK ON A LAUNCH CARD WAS LOST WHEN THE 5 s BROADCAST LANDED UNDER IT (lane office-desktop, 2026-09-27)

**Symptom.** test-desktop-app-window's share-at-launch leg went red in 4 of 7 runs on the lane (0 of 6 on master): the trusted click on the xterm card launched nothing, no toast. **Evidence** (the leg instrumented — a MutationObserver on the catalog, capture listeners, the catalog's innerHTML setter wrapped for a stack): `pointerdown` on the card's label at T, the WHOLE catalog rebuilt at T+2 ms from `ws.onmessage` → the dialog's `desktop-apps-updated` handler → `render()`, no `click` ever — the element under the pointer was replaced between pointerdown and pointerup, and a click whose down and up land on different elements never fires. The broadcast is the machine keeper's 5 s tick commit (the resource report's live row) while any app runs; the lane's four more catalog rows shifted the suite's timing so its press kept meeting a tick. **A person hits it too**: a human press lasts ~100 ms, so ~2 % of clicks on a card (or on a Running row's Open / Stop) while any app ran were lost. **Fix:** the Running rows are their own renderer (`renderRunning`), rebuilt only when what they show moved (ids / labels / states / host / a pending Stop / the slot count — a key compare); the broadcast calls it and never touches the catalog. Measured after: 6 of 6 green. **Invariant: a broadcast re-renders only what it changed, and never the control under the user's pointer — a rebuild between pointerdown and pointerup eats the click.** Gate: test-desktop-app-window (the leg), test-office-open §9 (the pin: the broadcast calls `renderRunning`, not `render`).

## A DEFAULT THE USER SET AFTER A SESSION STARTED REACHED IT THROUGH ITS LATE BROWSER KEY (B-f7ab verify r2, 2026-09-27 — reproduced on the real keeper + routes and on a real worktree server before the fix)

- **What happened.** Round 1 dated the late key's default pin at the session's START (`latePinAt`), so a narrowing made after the start won. But the late key still READ THE LADDER AT THE MINT: instance default Old at the start; the user narrows Bank to First chat (T1); a keyless session starts on Old (T2 > T1); the user makes Bank the instance default (T3) — or the Task Group's; the agent's first browser command (T4) picked Bank and dated the pin T2 ≥ scopeAt ⇒ ADMITTED to Bank (the owner's logins). The spawn-keyed twin that started at the same instant had landed on Old and never saw Bank — a default reaches a conversation only at its start (the spawn reads the ladder once; the cap's law, lane P finding 5), and the late key had no record of what was in force then. The same shape: the Task Group's cap edited after the start was stamped on the late key (5 where the twin kept none); an adopted fork's late key took the instance default dated at the fork's own start instead of the parent's stale pin copy (`copyPin`'s verbatim row); a profile picked in the New Session dialog while the switch was off was lost (the dialog's row is not gated on it).
- **The fix.** A keyless spawn now RECORDS its ladder's pick as a WITNESS — `browserPinAtStart: {profileId, origin, at, by, cap}` in the session's record (ws-create: the instance / Task Group / chosen pick dated at the start; a fork's = its parent's row verbatim; the ladder picking nothing is witnessed too, with the group cap in force). The late key restores exactly that (PURE `B.lateDefaultPin`: the witness wins over the ladder, dated no later than the start; keeper `restorePin` writes the row as the spawn would have — no `by:'agent'` re-admission; `stampGroupCap(…, {value: B.witnessCap(witness)})` — the group is never read live). A record WITHOUT a witness (from before r2) gets the default the user has now as a LANDING dated 0 — `userPinAuthorizes` reads 0 ≥ scopeAt as false the moment a narrowing exists, so it never authorizes a narrowed profile; the agent's bare command still names it and is refused `not_owner` by the button (never a silent temporary browser); a never-narrowed profile admits everybody anyway. The spawn ↔ late parity table (scope all / one:X × started before / after the narrowing × default set before / after the start) answers identically in both columns. Beside it (LOW): a key minted by a call that is then REFUSED (not_owner, launch_failed…) rides the refusal as `minted` and the CLI prints `[browser_key_minted]` there too.
- **Invariant.** A default reaches a conversation only at its START; a path that applies one LATE applies what a WITNESS says was in force then, and without a witness applies nothing it could be asked to authorize. An unwitnessed authorization is dated 0 (the earliest possible), never at the start it cannot prove.
- **Gates.** test-browser-share-model ③f (r2): the `lateDefaultPin` table, the four reproduced scenes on the real keeper + routes (instance default / group default + cap / adopted fork / the dialog's pick) each beside its spawn-keyed twin, the 8-row parity table, and TWO patched-copy controls (the r1 engine — ladder read at the mint, dated at the start — ADMITS; a copy stamping the cap live stamps the later cap). test-browser-continuity ⑤ (heavy, a real server) asserts the witness on a keyless spawn.
- **Verify r3 (2026-09-27, LOW — both by construction, neither written by the product).** ① `userPinAuthorizes` read `0 ≥ (scopeAt || 0)` as TRUE on a narrowed profile with no scope date (owner kind session / task and no `scopeAt`: a hand-edited or restored-after-the-migration registry — every narrowing the product writes stamps `scopeAt`), so the landing dated 0 ADMITTED the legacy session there (the r2 sentence "never an authorization on a narrowed profile" was false for that shape). Now a pin dated 0 authorizes NOTHING (an authorization is dated; a profile open to all admits without a pin in `mayAttach`). ② `lateDefaultPin` dated a witness on a record with NO known start by the witness's own `at` (a future date in a damaged record ⇒ `restorePin`'s clock ⇒ admitted to a profile narrowed just before); now such a witness is dated 0 like r1's unknown start (ws-create writes `createdAt` in the same write as the witness, so a real record always has one — this instance: 75 records, 0 without a start, 0 narrowed profiles without a date, counted read-only). Everything else attacked in r3 was REFUTED on the real keeper + routes + the real meta choke point and on a real worktree server: the witness write is synchronous with the spawn (no `await` between `pty.spawn` and the origin meta write — a route cannot land between; every later meta writer spreads the base), it equals the keyed twin's pin row + cap stamp field for field (group pick + cap, the dialog's pick + the `instance` hint downgrade, a keyless fork of a keyed parent = the parent's row verbatim), a shell's witness is inert (`conversation_unknown`), a keyless fork of a keyless parent re-reads the ladder exactly as the keyed twin does (no parent key ⇒ no copy — a FACT, not a leak: the fork is a new conversation at its own start), the witness survives a restart unchanged and the first route at boot+27 ms restores it, a mint then a restart is identical, a keyless resume keeps its conversation's own row over a stale (empty) witness and a cleared row lands on nothing, a deleted / foreign / wrong-`by` / string-dated witness pins nothing. Gate: test-browser-share-model ③f (r3) — 12 + 4 PURE rows, the real keeper over the constructed no-scopeAt registry, one patched-copy control (the r2 verdicts admit 6 + 3 rows).
- **Since 2.369.196 (the list integration).** The witness (`browserPinAtStart`, PURE `lateDefaultPin` / `isPinWitness`, keeper `restorePin`) is kept as a PREFERENCE witness: the late key restores the pin the ladder picked at the start (so the profile a bare command opens is the one in force then, never a later default), dated by the witness's own record — informational only. A restore NEVER edits any profile's `owner.who` (a witness widens nothing — only the user's own `chosen` pick adds a conversation to the list); test-browser-share-model ③f pins it on the real keeper and routes (a `chosen` witness and a landing on a profile kept to another conversation: every profile's owner byte-identical after the mint, the list refuses `not_owner`) with a patched-copy CONTROL (a `restorePin` that also calls `addConversation`: the same judge sees the owner change and the list admit the key). A no-witness record lands on the current default without a date; the list refuses it on a narrowed profile exactly as it refuses the spawn-keyed twin.

## THE LATE BROWSER KEY'S DEFAULT PIN WAS A FRESH AUTHORIZATION (B-f7ab verify r1, 2026-09-27 — reproduced on the real keeper + routes before the fix)

- **What happened.** B-f7ab lets a live session that has no browser key (it started before per-session browsers, or while they were off) mint one on its first browser use, through the spawn's own pin ladder: the Task Group's / the instance's default profile becomes its pin, `setPin(…, {origin})` — and the keeper stamps a pin `at: now()`. A pin the user configured is an AUTHORIZATION (`mayAttach`'s `pinned` = `userPinAuthorizes`: the pin is admitted only when it is not older than the profile's last "Who can use it" change, `scopeAt` — THE USER'S LATEST CHOICE WINS). So: instance default "Bank"; the user keeps Bank to First chat at T1; a keyless session that started at T0 < T1 runs `vibespace-browser open` at T2 — its pin is dated T2 > T1, `userPinned` says yes, the agent is IN Bank (the owner's logins). The same session keyed at spawn (pin dated T0) is refused `not_owner` (the control leg). No user act happened at T2; an agent's command minted a user-grade authorization fresher than the user's narrowing.
- **The fix.** The late key stands in for the key the spawn would have given, so its default pin carries the instant the session STARTED: PURE `B.latePinAt({recordedAt: meta.createdAt, liveAt: session.createdAt})` = the OLDEST finite start (a restored session's record beats its restore instant; nothing finite ⇒ 0, which outranks no narrowing), handed to `keeper.setPin(…, {at})`, which only ever dates a pin EARLIER than its own clock (`min(now(), at)`; a non-number ⇒ `now()`). A session that started after the narrowing is admitted by the default as its spawn would have been. Beside it: every `vibespace-browser` verb prints a refusal's `remedy:` line (only the page verbs' path did).
- **Invariant.** A default applied LATE is dated when the thing it defaults for BEGAN, never when it was applied — an automatic act can never mint an authorization fresher than the user's latest choice (copyPin's "a fork never launders an authorization", the same law); a store that stamps time takes a caller's `at` only to make the record OLDER.
- **Gates.** test-browser-share-model ③f: the `latePinAt` table, the real keeper + routes scene (started-before ⇒ `not_owner` with the pin dated at the start and nothing opened; started-after ⇒ admitted; restored ⇒ the record's start), `setPin`'s clamp, and a CONTROL copy of browser-key.js that stamps the mint instant — the same judge ADMITS on it. test-browser-pin: the CLI's remedy line on a non-page verb.
- **SUPERSEDED (2.369.196 integration, spec-who-may-use §3.3).** "Who can use it" became a LIST and `whoMayUse(profile)` is the ONE admission source: a pin is a PREFERENCE and authorizes nothing, so its date authorizes nothing either. `latePinAt`, `userPinAuthorizes`, `userPinned`, every `pinned:` argument to admission and `setPin`'s `at` are DELETED, and the ③f legs that pinned the dated-pin rule ("a pin dated 0 authorizes nothing", the started-before / started-after split, the keeper's date clamp) went with them. The bug this entry fixed cannot recur by construction: no clock is read by any admission. What stays: the late key restores the PIN its start picked (the witness below), and whether that profile admits the conversation is asked of the list at every command. 不变量 = a timestamp is never an authorization.

## A DIALOG'S WHOLE-LIST SAVE REVOKED A GRANT IT NEVER SAW; A CONVERSATION WINDOW DREW ITS MESSAGES THREE TIMES; TWO GATE JUDGES READ THE RUNNER'S SCHEDULER (mirror-193, 2026-09-27 — the 2.369.193 Actions mirror: test-channels-aggregate-ui red on both heavy attempts, test-exit-forensics flaky)

- **What happened.** Attempt 1: `授权访问…` opened on `["Agent · reader"]` where the account held the agent Xi, and the Save's wire was `[reader, 工作]` — Xi's access (and any notification of Xi's) revoked by a write nobody meant as a revocation; the next leg then threw on the missing Xi (the log cut the throw at 900 chars before it named a line). Attempt 2: the owner's Notify save read its toasts as `[]`. test-exit-forensics: the dtach `'w'` control read `json=false buf=false`. Green here on every idle run.
- **Reproduced first (the house recipe: `taskset -c 0 nice -n 5` beside two pinned busy loops).** Pre-fix, 14 runs: the attempt-1 shape 5/14 with the runner's exact wire; attempt 2 0/14 naturally (9 reached it); and a THIRD shape the runner had not shown — the picture legs 5/14. test-exit-forensics pre-fix: the control red 3/4; with only an evidence-based settle wait (the obvious "it was slow" fix) STILL red 4/5, each trial settled in 80–330 ms — so not slowness.
- **Cause 1 (product).** The Grant access… / Notify… dialogs of the ACCOUNT and RULE grains drew `target.adapter` — the panel's broadcast-fed digest — while the conversation grain re-read its lists; the seed PUT's `channels-updated` had not reached the runner's page when the dialog opened (the panel copy: no access at all ⇒ the dialog's default row = the first live agent), and Save sends the grain's WHOLE list. The suite's `Xi`/`reader` question was never a naming race: it was a different principal, from a stale copy.
- **Cause 2 (judge).** The toast judge counted `#global-toasts` before the click and sliced after: a toast lives 3 s and the stack is capped at 4, so an OLDER toast leaving during a slow save shifted the count and the new toast fell outside the slice — constructed on the same save (an older toast removed after the click): the pre-fix arithmetic reads `[]`, the runner's exact value.
- **Cause 3 (product, found by the emulation).** channel-window's `render()` cleared the list, awaited its page, then appended — and it is re-entered by the open, by the broadcast the watch beat's fetch sends and by the one the open's mark-read sends: two or three renders in flight each appended (diagnosed in the page: room-2's six messages ×3; the picture legs' selector found the stale copy's lazy `<img>`, never loaded). Second path: a repaint's clear drops `scrollTop` to 0 and the scroll event it causes asked for the page above a boundary the clear had just reset — the tail again, prepended.
- **Cause 4 (judge).** The dtach kill-path trial spelled the server's order (SIGTERM the master, then unlink). On a starved CPU the SIGTERM wakes the sleeping master on the SAME CPU, the scheduler preempts the sender for it, the master's exit SIGHUPs the wrapper, which preempts too: the handler ran BEFORE the unlinks (8 of 8 codex trials; evidence: no `record skipped`, and the files gone at the end ⇒ the unlink came after every write). The `'w'` copy wrote into the file the test then unlinked — "re-created nothing". The real legs were VACUOUSLY green in the same trials. Same class in the pad legs: the codex wrapper's 200 ms meta timer replaced the inflated file between the leg's write and its signal (the spy saw the handler open a normal-sized file).
- **FIX (product).** PURE `grainStamp` / `grainBaseVerdict` (src/channel-filter.js): every dialog Save sends `base` = the stamp of the lists it drew; setGrain refuses a moved grain `409 grain-changed`, nothing written; the dialog says "The list changed while this dialog was open … nothing was saved" and re-opens on the lists as they stand. The account/rule dialogs draw from `GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/view` (fresh), never the panel copy. channel-window: every render takes a generation, a page is applied only by the newest render, an upward page never runs while the list is being rebuilt, one at a time. (Superseded at 2.369.195: the merge kept lane channel-render's serial queue + this list-ready rule as the ONE mechanism — the integration essay at the top.)
- **FIX (gates).** test-channels-aggregate-ui: the Grant access… leg runs with page 1's `channels-updated` frames HELD from before the seed (the runner's order, constructed on every machine) and asserts the dialog read `…/view`; every save judged by its toast's ARRIVAL (a MutationObserver log) with a deadline only for a save that never answers; ⑧ a grant landing while the dialog is open ⇒ refused + re-opened + kept; ⑨/⑨b the window race constructed (page answers held, broadcasts injected, the repaint's scroll event dispatched) and judged once every page PARSED; CONTROL = ONE rebuilt scratch bundle (the dialog's panel-copy read, the page guard and the ready guard reverted): the stale list drawn (the server's stamp still refuses its save), 27 for 9, 18 for 9; a page throw names its line (V8's own parse for a SyntaxError). test-exit-forensics: the kill tick CONSTRUCTED unlink-then-SIGTERM (the handler cannot run before the kill that triggers it), a trial counts only on the handler's own evidence (`record skipped` / the control copy's `ctl-open … existed=false`), repeated ≤ 8 and counted; a pad trial only when the spy saw the handler open the inflated file; samples after the wrapper AND the child are gone. test-channels-engine ⑬ (the route: 409 + nothing written, the view stamps like the store, a wake is not an edit; CONTROL: the engine without the verdict line writes `[reader, 工作]` exactly), test-channel-filter ⑪ (the stamp's tables).
- **Gates (measured).** Under the recipe: test-channels-aggregate-ui ×10 green (52–63 s each; the attempt-1 shape 0/10 after the dialog fix alone, the picture legs 3/10 until the window fix); test-exit-forensics ×10 green (0 inconclusive kill trials; one codex pad trial repeated once). Idle: ALL PASS (78).
- 不变量 = a whole-list write carries the stamp of the list it read and is refused, never applied, over a list that moved; a dialog draws from the server, never from a broadcast-fed mirror. A view rebuilt by a fetch that broadcasts re-enter has ONE writer: a generation, applied only by the newest. A judge reads an event's ARRIVAL, never a count of a set that also shrinks. A trial that constructs an interleaving counts only on the mechanism's own evidence that the interleaving happened — spelled in production order, a starved CPU samples the benign one (the woken process preempts its waker), and "passed" there is vacuous.

## A CLOSED SPLIT VIEWER CAME BACK AS A WINDOW AFTER TWO DESKTOP SWITCHES (inc-mukeyzpt-lpou, the owner 2026-09-27 22:52Z, client 2.369.193)

- **What happened.** "刚才用ctrl+点击，并排模式打开了个文件查看，切换桌面-回到桌面-关闭这个并排的文件查看器-重新切换桌面-回到桌面-刚才关掉的查看器变成了独立窗口". The bundle's action ring: a Ctrl+click on a path in a chat that sat in a SPLIT group (22:51:36.75) ⇒ the editor was born beside it; desktop away 38.08 → back (the click at 38.88 landed inside switchTo's 1 s gate: QUEUED, drained at 39.11 — the ring's twin `desktop` event 127 ms apart); the editor tab's ✕ in its strip half 40.82; away 41.69 → back 42.74 ⇒ a FREE editor window. Its id `win-mukexu05-37lz` decodes to 22:51:36.869 — the Ctrl+click — so it was the closed window's own record REPLAYED, not a new open. No inbound layout-sync in the ring: a purely local path.
- **Root cause.** The strip's ✕ called `removeFromTabChain` directly; only `closeWindow` ran `desktopManager.purgeClosedWindow` (the 2.151.1 fix for the same symptom) and `stage.onWindowClosed`. The switch-away at 38.08 had cached desktop One's state WITH the editor; after the ✕, the next switch-away's capture lacked it, but switchTo's MERGE-PRESERVE carries a prior record that is openSpec-backed and absent from the DOM ("not yet materialized" — indistinguishable from "closed"), so the editor record rode forward (and was broadcast to the disk: the server layout listed it); the return's step 6 replayed it with its old id. The group's record no longer named it ⇒ a free window. It needs one switch round trip while the window is open (to enter the cache) and one after the close.
- **Fix (by construction).** ONE retirement, `wm._retireWindow(id)`: the stage, every cached desktop record, and the layout manager's held close, run by BOTH terminal deletions (closeWindow's free branch and removeFromTabChain); the tab ✕ is a user close through `requestClose` (the one door, the window may still veto). Two more resurrection routes of the same class closed with it: (a) THE HELD CLOSE — a remote layout-sync that still lists a window this client closed, arriving before a save carrying the close left (inside the 500 ms debounce, or its user-dirty clear dropping that save), re-created it and the close was lost; now `noteClosed` holds a close made while the user is active, the apply never re-creates a held id and reads the record's chain through PURE `withoutMembers` (the local close's own removeTab — same key, the split kept, never a rebuild around the gone pane that flattened it), re-sends the close once (`_resendHeldClose`, §6b's expiry kept), every save that leaves releases it (autosave + a switch's broadcast), 60 s expiry; (b) THE PARKED CLIENT — a second client showing another desktop only CACHED One's newer record and kept its hidden stale copy; its next switch showed it and its next save wrote it back to everyone. Now `dm.cacheRemoteState` closes a hidden window the LAST record on the wire for that desktop listed (`dm._wireIds`: sent, applied, cached or booted from) and the new one drops; a window the wire never listed there (moved/opened on this client, unsent) stays; a stage window is never touched.
- **不变量.** A window's life ends in ONE place and every register that can re-materialize it forgets it in the same tick (the census in test-window-binding-model ⑥: every window-ending `windows.delete` runs `_retireWindow` first — comment-aware, with a control). A local close is a local change: a record older than it never resurrects it, on this client or through another. A cached remote record is diffed against the last record on the wire, never against the DOM. Residual (recorded): a crossing race — a record another client sent before it saw our save, arriving after our save left — can still re-create a closed window (the held close is released at the send, the held-ratio precedent; holding longer would refuse a legitimate re-creation such as another client's preset load); and the parked-client close can drop a window in a crossing race of two saves of one desktop within one RTT, restored by the other client's next save. Gates: test-split-close-resurrect (heavy: the owner's sequence twice with the bundle's timings + the pre-fix ✕ control; the echo + the ledger-neutered control; the parked page + the no-base control), test-chain-layout ⑭ (withoutMembers table + the filter-rebuild control), test-window-binding-model ⑥, test-desktop-apps (the tab ✕ user-close pin).

## A REFUSED BORROW OPENED THE MOUNT'S SECRET FIRST, AND CONNECT IGNORED A SECOND CLIENT (lane client-from-mount verify r1, 2026-09-27, credential class)

- **The door.** 2.369.195 lets a Gmail account borrow the custom Google client of a storage mount (`fromMount`): the mounts module decrypts the secret with `.mounts-key`, the channels engine re-seals it under `.channels-key` in the same call. The lane's law: the plaintext leaves the server only in Google's token exchange, and nothing is decrypted for a body that is refused.
- **Finding 1 (MEDIUM, order).** `clientFromMount` asked `mountClients.of(mountId)` — a decrypt — and compared the vendor AFTER. Payload `{kind:'gmail', fromMount:<a OneDrive mount>}`: one `.mounts-key` decrypt on a body refused `400 mount-client-vendor`. The sharper symptom: a OneDrive mount whose secret cannot be opened (sealed under another key) answered `409 mount-secret-undecryptable` — a refusal about the key state of a mount the account may not borrow at all — instead of `400 mount-client-vendor`. No byte left the server (the plaintext died in the call); the order contradicted the law and the refusal named the wrong fact. FIX: the vendor rides DOWN — `MountManager.oauthClientOf(mountId, {vendor})` refuses `mount-client-vendor` before `_dec`; the engine maps it to 400 and keeps its own comparison as a belt. PIN: test-channels-engine ⑮ counts every `.mounts-key` decrypt across the whole refusal table (zero) and probes the undecryptable other-vendor mount; CONTROL: a mounts copy with the two lines swapped answers `mount-secret-undecryptable` after one decrypt.
- **Finding 2 (LOW, consistency; fixed).** `connectFromFlow` judged "the sign-in's own mount" by `typeof b.fromMount === 'string'` alone, so `{flowId, fromMount:<the sign-in's mount>, credentialKey:'cluster:org1'}` was ACCEPTED with the stale field ignored, while start and re-authorize refuse the same pair `ambiguous-client`. The flow's client won, so no wrong binding — but a rule asked by two verbs and skipped by the third is the shape every stale-hidden-input bug takes. FIX: `namesMount(b)` = the ONE-client rule, asked by `clientChoice` and by Connect's own body before anything is read. PIN: ⑬ (the refusal, and the flow still pending afterwards — Connect naming the mount alone lands); CONTROL: an engine copy with the old line accepts.
- **Words (LOW).** `GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/config` (D3, the owner-only Edit prefill — the same rule as `GET /api/mounts/:id/config`) returns the copied secret in plaintext, as for every custom client. The sentence "the secret never passes through the page" is the sign-in's; the design and CHANGELOG now say so. Not changed.
- **Held (83 probes, the attack script under /tmp/vibespace-lanes/cfm-verify/).** The leakage census over every body / frame / log line / audit line / scratch file (a marked fake secret; the mount's ciphertext only in mounts.json); `vsst_` / `jbt_` bearers 403 on the list and on every verb naming `fromMount`; a path, `../`, an array, a child, a preset, an id-only mount, a Lark type — each the typed refusal with zero decrypts; the R5 identity door on a rebind; the secret rotated between sign-in and paste-back (the exchange uses the start-time copy, taken once); the mount removed before Connect (the copy lands, the mount is not re-read); two concurrent sign-ins on one mount (two independent ciphertexts); the same-client re-authorize replaces the secret in place with one audit line; the eight codes worded in zh / ja / en.

- **不变量.** A refusal is judged on the facts that need no key (vendor, lendability, ambiguity, authority) before any fact that needs one; the module that owns the key does the refusing, with the fact it needs handed down. A rule asked by one verb is asked by every verb that reads the same field. "Never reaches the browser" is scoped to the flow it describes when an owner-only door exists by design — say which.
- **Verify r2 (2026-09-27, a fresh adversary: a decrypt spy per request over a 32-body table on every verb; 102 probes).** The r1 law held for the facts r1 named and failed for three it did not: (a) the OPTIONS — `{kind, fromMount, options:{bogus}}` on start / connect (newAccount) was refused `unknown-option` / `bad-request` after one `.mounts-key` decrypt (`clientChoice` ran before `normalizeOptions`); (b) the registry's ID RULE — a Drive/Gmail mount holding `clientId: 'not-a-google-client-id'` (the storage side never validated an id) was refused `invalid-client` by `sealCustom`, after the decrypt, on start / connect / reauthorize; (c) ANOTHER MOUNT AT CONNECT — `{flowId, fromMount:<a mount whose id is not the sign-in's client>}` was resolved through `clientChoice` (decrypt + seal) and only then compared; an undecryptable google mount there answered `409 mount-secret-undecryptable` (its key state) where the truthful answer, needing no key, is `flow-client-mismatch` — r1's finding 1 in a second coat. A pending record whose loopback flow is gone answered status `{running:false, done:false, error:null}` — the dialog's poll stopped without a word; not reachable by the two clocks (the engine's TTL runs from START, the machine's retirement from END, both `>`), worded anyway ("the sign-in is no longer running — sign in again").

- **不变量 (r4).** A closure handed to a shared machine is judged by the SCOPE it was born in, not by what it names: every closure of one scope holds the whole scope, so "drop the one that captured the secret" is not a rule a machine can enforce — it drops EVERYTHING the caller handed it at the end. An end that is the machine's own act is REPORTED to the consumer once and named by its own cause; a cause shared between "a newer one of yours stands" and "the machine made room" is read as the former by every consumer. A vendor's words are the vendor's, but what WE sent is ours: scrub by exact value before the typed error exists (its stack is a copy of its message). A begin that awaits has exits on both sides of the await — the flow may have ended in between.
