## THE FORK CLASS IS CLOSED BY CENSUS, NOT BY THE NEXT EXAMPLE (lane channel-withdraw verify round 7, 2026-09-27 — the addressing-read census as a gate, the harmless list attacked one site at a time, the ladder once more, the caps consumers, the window keys after adoption, the money re-run, the .195 checklist made current)

Six rounds each closed the fork class one reader at a time (verb → msg/request → rosters/jobs/asks → the ladder's three lookups + emitPeerCard + window keys + group reports). Round 7 asked the terminal question — is the class CLOSED — and answered it by CENSUS instead of by finding a seventh example. **No new defect. Only the census gate and this record.**

- **THE CENSUS AS A GATE (test-msg-cli-groups §2c, 7 asserts).** The vulnerability's grep signature is the ADDRESSING-COMPARISON idiom: a loop over live sessions matching `(x.claudeSessionId || x.backendSessionId) === <cid>` (either field order, `===`/`!==`) — "which live session carries this conversation id". The correct sites the six rounds produced read `addressableId(s) === cid` (no `||`), so the idiom regex never matches them; reverting one to the raw form re-adds an unlisted idiom hit and the gate goes red. A grep over src/ + server.js + data/bin (never src/lib, never the generated agentd bundle) finds EXACTLY SIX raw-idiom sites, every one classified in a checked-in table {file, needle, verdict, why}; an unlisted site fails; a patched copy that adds a raw addressing read on a fresh module fails (the negative control writes `src/server/new-feature.js` into a scratch root and the census flags it). The six: ① `agent-routes.js:1291` `_msgEndpoints` finder — **predicate** (fenced `&& !liveForkPending(t)` on the same line, r4); ② `jobs-wiring.js:38` — **harmless**, a display NAME only, and `ownerCid` is the job's own owner recorded fork-aware at create (r5's `jobsCaller`); ③ `transcript-service.js:83` — **harmless**, serves the transcript a pending fork SHARES with its parent (same bytes, a read); ④ `ws-handler.js:751` rename + ⑤ `ws-handler.js:1296` kill — **harmless**, both fallbacks reached only when the client's OWN webui id is stale (missing from activeSessions); user-explicit, a display rename / a kill, self-healing at adoption, no bill/grant/record; ⑥ `server.js:1154` `recordUsageAttribution` — **harmless for this class**, the REAL inference odometer (the reading-attribution campaign: slot-transitions / reading-repair), NOT the addressing lane — the pool MEMBER is chosen by `poolMemberOfSession` keyed on the found session's webuiId, and pre-adoption requests share the parent's transcript rid. The gate also pins that the ladder's three lookups + `emitPeerCard` read `addressableId`, never the idiom.

- **THE HARMLESS LIST, ATTACKED ONE SITE AT A TIME (each reproduced by code-path, nothing named/billed/granted/recorded on the parent).** The `helper-asks` item key is `sessionStatusKey` (the parent's `claude:<cid>` for a pending fork), but the Allow/Deny answer routes by `answerFrame` → `sessionForAnswer(data.sessionId)` = the FORK's own webui id (the item carries `sessionId: idOf(session)`), never the item's scope key; the item is a permission ACTION, not a text-reply item; and a fork adopts its own id on its first id-bearing stream line, BEFORE any Task/helper can spawn — so a pending fork with a live helper-ask is a nil window (cosmetic jump-scope at most, r5's status-writes class). The **reset-credit** For-you item's scope key is the parent's, but the credit is spent by `consumeResetCreditFor(accountKey, {preferSessionId: session._webuiId})` — as the member the FORK's PROCESS holds (webuiId), on an ACCOUNT identity, never a conversation; the rung fires only at a wall on a live turn-having session (nil for a pending fork). The **unresumable breaker** stamps `session.claudeSessionId` (the parent's for a pending fork) — but it is keyed on TRANSCRIPT EXISTENCE, which the fork and a plain resume of the parent share; blocking the parent's resume when the fork could not find the parent's transcript is correct, and the create-side offers a retry when a transcript IS found. `conversationDisplayName` (pool) resolves the parent's custom name — DISPLAY only. The **normalizer thread default** keys a pending fork's render under the parent's thread id — but codex records are file-tagged (`tagRecordThread`), so the default only affects records that carry no file tag (dedup/render, not money). **Incident capture** freezes the parent's transcript tail alongside the fork's — read-only over-capture BY DESIGN (`_incidentTargets` adds both ids). **Persistence payloads** map the parent's id to the parent's key for layout window-attach — a display association; layout restore attaches or opens read-only, it never spawns a resume. None bills, grants reach, or records persistent authority on the parent.

- **THE LADDER ONCE MORE, and the caps consumers.** With the parent DEAD and its pending fork alive, the parent's notification FALLS TO THE STASH (`addressableId(s) !== cid` at every rung ⇒ no live carrier ⇒ `stashFor(P)`) and stays the parent's; when the fork adopts its own id it never hears the parent's job again (proved: the codex census-control leg — `forkFrames 0`, `charged` never `slot-FORK`, `stashedForParent`). A HELPER of a pending fork has no prompt-context route of its own (it runs inside the parent-session process); the fork's OWN prompt-context group reports (`ownConversationIdOf`, r6) and its msg/job stash drains (`jobsCaller` → null cid, r5) read nothing of the parent's. Every other `caps.peerMessage` / `notificationSteer` consumer is fork-safe: `findRpcPeer` reads `wc.peerMessage` AFTER the `addressableId` guard; the steer/notification-fold lane (`!rpc.wc.notificationSteer`) flows through the same guarded `findRpcPeer`; the attach payload's `queueNotifSteer` and the queue-op / steer verbs are keyed by the session object / `data.sessionId` webui id, never a cid→session loop; the `expectWakes` echo counts members from the addressableId-guarded `liveSessions` roster (a pending fork is never in it, so never a wake target).

- **WINDOW KEYS AFTER ADOPTION (proved, no defect).** A grant stored under a pending fork's `webui:<id>` placeholder SURVIVES adoption because `R.callerKeys(s, id)` ALWAYS appends `webui:<id>` (its second entry whenever the webui id is present) — so after the fork adopts its own conversation id its keys are `[claude:<ownId>, webui:<forkId>]` and still match the placeholder grant; the parent's keys never include `webui:<forkId>`, so it never reaches the fork's window (test-window-reach §10). The DISPLAY names the fork (the row's captured name), never the parent. Two pending forks carrying one id + a client-spelled raw `<backend>:<cid>` key ⇒ `bad_principal` by name; that sentence stays the engine's own English (the client's `failText` deliberately does NOT map the GENERIC `bad_principal` code — mapping it to one sentence would LIE for its other uses, per r6's own "reusing a code for a different fact lies" invariant), and the CURRENT picker sends the live webui id (`r.id || r.key`) so it never reaches that legacy branch.

- **MONEY (item 5, every r3–r6 attack re-run on f14a4299 + the committed gates).** The committed money gates are green: test-channel-outbox 270, test-spend-paths 310, test-channels-engine 279, test-msg-cli-groups 136, test-window-reach 110, test-browser-takeover 292. The ad-hoc round scripts' handful of reds are all stale-SCRIPT artifacts, not regressions: `attack.mjs` A6c expected `+1` receipt where the withdraw lane now emits `+2` (a withdrawal is a terminal state with its own receipt — created exactly ONE draft, money-safe); `attack5-words` flags the deliberately-kept word "agent" in zh and a FICTIONAL `no-inbox` refusal code the ladder never emits (its real codes — `no-wake`/`spend`/`hour-cap`/`wrapper-no-steer`/`row-unwritten` — all render worded); `attack3-client` is a DOM Esc leg; `attack5-prune` is a heap-OOM in the throwaway. No double-bill, no cap breach, fail-closed intact.

- **THE .195 MERGE CHECKLIST — APPLIED (integration 2.369.195, 2026-09-28).** The stash region's ①–⑨ are now the merged `src/server/conversation-deliver.js`, stated ONCE as rules in the integration essay at the top of this file ("THE STASH TWO LANES BUILT ON"). ⑩ the ladder's three cid→session lookups read `addressableId(s)` beside channel-jump's stash region (disjoint; `create({…})` takes both the top-of-file `addressableId` require and `onStashChange`; `emitPeerCard` in server.js reads `addressableId`); ⑪ `jobsCaller` is withdraw's fork-aware body — it composes with channel-jump's `drainStashUnderCap(deliver, caller2.conversationId, …)`, which returns '' on a null cid, so a pending fork drains nothing of its parent's; ⑫ the group-reports block keeps channel-jump's budget order AND withdraw's `myCid = ownConversationIdOf(s).cid`; ⑬ the create route's no-cid words are withdraw's r6 sentence ("wait a moment and repeat the command …"), `vibespace-msg` prints its `bad-member` remedy, window-request answers `fork_pending`. The agent-routes hook routes keep both lanes (withdraw's `msgCaller` / `ownConversationIdOf` / `addressableId` guards, channel-jump's `drainStashUnderCap` / `drainNotifsUnderCap`); the reply / compose / request verbs keep withdraw's guard + `--replaces` AND channel-jump's `touchChannel` witness (a withdraw is exempt from the §63 census by name — it reads and drafts nothing). Re-pinned on the merged tree: test-msg-cli-groups, test-window-reach, test-browser-takeover, test-channel-outbox (d) + merge-a…e, test-stash-strip ②c/②e/②f, test-spend-paths.

- **不变量 (r7).** The fork class is closed by a CENSUS that a new raw addressing read fails, not by a growing list of examples. A live session is addressed by its OWN conversation id or not at all — the ONE idiom `(x.claudeSessionId || x.backendSessionId) === cid` may appear only where the fork predicate fences it or where the read names/bills/grants/records NOTHING on the parent, and both are written down. A key a pending fork answered to under its placeholder it answers to for life because `callerKeys` always carries the webui key. A refusal's client words are the code's own — a GENERIC code (`bad_principal`) is never mapped to one sentence.

## THE LADDER STILL FOUND A SESSION BY THE RAW ID; A WINDOW SHARED WITH A PENDING FORK WENT TO ITS PARENT; A FORK'S PROMPT ATE THE PARENT'S GROUP REPORTS (lane channel-withdraw verify round 6, 2026-09-27 — the predicate's last three readers, the adoption hand-off, the frozen memo, the durability verdict, the money re-run, the words)

- **The delivery ladder's own cid → session lookups (MEDIUM, money + authority; reproduced over the REAL ladder + REAL spend guard with a fake pty and the sidecar written the way codex-chat-wrapper writes it at boot).** r5 put `addressableId` behind every ROSTER and every CALLER resolver; `conversation-deliver.js` still answered "which live local session carries this conversation" by the raw `backendSessionId || claudeSessionId` at THREE sites — rung 0 (the experimental channel socket), rung 1.5 (`findRpcPeer`, a codex wrapper's stdin) and `localSessionFor` (the credential slot a turn is CHARGED to + the machine-turn stamp). A codex fork's wrapper advertises `caps.peerMessage` in its sidecar at boot, BEFORE `thread/fork` answers, so for those seconds the fork is a live rpc peer carrying its PARENT's thread id: with the parent stopped (the common fork — "fork this stopped conversation"), a Background Work notification owned by the parent was written into the FORK's wrapper (`{"type":"peer-message",…}` on its stdin — a billed turn on the fork, `spent()` charged to the fork's slot; after adoption the fork never hears that job again, so the one frame was a message it was never meant to get); with the parent live but the fork FIRST in `activeSessions` (a boot restore lists sockets, not creation order), rung 1 delivered to the parent's CLI while the authorizer was asked with the FORK's session — the parent's turn charged to the fork's credential slot, the machine-turn stamp on the fork (its next prompt read as "a turn nobody typed" and held the owner's group reports). server.js's `emitPeerCard` had the same lookup (the card drawn in the fork's window). FIX = the three lookups + the card site read `addressableId(s) === cid`: a pending fork is never the wrapper a frame is written into, never the slot a turn is charged to. Controls (test-msg-cli-groups r6): the raw-lookup copy of the ladder writes the parent's frame into the fork's wrapper (`lane rpc-queue`, charged `slot-FORK`) and, fork-first, charges the parent's inbox post to the fork's slot; server.js's card line pinned by name. The browser handback's `conversationIdOf(s)` (r5 had judged it unreachable) reads the same predicate now — a pending fork's handback rides its own next message as the notice, never a billed `browser-handback` turn on the parent (test-browser-takeover ③ + its raw-cid control).
- **"Share with agent…" on a pending fork granted the PARENT, and the fork lost the grant at adoption (MEDIUM, authority; reproduced over the REAL window-targets engine).** The engine's `resolvePrincipal` / `ctxOf` / `liveReached` / the opener's row all spelled a live session's key through PURE `R.sessionKeyOf` = `<backend>:<conversation id>`, and the picker (src/lib/window-share.js) sent that key. A pending fork's conversation id is its parent's, so the row was stored under `claude:<parent>`: the PARENT answered to it (`callerKeys`) — it listed the window, could attach and act on the user's desktop app, and reached the app the fork itself OPENED — and the moment the fork adopted its own id its keys no longer included the parent's: the agent the user picked reached nothing, the one he did not pick kept it for good (rows are persisted; nothing re-keys them). FIX (ORCH, the engine — window-reach.js is PURE and bundled, it cannot ask claude-lock-capture) = `keyOf(s, id)` / `keysOf(s, id)`: a session with an addressable id keys as before, a pending fork keys as its `webui:<id>` placeholder (the same rule as its For-you item and its status record — a key it answers to for life); the picker sends the LIVE webui id and the engine spells the key; a KEY an older picker spelled that no addressable session answers to while exactly one pending fork carries it resolves to that fork's placeholder, two such forks are refused `bad_principal` by name (never a guess). Controls (test-window-reach §10): the raw-key engine copy stores the parent's key, the parent lists and attaches, the fork loses the window and its own opened app at adoption; the picker's spelling pinned.
- **A pending fork's prompt rendered the PARENT's next-turn group reports and moved the parent's markers (MEDIUM, a message loss; reproduced over the REAL groups engine + REAL routes).** r5 fixed the msg-stash and job drains of `prompt-context` through `jobsCaller` (null while borrowed); the GROUP REPORTS block in the same route still read `myCid = s.claudeSessionId || s.backendSessionId`: a group message posted to the parent (no wake, "reads it on its next turn, free") was rendered into the FORK's next user prompt and `commitReports(parent, marks)` moved the parent's `reportedUpTo` — the parent's own next prompt carried nothing; the messages were never seen where they were addressed (still in the log, but "your next turn" had happened on another session). FIX = `myCid = ownConversationIdOf(s).cid`. Control: the raw-id copy renders the report into the fork's prompt and leaves the parent's empty.
- **`no_conversation` was the wrong advice for a fork (LOW, words).** r5's window-request refusal for a pending fork reused the `no_conversation` code, and the Share dialog words that code as "That agent has no conversation yet — say something to it first" — a fork has the parent's whole conversation; saying something changes nothing (the remedy is a wait). Its OWN code now, `fork_pending` (window-reach's closed REFUSALS, both routes' status maps: 409), worded "That agent is a fork that has not announced its own conversation yet — try again in a moment", zh + ja. The `FORK_PENDING` sentence every agent verb answers with said "try again after its first turn" — a chat fork adopts BEFORE its first turn and a terminal fork off the lock capture (2 s, then 1 s × 14), so the turn was never the event; it says "wait a moment and repeat the command (a fork announces its own id within seconds of starting)" and `vibespace-msg` prints a remedy line for `bad-member` (it had none). The manual's line said the same wrong thing.
- **REFUTED (reproduced, no defect).** THE ADOPTION HAND-OFF: an ask a pending fork files (`webui:<id>`) is found by the owner's reply after adoption (`sessionForItem` matches `webui:<id>`), re-keyed to the fork's own key at its next ask and still listed/shown; the parent's own item is neither listed nor resolvable by its pending fork; a message to the fork BY NAME while pending is `unreachable` (404, the uniform refusal — no oracle) and a retry after adoption mints the pair under the fork's OWN id; a window grant under `webui:<id>` is the fork's for life. THE FROZEN MEMO: every engine reader of `outbox.snapshot()` either reads, spreads (`proposalView`'s `{...p}`) or builds a NEW array (`Object.values(...).sort`) — every mutation of a proposal sits inside `update(fn)` on the live `ob`; `nextId()` runs inside the door; `live()` is read-only (`viewCtx`); the PURE channel-policy functions never assign into their argument; the memo is cleared after `fn(ob)` and on a rejected update, and the boot loader / the prune / `sweepReplaces` all write through `update`. THE DURABILITY VERDICT: a ref'd entry is never "unwritten" (r4's take-back — the receipt fate says `stash-failed`, honest); the 30 s retry writes whatever the queue holds (an empty queue too, r5); an entry that WAS written, drained and whose drain write failed is re-delivered at boot — a duplicate, never a loss; the `unwritten` event reaches the channels engine's listener as a no-op (it keys on `drained`/`stashed`/`evicted`); channel-jump's claim door (the .195 checklist's ⑧, applied: a claim write that fails leaves the `ho` stamp in memory — a crash re-delivers — and is now logged by name). MONEY (every r3–r6 attack re-run on the fixed tree): 20 concurrent wake-now under cap 2 ⇒ 2; the double press; approve ‖ withdraw; the authorizer throw fails closed; row-unwritten; the wake charged to the member held — no regression.
- **Measured, judged LOW (the design's, noted for the owner).** The `channel-outbox-updated` broadcast at the store's bound with 16 KB texts is 6.46 MB per change (the 200-row view, each row `text` + `originalText`): the server's stringify 5.8 ms once, a client's parse 2.2 ms each — CPU is nothing; the WIRE is the cost: an agent's replace loop at 5 changes/s is 32 MB/s per client (97 MB/s with three), a phone over a tunnel falls seconds behind per second; at a realistic 2 KB draft it is ~0.8 MB per change. A delta broadcast (`changed` ids + the changed rows, the windows already re-fetch) is a design change across the panel and two windows, not a verify fix. The `charged: [null]` the ladder answers when NOBODY addressable carries the conversation is the `__unattributed__` bucket by design.
- **不变量.** A live session is addressed by its OWN conversation id or not at all — ONE predicate (`addressableId`) behind every roster, every caller resolver, every cid → session lookup the ladder makes, every key a grant is stored under, and every drain a prompt performs; a borrowed id is neither a sender, a target, an owner, a claim, a slot nor a key. A refusal's client words are the code's own — reusing a code for a different fact lies where the user reads it.

- **The stash cap (reproduced with the REAL ladder, then pinned).** `conversation-deliver.js` holds ≤ 30 entries per conversation and dropped the oldest with `splice` — no event. A receipt stored for the drafter's next message (the default delivery) fell off after 30 later entries (a Task-Group sibling's `vibespace-msg send`s at the pacer's 1/30 s, channel notifications): it was never read, `receiptFateOf` kept "Waiting for <agent>'s next message" (no `drained` ever came), and round 1's boot reconcile — which reads a MISSING entry as drained — printed "Handed to <agent> with an earlier message" over a receipt nobody saw. Worse: a peer could make a user's decision vanish from the drafter's queue and have the card say it arrived. FIX = the ladder emits `('evicted', cid, entries, {held})` for entries with a `ref`; the engine stamps `receiptEvictedAt` + `receiptEvictedHeld` (a later `stashed` clears it, a `drained` too), the PURE fate is `evicted` ("Not delivered — <agent>'s queue was full; the receipt is kept here"), the reconcile skips a recorded eviction. The cap's policy is unchanged (it protects the agent's context); the receipt stays on the proposal. Control: a ladder copy whose cap drops silently reads "waiting" live and "handed" at boot.
- **A replace cut in half.** `replaceProposal` stamps `replaces` on the new draft in one write and withdraws the old one in the next; a process dying between them left both `awaiting-approval` — two approvable copies of one message, each a vendor send. FIX = `sweepReplaces()` at `start()`: every draft whose `replaces` names a proposal its OWN drafter may still withdraw (PURE `withdrawVerdict`) is finished through `withdrawNow` on the proposal's chain (`replacedBy`, the pointer retracted, the receipt recorded, nothing handed back). Control: a copy without the call keeps both awaiting.
- **The identity form.** `channelPrincipal` answers `webui:<id>` for a session with no conversation id yet (a chat before its init record, a terminal before discovery links it — longer on a paired machine). A draft made then recorded that as `draftedBy.id`: the receipt was delivered to — and stashed under — `webui:<id>`, a key the hook route never drains (it drains by the conversation id); `liveSessions()` never lists it, so the card called the live session "gone" (round 1's LOW 3 in its real shape); and the same session, once it had its id, was told `not-yours` for its own draft. FIX = `reply` / `compose` / `withdraw` refuse 409 `bad-member` with `msg send`'s sentence before anything is created (the ONE constant `NO_CID_YET`). Control: a copy without the three guards creates a `webui:` drafter.
- **Two Check-outcome presses.** `reconcile` was not on the proposal's chain: two concurrent presses on one lost send both asked the adapter (a Lark reconcile re-issues its uuid). FIX = exported as `onProposal(id, () => reconcile(id, o))`; the second finds `sent` and is `bad-state`. Control: the bare export asks twice.
- **Round 1's LOWs, fixed:** (6) a browser on the agent withdraw route (a cookie / `sec-fetch-site`, no Bearer) is 403 `not-yours` "only the agent that proposed it can withdraw a proposal — reject it from the card instead" (a bare call stays 401); (5) `keyedCard`'s in-use branch patches the primary Approve's label + `data-deliver` when the remembered choice moved on another card (the click already followed the new choice; only the words lagged); (4) above; (3) above (its cause was the `webui:` identity, not remote liveness — `liveSessions()` lists every session in `activeSessions` with a conversation id, paired machines included). A real drain after a boot guess now records its time (`receiptDrainedHow: 'drained'`).
- **Counted, no defect:** every outbox write runs the PURE table inside the store's serialized callback; approve / reject / withdraw / replace / reconcile queue per proposal (the sweep's `unless` sees the hold); the pairs not on the chain are disjoint by state — a sweep during a vendor-parked approve 25 h after the draft expires nothing (sent, one receipt), two overlapping sweeps expire each draft once with one receipt each; the legacy text match needs the engine's own `source`, so a peer's "proposal <id>:" keeps nothing waiting; the failed-send wake's ledger row is `{at, reason:'channel-receipt'}` on the identity the ladder authorized (no retry UI exists for a `failed` proposal; a re-propose is a new decision); the receipt's pace grant (auth off) is taken only after the awaiting read and the hold keeps the state until the transition, so it cannot leak.
- **不变量.** A queue that can drop what it holds says so to the producer that put it there — a fate the product prints is a state it can observe leave by EVERY exit, eviction included. A two-write act is finished at boot from the first write's evidence, by the rule the act itself used. An identity a route mints as a placeholder never becomes a record's owner. A verb a person can press twice runs on the record's chain.

## THE 24 H SWEEP EXPIRED A DRAFT THE AGENT WAS REPLACING; A RECEIPT THE AGENT HAD READ SAID "WAITING" FOR GOOD (lane channel-withdraw verify, 2026-09-27)

- **The sweep window (reproduced, then pinned).** `expireSweep` filtered its due list by `proposalHolds.has(id)` and then transitioned each proposal in turn, awaiting the earlier ones' receipts (a ladder call) in between. A `replaceProposal` of a LATER due proposal took its hold (synchronously, before its first await), read the snapshot — still `awaiting-approval` — passed `withdrawVerdict`, and ran `make()`; the sweep's write on that id then landed BETWEEN the replace's check and its `withdrawNow`: the old draft went `expired` (the table allows `ttl` from awaiting), the agent received an "EXPIRED unapproved (24 h)" receipt for a draft it had just replaced, and the replace answered `replaced: null, replaceCode: not-withdrawable` beside a new draft that was created. Constructed with a 40 ms ladder delay on the earlier proposal's receipt and an 80 ms `make()`. FIX = `transition(id, to, by, patch, {unless})`: the guard runs INSIDE `store.outbox.update`'s callback (the serialization point of the state); the sweep passes `unless: () => proposalHolds.has(p.id)`. The hold is visible at apply time whenever the replace was called before the write; a replace called after it reads the expiry and refuses before `make()`. Control: a copy with the guard line removed reproduces `expired` + two receipts.
- **The legacy fate (the owner's three receipts).** The fate line reads `receiptDelivery.stashed && !receiptDrainedAt` as "Waiting for <agent>'s next message"; the `drained` event that flips it fires only for a stash entry carrying `ref` — every receipt stored before this lane (the three of 2026-09-27: p-muket1b7-1, p-muket4nb-2, p-mukevae4-3, drained at 22:50:23Z and 22:55:47Z) has none, so after the update their cards would have said "Waiting" for good about receipts the agent read an hour earlier. FIX = `reconcileReceiptFates()` at `start()`: each stored-and-not-drained receipt is looked for in its drafter's queue through the ladder's read-only `stashPeek(cid)` — by `ref`, or (a legacy entry) by the `proposal <id>:` line its text carries; a missing one is stamped `receiptDrainedAt` + `receiptDrainedHow: 'reconciled'`, the PURE fate is `handed` with `at: null` and the words are "Handed to <agent> with an earlier message". Control: a copy whose reconcile returns nothing keeps "waiting".
- **Forensics correction.** The lane's paragraph said the three receipts "reached it together 21 s after the last one"; the audit log and the drafter's transcript say two batches — the rejection's at 22:50:23Z (21 s after its receipt), the two approvals' at 22:55:47Z (20 s after the last) — the 15:55:48 the lane quoted is the stash file's mtime of the second drain.
- **Counted, no defect (pinned):** a double click / two tabs / a retry / reject‖approve / edits / a replace chain bill ONE turn per proposal (the second decision is `bad-state` naming the state); the ceiling's refusal is named on the card and the receipt stays stored; a drafter not live ⇒ next-turn `gone`, never another session's cid; a bogus `deliver` is 400 by name, a missing one next-turn, a wake-now without the `expectWakes` echo 409 with nothing billed; a withdraw landing while the vendor call is parked is refused `not-withdrawable` after the send (`sent` + receipt, never "withdrawn"); hostile `--replaces` ids create nothing; a refused replacement leaves the old draft byte-identical; two concurrent replaces make ONE draft. A wake-now approve whose send the vendor refused still wakes once with the FAILED receipt — by design (the decider asked to hear now).
- **不变量.** A guard that fences a WRITE is asked inside the write's serialized section, never only before it (the fifth strike of check-then-write across an await in this campaign). A "waiting" the product prints is a state it can still observe leave — a record that can never receive its exit event is reconciled against the queue it claims to be in. A forensic sentence names its source (audit / transcript), never a file's mtime.


## A RESTART MID-HAND-OVER DELIVERED TWICE; A CODEX `ok:false` MADE FIVE NOTICES ONE (channel-jump verify r2, 2026-09-27)

- **The restart (MEDIUM, reproduced on the real ladder + the real jobs store).** Round 1's claim was an in-memory Set. `shutdown()` flushed and called `process.exit` while the hand-over awaited the ladder's post: the frame was in the CLI's inbox, the entries were still in `data/msg-stash.json` / `job-notifications.json` (unclaimed on disk), and the next boot's prompt-context drain carried them again. A second window sat AFTER a delivered hand-over: `drainStash` persisted on a 500 ms debounce and `drainNotifs` on the engine's 2 s save tick, so a process killed inside it re-delivered too — the injection route's own full drain had the same window. FIX = (a) every hand-over mints an ID (`ho-<ts36>-<seq>`) and its frame says `(hand-over <id>)`; (b) THE CLAIM IS THE ENTRY'S OWN `ho:<id>` STAMP, written to both stores synchronously before the post (`claimStash(cid, entries, id)` → `writeStashNow`, `claimNotifs` → `_saveNotifs`); a full drain keeps a stamped entry; (c) EVERY drain (by identity and full) and every restore persists synchronously; (d) `shutdown()` WAITS for a hand-over in flight (`stashView.settle(5000)` — bounded by the ladder's own timeouts: `postToPeer` 5 s, the daemon's `peer-post` 15 s behind a 6 s bounded connect) and only then flushes and exits — a SIGTERM restart is exactly-once by construction; (e) a stamp a DEAD process left (SIGKILL / OOM inside the socket round-trip — whether the CLI took the frame is unknowable) is RELEASED by both loaders at boot, named in the log with its id (`releasedAtBoot`): a repeat is visible and traceable, a loss would be silent.
- **The collapse (MEDIUM, reproduced through the real codex-events consumer).** The codex wrapper answers `peer_message_result {ok:false, text}` for a frame it could not run (a `turn/start` error, a Stop that dropped the queued item, a queue removal), echoing the frame's WHOLE text; the consumer re-stashed that text as ONE entry. After a hand-over of five the strip said "1 VibeSpace notice", every kind and label was gone, and the job results had left `pendingNotifs` for good (they were part of an agent-source blob). FIX = the hand-over remembers what it delivered (`delivered`: id → the drained entries of both stores, 10 min, ≤ 50); the two stdout consumers ask `deliverRef.restoreFrame(cid, text)` BEFORE the re-stash (property access on the lazy ref); the ladder asks its registered restorers (server.js registers `stashView.restoreHandedOver`), which reads the id off the text and puts the ORIGINAL entries back — `deliver.restoreStash` / `jm.restoreNotifs`, each entry as itself, in ts order, on disk at once. A frame echoed twice restores once (the record is marked, the second echo is handled — never a blob of the copy); a frame naming no hand-over, another conversation's, or one past its memory is re-stashed as itself, as before.
- **The second client (LOW, fixed).** A second click answered `in_flight` but the second window's button was live the whole time. The fact now carries `inFlight` (re-published when a hand-over starts and when it settles); the strip's button reads "Handing over…" and is disabled; the 409 names the hand-over (`id`, `since`).
- **The overflow (LOW, fixed — round 1's LOW 3).** A stash over the hand-over's 12 KiB budget is delivered in part (`renderMsgStash` → `rest`). The fact carries `held` (the same render, dry), the strip's cost line says "N more are held for the next hand-over", the result carries `held`, the toast names the rest.
- **No lane, no button (LOW, fixed).** A harness whose notification lane is `stash` (opencode — its wrapper drains at prompt-context) could only answer `unreachable`; the fact carries `reachable` and the strip says "they ride your next message" where the button would be.
- **The witness's cost (MEDIUM by rate, measured).** `recordMany` broadcast once per agent call: a read loop of 200 reads in 2 s was 200 `channel-touch` broadcasts to every client for ONE ring entry (the ring merge already folded them). FIX = a NEW touch is said at once; a MERGED one joins the session's next coalesced broadcast (`BROADCAST_MS` 250) — 200 reads = 2 broadcasts; the meta write was already one per 1.5 s debounce (pinned).
- **LOWs left.** ① `billed` is a prediction off the harness's lane: a codex session mid-turn whose wrapper predates steering shows no cost and the click answers `held_for_next_turn`; a remote codex session shows "starts a turn" and answers `unreachable` (the daemon's registry is claude's). Neither writes a ledger row. ② A process KILLED inside the socket round-trip leaves stamped entries the boot releases — one repeat is possible if the frame had landed; the log names the id. ③ A frame that comes back after the 10-minute memory is re-stashed as one notice (the ladder's own settle window is 120 s).
- **不变量.** A claim lives where the entries live (on disk, under an id) — never beside them in memory. A drain IS a delivery: it is on disk before anything else happens. A process that starts a delivery finishes or names it before it exits. What comes back undelivered comes back as what it was. A fact that a second client acts on carries the state a first client's act put it in. A count never hides what an act will leave behind. Gate: test-stash-strip ②c (every path pair with a parked post; the table `billed` × harness × turn × wrapper against the ledger) + ⑤ (six r2 controls: the shutdown that does not wait, both debounced drains, the restorer removed, `held` dropped, `inFlight` dropped) + ⑥ pins; test-channel-touch ② (200 reads) + ④ (the coalescing removed ⇒ 200).

It can, and on the most ordinary day: every seen-marker (`_groupSeenAt`, `_groupSnap`, `_toolsIntroSeen`, `_mgrIntroSeen`, `_preambleSeen`, `_jobsEventsSeenTs`) is in memory only (session-schema: persisted null — "restart = full redelivery"), so the first prompt after EVERY server restart re-delivers the FULL context of every group: 8.6 KB for two groups with a long owned backlog, 9.5 KB for three (the codex first prompt is the same shape). Each producer is pushed where it always rode — the payload's ORDER is unchanged (byte-identical to r5's module on the full / diff / quiet / reminder shapes). The head alone over the cap (three groups) stays the accepted design (the group markers advance, the trim names `show --full`); what changed is that nothing behind it is consumed until it fits.

## A FENCE OPENER WITH NO CLOSER WALKED THE WHOLE TEXT — PER OPENER (channel-render verify round 4, 2026-09-27)

- **What happened (measured, in-process, the regex census of every pattern over peer bytes).** `linesToBlocks`' code fence: an opener line (`^\s*```\s*(info)?\s*$`) walks forward for a closer (`^\s*```\s*$`); none found ⇒ the line falls through to a paragraph line — and the NEXT opener walks to the end again. An info string is an opener the closer rule never matches, so 13 107 lines of "```x" (64 KiB) cost **897 ms** in the generic rung and **1 090 ms** in the mail rung (4 000 lines: 104 ms; quadratic) — at ingest (a Lark text / a Gmail body), at every page read and every broadcast for a record stored before this layer (the engine's read-time `blocksOf`), and in every client (`blocksOfRecord`'s fallback). Every other pattern in channel-blocks.js, channel-record.js (`FRAME_TAG_RE` after round 3) and channel-words.js measured ≤ 18 ms at its 64 KiB bound on its worst shape (the table: link openers, `<at`, ordinals, e-mail, URL + 60 000 ")", `www.` runs, mailto, autolinks, "@" × 64 K with 256 names of 200 characters sharing a 199-character prefix (2 ms; the prefix shape 17 ms — the alternation's cost is bounded by text × names because the text must CONTAIN what each alternative walks), quotes, blank lines, signature delimiters, "On … wrote" runs, header blocks, the banner, the rules, the mobile signature, cleanSubject, `linkText`'s site label at 64 KiB, the frame regex).

The tree is byte-identical to the walk-per-opener rung's — asserted on six fence shapes in the gate and on 3 000 seeded random line mixes in the round's probe.
- **Gates.** test-channel-blocks ⑬: three linearity rows (the generic rung, the mail rung, the info-string-with-spaces opener) + control (r) (the memo removed: ≥ 4× slower on 4 000 lines, the same tree; the six shapes identical).
- **不变量.** A scan that can fail and be retried from the next line is quadratic unless the failure is REMEMBERED; "the first walk proves the rest" is the memo. A regex census over peer bytes is a TABLE — pattern, bound, worst shape, ms — re-measured whenever a rung gains a pattern.

- **What happened (reproduced in chrome with TRUSTED CDP input on the lane as delivered).** ① Round 3's `enterTarget` disarms the first-row fallback when a roster patch moved another row to the top — correct — but the refusal was invisible: the person saw the new first row, pressed Enter, nothing; pressed Enter again, nothing; only typing re-armed. `active-sessions` is broadcast on every turn-state change (a 1 s digest over every live session — every second on a busy fleet), so a Grant access… picker's Enter went dead often and said nothing (the no-silent-failures law). ② `drawList` ended in `list.replaceChildren(...out)` — every row detached and re-attached on every patch, even one that changed NOTHING — and Chrome drops a click whose mousedown node was detached before the mouseup: a trusted click on a row with a no-change broadcast between the press and the release was lost 2/2 (the plain click 1/1). The chips (`drawChips` rebuilt them all) had the same hole for a ✕.
- **What held.** ↓ ↓ then the highlighted row removed by a patch: Enter picks nothing (never a shifted neighbour); a row replaced by a NEW session of the same name (new id): Enter picks nothing (the key changed); a mouse press on a row the patch replaced under the pointer: nothing picked (the click is dropped, never the neighbour); Space types into the box, Tab leaves it.

Also (r3's LOW): the Grant access… save freezes the picker and every row control (`setBusy`) until the write answers — the list in flight is the list saved.
- **Gates.** test-principal-picker ① (pins: the refused-Enter highlight, `reconcile(list, out)` / `reconcile(chips, out)`, never `.replaceChildren(`); test-channel-window-render ⑫c (trusted: the refused Enter highlights pager-02 by aria-activedescendant; the vanished highlight's Enter highlights the row now first and the next Enter takes it by key; a trusted click with a no-change `active-sessions` broadcast between press and release still picks) and ⑫b (five no-change broadcasts move NO node — childList records 0).
- **不变量.** A refusal the person cannot see is a silent failure; the picker's answer to a disarmed Enter is a visible highlight, never nothing. A keyed patch that keeps the nodes must also keep them ATTACHED — `replaceChildren` with the same nodes is a detach, and a detach drops the click in flight.

It ran at INGEST (the mail rung + `makeRecord`: 5.9 s per message), at every READ of the page holding it (`withBlocks` judges every stored tree per page: 1.8 s per record, ~90 s for a page of 50, per broadcast naming the conversation — every open window re-reads its page) and again in every client (`renderBlocks` → `validateBlocks`). Also: a label-less link SHOWS its href, so the href is the text it COUNTS in `validateBlocks` (4 000 empty-label links × 2 048-char hrefs passed the 64 KiB text bound as 0 characters — a 16 MB tree per record; only a hand-written log could hold one).

- **不变量.** Two adjacent quantifiers that can eat the same character class are quadratic on a run of it; a regex the judge runs on every stored string at every read is in the linearity table with its worst run.

## THE RENDER RUNGS WERE QUADRATIC AND WALKED THE RAW BODY (channel-render verify round, 2026-09-27)

- **What happened (measured, in-process on this box).** `textToBlocks('b'.repeat(64 KiB))` = 2 280 ms; `textToBlocks('https://x.example/' + ')'.repeat(60 000))` = 11 394 ms; `textToBlocks('-- \n'.repeat(16 K))` = 1 074 ms. Gmail's `toRecord` runs `emailToBlocks(text)` over the RAW plain-text body (before `makeRecord`'s 64 KiB `MAX_TEXT` cut), Lark's over the raw `c.text` — a 1 MiB single-line mail (any stranger can send one to a linked mailbox) would have held the SERVER's event loop for minutes at ingest, and the same rung ran in every client's `blocksOfRecord` fallback at render. A `system` template of `{a}` × 100 000 over a 64 KiB part threw `RangeError: Invalid string length` out of `larkSystemSentence` → `toRecord` → `history()` (which maps every item with no per-item catch) — one poison item and the account's pass fails until the item ages out.
- **Root cause.** Three unbounded quantifiers on peer text: the e-mail alternative `[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@…` (the engine eats the whole word and backtracks at EVERY position — O(n²) for any long token without an `@`), `trimUrl`'s per-trimmed-character `countCh` (O(n²) on a bracket-heavy tail), the `-- ` test's `nonBlankCount(rest)` per delimiter line (O(n²) over repeated delimiters); no input bound at the rung's entry; a rung that could throw.
- **Fix.** Every part of the e-mail pattern is RFC-bounded (`{1,64}@{1,63}(\.{1,63}){0,8}\.{2,24}`); the bracket census is taken ONCE and decremented; `nonBlankUpTo(lines, from, cap)` stops at the signature bound; `bounded(text)` at every rung's entry (`textToBlocks` / `emailToBlocks` / `larkToBlocks` / `larkStoredBlocks`); `guarded(text, fn)` — a rung never throws, it answers `plainOf(text)`; the Lark system template is bounded to 2 000 characters and each filled part to 200, an emotion's type to 40. Measured after: 3–73 ms for all fifteen inputs, the 1 MiB mail 13 ms.
- **Gates.** test-channel-blocks ⑬: the LINEARITY TABLE (fifteen inputs, each < 800 ms = ~10× the slowest measured), the 1 MiB body → a valid tree of ≤ 64 KiB, the throwing item → the plain paragraph (both rungs), the chip / emotion / template bounds; controls (j) the unbounded e-mail alternative is ≥ 4× slower on a 16 KiB word, (l) the per-character trim ≥ 4× on a URL + 8 000 `)`, (m) the unguarded rung throws out, (n) the input bound. test-channel-window-render ⑨ (a 100 KB body, a 3 000-char URL in chrome).
- **不变量.** A parser over peer-controlled text is LINEAR BY CONSTRUCTION — every quantifier that can backtrack is bounded by the grammar it parses (an e-mail local part is 64, a label 63), a census is taken once, a per-line test stops at its own bound — it bounds its input BEFORE it walks, and it never throws out of an ingest path. "Never block the event loop" covers regexes over vendor bodies, not only fs and exec.

## A MAILTO LINK CARRIED A COMPOSE FORM (channel-render verify round, 2026-09-27)

- **What happened.** `safeHref('mailto:you@x.example?bcc=evil%40y.example&subject=hi')` answered the string: the mailto rule was `^mailto:[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+$` — "exactly one @" — and `%40` is not an `@` until the mail client percent-decodes the RFC 6068 hfields. A link the user clicks in a channel message opened a compose window with a hidden recipient (and `?body=` / `?subject=` prefilled by the sender).
- **Fix.** `MAILTO_RE` in channel-record.js: `mailto:<local>@<dotted host>` in the e-mail rung's own alphabet — no `?`, no `#`, no percent-escape, no path. Anything else stays words (the linkify's bare `mailto:` alternative goes through the same `safeHref`).
- **Gates.** test-channel-blocks ②: eight refused forms, a plain address accepted, the linkify row "mailto with hfields is WORDS"; control (i) the old one-@ regex accepts the percent-encoded bcc. test-channel-window-render ⑨: no href with `bcc` in the hostile window.
- **不变量.** A link's accepted grammar is spelled from what the CONSUMER decodes (a mail client decodes hfields; a browser decodes `\t` out of `java\tscript:`), never from the raw string's shape.

- **What happened.** `withBlocks` served a record that already carried `blocks` untouched (`if (!r || r.blocks) return r`) — only a record WITHOUT a tree went through the adapter's rung and `validateBlocks`. ## A RE-AUTHORIZATION DID NOT REACH THE THREADS ALREADY JUDGED (inc-muk9jj0j-rel3, 2026-09-27, lane channel-render)

- **What happened.** The owner re-authorized both Gmail accounts (server log 20:19:29Z / 20:20:02Z; `data/channels/adapters.json` then held `gmail.readonly` + `gmail.compose` for both), opened a thread at 20:20:11Z and it STILL said read-only — "sending needs the send permission …" ("已经重新授权过 但还是有个邮件提示没有发送权限"). The index held that thread's `convCaps: {read:'yes', sendAs:[], why:'send-scope-not-granted', at: 18:05:43Z}` — judged BEFORE the consent and never recomputed — while a thread the forced pass after the consent happened to touch carried `{sendAs:['user'], at: 20:20:10Z}`.
- **Root cause.** `convCaps` is a CACHE per conversation (a vendor round trip, 6 h TTL), and nothing invalidated it when the account's CREDENTIAL changed: the re-authorize wrote `rec.auth.scopes`, dropped the live adapter, re-asked auth, broadcast, and forced ONE pass — which visits only what is due. Every other conversation of the account kept its pre-consent verdict until its own convCaps happened to be re-asked. The send half of that verdict was never a vendor fact at all: Gmail's and Lark's are a pure function of the held scopes.
- **Fix.** (1) THE ADAPTER DECLARES THE PURE RULE: `sendCapsOf(scopes)` (Gmail: `sendVerbsOf(scopes).reply`; Lark: both send scopes held), which its own `convCaps` now uses too — one rule, two callers; the registry refuses a non-function or one on a read-only adapter. (2) THE CREDENTIAL'S CHANGE IS STAMPED: the engine's token door stamps `auth.scopesAt` when the scope SET changes or a consent lands (never on a same-scope refresh — `updatedAt` moves every hour), `clear()` and the switched-client rebind stamp it too; `credentialChangedAt(rec)` = max(`scopesAt`, `lastAuthAt`). (3) `effectiveConvCaps(rec, en)` — THE ONE READER of a cached verdict (the digest row, the conversation view, the watch's stale check, `authorityCapsFor`, `sendIdentityFor`): a verdict judged after the change is itself; an older one's send half is recomputed from the held scopes (read `yes` kept, `at` = the change) or, with no pure rule / a read not verified, it is marked STALE (`at: 0` — the next open re-asks the vendor). (4) AT THE WRITE: the consent hook, the rebind, the disconnect (and once at boot, for a consent that landed before this code — the owner's state) persist the re-judged verdicts in ONE index write BEFORE their one whole `channels-updated` digest; the window's footer re-renders on it in place.
- **Gates.** test-channels-engine ⑯ (a scoped fake, a DISABLED account no pass touches, two threads judged read-only before the consent: after the consent — through the engine's own token door and consent hook — both writable on read, in the ONE whole digest and on disk, zero vendor calls; a same-scope refresh moves no stamp; no pure rule ⇒ stale; control: the engine copy that skips the re-judge keeps both read-only; pins: every consumer goes through `effectiveConvCaps`, every credential write re-judges before its digest). test-channel-window-render ⑦ (chrome: a Disconnect's digest turns an OPEN Lark composer read-only in place; the owner's exact state across a restart — the Gmail window left open shows the composer after its reconnect, a thread opened afterwards is writable at once).
- **不变量.** A capability derived from a credential is re-judged when the credential changes, not when a pass happens by. The invalidation entry point (the credential write) recomputes what it can without the vendor, marks the rest stale, and NOTIFIES once; every reader of the cache goes through one function that knows the credential's age.

Measured pre-fix: a cancel / the timer's cancel / a newer sign-in / a stop() landing in that window ⇒ live + disk token = the consent's, `authState` connected, `lastAuthError` = "nothing was connected", no "connected as" line, NO pass kicked — the card connected, its last sign-in line contradicting it. A stop() while the exchange was in flight: the door refused by name (good), then `onAuthDone` stamped `lastAuthError` into adapters.json AFTER `store.close()` (`adaptersUpdate` is not gated on `closed`; the index family drops post-close writes).

- **不变量.** The report of a flow is derived from what its exchange DID, never from a mark that arrived after; a consumer whose durable write is still ahead judges the carried cancel at ITS apply time; nothing is written after stop. Recorded, no code: a refused door still rides the store's unconditional atomic rewrite (same bytes, new inode); `flows.take()` is never called (finished flows stay in the loopback's map). Held: 20 orderings of "A's exchange in flight, B (same account) supersedes it" on both paths — A first / A after B's write refused (never a second write), B cancelled ⇒ the pre-flow record, a disconnect ⇒ nothing of A ever written; the real 300 ms deadline mid-exchange (refused by name, untouched, no For-you item) and after the write (stands). Gates: test-channels-accounts ⑫ (l) (196; controls: a loopback copy with r7's override ⇒ the contradiction, an engine copy without the stop guard ⇒ a write after stop), test-oauth-loopback ⑥ (48), test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c (m) (139, re-pinned to the rule).

- **What happened.** Round 7 attacked round 6's closure — the compare-and-swap door, the boot stamp, the nameless refusal — on the real engine + real store + the real adapters over scripted vendors with the consent's PROFILE READ held mid-flight. A human act landing while the consent was being completed was undone by the consent landing late: a DISCONNECT ⇒ the record connected again (live + disk) and the pass it kicked made 4 vendor calls on the account the owner had ended; a NEWER sign-in for the same record ⇒ the older flow's late completion overwrote the newer's token; `cancelAuth` ⇒ ignored; a client-switch REBIND completing after the disconnect ⇒ landed. The loopback's `cancel()` only marked the flow — `finish()` still stored what the exchange returned and reported `ok:true`. Lower: the door's identity judgement sat BEFORE the store's await, so two consents of one tick on an UNBOUND record were both judged against nothing and the record ended bound to whichever was enqueued last; a consent naming WHITESPACE (or a bare word) passed the adapter's truthiness check — the r6 hole back through an off-contract vendor (a whitespace Lark open_id the same); a CAS write naming '' landed on a CLEARED store; the boot stamp took a Lark display name containing '@' ("Alice @ Sales") as an email and named none of the records it could not stamp.

EVERY judgement of the door — cancelled, nameless, identity, the CAS — runs inside the callback at apply time; a CAS write never lands on a cleared store; `identityOf` / `heldIdentity` accept an `email` only when it looks like an address (`EMAIL_RE`); Lark ids are trimmed; `stampIdentities` logs ONE line naming the stamped and the unstamped.

A CAS write onto a cleared store never lands. An identity is an address or an id, never a truthy string. What a boot stamp could not stamp is named, never guessed. ## A NAMELESS CONSENT BOUND NOTHING, A LEGACY RECORD HELD NOTHING, AND THE DOOR'S ORDER WAS A FACT ONE EDIT REOPENS (lane R5 verify r6, 2026-09-27, credential class)

- **What happened.** Round 5 gave the record an identity and the refresh a rule ("write only while the store holds the token you tried"). Round 6 attacked the identity door's three edges and the rule's mechanics, on the real engine + real store + the real adapters over scripted vendors. (1) A consent whose profile / user_info read FAILED was stored with no identity: a brand-new account was UNBOUND, so a stranger's later consent bound it (every assignment and reach grant retargeted); and a stranger's consent whose profile read failed landed on a BOUND record unjudged — the r5 rule "no common key = nothing to judge" (pinned as accepted in the PURE table) let a nameless token through. (2) The migration edge: a LEGACY Lark record (pre-r5, no stamp) has `auth.user` = the display NAME, so `heldIdentity` read `{}` and a stranger's consent bound it; a legacy Gmail record DISCONNECTED after the upgrade lost its `auth.user` (clear() wipes it) and took a stranger too; nothing stamped legacy records at boot. (3) The r5 write order (re-read the store synchronously, then enqueue the write) was correct only because no await sat between the two — a patched adapter with one reverted a re-authorize again; and the single-flight persist handed a write of ANOTHER token the in-flight promise and dropped it (under Lark's rotation the store then kept a retired token ⇒ the next refresh `invalid_grant` ⇒ logged out; unreachable on the real store, which mutates memory before the file write, reachable on any store that does not). (4) Lark's refresh captured its token BEFORE the pace wait: a disconnect / re-authorize landing during the wait still sent the POST with the dropped / superseded refresh token. (5) A refreshed sign-in the disk refused was logged only; the owner learned of it as `needs-reauth` after the next restart.
- **Fix.** (1) A CONSENT MUST NAME ITS ACCOUNT: the adapter's exchange refuses (`namelessSentence`, `vendor-error`, nothing written — retry the sign-in); the door refuses a nameless consent (`meta.consent`) onto a record that holds an identity (belt). (2) `heldIdentity(rec, storedToken)`: a record with no stamp is judged by the token it HOLDS (Gmail's email, Lark's open_id), else its `auth.user` when that is an email; `stampIdentities()` at engine create stamps every legacy record once (a disconnected legacy Lark record holds no evidence and takes the next consent — said). (3) The door is a COMPARE-AND-SWAP: `tokens.write(token, {supersedes})` lands only while the store holds `supersedes` at APPLY time, inside the serialized callback, answering `{superseded}`; the adapters pass what they tried (the refresh, the invalid_grant stamp, the unsaved flush) and treat superseded as "wrote nothing, re-read"; `persistToken(next, supersedes)` chains a different token's write behind an in-flight one instead of returning it. (4) Lark's refresh re-reads the token after `pace(1)`, before `meter(1)`: cleared ⇒ refused by name (no POST), replaced ⇒ superseded. (5) The door files ONE "For you" item per account when the store refuses a token write ("its refreshed sign-in could not be saved to disk", what a restart before a write lands means), retracted by the next write that lands (a token write, a passing pass). Held (no code): 50 trials × {re-authorize, disconnect, rebind, remove} × {gmail, lark} with the refresh POST held and 50 same-tick microtask orderings — 0 reverted, 0 vendor calls with a wrong bearer; Gmail case-folds and compares the profile's canonical address exactly (a `+tag` / an alias spelling is another string — the vendor never returns one for the same person); Lark accepts a rebind under another app on union_id / user_id and refuses an open_id-only consent under another app (not provable); `unsaved` is one slot per adapter instance; an attacker holding the owner's browser mid-consent is out of scope (the owner drives the consent).
- **不变量.** A consent that cannot name its account connects nothing. A record with no stamp is judged by the token it holds, and is stamped from it before anyone else may consent. A token write states what it supersedes and the STORE judges it where the write applies — never the writer, never before an await. A single flight is per value, never per slot. A paced call re-reads its credential after the wait, refresh included. A sign-in that could not reach the disk is said to the owner when it happens. Gates: test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c (h)–(j) / test-channels-lark-shape ⑥c (h)–(k) (the r5 persist restored in a copy as the control), test-channels-accounts ⑫ (f)–(i) (an engine copy without the CAS + an adapter copy with an await in the gap as the control).

## THE ONE GATE HAD ONE MORE INPUT — THE TOKEN — AND ITS WRITERS RACED THE OWNER (lane R5 verify r5, 2026-09-27, credential class)

- **What happened.** The r4 closure judged every vendor CALL (one gate, one exit), but the token a call carries has its own writers, and they were unordered: the single-flight refresh's success path wrote `{...capturedToken, access_token}` unconditionally. Measured on the real adapters over a scripted vendor: a re-authorize landing while a refresh was in flight was REVERTED to the old refresh token in 25 of 50 trials (both adapters); a DISCONNECT during a refresh was undone — the late write put the token back and the next pass made 4 vendor calls on an account the owner had ended; a client-switch rebind landing during the old client's refresh ended 10/10 with the OLD client's token on a record keyed to the NEW client ⇒ the next refresh `invalid_grant` ⇒ needs-reauth — the owner's fresh consent logged the account out. Beside it: under Lark's ROTATING refresh token ONE failed store write (a full disk) retired the only valid token ⇒ the next refresh `invalid_grant` ⇒ logged out; a queue longer than the token's remaining life (50 thumbnails at the 5 units/s floor = 200 s against a 60 s margin) sent 34 requests with an EXPIRED bearer (401 — a spurious `auth-expired` on each thumbnail); and a consent naming ANOTHER Google / Lark user on an existing account was stored `ok:true` — every assignment and grant on the record retargeted onto a stranger's mailbox, the cursor and index still the old user's.
- **Cause.** Three writers of one fact with no rule between them: the refresh wrote what it captured, the consent wrote what the vendor answered, the disconnect cleared — last writer wins. The gate re-read the bearer after the wait (r4) but never asked whether it was still alive. Nothing named whose account a record is.
- **Fix.** (1) A refresh's write happens ONLY while the store still holds the token it tried (r4's rule for the `invalid_grant` stamp, now on the success path too): cleared ⇒ discarded + refused by name; replaced ⇒ superseded, `null`, the caller re-reads the store (a straggler's `invalid_grant` for a since-replaced token is superseded the same way — its caller is served). (2) A write the store refuses keeps the vendor's token in memory (`unsaved`), served while the store holds the token it supersedes, flushed single-flight at the next request. (3) After `meter`, `bearerExpired()` ⇒ one single-flight `accessToken()` before the send. (4) `src/channel-identity.js` + the engine's ONE token door / `applyRebind`: a consent naming another identity is `forbidden` by name (the card's last sign-in line names both), `rec.identity` stamped by the first consent, kept across a disconnect; Lark compares open_id / union_id / user_id, so a rebind under another app still matches the same person. (5) `failPass` on an outlived entry stamps nothing; the budget / pace views read the ghost.
- **不变量.** A token write states the token it replaces and lands only while the store holds it. A refresh result is not a fact about the account once the account moved on. A bearer is checked for life at the send, not at the entry. A record names whose it is, and a consent that names someone else is refused where the write would happen — never after. Gates: test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c (d)–(g) (128), test-channels-lark-shape ⑥c (d)–(g) (110), test-channels-accounts ⑫ (140), test-channels-aggregate ③g (viii) (351) — each with a patched copy as the control (the r4 write reverts the re-authorize; an engine without the door stores the stranger).

- **What happened.** Four verify rounds of the per-second pace (the owner's "gmail一直被限速") each found a NEW way a vendor call slipped past it: r1 a request judged only when the sleep ended, r2 a check-then-charge across an await, r3 a caller queued behind a removed account let through unpaced.
