THE GATE CENSUS (every outbound HTTP call in src/channels/gmail.js + lark.js + live/gmail.js): a Lark SEND was neither paced nor metered (`sendImpl` called the primitive directly — an agent's direct-policy reply loop was N unpaced sends); the token refresh had NO single flight — 20 concurrent thumbnails at one expiry were 20 refresh POSTs (G3), and under Lark's ROTATING refresh token 11 of 12 came back `invalid_grant`, each stamping the STALE token (plus `invalidGrantAt`) back over the sibling's fresh one: the account logged itself out and asked the owner to re-authorize (L2, on the real adapter over a scripted vendor); every `api()` captured its bearer BEFORE the pace wait, so after a disconnect 20 requests still left with the dropped token (G1) and after a same-client re-authorize 20 left with the OLD one (G2). THE EXIT CENSUS (every lifecycle end of an account's right to call): `setEnabled(false)` and `disconnect()` only disarmed the push lane — 18 queued fetches (360 units) finished, paced, after the owner had ended the account (r3's recorded low); a `remove()` while a pass's fetch was in flight let the page land AFTER the removal and resurrect the removed account's index row + log file, and an attachment fetch in flight wrote its cache file under the removed account; a disable/enable (or a disconnect/re-authorize, an options rebuild, a client switch) rebuilt the live entry with a FULL bucket and minute window — a fresh 80-unit burst per toggle.
- **Cause.** No closed list. "Which calls are paced" and "which verbs end an account" were each answered by reading the code, and each round's fix added one more site beside the others. The primitive (`callJson`) was reachable from anywhere; the live entry could be deleted (or left alive) by any verb; a fetch's write never asked whether its entry still existed.
- **FIX.** ONE GATE: the adapter's `api()` (token → pace → meter → `bearerNow(at)` = the store re-read synchronously after the wait → send); `sendImpl` paces + meters + re-reads; the refresh is single-flight (`refreshing`: siblings await the one POST and re-read what it wrote) and a refused refresh stamps `invalidGrantAt` only while the stored token is still the one it tried. Every other outbound call carries `// gated-inline: <id>` (its own `await pace(1); meter(1)` within the 8 lines above) or `// ungated: <id>` with a row in the module's frozen `UNGATED` (Gmail: token-refresh / consent-exchange / consent-profile / pubsub; Lark: consent-exchange / consent-user-info / integration-test — each a reason an agent or a loop cannot multiply). ONE EXIT: the engine's `dropLive` — remove / disable / disconnect / options rebuild / client switch (applyRebind, inlineLegacyClient) / a refused connect take it, stop wakes the same sleepers; `paceWait` re-checks the entry after EVERY await and aborts by name; `outlived(rec, e)` (= stopped || the entry changed) guards the write after every vendor call (ingest / discover / loadOlder / attachment); `paceCarry` keeps a dropped entry's minute window + bucket as a ghost the in-flight meter still charges and the rebuilt entry inherits (an exit never refills); `attachment()` refuses a disabled account.
- **Measured (real engine + real store; the real Gmail/Lark adapters over scripted vendors; real timers; zero vendor calls).** After the fix: disable / disconnect / remove / stop under 20 queued 20-unit fetches ⇒ 0 vendor calls after the event, every queued caller `transport` "the account changed … the request was not sent", a fresh fetch on a disabled account `disabled` with no call; 20 concurrent callers at one expiry ⇒ 1 refresh POST (Gmail and Lark), the rotating vendor leaves the account `connected` holding the rotated token; a re-authorize landing mid-queue ⇒ 38 of 38 requests carry the NEW bearer; a remove() mid-fetch ⇒ 0 index rows, 0 log files, 0 cache files of the removed account, the pass ends `account-changed`; disable + enable after an emptying burst ⇒ the next fetches WAIT (≥ 400 ms) with the minute's spend kept; 200 pokes 1 ms apart ⇒ ≤ 40 units/s, min gap 1 001 ms, 36 ms CPU; a SIGKILL mid-wait persists nothing (no bucket / reservation / queue / sleeper in the store) and the next boot's first fetch leaves in < 500 ms.
- **Gates.** test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c + test-channels-lark-shape ⑥c (the grep census over the markers vs `UNGATED`, the gate's order pinned on the gate line, the single flight + stale-stamp guard; controls: a bare `callJson` added, a send's pace removed, a marker with no row, a row with no marker, the refresh's marker removed — all red; the r3 tree as a best-effort control; runtime: the single flight, the rotating vendor, the bearer after the wait — a re-authorize's token sent, a disconnect refused by name); test-channels-aggregate ③g (v)–(viii) (the exit census over the engine's code with four text controls; disable / disconnect under a full queue with the r3 setEnabled as a driven control; the outlived write with the r3 ingest as a driven control; the carry with a forgetting exit as a control).
- 不变量=ONE gate for every vendor call and ONE exit for every lifecycle end, both a CENSUS the suite reads off the code (a new call outside the gate, a new verb that drops without the exit, a write after the entry ended — each red before it ships); a queued waiter re-checks the entry's identity AND its bearer after every await; a refresh is single-flight and a refused one never overwrites a newer token; an exit never refills a bucket.

## GMAIL SAID "RATE LIMITED" FOR 15 MINUTES WHILE THE MINUTE'S BUDGET HELD (lane R5, 2026-09-26, the owner on 2.369.185)

- **What happened.** The owner: "gmail一直被限速 你可能要控制下gmail默认的读取速度". The production journal (read only): three Gmail refusals in ten minutes on two accounts, each HTTP 403 "Quota exceeded for quota metric 'Total Query Cost' and limit 'Units per minute per user'" — each after ~2 000–2 800 units spent in ~13–26 s (fetches 150–320 ms apart, 100–200 units/s) from an idle quota, i.e. UNDER our 3 000/min budget and under Google's published 6 000/min per user. Every refusal climbed the account FAILURE ladder (30 s → 2 min → 5 min → 15 min) and the third filed a "For you" item; one account recovered only when the owner re-authorized. The card read like a 15-minute park.
- **Cause.** Two. ① The only brake was the drain's rule 9 — stop once the minute's budget is spent — so a pass ran back to back at full speed until 3 000 units were gone (~20 s), idled ~40 s and repeated: a per-minute cap is a SUM, not a SHAPE, and the vendor meters finer than a minute. ② A vendor rate refusal shared the ladder of a broken account (transport, auth), so a few seconds' wait became a 15-minute stop and a filed failure.
- **FIX.** ① Drain RULE 18, THE PACE (PURE src/channel-drain.js): a per-second token bucket per account in the budget's unit, declared by the adapter (`caps.pace`; Gmail 40 units/s = one thread read a second, Lark 5 requests/s), coupled by the engine to the minute (rate = min(setting, budget/60), burst = min(setting, budget/2)); a vendor action short of tokens is a `wait` (≤ 1 s) after which the drain picks again — never a refusal, never a skip, never ahead of a refusal; the adapters also await `deps.pace(units)` before every request (the exact cost, call by call). ② A `rate-limited` failure is a SHORT ladder — the vendor's Retry-After / `x-ogw-ratelimit-reset`, else 5 s doubling to 60 s — that never advances `consecutiveFailures`, empties the bucket, and speaks in "For you" only after 10 strikes in a row. ③ The card says "Google 限速中 · N 秒后继续" by the vendor's declared name from the first strike and "首次读取中 · 已 N/M 个会话 · 约剩 K 分钟" while reading; a long paced pass broadcasts its progress every 5 s. Gmail's 403 usageLimits / quota-metric refusals are typed `rate-limited`, not `forbidden`.
- **Measured.** The owner's 873-thread first read under the defaults: ≤ 80 units in any second, ≤ 2 440 in any minute (Google's cap 6 000), ≈ 872 s evenly — the pre-fix shape was 3 000 units in 1.5 s (2 040 inside one second) then nothing for the rest of the minute.
- **Gates.** test-channel-drain (rule 18 in a paced walk against the sim's own bucket + window checks; ②b the 873-row first read + the pace-off control; mutants pace-no-refill / pace-ignored / wait-counts / wait-before-refusal / wait-unbounded); test-channels-aggregate ③d (5/10/20/40/60/60… s, Retry-After 7 ⇒ 7 s, no failure count, the item at strike 10, auth still 30 → 900 s; CONTROL = the pre-R5 failPass copy parking 30 → 900 s) / ③e (the real engine at 40 units/s + the pace-off control + ≤ 1 progress broadcast per 5 s); test-channel-caps, test-channel-adapter-contract, test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥b (the vendor's cost table pinned, the production 403), test-channels-lark-shape ⑥b; test-channels-e2e ⑰ (heavy: the zh card over a paced, rate-refused fake).
- 不变量=vendor calls are paced per SECOND and per MINUTE (a per-minute cap is a sum, not a shape — a vendor's minute limit is enforced below a minute); a rate refusal is a short wait that names the vendor, never a 15-minute park, never a failure count.

## TWO VIEWS HELD ONE CHROME ON THE WIRED PATH, ONE CLICK WOKE EVERY CONVERSATION ON THE BROWSER, AND A CALL STILL UNANSWERED WAS CALLED "CUT" (lane S2 verify r7, 2026-09-27)

- **What was found (each reproduced red first on 3ab9fcfe, through the REAL bridge / announcer / mediator).** ① MEDIUM: r6's "a second viewer of the same browser meets `held`" was pinned with the keeper's `holderAlive` defaulting true; the bridge computes it PER RELAY (`relay.viewers.has(relay.holder)`) and a sibling conversation's holder sits on ANOTHER relay by construction — so on the wired path it read as gone: B's own view driving, A's view clicking Take over ⇒ mode-ack ok, holders [1, 2], both views' `input_mouse` forwarded to one Chrome; A driving (B, C with it), C's view clicking ⇒ ok, then A's handback released A + B and left C paused under viewer 3 until its own handback or the 10-min idle. ② MEDIUM (spend): the mirrored handback of every sibling went through `deliverToConversation` (`kind:'notification'` — a billed turn on an idle claude session) even when the sibling's cycle had interrupted and refused NOTHING; on a shared "remember login" profile with N conversations one click = N billed wakes, N−1 to idle agents told "the page is now X" about a page they were not on. ③ MEDIUM (the request's own rule): a click whose success reply arrived 450 ms after the takeover — past the audit's 250 ms settle-wait — was answered `landed: 0` with no mark, and the CLI printed a definite "cut short"; the reply then landed (a re-run is a double click).
- **FIX.** ① the bridge answers `viewerAlive(id)` across every relay (ids from one counter) and hands it to `keeper.takeover`; the keeper consults it for its own lease's holder and, at the door, for every sibling's — a live holder anywhere on the browser ⇒ `held` naming it (`heldBy`), a dead holder never blocks and the browser moves WHOLE (`siblingTakeover` re-seizes dead-holder siblings; no second card). ② the mirrored handback event carries `sibling`; PURE `announceVerdict({cause, sibling, rerun})` delivers a sibling's explicit handback only with something to re-run, else the zero-spend notice — no new ladder site. ③ `interruptionFor` carries `unsettled`; the CLI: "— and one of its calls had not been answered by the page when this was written, so whether it took effect is unknown: check the page before running it again".
- **Held.** A child handle is the helper's OWN ephemeral browser (never on the shared browser — `/resolve` by handle is keyed `(child, null)`, not paused; a helper's bare command acts as its parent's key and is paused with the parent); the keeper's `attach` would admit a child KEY on a named profile but no route hands one in. The dedup: two identical deliveries ⇒ two cards on both paths; a stub CLI that acks and drops one record / every record ⇒ the held card renders once each; a prefix-shaped pair with the SHORT record lost cross-matches (`includes`) — contrived, needs a lost record AND a prefix relation, recorded. `landed` on a sibling's call is the sibling's (per grant).
- **不变量.** ONE browser, ONE holder — a holder's liveness is a fact across every relay, never one relay's. A click on one view wakes only the conversations whose agents were told to wait (something interrupted or refused); the rest are told for free. What a bounded wait could not settle is said as unknown, never as a definite outcome.
- **Gates.** test-browser-takeover ⑨ r7 (287: held across leases + `heldBy`, the dead-holder re-seize, the PURE spend rule + the WIRED count, the REAL bridge over a fake upstream — held on the wired path, one input forwarded, viewer-left; CONTROLS: a keeper copy ignoring the cross-relay fact + a per-relay bridge copy), test-browser-mediation ⑦ (228: `unsettled` 3 → 0 in the keeper's answer), test-browser-verbs (557: the unanswered sentence, alone and beside `landed`).

## A SHARED BROWSER WAS TAKEN OVER ONE CONVERSATION AT A TIME, A DELIVERED NOTICE RENDERED TWICE AFTER THE FIRST ATTACH, AND "CUT SHORT" HID A FILL THAT LANDED (lane S2 verify r6, 2026-09-27)

- **What was found (each reproduced red first on 39555214).** ① MEDIUM: a takeover was keyed per (conversation, profile) — on a shared mediated profile (S5's default for a named profile) the user's takeover from conversation A's live view left conversation B's `fill` + `eval` running on the same Chrome, B's `/resolve` allowed, B's `Target.activateTarget` FORWARDED (the r3 "moved what the user was looking at" class, across conversations), B never told, never reminded. ② MEDIUM: r5's held-card replay (a card fed before the chat window's first attach) also replayed the delivery ladder's card — but the CLI RECORDS a delivered message as a JSONL user record (origin peer) the rebuild renders, so a handback / job notification delivered before the first attach showed TWICE (a same-body repeat ×4). ③ MEDIUM (the request's own rule): on the real 0.38.1 + Chrome 153 a `fill` caught on its one `Input.insertText` holds all 4000 chars while the CLI said "cut short" — a lie by omission. ④ LOW: the 32-card bound dropped silently; the human was never told a page script was stopped by the takeover's `terminateExecution`; a mediated command refused at its next call had no third line.
- **FIX.** ① the keeper takes every sibling lease WITH the primary (`siblingTakeover`: same viewer, its calls interrupted, its own cycle / card / notice), a lease attached while the user drives joins at birth (`joinTakeoverIfDriven`), handback / pass / idle input mirror to the siblings the viewer holds; a second viewer meets `held`. ② the ladder's card carries `recorded` (the posted text); the replay skips a recorded card answered by a rendered peer record, consuming one record per card (`replayContext` / `replayCard`), display-only cards always replay. ③ the proxy marks an aborted call `landed` when the browser's late reply is a success; the audit route waits ≤ 250 ms for the unsettled ones (`awaitInterruptionSettled`); the CLI says "cut short … but one of its calls had already reached the page and took effect: check the page" / "the takeover came between its calls". ④ a journal line at the first drop and every 32nd; `interruptionView.terminated` → the mode record → the toast "A script running in the page was stopped with it."; the third line for the refused-between case.
- **Held.** The audit join: a verb audited after the handback joins nothing (both orders ×20), one audited while the user drives again joins THAT open cycle (the CLI promised the handback names it) — once even when audited twice; exactly ONE `terminateExecution` per session per cycle across three takeovers (×20), none when nothing of the agent's is pending or only a read is; a killed session takes its held cards with it (WeakRef + gc); the 3 kinds × 4 verbs table on the real binary — every cell's words match what happened (mediated: eval cut, fill/type cut + landed, read came-between; ephemeral / owner-shared: ran to its end in every cell).
- **不变量.** A takeover is of the BROWSER: every conversation on it is interrupted, told and reminded of ITS OWN verbs — nothing crosses. A card the transcript will render is never replayed beside the record (each record answers for one card; a repeat keeps its count). "Cut" is said only of what was cut; a call the browser answered with a success LANDED and is said so. A measured-and-documented collateral (the page script) is told to the person who can see it.
- **Gates.** test-browser-takeover ⑨ (272; CONTROL: a keeper copy without the sibling call), test-browser-mediation ⑦ (228: the sibling on the real proxy, landed / unsettled / the bounded settle-wait), test-attach-rebuild ④ (100), test-browser-verbs (555: the CLI's four sentences).

## A TAKEOVER WAS A SILENT PAUSE — THE AGENT'S SCRIPTS RAN ON UNDER THE USER'S HANDS, NOBODY TOLD IT, AND THE HANDBACK NEVER SAID WHAT TO RE-RUN (the owner's ruling, 2026-09-27, lane S2)

- **The ruling (verbatim).** "关于接管浏览器的时候agent脚本，其实应该直接打断所有脚本和agent操作，告知agent发生了打断，交还时提醒它重新运行" — when the user takes over the agent's browser, INTERRUPT every script and operation of the agent there, TELL the agent it was interrupted, and on the HANDBACK remind it to re-run.
- **What it replaced.** D6 left script evaluation OPEN while the user drove a shared browser (r4 put the whole `page-mutation` class behind `browser.fenceScriptsWhileDriven`, default OFF — the owner's ask was open). A takeover only refused what came NEXT: a call already in flight ran on, a running `eval` kept mutating the page the user was driving, the agent learned of the takeover only when its next verb bounced (`browser_paused`), and the handback named the URL but never what had been cut.
- **FIX (three parts, design §6.2.2).** (1) INTERRUPT: the keeper's `takeover` calls `cdpMediator.interrupt` first — PURE `interruptPlan` answers every in-flight call of the lease whose class is refused while the user drives with `browser_interrupted` AT ONCE (≤ 2 ms in the fast gate) and sends ONE `Runtime.terminateExecution` on each session that was running an aborted script; the census refuses input + view + page-mutation while the user drives; the switch is retired (a stored value ignored, said once). (2) TELL: PURE src/browser-interrupt.js — what was in flight = `inFlightAt(the recorder's ring of the daemon's command / result records, the instant)`; the running `vibespace-browser` command ends `[browser_interrupted]` (the audit's answer on the keeper's clock); ONE conversation card per takeover → handback cycle (`normalizers.feedPeerCard`, display only) + ONE zero-spend `browser-takeover` notice — free, no producer added (test-spend-paths §2). (3) REMIND: the handback closes the cycle and its words end "Re-run what was interrupted: …" once (interrupted, then refused, each verb once; a nothing-cycle byte-identical to before); a held delivery rides ONE carrier (the stash — stash + notice made the agent read it twice).
- **What cannot be recalled (MEASURED on Chrome 153.0.8010.47 + agent-browser 0.38.1, test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑦).** A RUNNING script stops (0.38.1's `eval` = `Runtime.evaluate` awaitPromise; a 5 s busy loop: the CLI answered 2 ms after the takeover, the page answered a probe at once, the loop's last statement never ran); `terminateExecution` with nothing running changes nothing (a raw-CDP measurement: the page's own timer still ran); a script AWAITING a timer / fetch is not running — its continuation still runs; an `Input.*` call that already left the proxy reached Chrome — `fill` is ONE `insertText` and COMPLETES (4000 / 4000 chars), `type` is one per character and STOPS (20 / 300); even `get title` reads by script on 0.38.1 and is refused while the user drives. A browser that is NOT shared instance-wide has no proxy: its in-flight command runs to its end — the agent is still told.
- **Traps met on the way.** A `key: INT.x` entry in a CJS `module.exports` STOPS node's named-export detection at that key — the client's `import { ownerOf } from '../browser-takeover.js'` broke (the bundle did not: esbuild reads CJS whole) → shorthand only. The recorder and the keeper must share ONE clock (the fast gate injects both). A live-injected chat card is lost when an attach REBUILDS the normalizer from the transcript (a chat window attached after the takeover shows no card — the notice still reaches the agent); the heavy leg takes over with the chat window loaded, the everyday shape.
- **不变量 = a takeover INTERRUPTS, TELLS, and the handback REMINDS — never a silent pause.** Gates: test-browser-mediation ⑦ (the real keeper + proxy; CONTROL: the old pause), test-browser-takeover ⑧ (PURE(trace, instant), one card + one notice + one reminder per cycle; CONTROL: an announcer without the takeover moment), test-browser-verbs (the CLI's words), test-spend-paths §2, test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑦ + test-browser-live ⑧ (heavy, real binary).

## "WHICH BROWSER IS THIS CONVERSATION USING" HAD THREE ANSWERS — AND THE LIVE VIEW, THE KEYBOARD AND A DELETE EACH TRUSTED A DIFFERENT ONE (naive-user study 2, 2.369.186, tasks T4 / T5 / T7, lane S2, 2026-09-26)

- **What happened.** Two fresh-eyes testers, one instance each (SharedContext/vibespace-naive-study-2.md, sections 坏了 + 让人困惑): Session Properties said pinned "work", the status-bar chip said "Agent browser · tester-b-scratch" then "(ephemeral) Second chat", the live view's title said "ephemeral (no profile)"; after a detach the chip still said "work"; the strip tab said "work (default)" while the chip's menu said "pinned: ephemeral (no profile)". A recreated "work" left the open live view on the OLD browser behind a red "Live view unavailable: this session is not attached to bp-56a75ced" — Reconnect did nothing ("点 Reconnect 没反应"). Typing during a takeover reached nothing through the side pane, a floating window or the keyboard box while the bar read "You are driving · Typing goes to the browser" ("字全都没到页面里，也没有任何'没送到'的提示"). "Delete permanently" left conversations pinned to "bp-17eb27c4 (your choice for this session)" and the next browse silently used a temporary browser. The New Session dialog listed only "None (ephemeral)" while the panel listed the recreated "work". Session Properties did not update after a pin until reopened, wrapped the name "wor / k", wore white native buttons and ignored Esc.
- **Cause.** No published answer existed: each surface derived its own from a different pair of raw fields — the pin (`browserProfileId`), the last command (`browserProfileActive`), the live holder (`browserLive`), the attachment set's `isDefault` — and each pair disagrees with the others by construction (a pin the agent's attachment overrides, a default that is not the pin, an own browser that opens the pin's directory on rung D). The pin route never re-published active-sessions (`onPinChanged` was never wired), so Session Properties re-rendered stale rows. A live view held the ref it was opened with; nothing moved it when the conversation's browser changed, and Reconnect re-asked the same dead ref. MEASURED on agent-browser 0.38.1 through the real mediator (scripts/measure-input-receipts.mjs, three rounds: agent drives / user drives uncredited / user drives credited ⇒ the page reads "abcabc|202": the first and third rounds landed, the second — the shipped behaviour — not at all; all six credited receipts ok): ONE viewer input record = exactly ONE CDP `Input.*` call (6 of 6 kinds), the stream server answers NOTHING for it, and a MEDIATED (instance-shared) lease's live view streams from the session's own daemon THROUGH the mediator — whose paused fence (the user drives) refused every one of the user's own keys (`browser_paused`), silently. `removeProfile` dropped the keeper's pins but never the session's own record, never re-pointed its generated config off the moved directory, and the dialog's options filtered out every shared profile.
- **FIX.** ONE fact, computed at ONE choke point: PURE `browserFactFor(session, view)` (src/browser-fact.js) over the keeper's registry view (`keeper.factView` — pin + cleared mark, attachment set, each browser's state + last failure, the conversation's own browser + its last verb, who drives, what runs) ⇒ `{pinned, pinGone, pinCleared, using, own, lastUsed, differs, input, live, digest}`, published as active-sessions' `browserFact` (one LIVE_SESSION_FACTS row, a string digest) and re-published when a registry change moves a digest (`keeper.onChange`, debounced). PURE `browserFactWords(fact, t)` is the ONE spelling every surface prints — the chip, its menu, the card chip, Session Properties, the live view's title and the strip's in-use tab (an accent underline — zero width, so a split pane's strip never folds a neighbour — its tooltip and every menu/title say "(in use)"): the name, or both names in one line when they differ ("pinned work · running nothing — work could not start — another browser has it open"), plain words ("no profile (temporary browser)"), ids only in the tooltip. A live view FOLLOWS its session's browser (PURE `liveFollowPlan`: a following view — the default, the one the fact named before, a stale target — retargets; a view the user pointed elsewhere, a helper's, one the user drives, the first snapshot stay) and Reconnect re-resolves. Every input carries a `rid` and the bridge answers `input-receipt` (the browser's own reply for a mediated lease, the write for a direct one, the refusal otherwise; none in 1.5 s = not delivered); for a mediated lease the bridge mints ONE credit per forwarded record and the mediator admits the next `Input.*` on it past the paused fence (an uncredited `Input.*` is still refused). A PINNED profile's removal is refused `pinned` (count + names) unless `unpin` — then every live conversation is unpinned through THE pin route's own path (record, meta, env re-pointed off the directory, the agent's notice) and each entry keeps a cleared MARK the fact reads ("work was deleted — its pin was cleared"); the boot heals a dangling pin; leased / running is judged BEFORE any unpin. The dialog lists every named profile (a shared one attached at start, never a spawn pin) and refills while open.
- **VERIFY r4 (2026-09-27, fixed on the branch) — THE FENCE WAS A LIST, AND EVERY ROUND FOUND IT ONE METHOD SHORT.** r1 (`Input.*` + the navigation family), r2 (+ the tab acts), r3 (+ `Input.setIgnoreInputEvents`, + `DOM.focus`): a hand-written list names what somebody thought of; the vendor ships 664 methods (Chrome 153.0.8010.47, its own `GET /json/protocol`), and r3 itself still left `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` / `setScriptExecutionDisabled` / `Debugger.pause` / `Target.openDevTools` / `Cast.startTabMirroring`… — each moves or freezes what the user is looking at — open while they drove. FIX = a CENSUS: PURE src/cdp-census.js has ONE row per method of the pinned protocol (scripts/fixtures/cdp-protocol-153.0.8010.47/, written by scripts/cdp-protocol-fetch.mjs), classed input 15 / view 106 / page-mutation 195 / read 176 / session 11 / harmless 147 / refused 14; `judge` reads the CLASS (`pausedVerdict`), the old `ALWAYS_REFUSED` / `PAUSED_METHODS` are derived views; a method with NO row is refused by name while the user drives (the mediator logs it once per grant, `grantView().unclassified`); the page-mutation class is behind ONE switch `browser.fenceScriptsWhileDriven` (default OFF — D6's open door; the owner asked, not yet answered), read per message like `paused`. Tab scoping is LEASE-WIDE for every class (the mediator cannot tell a tab from an out-of-process iframe under the driven tab; the CLI rung refuses every page verb; the daemon's own `tab <n>` moves the active tab). `Page.bringToFront` is the ONE row fenced by the live view's anchor, not the mediator (measured r2 + r3). ALSO: the anchor's 1 s grace (r3 F6) was 50× the latency it covers — now 62 ms = ⌈3 × p99⌉ of the CLI-to-`tabs`-record span (scripts/measure-anchor-grace.mjs, 2 × 100 real switches: p99 15.37 / 20.37 ms), pinned to its measurement; the r3 anchor end-to-end re-run on it 11/11. 不变量 = **a fence is a CENSUS over the vendor's own method list, classed, unknown = refused by name; never a hand-written list** — and a grace is a measured constant, never a round number. FIX = the census reads several Chromes (`CENSUS_CHROMES`, a fixture each, rows marked `chrome` / `until` — a removed method keeps its row for the older Chrome that still ships it), a FAST gate (test-cdp-census) compares every censused fixture, and the two new whole-browser setters were classed by MEASUREMENT, not by name (Browser.addMockCamera / setGlobalPrivacyControl reach every browser context ⇒ refused). 不变量 = **a new Chrome is APPENDED to the census (its fixture + one row per added method + `until` on each removed), never swapped in; the judge never asks which Chrome is installed; a method a lease cannot scope to its own tabs is refused on every lease** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md (src/cdp-census.js).

Fencing `Page.bringToFront` (measured, with and without the screencast restart fenced too) does NOT stop the switch and leaves the switched-to tab hidden (no frames, mouse dispatches never answered, the stream dead after the handback). Every HELPER's denial — the user's Deny (our message rides after `v6`), an interrupt of its pending ask — carried no "user … rejected" words and read "✓ Allowed" whenever the result was the witness (no record of ours: the CLI's own decision, a lost echo, the restart matrix's `expired` case). So did the interrupt marker `[Request interrupted by user for tool use]`, the turn-ended markers, the parked approval print.ts retires 2 s into a resume ("[Tool call not completed: an approval request expired with no answer …]") and the two sentences whose own word is "outcome is unknown".

Bound by url now (`_provenanceReaskCard`, `noteHelperResult`'s `bind`).
- **THE ANSWER SIDE (⑲).** One builder of a control_response frame (`ClaudeCodeAdapter.buildPermissionResponse`), one caller chain (helper-asks.answerFrame → permission-answer → the adapter), the 2.1.281 inbound shape pinned; a hand-written frame anywhere in src/, server.js or data/bin is named by the census.
- 不变量=a permission outcome is read from a CENSUS of the CLI's own sentences, never inferred from "not the words I know"; an error the census does not know is `unknown` — a state, a word, a card — and unknown is never allowed; the census is read off the binary's own lists by a gate that fails by name when a build adds a sentence; a request whose id names no call is bound by what the CLI itself keyed it on.

## THE CLI'S OWN DEADLINE READ "✓ ALLOWED", AND THE WALK'S ORACLE COULD NOT SEE AN EXTRA EFFECT (lane S1 verify r4, B-6e95, 2026-09-27)

- **SYMPTOM.** 2.1.281 resolves an unanswered WebFetch permission request by ITSELF after 300 000 ms (`f4n`, read in the binary) with the tool_result `p4n` = "The permission request for this URL was not answered in time. Ask the user to approve the fetch or include the URL in a message, then try again." — `is_error`, none of the canned user-rejection words. `_resolutionFromResult` (the ONE result reader for a main card's `autoResolved` and the helper table's `result-*` rows) read it as `allowed`: the helper's card said "✓ Allowed", the For-you item resolved, for a request the CLI had denied. r3 had softened this exact claim as unverifiable; the binary on this box carries the constant.
- **FIX.** The deadline sentence is a denial in the one reader (`permission request … was not answered in time`), so a main card and a helper's ask both read Denied; the table's `result-deny → denied` row is the same cell. Gate: test-helper-ask ⑭ (`deadline` beside `expired` across the real rebuild) + ⑱ (the binary's sentence). Not measurable here (§ban-safety): whether the CLI ALSO sends `control_cancel_request` at its deadline — then the ask reads `cancelled` ("the helper was stopped"), settled either way.
- **THE ORACLE THAT COULD NOT SEE.** The r3 real-engine walk judged stdin frames, open items and the engine's state — an engine performing an effect the table does NOT name was invisible: a normalizer redrawing an unmoved ask (an extra `helperAsks` edit on every settle) and an engine writing the session meta on every sync both walked 600 steps green. r4 counts EVERY effect per step against the cell — For-you adds / dones by request id, card ops (a redraw ⇔ the ask moved), the pending-asks meta op and the session-meta write (each exactly one per change of the waiting set) — and found two real ones: (a) a rebuilt normalizer's first lifecycle edit re-announced an UNCHANGED (often empty) waiting set as a fresh `pending-asks` op (the attach payload already carried it) — `MessageManager.sealPendingAsks()` at the end of `rebuildHistory`; (b) a restart rewrote an unchanged `helperAskedAt` map whenever two asks tied on `at` (the live map in arrival order, the rebuilt one in card order — JSON key order) — the "changed?" key is order-insensitive. Two ENGINE mutants are the controls: the r3 oracle stays green on both, the effect oracle names them (test-helper-ask ⑬ r4).
- **THE UNKNOWN WORD.** A main card resolved in a word outside the table makes `settledState` null (the CLI decides): one press writes, our own echo settles it in the table's word, the second press is refused — never twice, never a lock. A control_request in a subtype the normalizer does not know is dropped by construction (no card, the chip says waiting — the studies' silence for a FUTURE shape) and the drift card could not name it: `claude:stream:control_request` declared only its envelope. r4 declares the request's own vocabulary (the binary's five outbound subtypes and can_use_tool's fields), so `request.subtype=<new>` is an enum-drift card and a new nested field is named (⑱; the measured 2.1.281 asks stay clean).
- **L3 CLOSED (the owner's 2026-09-27 ruling: a takeover interrupts ALL of the agent's operations on that browser).** The stale sweep now sees the helpers' pending browser approvals (`approvals.pendingHelpers` = normalizers.pendingHelperApprovals) and judges each by the browser its commands land on — the child handle a witness bound to its Agent call (`session._browserHelpers`) when it minted one, else the parent's default — answering through the same table lookup. After a restart the witness state is gone (in memory) and a child-keyed helper is judged as the parent's: an over-deny that costs one re-plan, never a stale step. Residual (lane J, pre-existing): a takeover of a CHILD browser also sweeps the parent's bare page commands (`takenFor` reads no attachments under a child key ⇒ `isDefault`).
- 不变量=a CLI's self-settlement is a denial when its sentence says so, in the one reader both cards share; a walk that judges an engine against a table counts EVERY observable effect per step, or an extra effect walks green; a nested request vocabulary is declared, or the next ask shape is silence.

## EVERY VERIFY ROUND FOUND A STATE THE ASK CARD DID NOT KNOW — THE ASK'S LIFE IS NOW ONE CLOSED TRANSITION TABLE (lane S1 verify r3, B-6e95, 2026-09-27)

- **SYMPTOM (the pattern, not one bug).** r1: a request answered twice on stdin, a killed parent's For-you item open forever; r2: an Allow written while the CLI's cancel was in the pipe read "✓ Allowed" on a stopped helper, one For-you item shared by two waiting asks resolved while a twin still waited, a stale View Log frame after Terminate + Resume reaching the resumed process; and round 1's F8 (the 60 s inbox clock restarting with the server) still open. Each fix was a branch in a different consumer (message-manager's settle, helper-asks' settledState / forget / sync, the ws case, the For-you reply, the renderer), each branch encoding its own idea of what an ask's state was.
- **CAUSE.** No single place said what states an ask can be in, which events move it, and what each move does — so every consumer compared `resolved` / `askState()` to its own literals (`=== null`, `=== 'cancelled'`), and every new event (a withdrawal after our answer, a dead parent, a twin, a stale id) was a state one of them had never heard of.
- **FIX — the closure.** PURE `src/helper-ask.js` `ASK_TABLE`: 7 states (asked · allowed · denied · cancelled · ended · parent-ended · unrouted) × 13 events (press-allow/deny · record-allow/deny · withdraw · result-allow/deny · helper-end · level-drop · parent-end · reattach · reply · timer) → `{state, effects ⊆ {write-stdin, refuse, resolve-item, file-item, redraw, nothing}}`, fully enumerated (91 cells), an unknown state / event THROWS. EVERY consumer became a LOOKUP: message-manager's `_settleHelperAsk` is the one writer of `resolved` and writes only the table's next state (over `ASK_RECORD_EVENTS`); helper-asks judges a press by `answerVerdict` (the ws case AND the takeover sweep go through ONE `answerFrame`), files the item only because asked+timer says `file-item`, forgets only because asked+parent-end says `resolve-item`; inbox-reply's `card_item` rung asks the `reply` row; the renderer and chat-view ask `isWaiting`; `settledState` answers in the table's vocabulary and hands a foreign harness word to the CLI (null) rather than throw. New rows the rounds had missed: the helper's own tool_result settles an asked request the CLI decided itself (`result-allow/deny` — the "expired" case, no record of ours exists; live from the stdout consumer's sidechain sites, at a rebuild from session-store's new `helperResults()`), a REAL terminal helper status refuses a press (`ended` — r1 forwarded it; the card had no buttons there since r1, so a press from `ended` is a stale frame by construction), `parent-ended` / `unrouted` have words. The 60 s clock: each waiting ask's first-seen instant is persisted (session-meta `helperAskedAt`, written when the map changes, restored by boot-restore, stamped onto the rebuilt ask) — filed at ask+60 s, not restart+60 s.
- **THE WRITE LAW (why the rebuild is order-faithful).** A control_response record is written only from `asked` (the table's two write cells), so in a real buffer a record can never FOLLOW the helper's result for the same ask; a rebuild that replays the buffer's records before the helpers' results therefore lands where the live path landed. The record rows on settled states exist for the one real reversed order — the buffer's cancel before our frame (cancelled + record-allow → cancelled, r2 C1) — and for a record on a derived end (more precise). The walk's generator honours the law; an event order outside it is not the product's.
- **Gates.** test-helper-ask ⑪ (the census of every cell against the laws + the PURE walk, 36 seeds × 2000 steps, all 91 cells; five table mutants each named by the census and reddened by the walk) · ⑫ (the consumer census over 17 files + two patched-consumer controls) · ⑬ (THE WALK ON THE REAL ENGINE: 2 000 seeded steps over the real normalizer + gate + helper-asks + THE one answer, ~130 real rebuilds, stdin counted per ask, the table as the oracle for BOTH asks after every event; a mutant table makes the engine write twice) · ⑭ (the restart matrix: six states across a server restart and Terminate + Resume) · ⑮ (a re-ask after a withdrawal) · ⑯ (the clock across a restart + the pre-fix control) · ⑰ (the takeover seam) · test-helper-ask-ui C4 (the clock LIVE across a SIGKILL restart) · test-architecture (helper-ask.js in the PURE set) · test-inbox-reply / test-attach-rebuild / test-browser-takeover (the wiring pins re-spelled to the lookup).
- **Recorded r3, CLOSED r4:** a helper's pending BROWSER approval was not part of the takeover's stale sweep (`pendingPermissions` reads main cards) — r4 hands the sweep `pendingHelpers` and judges each by the helper's own browser (the essay above; ⑰ rewritten).
- 不变量=an ask's life is ONE closed transition table, every consumer a lookup (a literal compared beside an ask outside the table is a census red); stdin is written at most once per ask over every event order; a control_response record is written only from `asked`, which is what makes a rebuild's records-then-results replay land where the live path did.

## A RECORD EMITTED IN THE HALF-SECOND AFTER A RE-ATTACH VANISHED FROM A PAGE THAT WAS NOT RELOADED (B-63f1 ②, 2026-09-26 — root-caused by lane S1 verify r1, fixed in verify r2; pre-existing on master)

- **SYMPTOM.** A page kept open across a server SIGKILL + restart (the ws reconnects, every chat window re-attaches): the records the server emitted in the first ~0.5 s after the `attached` frame — a typed line, the answer that followed, a helper's card — rendered live and then VANISHED when the view rebuilt, and never came back (they reappeared only at the next restart or a reload). Measured on real pages: 9 of 12 restarts on the lane build, 4 of 6 on master ab23b3f4; the S1 builder's own "1 run in 4".
- **CAUSE.** `ChatView._reattach`'s `attached` handler, epoch-changed branch: `_normEpoch` is set at once but the slab swap is DEFERRED — `_fullViewReset` on a 0–500 ms `Math.random()` jitter (the 2.338.0 stagger: N windows rebuilding in one tick froze the page). Every `create` / `edit` / `meta` op arriving in that window ran through `_onOp` into the OLD list and advanced `_lastSeq` (with `_seqEpoch` = the new epoch); the reset then rebuilt from the slab captured BEFORE them, and `_applyLiveMeta`'s "never backwards inside one epoch" rule kept the watermark PAST them — so no resume by seq ever replayed them either.
- **FIX (client, src/lib/chat-view.js; the stagger stays, the ops are HELD).** `_armViewReset(msg)` holds the snapshot and arms ONE timer (`_resetJitterMs()`, the seam a suite pins to its maximum); `_onOp` queues while `_resetPending` (`_holdResetOp`, each op tagged with the epoch the view believes); `_fullViewReset` consumes the pending state FIRST, renders the slab, then `_drainResetQueue` applies the held ops IN ORDER — skipping `seq ≤ opSeq` (the slab describes them: the server reads the slab and its `opSeq` in one synchronous step) and ops tagged with another epoch (a second restart inside the window); a create the slab holds anyway dedups by id; the watermark advances only for what applied. A second `attached` of the same rebuild inside the window (a `lagged`, a reconnect — the view still holds the OLD position, so the server answers a full slab, never a held resume) SUPERSEDES the held snapshot; a held resume arriving meanwhile has its replay queued; `dispose` ends a pending rebuild; a queue past 10 000 (`RESET_QUEUE_CAP`) sets `_resetOverflow` — the rebuild's own heal (`_seqPoisoned = false` after the slab) would otherwise CLEAR that poison, so after the drain the view is re-poisoned and re-attached at once with no seq (the full rung's slab heals it synchronously, no stagger); a rebuild whose `loadHistory` throws poisons the watermark (the held ops died with it).
- **Gates.** test-reattach-stagger (fast, 19: the real ChatView prototype over a fake ws + fake timers — the window's ops held, the slab then the ops, the watermark = the last applied; seq ≤ opSeq skipped + dedup by id; a lagged inside the window re-attaches from the old position and the newer snapshot supersedes with ONE rebuild; a held resume while pending, foreign-epoch ops, dispose, the cap — which survives the rebuild's heal — and a throwing rebuild; the seam; wiring; two patched-copy controls: the hold removed reproduces the loss, the overflow re-poison removed loses the op with a clean watermark) · test-reattach-stagger-ui (heavy, 15: chrome + a worktree server, the jitter pinned to 500 ms, the probe typed BY THE PAGE at its own `attached` frame (+1–4 ms, provably inside the window), 12 restarts on the fix = 0 losses (6 with a real-shaped `lagged` frame injected at +200 ms), the view whole and the watermark consistent at +8 s; the pre-fix control build (the hold removed, bundle rebuilt) loses 6/6 while its watermark claims the lost frames).
- 不变量=an op that arrives while a rebuild is pending is applied AFTER the slab it post-dates, never to the list the slab replaces; the watermark advances only for applied ops.

## A HELPER'S PERMISSION REQUEST HAD NOWHERE TO BE ANSWERED — "帮手要权限时没有任何地方能点'允许'" (lane S1, B-6e95, 2026-09-26; both naive-user studies, task T9)

- **What happened.** Study 1 (2.369.177) and study 2 (2.369.186), tester C both times: "use two helpers to read example.com and example.org in parallel". Both helpers sat on "running Fetch page" / "Running: WebFetch" for 4–18 minutes. The status bar's orange "waiting for you" chip said the assistant was waiting for the user; the assistant said it was not waiting; the For-you inbox said nothing needs you; the helper's View Log window had no Allow button. Nothing on any screen could be clicked. After Stop the helper cards read "⟳ running" beside a footer "finished" (study 2) or dropped their titles for the CLI's red internal string "The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use … STOP what you are doing …" (study 1).
- **Measured (CLI 2.1.281, one real parent turn through the CI OAT account, isolated HOME; `scripts/fixtures/helper-ask-2.1.281/parent-stream.ndjson` = that run, ids remapped).** A helper — foreground or background — runs IN the parent's process, and its ask rides the PARENT's stdout: the helper's own assistant records arrive tagged `parent_tool_use_id` (background helpers too, so its tool_use reaches the helper's view before the ask), then `system/session_state_changed {state:'requires_action'}`, then `{type:'control_request', request_id, request:{subtype:'can_use_tool', tool_name, display_name, input, description, permission_suggestions, tool_use_id: <the HELPER's call>, agent_id: <the helper = task_started.task_id>}}` — with NO `parent_tool_use_id`. The answer is the ordinary `control_response {request_id, response:{behavior:'allow', updatedInput, updatedPermissions}}` on the parent's stdin: the helper's tool_result followed 1.1 s later. `stop_task` on a helper whose ask was pending ⇒ `control_cancel_request {request_id}` + `task_updated {status:'killed'}` + `task_notification {status:'stopped'}`. The helper's JSONL did NOT yet hold the asked tool_use when the ask arrived (a file watcher cannot carry it). The binary also names a 5-minute auto-deny for WebFetch's URL-provenance re-ask (`p4n`) — the plain can_use_tool ask has no timeout, which is why the studies waited 18 minutes.
- **Cause.** `MessageManager._processControlRequest` looked the ask's `tool_use_id` up among the PARENT's cards; the helper's tool lives in the helper's view (the stdout consumer routes every `parent_tool_use_id` record there), so the lookup found nothing and returned — the ask was dropped, while `requires_action` still lit the chip. The helper's own view never saw control records at all (only sidechain records are routed to it), and a background helper's View Log opened the transcript on DISK (`sub-agent-<id>`), a snapshot that receives nothing live. Two more holes behind it: `activePendingPermissions` ignored `control_cancel_request` (a withdrawn helper ask — whose tool_result lives in the helper's transcript, never the parent's — would come back after every restart), and a restart's task REPLAY could not find a background helper's card (the launch ack's text blocks are an ARRAY in real records, so the ack synthesis never indexed an Agent card; every suite had fed the ack as a string).
- **FIX.** ONE model, PURE `src/helper-ask.js` (which record is a helper's ask; its Agent call through task_started; the chip / card / inbox words; `pendingAsksOf`; `isStopRejection` / `agentStatusWords`; `answerSessionFor`). The PARENT's normalizer hangs the ask on the helper's Agent card (`helperAsks`, held until the card learns the helper's id — a rebuild replays task records after the transcript), settles it from `control_response` / `control_cancel_request`, and derives `ended` when the helper's card is over; `_taskMsgFor` finds a card by its minted id (`<session>:t:<tool_use_id>`). THE LIVE GATE (`normalizers.feedLive` and the rebuild's drain) hands every control record to the helper's own view too (`routeToHelperView`), and a view created later — a restart's watcher re-arm, a late viewer — is seeded from the parent's cards (`seedHelperView`, at all three creation sites); an ask that reaches a view before its tool card is held for that card. The normalizer publishes `pending-asks` (a meta op + the attach payload's `pendingAsks`); the chip NAMES who waits (`waitingChip`) and a click jumps to the card (`ChatView.jumpToPendingAsk`: pages the card in by `msgIndex`, scrolls, flashes); it also stands on a pending ask alone (after a restart the turn state is unknown until the next record) and retires with the process (`_retireLiveClaims`). The card is THE permission card (`renderPermissionOverlay` with a `mount` — lane L's words and widened Always Allow included) inside the helper's Agent card, saying who asks and what for; the fold never swallows a card holding a waiting ask. A helper's View Log opens LIVE (`sub-<tool_use_id>`) while the helper runs, carrying `agentId` so the server falls back to the transcript once the live buffers are gone; its Allow names its own virtual id and the ws case routes it to the PARENT by the request it answers (`helper-asks.sessionForAnswer`), and an answer no live session holds is SAID (`permission-unrouted`). `src/server/helper-asks.js` files ONE For-you item (origin `agent`, action `helper-ask`) for an ask unanswered for 60 s and resolves it when the ask settles or on the reconciliation after a restart. After Stop: the helper card's chip is patched in place (`stopped` — "Stopped before it finished"; `killed` too), and a foreground Agent call stopped by the user keeps its title and says "Stopped before it finished" instead of the CLI's canned string. `control_cancel_request` is on the stream-type census (the study log's "unhandled" line).
- **Gates.** test-helper-ask (fast, 63: the PURE tables; the measured stream through the REAL normalizers + gate — one card per ask on the right Agent card, the same request on the helper's tool card, Always allow settling both, the stop withdrawing the other; restart in both orders, a late view seeded, a view that sees the ask before its card; session-store honouring a withdrawn request with its control; the inbox at 60 s and its resolution; a view's answer reaching the parent's stdin as EXACTLY the frame the CLI took; wiring pins; two patched-copy controls — the pre-lane normalizer drops the ask, the gate without its route leaves the helper's card button-less). test-helper-ask-ui (heavy, 40: a stub CLI speaking the measured shapes behind the real chat-wrapper — the cards under their Agent cards, the chip naming two helpers and landing on the oldest, Allow in the LIVE View Log answering the parent's stdin, a server SIGKILL + restart keeping the pending card on a reloaded page, Always Allow on the parent card, a foreground + a background helper stopped mid-ask; CONTROL: the pre-lane normalizer in the scratch worktree shows the studies' page — chip, no card, no button). test-turn-truth-ui's claims census gained the pending asks.
- **Observed, not this lane's (unverified against master):** in the heavy leg, a page that was NOT reloaded after a server SIGKILL + restart once (1 run in 4) showed a pre-restart slab after its re-attach had landed, and records written in the first seconds after the restart were missing from it; the leg now reloads the page after the restart (it then judges only what the restarted server rebuilt) and waits for a probe turn to render before its post-restart legs (5/5 green).
- **Verify r1 (adversarial, permission/kill class; two gaps measured on the lane's own normalizers, both fixed in the lane).** ① A `permission-response` for a request the parent already knew as settled wrote a SECOND `control_response` (an allow then a deny for one request id), and an allow was written for a request the CLI had withdrawn with `control_cancel_request` — the ws case now asks `helper-asks.settledState` BEFORE `answerPermission` and refuses with `permission-settled` + PURE `answerRefusalWords` (unknown requests still pass: older than the buffer = the CLI's). ② A killed / exited parent left its helper-ask For-you item open forever, and a 60 s timer armed before the kill fired on the dead normalizer and filed a fresh item for a session nobody can answer in — the kill path and the exit path now call `helper-asks.forget(session)` (timers cleared, items resolved, a late sync a no-op). ③ A `background_tasks_changed` level set that omitted a still-asking helper (message-manager's soft close, `status:'finished', closedBy:'level'`) made `askState` derive `ended` — the parent card lost its buttons ("the helper has finished") while the CLI still waited, and they came back only after a restart (no level set is replayed); `askState` now treats a level-closed card as open (a pending ask contradicts a guessed close), and `settledState` refuses only a RECORD-settled request, never a derived end. Recorded, not fixed: a typed For-you REPLY on a helper-ask item is offered (replyVerdict knows no card-answered action) — it never approves, but it resolves the item while the card still waits; a future CLI stamping `parent_tool_use_id` on the control_request would be routed to the helper's view only (the consumer's sidechain branch `continue`s before `feedLive`) — the parent card would go silent again; a session that died while the server was down keeps its item until dismissed.
- **Verify r2 (adversarial, fresh angles — the two recorded mediums fixed, the re-attach loss above fixed, three more fixed).** M1: a typed For-you REPLY on a `helper-ask` item now answers `card_item` (PURE `replyVerdict`, `CARD_ACTION_TYPES`; HIDDEN — no Reply button drawn; the route 409s by name, writes nothing, resolves nothing — before: `ok:true`, the item resolved `reply` while the helper still waited). M2: a CONTROL record a future CLI stamps with `parent_tool_use_id` falls through the consumer's sidechain branch to `feedLive` (`CONTROL_RECORD_TYPES` in claude-stream-json.js — routed to the helper view ALONE it left the parent chat silent again, round 1's F4); `helperAskOf` honours `parent_tool_use_id` with or without `agent_id`, `_noteHelperAsk` finds the card by the call the record names, normalizers' `helperCallFor` routes by it — pinned on the REAL consumer over a fake pty with a control. **New (C, each measured then fixed):** ① A WITHDRAWAL AFTER OUR ANSWER READ "✓ Allowed" — an Allow written while the CLI's `control_cancel_request` was still in the pipe reached the CLI after it withdrew the request (dropped: an unknown id), yet the card said Allowed on a stopped helper (race attack: 5 of 10 rounds on the stub's own stdin order); 2.1.281 removes a request's abort listener in its `finally` the moment it settles (read in the binary), so a cancel for a request we answered PROVES the answer was not taken — `_settleHelperAsk(rid,'cancelled')` now overrides our own `allowed`/`denied` (test-helper-ask ⑨ + control). ② ONE FOR-YOU ITEM, TWO WAITING ASKS — the store is idempotent BY TEXT per session, so one helper's parallel tool calls (two WebFetch in one turn) or two helpers with one description share ONE item re-pointed at the newest request; answering that one resolved the item while the twin still waited (the M1 class: the pointer gone). `resolveItems` now re-points an item whose request settled at a live twin with the same words and resolves it only when none waits; it also runs BEFORE the filing loop, so an ask past the store's 20-open-items-per-session cap is filed in the same sync that makes room, not one answer late (⑩ + two controls). ③ A STALE VIEW LOG ANSWER REACHED THE RESUMED PROCESS — the Agent call id is the CONVERSATION's, so after Terminate + Resume (or beside a fork) a View Log window's frame (`sub-<call>`) for the dead process's request matched the NEW session by its view id; `sessionForAnswer`'s view-id rung now routes only a request the matched session KNOWS (`knowsRequest`: parent index, orphan, main card, a helper view's card) — else `permission-unrouted` (⑧ + control). A CRAFTED frame naming the new session DIRECTLY with the old id still passes (r1's rule: an unknown id is the CLI's to judge; no UI surface produces it — measured: the resumed window renders no card for the old ask) and is inert on 2.1.281 (`handleOrphanedPermissionResponse` acts only on a `toolUseID`, which the adapter never sends). **不变量: never add `toolUseID` to the permission response without first refusing unknown request ids — with it a stale Allow into a resumed process RUNS the orphaned tool_use.** Attacks held (real page, stub CLI, `s1-verify-r2.md`): two helpers asking with the SAME tool + input are two cards and Allow / Always Allow on one leaves stdin with exactly ITS request id (the widening answers no other request); an answer racing the cancel writes 0 or 1 frame, never one after the server read the cancel (r1's settled guard), and the card now says what the CLI did; a frame naming the DEAD session is `permission-unrouted`; any authenticated ws client of the instance may answer any live session's card (one user per instance, multi-client by design — the rule) and its second answer is refused like anyone's; ONE answer path (census ⑤ (r2): `answerPermission` is called only by the ws case behind `settledState` and the takeover seam over pending cards; For you carries no answer control); an XSS-named helper's item is text in the store and on the page; 21 helpers asking at once: 20 items (the store's cap), one per request, no duplicate across a restart inside the 60 s window (the clock restarts — F8, LOW), the 21st filed by the answer that makes room, every item resolved by its answer. Recorded LOW: a dead window keeps its cards' Allow/Deny (pressing says "did not reach the agent"; pre-existing for main cards); a helper's pending BROWSER approval is not part of the takeover's stale sweep (`pendingPermissions` reads main cards only; including helper asks needs the helper's own browser key to judge `isDefault` — a lane J/P decision).
- 不变量=every permission request a running process makes is answerable where the user is looking — the parent chat, the helper's own log, the waiting chip and the For-you inbox all lead to ONE card, and a request is settled on every surface by whichever of them answered it — and ONE request gets ONE answer on stdin: a settled request is refused with a word, never re-answered.

## A GATE BOUND WAS THE RUNNER'S SPEED, NOT THE MECHANISM'S (2.369.191, lane dserve-bound, 2026-09-27 — the 2.369.189 Actions mirror red)

- **What happened.** The mirror of 2.369.189 (run 36313086151, a 2-vCPU runner, job `fast`) failed ONE assertion of test-desktop-serve, lane C r5 L4: every fact held (exit 125, the runner's line naming the lock, "the install did not start", the lock free) but `l4.fx.ms < 1000` read 1002 ms. Green here in every integration and on every mirror since the leg shipped.
- **Mechanism (measured).** The launcher's pidfile wait is a POLL loop, never an event: `while [ ! -s $P ] && [ ! -s $X ] && [ $n -lt 200 ] && [ -e /proc/$b ]; do sleep 0.05; n=$((n+1)); done` — 50 ms polls, cap 200 = 10 s. The runner is the launcher's background child (`setsid` execs in place, so `$!` is the runner): once it exits it is a zombie (`/proc/$b` still exists) until dash reaps it inside the next blocking wait — the one for that poll's `sleep` (`waitpid(-1)`) — so the loop leaves at the first check after the poll during which the runner died: at most one poll outlives it. Measured with a counting `sleep` on PATH: idle, the runner refuses ~12 ms after the launcher starts and the launcher answers at ~65 ms after ONE poll; inside the suite (its own 40-trial parallel section) 219–287 ms, 1 poll; the leg alone pinned to one CPU at nice 19 beside two `yes`: 930–1550 ms, 1–2 polls (the old bound failed 5 of 7); the whole ORIGINAL suite on two CPUs each shared with a `yes`: the mirror's single red reproduced, 2328 ms. The 1002 ms was the spawn chain (sh → id / sha1sum / mkdir / date → the setsid shim → setsid → sh → flock) on a starved box, never the wait.
- **FIX (gate only — the product was right).** The leg asserts the wait's own EXITS: no pidfile, no exit file, fewer polls than the cap (a PATH `sleep` counts them) ⇒ by the loop's only other exit, the runner was gone; beside it `ms < AT_ONCE_MS` = ½ × the cap READ FROM the module's exported launcher text (`waitOf`, spelled-once asserted), the slack stated (the control is killed at the bound, so ½ keeps it at 5 s; 2.3× over the slowest chain measured). CONTROL: the copy without `[ -e /proc/$b ]` still polling AT the bound, the runner's refusal in its log, its poll count past the fix's. The sweep converted every other upper bound in the suite (the table is in the commit): the launcher refusals (L5 / no flock / read-only / the L3 squat: `polls === 0` + AT_ONCE_MS; L8: the recorded exit 125 + polls < cap), M1 (code 0 = before its deadline), the SIGKILLed-holder leg (½ × the lock wait's 20 s cap, read the same way), the in-process host_needs_daemon and bootstrap-failure legs (`beforeTurn`: settled before a setImmediate armed beside them; the bootstrap asked once, never the deadline's words), the connect deadline (its own words `within <connectMs>s`, no upper bound), install past installMs (the code is the evidence, no upper bound). Lower bounds on a deadline the leg set use one named `EARLY_MS` (a libuv timer is armed against the cached loop time; slowness only raises a lower bound).
- **Gates.** test-desktop-serve (fast, 197): ×5 local + ×3 more, ×1 on two starved CPUs (the original: the mirror's red; converted: green); the leg ×3 under `taskset -c 0 nice -n 19` + two pinned `yes` (old bound red 3/3 at 1314–1550 ms; new green 3/3 with 1–2 of 200 polls; control green 3/3).
- 不变量=a wall-clock bound in a gate is the mechanism's constant × a stated slack (read from the module, never a literal), and the EVIDENCE that the mechanism acted — which exit a loop took, which words a deadline says, whether a call settled before the loop turned — is the claim; the clock only separates it from the pre-fix. A mirror-only red names the machine-dependent gate first and is reproduced by starving the box (two CPUs each shared with a `yes` reproduced this one exactly).

## A LARK PICTURE WAS "[image]" AND A BARE "image ⬇"; THE PANEL OPENED ON 879 CONVERSATIONS (R3, 2026-09-26, the owner on 2.369.185)

- **What happened.** The owner, on the aggregated-IM release:
  - "lark图像不能预览吗？" — a Lark message with a picture drew the text "[image]" and an "image ⬇" chip.
  - "开头不要把所有消息都放进来，很多是没用的，建议只放重要消息/conversation（比如推送给agent了的，或者某个agent刚刚读取了的），并展示一个小tag表示状态。" — the first screen was "879 个群 · 0 条未读", every conversation by time.
- **Cause (pictures).**
  - The record → on-demand fetch → cache → route chain worked: production held the two JPEGs, one fetched 5 minutes after the other. The chip was `img.onerror`'s FALLBACK, and it threw every reason away.
  - The first walk after the boot spent the 60/min budget (≈110 requests in 75 s). A picture refused in that minute became a permanent silent chip, and so did one from a dissolved chat or a non-raster type.
  - Around it: no single-flight (N thumbnails of one picture = N charges); no memory of a vendor refusal (every re-open re-asked it); the owner record found only in the newest 5000 records; a sync LRU write per cache hit.
- **Cause (first screen).** The first screen was `groupListRows` sorted by activity with nothing to rank on. No agent read was recorded anywhere (`readFor` returned the tail and forgot). The wake ledger did not name its target. The owner's own replies were not indexed.
- **FIX (pictures).**
  - PURE src/channel-attachments.js `fetchVerdict` is the ONE order: cache first · a remembered vendor refusal · ours only (`?msg` via `store.findRecord`) · fetchable · enabled · JOIN a fetch in flight · the back-off (a vendor rate limit is the account's) · the budget · fetch. The route adds `retry=1` (the person's Retry), a 429 for `rate-limited`, and `no-store` on every refusal.
  - The window: `thumbVerdict` — a wait retries itself (≤ 2), anything else is the NAMED chip with Retry, a non-raster file is the download chip "no preview"; telemetry `chan-attachment-failed`. The drawn picture's placeholder leaves the text line.
  - Lark images carry `placeholder` and no invented name; a wrapped post reads one body.
  - The LRU ledger is coalesced.
- **FIX (first screen).**
  - PURE src/lib/channel-focus.js `statusTag` / `focusRows` / `firstScreen`: a conversation matters when awaiting / unknown / assigned on its own (a rule / account grain only once a wake was DELIVERED in 24 h or is held — D4, 2026-09-27) / read by an agent in 24 h / held / replied by the owner in 24 h, with ONE tag by that priority.
  - The engine publishes the facts on `rowView.touch`: `agentReads` stamped by readFor after the reach check (60 s per tail, 5 principals, one partial broadcast), `wk.name`, `selfAt` (isSelf / the owner's sent proposal / the one-shot `healSelfAt`).
  - The panel: "{n} need attention | All {n}", the filter, "{n} more in All", the message search across accounts.
- **Gates.**
  - Fast: test-channels-images (61), test-channels-focus (116), test-channels-lark-shape ⑨ (94), test-vendor-whitelist §7 (91: the ORDER as a census of the source, six ungated copies red), test-channels-groups-ui (62).
- **Verify r1 (2026-09-26, the adversarial pass).** Two mutants of the engine fetched every picture at INGEST and BOTH gates stayed green: (a) an internal `attachment(rec.id, convId, id)` queued per fresh record on the next tick — §7's ON-DEMAND census counted `.fetchAttachment(` (still one) and a RECEIVER-NAME list of `.attachment(` callers (`engine()`/`eng`/`channels`/`c` — an internal call has no receiver, a wiring file's `engine.attachment(` has another), and test-channels-images' "ingest fetched NO bytes" pin counted SYNCHRONOUSLY before the tick; (b) a wiring file's own `engine.attachment(`. FIX = §7 counts EVERY `.attachment(` in the server tree (exactly one, the route) and every BARE `attachment(` in the engine (exactly one, its definition); the images pin settles 80 ms first; both mutants are controls (six copies now). Also: a reader / a principal that arrives without a display name was worded by its RAW id (`rd.name || rd.id`) — a tag is worded by its KIND instead ("an agent" / "a Task Group", `channel-focus.js` carries `kind`, never the id; test-channels-focus ④ NEVER A RAW ID, three languages). 不变量=an ON-DEMAND gate counts every spelling of the call (bare and every receiver) and settles before it counts; a tag never shows an id.
  - Heavy: test-channels-aggregate-ui ②b, test-channels-groups-e2e ⑨, test-channels-e2e ⑰ (every tag word fits 75 % of line 2 with ≥ 18 px for a name, en/zh/ja × two faces, a shrink-the-words control), test-channels-i18n.
- 不变量=a picture the vendor sent is shown as a picture, fetched on demand under the budget, and one that cannot be drawn says why; the first screen is the attention list, the full list one switch away.

## TWO VIEWPORT SETS IN FLIGHT WERE TOLD APART BY SIZE, A DESKTOP SWITCH NEVER STOPPED THE VOTE, AND A SECOND SPLIT HOST PUSHED THE PHONE'S ACTIVE WINDOW OFF THE SCREEN (lane S4 verify r1, 2026-09-26)

- **What happened.** The adversarial pass on lane S4 (the live view fits its pane), each finding reproduced before its fix. ① THE SELF-CALL IDENTITY: the bridge recognised its own `set viewport` mirror by the size it asked for. Constructed on the fake upstream that mirrors as 0.38.1 does (a `launch` pair, then the verb's pair, in the daemon's processing order): the agent's `set viewport 800 600` landing FIRST and our 700×900 fit landing after it ⇒ the page ended 700×900 — the agent's explicit choice silently overridden, the bridge holding `applied 700×900` beside `agent 800×600` and the next fit announcing "Agent's size 800×600" over a 700×900 page; the reverse order ⇒ the page 800×600 while the viewers were told "fitted 700×900" (`applied` set, no chip, a letterboxed picture with no words). A launch pair while ours is in flight and un-id'ed is taken as ours too (the agent's click's launch pair never reaches a viewer — LOW, recorded). ② A DESKTOP SWITCH: `_hideWin` writes `visibility:hidden` on the window element — no resize, no `visibilitychange` — so the live view kept reporting `visible:true` from the other desktop (measured on the real rung: `fitSent.visible` true, `checkVisibility()` false, the page stayed 599×695, no restore). ③ THE RESTORE RAN MID-TURN: nobody watching for 5 s put the page back to 1280×577 while the conversation was streaming — a reflow under the agent's feet (the phone's "Back to the chat" does exactly this every time). ④ THE AGENT-SET FLAG WAS IN MEMORY: a server restart forgot the agent's choice and the baseline (the builder's known limit). ⑤ THE PHONE: the builder's own phone legs went red twice on this box — a 100 % dark census, no click, no takeover — because the phone's active host sat at y = 844 on an 844 px screen: `.window.tab-split { display:flex !important }` (≤768 px, P7 §4.6, 2026-09-21) displayed EVERY split host, and the phone's windows are `position: relative`, so the desktop leg's earlier split host (chat + live view) pushed the second conversation's host below the screen. Pre-existing on master; lane S4's phone auto-open (a split per browsing conversation) is where a user meets it.
- **FIX.** ① `ownSetOutcome` (PURE): `relay.ordSeq` numbers every ordered record; our command's position (`pending.seq`, kept as `ownDone` past the clearing result) against the agent's (`agent.seq`) — the agent's after ours ⇒ 'agent-stands' (nothing applied, the viewers told `agent`); ours after the agent's, or ours not yet mirrored ⇒ 'agent-overridden' ⇒ `reapplyAgent` puts the agent's choice back through the keeper (`agentSetArgs`: its factor, or `set device NAME`; `ownViewportRecord` knows a pending device by name and a factor only at that factor). ② a MutationObserver on the window element's style/class re-reports the pane (the stage hides the same way). ③ `restoreDeferred(turn)`: a KNOWN 'running' / 'waiting' turn (turn-facts, the keeper's own release rule) re-arms the restore every grace; unknown / idle restores on the clock. ④ `fitNoteOf` on the keeper's browser record (`viewportNoteFor` / `noteViewport`, replaced at every launch); a new relay's first picture forgets an agent choice no longer on the page. ⑤ `.window.tab-split.window-active` on the phone.
- **Measured after.** test-browser-fit 142 (both orders of the race: sets `[[700,900],[800,600]]`, page 800×600, last `agent`; the deferred restore; the note across a new bridge; a stale note healed; controls: no-outcome overrides for good, no-defer restores mid-turn). test-browser-live-fit 50 on the real 0.38.1: the desktop switch ⇒ `visible:false`, the page back at 1280×577 after the grace, fitted again on return; two split hosts on the phone ⇒ 1 displayed of 4, the active at the workspace top (44 = 44), the phone's census 0.06 % dark, the click, the pinch ×2.00, the chip inside the bar under zh / ja with DejaVu Sans forced.
- **Continuation (the verifier died on a usage wall mid-fix; finished by a second pass).** ⑥ THE ORDER JUDGED ONLY AT THE RETURN: the outcome was decided when our CLI call returned, so a mirror landing AFTER the return was outside the judgement — both late (the agent's, then ours) ⇒ 'fitted', then the agent flagged, then ours landed last: page 700×900 under a bridge that said agent 800×600 (the ① bug again); ours late ⇒ the put-back replaced `pending` and our own late 700×900 mirror was read as the AGENT's new choice. FIX = `beginOwn`/`setAsideOwn` keep an un-landed set of ours in `prevOwn` (still recognised as ours), and the result that lands after its return is judged THEN (`lateJudge`, never for a put-back). ⑦ (LOW 8) a picture neither exact nor 'scaled' once the page had its time (6 frames AND 1.5 s, or 5 s) ⇒ `applied = null`, `failed` for 30 s, ONE `unavailable` (`viewport_not_taken`) — never over the agent. ⑧ the first-picture forget of a stale agent choice asked 'exact': a headed browser draws an agent width < 500 px 'scaled' ⇒ the choice was forgotten on a reconnect and fitted over; now only 'other' forgets. ⑨ (F6, MEDIUM) OUR resize is ONE `viewer-fit` trace row (kind `viewport`, `live view: set viewport W H (fit|restore|put-back)`, "page size" in the Actions pane) tapped to the recorder at our result mirror — never our raw mirror, never a viewer's command; the agent's own `viewport` stays an observation. The other half of F6 (the viewport in `session info`) is NOT done: `session` is a refused verb of `vibespace-browser`. ⑩ F4's fix turned two gates red that the first pass never ran: test-window-binding-model's stylesheet pin (the old unscoped rule, spelled verbatim) and test-browser-multiview's phone leg — which counted the group's pane while the LAST-CREATED live view was the active window: it passed only because the unscoped rule displayed an inactive split host beside it (the ⑤ bug); the leg now brings the group on screen through `goToWinId` and asserts it is the ONE window displayed.
- **Measured after the continuation.** test-browser-fit 158 ×3 (13 patched copies: + no-late-judge ⇒ page 700×900 under agent 800×600; no-prev-own ⇒ bridge agent 700×900 over an 800×600 page; no-not-taken ⇒ applied 700×900 over a 1280×577 page, silently; agent-exact-only ⇒ a headed 390×844 fitted over; no-trace-row ⇒ 0 rows). test-browser-live-fit 53 (+ CONTROL: the view built without the observer keeps `visible:true` from the other desktop, the page never restored; CONTROL: the pre-fix phone rule displays 2 windows, the active at y = 844 under a 44 px workspace top). test-browser-live 217, test-browser-multiview 37, test-window-binding 63, test-split-ux 193, test-window-binding-model 134.
- 不变量=two commands to one daemon are ordered by the daemon, never by the size they asked for; a viewer's vote follows what it can see, and every hider that writes the element's style is a hider; the restore never reflows a page the agent is reading; a choice the bridge must honour across a restart lives with the thing it describes; on the phone exactly one window is displayed.

## THE LIVE VIEW'S PAGE WAS NOT THE PANE'S SIZE — A BAND ON THE DESKTOP, A 260 px STRIP ON THE PHONE, A WHITE PICTURE UNDER A LOADED URL (lane S4, naive-user study 2, 2026-09-26, all three testers)

- **What happened.** Study 2 on 2.369.186 (docs: SharedContext vibespace-naive-study-2.md, 坏了 "手机上的实况窗口" + 让人困惑 "实况画面只占窗格上面一截"): on the desktop the picture was top-aligned and full width (lane J) but used only the top 40–60 % of the pane, black below (tester-a T2-03, tester-c T10); on a 390 px phone the page rendered at DESKTOP width and shrank into a ~260 px strip, the "Pricing" link 20 px wide, no pinch; the live view did NOT open when the assistant started browsing (the desktop did) and its only entrance, the status-bar "Agent browser" chip, sat entirely off-screen at x≈403 (tester-c T12); a live view stayed blank WHITE while its URL said example.org and the assistant said it had loaded (tester-b T7-08).
- **Cause, measured on agent-browser 0.38.1** (the real binary through the keeper of a scratch instance; the shapes are scripts/fixtures/browser-stream/fit-0.38.1.json). ① The stream draws the page at the viewport it HAS — headless 1280×577 (a 1280×720 claim), headed a 1241×1252 page downscaled into 714×720 — and nobody ever sized it: `set viewport W H` makes every frame W×H (headless; headed ≥ 500 px wide), so a view could have asked. ② The phone had no auto-open at all (`autoBindLiveViews` returned [] on `isMobile`) and the chip was one item of a swipe scroller, in the middle. ③ THE BLANK PICTURE: the bridge's per-viewer `frameGate` DROPPED a frame that arrived inside a viewer's fps gap, with no trailing delivery, while Chrome's screencast sends only on DAMAGE — a page that paints twice inside 66 ms (a white commit, then the page) and sits still had its final paint dropped for good (reproduced in the fast suite: the viewer keeps "white"); and a same-document navigation (a hash change) measured a `url` record and ZERO frames, so a view could not tell "the same pixels" from "no picture".
- **FIX.** PURE src/browser-fit.js + the bridge + the keeper + the view. The view REPORTS its pane (`fit {width, height, dpr, visible}` — the canvas's box in CSS px at net zoom 1, never device px: a DPR-3 phone asks for a 390-wide page; `visible:false` off-screen) on hello and on a settled ResizeObserver; THE RULE (`fitTarget`): the HOLDER's pane while somebody drives, else the LARGEST visible pane, ties → the earliest viewer, a hidden one never votes; the bridge sets the page through `keeper.setViewportFor` = the daemon's own `set viewport W H` under the target's own session (debounced 250 ms, single flight; factor 1 — measured: a factor never enlarges the frame and a factor change on a static page produced NO frame), never starting a browser (a stopped / absent / inactive one is refused with no CLI call); every viewer is told (`{type:'fit'}`, replayed to a late one) and letterboxes a page that is not its size by the page's own aspect (never stretched). The mirror of OUR set (its `launch` pair + `viewport` pair) is dropped before the taps and the fan-out; an AGENT's `set viewport` / `set device` is a flag on the target that outlives the relay — never overridden (the view letterboxes and its chip says "Agent's size W×H"; "Fit the page to the window" = `fit {force}` is the one act that takes it back). A headed window that cannot be that narrow (390×760 ⇒ a 390×593 frame of the page scaled 0.78) is read off the picture (`fitHonored` 'scaled') and re-fitted at 500 px, the pane's aspect kept. Nobody visible for 5 s ⇒ the page goes back to the size it had before the first fit (a return inside the grace cancels it). THE TRAILING FRAME: a viewer the gate refused a frame gets the relay's LATEST frame the moment its gate opens (`S.frameGateWait`), and a viewer back from 2 fps catches up. THE FRESH FRAME: a navigation no upstream frame followed within 1 s — or a viewer's `refresh` (≤ 1 per 2 s) — is answered with a picture asked of the page itself (`keeper.freshFrameFor` → `captureFrame`: CDP layout metrics + one jpeg `Page.captureScreenshot`, server-side; measured: the capture makes the screencast emit its OWN next frame 3/3, so the captured picture is the fallback). THE VIEW'S CLOCKS: no frame 2 s after the stream opened / after a navigation ⇒ "Waiting for a picture…" (a stale picture dimmed, one `refresh` asked), 10 s ⇒ "No picture … came in 10 s" + Reconnect. THE PHONE: `autoOpenOnPhone` opens the live view as the desktop does (the same NEW holder row, the same `win-blive-<session>`, born as the chat's split partner) only when that conversation is ON SCREEN, reveals it full screen with a "Back to the chat" toast; two fingers pinch-zoom the picture in watch mode (a transform, origin top-left, 1–4×, pan, double tap), a tap maps through it (the pointer reads the TRANSFORMED rect), a second finger in takeover is refused with a hint; the "Agent browser" chip is sticky at both edges of the swipe bar, cut to 46vw. Setting `browser.fitPageToView` (default ON; OFF = the pre-S4 view). The toast stack is `width: max-content` (a `left: 50%` box shrink-fitted every phone toast into half the screen).
