## A TAKEOVER FOUND NOTHING TO STOP — THE RUNNING ACT WAS KEYED ON A LEASE OBJECT A RE-ATTACH HAD REPLACED (desktop lane E, verify r3 F1, 2026-09-26)

- **What happened.** The r2 fix (the entry below) made a running injection cancellable: `act()`'s `injecting` registered its AbortController on `lease.acting`, where `lease` was the object `requireLease` returned at the TOP of `act()`, and `takeover` / `dropLease` cancelled `leases.get(h).acting`. Between the two sits the verb's probe (`ensureResolved` up to MODE_PROBE_MS on a young `auto` share, the window plan, the input-backend probe on a cold cache). If the same session DETACHED and RE-ATTACHED there — or the user revoked, shared again and the agent re-attached — the lease map held a NEW object: the re-check (`held()`) passed on it (same `sessionId`), the injection registered on the DEAD object, and the takeover's cancel looked at the new one and found nothing. Reproduced deterministically (the user act fired at the start of `probeInputBackends`, a takeover 100 ms into a 400 ms type): `ok` after 403 ms, `killed: []`, `lease.input === 'user'` — the agent's text kept landing through the takeover, exactly the interleave r2 closed. The fix's own mechanism, defeated by an identity it assumed.
- **FIX.** Running acts are kept PER WINDOW HANDLE in the engine: `acting: Map<handle, Set<AbortController>>` (in memory, never persisted); `injecting` registers on `actsOn(rec.id)` in the same tick as the re-check that precedes it, removes itself when the child is gone, and `cancelActs(handle, why)` — called by `takeover(h)` and `dropLease(handle)` — aborts every act running on that window, whichever lease object started it. An injection belongs to the window's DISPLAY: that is where the user's keys and the agent's would interleave.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A running act belongs to the WINDOW HANDLE, not to the lease object that started it; a takeover cancels by handle. (2) A value captured before an await is a SNAPSHOT: an identity check after the await (`sessionId` equal) does not make the captured object the live one — register on, or look up by, the key the canceller uses. (3) When a fix adds a canceller, the race legs include the actor REPLACING the object between the capture and the act (detach + attach, revoke + re-share + attach), not only the actor withdrawing it.
- Gates: test-window-targets §5 — two legs (`at: 'probeInputBackends'`, the user act `detach + attach` / `revoke + grant + attach`, then a takeover 100 ms into `type-keys`) ⇒ window_paused + did.partial + `killed = ['type-keys']` + the lease kept; CONTROL = the r2 lease-object-keyed act rebuilt as two edits of the source (registration on the captured `lease`, the cancel reading the current lease's set) ⇒ both legs answer ok after the whole injection while the r2 leg without a re-attach still passes on it.
- 不变量=a running act belongs to the WINDOW HANDLE, not to the lease object that started it; a takeover cancels by handle.

## A TAKEOVER DID NOT STOP THE AGENT'S TYPING — THE RE-CHECK RAN BEFORE AN INJECTION THAT KEPT RUNNING (desktop lane E, verify r2 L5, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** Verify r1's `stillHeld` stops a verb BEFORE it injects — but an xdotool already running after that check was never cancelled. `type` injects 12 ms a character (measured 12.5): a takeover 1 s into a 15 s type let the agent's remaining text keep arriving on the same display while the user typed, their keystrokes interleaved; a revoke did the same. Reproduced with a fake xdotool that runs 2 s and a takeover 300 ms in: `takeover` answered ok, the type ran to its end and answered ok at 2009 ms. Beside it: `TYPE_MAX` 4000 × 12 ms = 48 s against a FIXED 20 s timeout — a long type was killed mid-text and answered `inject_failed` after ~1,600 characters. And the obvious fix is itself a hazard, MEASURED on Xvfb with an xev witness: SIGKILLing a running `xdotool type` between a key's press and its release leaves that key HELD, and the X server autorepeats it — 37 presses in 1.5 s; a CJK character typed through xdotool's scratch keycode stays held the same way. The old timeout kill had that hazard too.
- **FIX.** Every injection runs as the LEASE's cancellable child: `act`'s `injecting(call)` keeps an AbortController on `lease.acting` (in memory; r3 F1 — above — moved it to the WINDOW HANDLE: a re-attach replaced the lease object); `dropLease` (a revoke, endHold, the consent switch, detach, a session ending) and a new `takeover` call `cancelActs`, which aborts it — `runInject` passes the signal to `execFile` with `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'`, so node kills exactly THAT ChildProcess by its handle (never a name, never a group) and resolves only after its 'close'. Every killed run (the cancel or the timeout) then goes through `releaseHeld`: each keysym the act could have pressed (the text's distinct characters, the shift levels, ctrl + a for `--replace`, a chord's modifiers + key, a click's / scroll's button) is mapped to its keycode on the display NOW and released through XTEST (python3 + ctypes; an unmapped keysym is skipped for free — no remap storm; a release of a key not down is dropped by the server), falling back to `xdotool keyup` / `mouseup` of the always-mapped keysyms. The cancelled verb answers what `stillHeld` says (`window_paused` / `not_exposed` / `not_attached`) with `did: {partial: true}` — the route carries it and the CLI says "stopped part-way, look again". `TYPE_MAX` = 1500 and `typeTimeoutMs(n)` = 5 s + 2 × 12 ms × n.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A running act is cancellable by the takeover: whatever the user's "stop" withdraws must reach the act that is ALREADY executing, not only the next one — the lease owns the act's child, and dropping the lease or taking over kills it. (2) A cancel kills only what the lease owns, by its handle — never a name. (3) Killing an input injector is not stopping it: the keys and buttons it may hold are released before the verb answers (a kill alone types into the user's window). (4) An act's time limit is derived from its size — a limit the largest legal act cannot meet turns every large act into a mid-way kill.
- Gates: test-window-targets §2b (the budget pin + the 4000 / 20 s control; an aborted type answers at once, its child dead, a same-named decoy alive; the release fallback recorded; a chord killed by its timeout and a cancelled click released), §3 (THIS box's Xvfb + the GTK fixture: a type cancelled mid-key leaves exactly `entry 'q'`; CONTROL = a patched copy without `releaseHeld` ⇒ `entry 'qqqq…'`), §5 (a takeover 100 ms into a running type ⇒ window_paused + did.partial + the child killed + the lease kept; a revoke 100 ms into a running scroll ⇒ not_exposed + did.partial; CONTROL = `cancelActs` neutered ⇒ the type runs to its end through the takeover; the route's 409 with `did` and the CLI's "STOPPED PART-WAY").
- 不变量=a running act is cancellable by the takeover — kill the lease's own child by its handle, then release what it held.

## A REVOKED WINDOW STILL TOOK THE AGENT'S CLICK — THE REACH CHECK DID NOT SURVIVE AN AWAIT (desktop lane E, verify, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** Lane E's window-targets engine checks reach ONCE, synchronously, at the top of every verb (`requireLease` → `requireReach`). Everything after it awaits: an `auto` share's tree probe (up to MODE_PROBE_MS = 3000 ms on a young app), the helper's snapshot, the input-backend probe, the window plan, the display geometry, the focused node, the screenshot grab. A revoke that landed there did not stop the verb. Reproduced with a fake keeper and a wt whose calls sleep 400 ms, the user's revoke 100 ms in: `revokeReach` answered `leaseDropped: true`, then `click --at` still injected, `click @ref` still ran the node's do_action and answered ok, `snapshot` handed the revoked session the tree, and `attachWithMode` answered "attached" with a lease that no longer existed. A Task Group left mid-probe, a takeover mid-verb (§6.6: "a takeover STOPS INJECTION") and the real-desktop switch going off had the same hole. Bounded to one verb, but it is the one rule the reach model exists for ("revoking … the agent's next verb answers not_exposed" — the verb IN FLIGHT was the leak).
- **FIX.** `stillHeld(rec, facts, verb, {paused})` in src/server/window-targets-engine.js re-asks the whole decision — the window still live, the desktop switch still on, the caller still reached (`requireReach`: audited by:reach, a lease it still holds dropped), the lease still its own, not taken over — IMMEDIATELY before every act (actOnNode / injectClick / injectScroll / focusNode / injectType / injectKey — no await between the check and the call) and before every hand-over (a snapshot's nodes + refs, a screenshot's file — unlinked first — and an attach's answer after its probe). The verb is linearized either before the withdrawal (it ran) or after it (`not_exposed` / `window_paused` / `not_attached`) — never across it.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) An authorization checked before an await is a claim about the past: every act and every hand-over re-asks it after the LAST await before it, with nothing awaited in between. (2) The withdrawals are one set — a revoke, a group left, a takeover, a consent switch off — and one re-check covers them all; a second copy per withdrawal drifts. (3) A refused verb hands NOTHING over: the image it grabbed is deleted, the tree it read is not returned, the lease it did not keep is never reported as held.
- Gates: test-window-targets §5 — seven race legs over a delayed fake wt (click --at, click @ref behind an unresolved auto probe, snapshot, attachWithMode, a Task Group left during a key, a takeover during a type, a screenshot whose image is deleted) + the linearization's other side (a revoke after the act was issued lets it stand) + CONTROL = a patched engine copy with `stillHeld` neutered through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs ⇒ the revoked `click --at` is injected. **Verify r2 (M1, 2026-09-25):** the whole-function control proved nothing about ONE site — four single-site mutants (the scroll, the typed keys, the app-window screenshot, the tier-3 screenshot) passed every behavioural leg of the suite (the verifier: 244/0; reproduced on a copy of the tree). Now THE PER-SITE CENSUS: every `held()` / `heldOrUnlink(` / `stillHeld(` call is grep-derived and printed, a patched copy with only that call replaced by the unchecked lease must turn ≥ 1 deterministic race leg red, a `// no-await-before` site is listed as redundant by construction with its claim checked in the code. 不变量 (5): a re-check is pinned per SITE — a control that removes the whole mechanism proves the mechanism matters, not that each call of it does.
- 不变量=an authorization checked before an await is a claim about the past — re-ask it after the last await, immediately before the act.

## A SNAPPED DESKTOP-APP WINDOW HUNG PAST THE WORKSPACE AND WAS CUT (inc-muhmqvzf-jodk, 2026-09-26 — the owner on a Mac, 1920×963 CSS, DPR 2, UI 100 %, the sidebar open, a desktop on a 1×3 grid: "chrome吸附在右侧，右侧有截断")

- **What happened.** A Google Chrome desktop app dropped into the right third of the 1×3 grid showed its right side cut off (the action ring: two clicks at x = 1912, on the last visible pixels of Chrome's half-cut ⋮). MEASURED by a live reproducer (real xpra 6.5.3 + google-chrome 153 / gnome-calculator 50, headless Chrome over CDP at 1920×963, every act a trusted drag / resize / the product's maximize; 202 states on 2.369.177 and lane D) — every candidate inside the picture was ruled out: the main window mapped at 0,0 and equal to X's own geometry in every state, the canvas backing = the X size, Chrome accepted every fit down to its minimum, the pane covered the picture to ≤ 1 CSS px, every map-window already final (no F3 race). The picture was complete; the WINDOW hung off the screen. The owner's snapshot (1 canvas, 1.6 Mpx = 1000×1606 = Chrome at its minimum width) and layouts.json (grid {1,3}, sidebar open) matched exactly one state: the grid's right cell with the window held at its minimum. `WindowManager._positionToCell` wrote `left = g + col·(cw+g)`, `width = cw`; the cell (478 CSS on the owner's ~1450 px workspace) was narrower than the window's own minimum (the app's `minimum-size` through `windowMinForPane`: 502 CSS on 2.369.177, 512 on lane D where Chrome draws its own frame), so CSS held the element at its minimum and it grew RIGHTWARD from the cell's left edge — 20 (29 on lane D) CSS past #workspace, whose `overflow: clip` cut it: 38 / 58 device px of Chrome (the ⋮, lane D Chrome's own ✕, on 2.369.177 our title-bar ✕ and Paste). The same pattern sat in `_applySnap`, `snapToHalf` and `_snapToGridRange` (the calculator, 618 CSS tall at 2×, on the bottom half: 360 device px of its keypad under the taskbar; DPR 1: 180), in `_applyGridBounds` (layout restore / sync / desktop switch / the workspace reflow when the sidebar opens), the restore from maximize, and createWindow's default cascade (UI 125 %: 70 + 620 on a 685.6 layout px workspace ⇒ 9–11 device px cut at rest). `keepInside` existed but only `_applyOwnMin` (a minimum ARRIVING) and lane D's `resizeWindowTo` called it. And the written law said the opposite of what happened: window-min-size.js's header promised a cell smaller than the minimum leaves the window "overlapping the neighbouring cell honestly (never squeezed, never cropped)" — at the right / bottom edge there is no neighbouring cell, so the overlap was a crop.
- **FIX.** ONE placement for every path that puts a window into a zone: `WindowManager._placeWindow(win, zone, gap)` over PURE `zoneBox(zone, min, ws, gap)` (window-min-size.js) — the zone raised to the window's effective minimum (the workspace-capped `_ownMinOf`, the .window floor included) with the growth slid toward the INSIDE: a box that would end past the workspace edge (less the 4 px snap gutter) slides left / up just enough, never past the workspace's own left / top edge; a zone that ALREADY ended past the edge (a window the person dropped hanging off the screen) keeps its own right / bottom edge — the minimum never adds a crop, and a window without a raised minimum is never moved. ## A PAGE THAT MISSED A BROADCAST WIPED ANOTHER CLIENT'S PER-APP CHOICES (desktop apps lane D verify, 2026-09-25 — found by the adversarial verifier before the lane shipped)

- **What happened.** `src/lib/desktop-app-prefs.js` (the ONE loader of the per-app maps `desktopAppScale` / `desktopAppFrame` in user state) read user state ONCE per page and then only listened to the `user-state-updated` broadcast, and a save PATCHed the WHOLE map built from this page's copy (`{desktopAppScale: {...}}`). The route's PATCH is the B-b87b belt — merge-only at the TOP level (`{...cur, ...data}`) — so the belt bounded a stale page's damage to "the key it edited", and for a nested per-app map that key is every app. Measured on a real server with two headless-Chrome pages, the launch dialog open on both: B's socket dropped (WsManager reconnects by itself in 2–3 s — a lid, a network blip); A stored xterm 2× ⇒ `{"xterm":2}`; B reconnected, its xterm card still read "Auto" (nothing re-read); B stored the Calculator 1.5× ⇒ the server held `{"gnome-calculator":1.5}` — A's choice gone, no toast anywhere. B saving while its socket was still down did the same (`{"gnome-calculator":2}`). The frame map rode the same loader.
- **FIX.** (1) The loader RE-READS on every (re)connect (`ws.onStateChange` ⇒ GET; a GET answer never overwrites a map a broadcast replaced while it was in flight) — the rule desktop-app-window.js already kept for its record ("a server restart adopts before any client reconnects — re-read on every reconnect"). (2) A save is an EDIT of ONE app's entry, `saveAppPrefs(key, (map) => setScaleChoice(map, appKey, choice))` (a whole map is refused): shown locally first (the view = the server's map + this page's edits in flight), then applied to the map the server holds NOW (a fresh GET) and PATCHed as that one key; one save at a time per page. (3) A refused save rolls the view back to the server's map and toasts the reason (it used to keep showing the unsaved choice until an unrelated broadcast silently reverted it). After, same recipe: B read "2×" once reconnected, the server kept `{"xterm":2,"gnome-calculator":1.5}`; saving while disconnected kept `{"xterm":3,"gnome-calculator":2}`.
- **Residual (named).** Two pages editing the same map inside one GET→PATCH window (tens of ms) are last-write-wins for that map — the same-key race the B-b87b belt already documents for user state until a rev protocol lands.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A client-side mirror of server state is re-read on every reconnect — a broadcast sent while the socket was down never arrives, and a missed broadcast must not become a permanent divergence. (2) The merge-only write protects only at the granularity it merges: a NESTED map written from a local copy is a whole-document write one level down — write an entry edit applied to the server's current value, never the value itself. (3) An optimistic local write is undone when the server refuses it.
- Gates: test-desktop-app-scale §8 (two pages over a fake server that merges exactly as src/routes/persistence.js does and broadcasts only to connected sockets, both maps: the reopen re-reads; a save after it, and a save from a copy that missed a broadcast, keep the other page's key; a refusal rolls back, told twice, one toast; two quick saves both land; a whole map refused — CONTROLS as patched copies: no reconnect re-read, the old local-map PATCH, a kept refused edit) + the §7 census (every `saveAppPrefs` call passes an edit) + heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §14 (1b) (the verifier's recipe on two real pages). The same suite's §12 (8) read user state ONCE right after the local-first view flipped — a judge racing the write (red on both attempts once the save gained its GET); both reads now wait for the server's copy, the assertion unchanged.
- 不变量=a mirror re-reads on reconnect, and a nested map is written as an edit of the server's current value — a page that missed a broadcast never writes its copy.

## A SCALE ▸ RELAUNCH FROM 2× TO 1.5× FILLED THE WINDOW WITH THE APP'S OWN BACKGROUND (desktop apps lane D (a), 2026-09-25, the owner with a screenshot: "从2x切换到1.5x之后出现大量白边，你窗口尺寸计算不对")

- **What happened.** GNOME Calculator relaunched through its window's Scale ▸ from 2× to 1.5× on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen showed its keypad in a narrow column with wide white bands either side. MEASURED on the real rung (xpra 6.5.3 + gnome-calculator 50, headless Chrome at DPR 2 / 1.5 / 1, the window's own Scale ▸ path): OUR geometry was exact at every transition — the X main window equal to the pane in device px, margins 0/0/0/0, 0.0 % of the pane uncovered. The white was the calculator's own background: `scaleKnobs` spelled a fraction by the FLOOR rule (1.5× = GDK_SCALE 1 + 144 dpi — GTK has no fractional GDK_SCALE on X11, so the widgets stayed 1× and only the text grew), and libadwaita clamps its content column (~676 logical px). The relaunch HALVED every widget and the column (676 → 338 CSS px at DPR 2) in a window that kept its size: the app's own background went from 25 % to 62 % of the width. The "1.5× (text only in GTK apps)" label had said so; nobody reads a label as "your window will be two-thirds empty".
- **Three smaller places OUR margins did appear (measured, fixed with it):** every CSD connect mapped the app at the pane with the bars still unfolded (the fold waited for `on.main`, emitted after the fit) and re-fitted ~160 ms later; a pane below the app's minimum was scaled to fit with bands of pane background (DPR 1 at 2×: 116 CSS px each side, 25.8 %); GTK's own snap ~650 ms after the map plus the belt's same-task re-fit shrank and regrew the canvas backing, clearing the rows in between for ~110 ms.
- **FIX.** (1) A fraction is a REAL scale: `scaleKnobs` draws at GDK_SCALE ⌈s⌉ (96 dpi) and the record carries `pictureScale` = s ÷ ⌈s⌉, which the view divides into its ratio (a resampled picture; integers stay 1:1; the browser rows keep the dpi rule — Chrome scales whole from Xft.dpi, measured). The record stores what it was drawn at (`gdkScale`, `pictureScale`) and the client reads the record (`renderOf`) — an older record or an older paired machine is shown as it was drawn. (2) The window keeps the app's LOGICAL size across a relaunch (PURE `relaunchPaneCss`, applied by the asking client through `WindowManager.resizeWindowTo` after `retarget` has cleared the old minimum). (3) F3: the client names the main before it fits it; the fit keeps the pane's shape below the minimum; a shrinking window keeps its backing 1 s.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) "Scale n×" means everything the app draws is n× — a knob that scales only the text is a different setting, never a spelling of the scale. (2) A relaunch that changes an app's scale keeps the app's LOGICAL size; the window is the app's frame, not a fixed rectangle the app is poured into. (3) What the machine drew with is a FACT of the record (`gdkScale`, `pictureScale`) — a client never re-derives it from the number (an older machine drew differently). (4) Before blaming the window, measure the app's own pixels: margins 0 with a white screenshot means the white is the app's.
- Gates: test-desktop-apps §14 (the knob table, `renderOf`, `relaunchPaneCss` + round trips, a floor-knobs CONTROL copy), test-xpra-client §7 (F3 with the old-order CONTROL, the picture scale, the kept backing), heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §15 (DPR 2 and 1, auto → 1 → 1.5 → 2 → auto → 1 + a resize: ≤ 1 CSS px margins and 0.00 % bare pane at every step, the window = relaunchPaneCss, the column ∝ the widgets' true scale, every map = the final size; CONTROL copy: 2× → 1.5× column ratio 0.500 in a window that kept its 898 px).
- 不变量=a scale scales the widgets too, and a relaunch keeps the app's logical size — the white was the app's own background, measured before the window was blamed.

## A WORKFLOW WINDOW SAID "RUNNING" AND "(agent)" ×11 FOR A RUN THAT HAD STOPPED TWO DAYS EARLIER (2026-09-26)

- **What happened.** The owner opened a View Workflow window: chip 运行中, "11 个 agent · 10 完成 · 运行中…", a note claiming phase names and labels appear when the run finishes, eleven "(agent)" rows under ONE phase titled with that same sentence ("…这个workflow怎么没有细节"). The run's newest file was two days old; its 11th agent never wrote a `result`; there was no terminal snapshot `wf_<runId>.json`; the server had restarted seven times since (first 7.5 h after the stall), so the launching session's normalizer no longer held the run's `task_progress` tree and the persisted 40-record `taskRecords` ring had been displaced by later runs. The window fell back to the disk skeleton, `routes/sessions.js liveWorkflowFromParts`, which wrote `label: ''`, `model: ''`, that phase title and `status: 'running'` UNCONDITIONALLY. Every `started` line of the run's journal carried `label` + `phase`, and every `agent-<id>.meta.json` carried `description` / `workflowPhase` / `model` — since CLI 2.1.267 (measured over 495 run dirs); the memory-level fact "journal.jsonl = resume cache, no labels; no live progress source" had been true for ≤ 2.1.263 and went stale.
- **FIX.** PURE `src/workflow-disk.js` `parseRunDir`: labels (journal ?? meta), phases in spawn order, model, the journal's state arithmetic moved verbatim (+ a `failed` record ⇒ `error`), and a LIVENESS verdict — a live tree ⇒ running; else the newest file of the run younger than 10 min ⇒ running; else **stalled** with `{lastActivityAt, unfinished}`. The route's four live returns go through ONE seam (`liveView`), the local read is async, the remote compound probe ships the metas and the HOST's clock. The window says 已中断 · "最后活动 2 天前；1 个 agent 未完成" and marks the resultless agent unfinished; the chat card's chip gets the same verdict through the status bar's existing poll (one `stallWords` for both).
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) The run dir is the truth when the stream is gone: labels and phases from journal/meta, liveness from mtimes — a run with no result and no recent write is stalled, never running. (2) A fallback view states what it KNOWS; it never claims a later source will fill in what is already on disk, and a status nobody observed ("running") is a verdict, not a default. (3) A file-format belief is re-measured when the CLI moves — the census (record types × key sets × CLI version) is cheap and its absence cost this report.
- Gates: scripts/test-workflow-disk.mjs (fast — the pre-move arithmetic reference, the parse + liveness tables, zh/ja words, the REAL route over a scratch home incl. snapshot-untouched / resume / live tree, the REAL remote probe script, two patched-copy controls); test-fold-ux F5 (heavy, chrome, zh — the window over a real stalled run dir and the card's chip; control: the pre-fix server answer fails the same judge).
- **Lane Q verify (2026-09-26, six findings, each reproduced red first).** ① (minor) a tree REPLAYED after a restart re-proved a run that stalled days ago running (liveness `tree`) — the builder's own known limit: `taskInfo.aliveAt` (live now / the persisted `cur.at` on replay / none from a history conversion) + PURE `treeAlive` (open AND fresh < 10 min); trade-off: a run whose agents and tree are both quiet 10 min reads Stalled until its next record. ② (minor) the level set closed a running Workflow through its SECOND key (the wf_ run id the ack registered; the set names only the short task id) — so any quiet stretch after a level set read Stalled while the card said finished: the set names a CARD by any key, plus the belt (`treeAlive` counts a level close — a guess — as open); control = both layers stripped. ③ (minor) a stalled run was dropped from the status bar's poll, so a run that wrote again flipped the window to Running while its card kept Stalled: it stays tracked (`wf.stalled`, 15 s) until a terminal answer or a 404. ④ (low) a stalled view with a merged tree drew the live-tree note beside the Stalled chip: PURE `liveNoteKind`, the stall first. ⑤ (low) a clipped 500-char label had no title. ⑥ (low) the remote probe's newest mtime missed meta.json (NMT added) and a missing NOW fell back to the hub's clock (now: 0 ⇒ `unknown`). Gates: test-workflow-disk §3b/§5/§7/§8 (the REAL rebuildHistory + the REAL normalizer under the route, patched copies of the route / normalizer / probe as controls), test-workflow-live-view §2 (per-KEY control), test-task-lifecycle (the stamp), test-fold-ux F5 (the card comes back in 16 s; control = the pre-fix drop on a twin run).
- 不变量=a proof of life carries its own clock — a replayed record is as old as its arrival, never as young as the replay; and a guard that judges by KEY must know when two keys are one thing.
- 不变量=the run dir is the truth when the stream is gone: labels and phases from journal/meta, liveness from mtimes — a run with no result and no recent write is stalled, never running.

## A LIVE VIEW THAT JOINED AN OPEN STREAM NEVER HEARD IT OPEN — THE TAKEOVER NEVER TOOK THE KEYBOARD (2.369.180, lanes H + J integrated)

Found by the heavy tier on the integration tree (test-browser-live ⑥, red twice, green on lane J alone): Take over answered `mode: takeover, mine`, focus went to the view's sink, and yet `ownsKeyboard()` was false — chip hidden, no ring, the attach's `chatView.focus()` took the caret back and "tomsmith" landed in the chat composer. `keyboardOwnership` (lane J r2) takes `connected` from the view's `st.connected`, which only the bridge's `upstream-open` BROADCAST sets; lane H's recorder taps a holder's relay (and so opens its upstream) before any view joins, and `attachViewer` replayed status/tabs/url/frame/viewport to a joiner but never the bridge's own transition record. So every live view of an ephemeral browser read itself disconnected — harmless before lane J, fatal for ownership after. FIX: a viewer that joins a relay whose upstream is open gets `{type:'status', state:'upstream-open'}` after the hello; the bridge leg asserts it for the late viewer, and a copy without the line reproduces both reds (9 FAILED). 不变量=a state a fan-out relay broadcasts on a transition is also said to whoever joins after the transition; a fact two lanes read is checked on the path the OTHER lane creates.

## GATE SUITES SHARED THE SINGLETON DESKTOP'S :7 / 5901 — AND LEFT IT RUNNING (the heavy RED on 69720f2b, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** The heavy tier went red on test-desktop-app-window's last leg — the singleton Desktop's status chip never settled (`null`), twice — while the same tree passed 133/133 in a lane's own run and a lone re-run passed. src/vnc.js's singleton takes X display `:7` and RFB port 5901 unless `VIBESPACE_VNC_DISPLAY`/`_PORT` say otherwise, and ADOPTS any listener on its port (by design). This box got Xtigervnc on 2026-09-21, so every scratch server that opened the Desktop started or adopted ONE Xtigervnc shared by every run and by the owner's production instance — and nothing stopped it at server exit. Observed live three times in 20 minutes from other lanes' runs: `Xtigervnc :7` alive in a deleted `/tmp/vs-deskapp-smoke-*` scratch dir; 40 s later another run's server connected to it (ss: ESTAB from that server's pid to the orphan) and the leg printed ✓ with the message "this box has no Xvnc". The reaper never listed it: its argv[0] is `Xtigervnc`, not on `REAP_NAMES` (dry run: master 0 display orphans, the fix 1). And `:7` is in the band `-displayfd` hands out lowest-first to every desktop-app keeper's Xvfb (measured picks `6 9 11 12 13 14` around a live :7): with a keeper-style Xvfb holding :7, master's suite goes red with the heavy gate's exact `null` (Xtigervnc :7 exits "already active", 5901 stays dark, the chip reads "VNC server failed to start").
- **FIX.** (1) Per-run names: scripts/scratch.mjs `vncEnv()` (a free port + a display from 1000 up with neither lock nor socket), spread into the env of every `server.js` spawn in 60 suites; test-architecture §57 is the census. (2) A THROWAWAY server (code under the temp dir — server.js `throwawayRoot`) stops, at SIGINT/SIGTERM, the Xvnc THIS process spawned (pid + /proc start time; never an adopted one, never the pid file's pid); an installed server's desktop still outlives a restart. (3) `Xtigervnc` joined `REAP_NAMES`.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A server's DEFAULTS are machine-global names too: a gate suite hands every default that names a machine resource (a port, an X display, a socket) a per-run value — the §6 rule for literals extended to the env. (2) A resource a process STARTS is its to end, identified by what it recorded at the start (pid + start time), never by a file that outlives it; ADOPTION is the one thing a shutdown never undoes. (3) A leg that accepts two outcomes must say which one it saw and why — "✓ … since this box has no Xvnc" hid an adoption for four days. (4) A guessed display number is a bet against every `-displayfd` user on the box (the residual: production's `:7`).
- Gates: test-desktop-app-window (the chip by the box's own facts, the run's own names, SIGTERM ⇒ no Xvnc and nothing on its display; CONTROL = a patched server copy without the hook leaves its Xvnc alive), test-vnc-view (the stop rule over stand-ins; CONTROL = the pre-fix pid-file `stop()` signals a stranger), test-ci-gate §9b (fake /proc incident row, the stale rule with the pre-fix name set as a patched-copy control, a dry run on the real /proc), test-architecture §57.
- **Same day, same class — the root only in the arguments.** test-browser-resources' worktree server started two shell sessions under dtach; killing the server ended neither (detached by design), and they ran with the REAL HOME and cwd `/tmp`, so the reaper — which read roots off cwd/HOME/device env only — never saw them: 140 dtach + pty-wrapper + zsh from 20 runs. FIX = `argvScratchRoots` in the reaper (any argv token that starts with, or after `=` names, `/tmp/vs-…`; never the product's `/tmp/vs-ab-<uid>`; test-ci-gate §9c + two patched-copy controls) and `endRootedProcesses(root)` in scratch.mjs, called by the suite's teardown, which now asserts nothing its server started is alive.
- 不变量=a gate suite gives every machine-global default a per-run value, and a throwaway server ends what it started — never what it adopted; a suite that boots a server owns what that server detached.

## A HEAL THAT REMEMBERS NOTHING IS A LOOP: THE HEAL IS EVIDENCE-BOUND AND BUDGETED (lane H verify r5, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** r4's heal (the keeper's own `get cdp-url` relaunching a closed profile browser inside its live daemon) remembered nothing but its failed-heal gate — `rec.closed`, set only when `get cdp-url` FAILED — and cleared `browserLost` / `closed` after every answer, whether or not a browser was then identified. Two shapes, one root. (a) THE STORM: a Chrome that dies ~1 s after every relaunch (a crash-on-load page, a headed window the user keeps closing, an OOM-killed Chrome) was relaunched on EVERY tick while any conversation held the profile — forever, the record `ready`, the panel "running", nobody told, the agent's lease seeing a new blank browser every 5 s (`tab_gone` on every verb), and under memory pressure a positive feedback loop (a 165 MB headless Chrome every 5 s). ## A PROFILE BROWSER THE PRODUCT CANNOT RELAUNCH IS A DEAD LEASE: HEAL WHERE THE ABSENCE IS SEEN (lane H verify r4, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** r3 built its re-capture on the measured fact "when the daemon's Chrome dies the daemon lives and ITS NEXT VERB relaunches Chrome in place" — and in the product nothing ever sent that verb for a named profile. Agents run under their LEASE's session over `AGENT_BROWSER_CDP` (a CDP client of the keeper's Chrome — it cannot launch), and the keeper asked under its own session only when the record's cdp url was null, which `followRelaunch` nulled only AFTER a relaunch had been seen. So after the user closed a headed profile window (or Chrome crashed) the profile stayed `ready` on a dead port for the rest of the conversation: every agent verb `CDP WebSocket connect failed … Connection refused` (mediated: `502 Bad Gateway`), the live view `stream_unavailable`, no typed code, no remedy, and a held lease with `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=0` meant nothing ever ended the state. The r3 suites drove the relaunch BY HAND under the keeper's pairs, which is why they were green. Ephemerals were not affected (their verbs run under the daemon's own session).
- **Reproduced before the fix.** The verifier's p1-real.mjs (real keeper + 0.38.1 + Chrome, 3/3): SIGTERM the Chrome → `/resolve` ready, `record.browser` null, the dead port; the lease verb and an `open` refused, 0 Chromes on the directory, the tick changing nothing, the view `stream_unavailable`. In the suites on 29795c01: test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (h) — after the leased tick / an attach alone / a view's port: 0 chromes, the lease's next `/resolve` carrying the dead url (…-<old pid>); test-browser-mediation-chrome ④ (the real binary): 0 Chromes after the tick and after an attach, every lease verb `Connection refused`.
- **FIX.** `followRelaunch` HEALS where the absence is seen — the tick (while a lease holds the profile: nobody is asking for a window to reappear otherwise), a start's live return (every attach / every agent verb) and a view's port: when the daemon is provably ours and the browser the record had identified is GONE (`rec.browserLost`, set by `recaptureBrowser` — a provider whose browser was never identifiable is never healed), `healBrowser` asks `get cdp-url` under the KEEPER's own session and launch view, which relaunches Chrome IN that daemon (measured 147–167 ms: a new pid whose parent is the daemon, a new `DevToolsActivePort`), re-captures it, and `leaseCdpUrl` repoints the mediated grants; a non-mediated lease gets the new port from its next `/resolve` (every verb asks). NEVER over a directory somebody else now holds: the lock is judged first and a foreign holder (the user opened the profile themselves) is REPORTED — the attach / view refused `profile_locked` naming its pid — never raced (a relaunch there would open a window in THEIR browser). A relaunch that fails is `browser_closed` by name (never a dead port), retried by a verb at once and by the tick after 30 s; a browser launched with a provider's own flags (cloak) is not healed by a bare re-ask (said, `browser_closed`). With `--pin-tab` (0.38.1's floor) the lease's bound tab died with the old Chrome, so its first verb after a heal is the binary's own typed `tab_gone` naming the remedy (`tab new <url>`) — the agent learns its page is gone instead of "Connection refused" forever (measured; deliberately not a silent rebind to a blank page).
- **Gates.** test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (h) (the fake's `get cdp-url` relaunches a dead chrome in a live daemon like 0.38.1: the leased tick, an attach alone and a view's port each leave ONE chrome under the daemon, marked, a NEW DevToolsActivePort, the record's and the next `/resolve`'s url on it; an UNLEASED profile is not relaunched by the tick and is healed by its next start; control: a keeper copy with no heal ⇒ 0 chromes, the dead url, via the tick and via an attach) · test-browser-mediation-chrome ④ (heavy, the real 0.38.1: SIGTERM the Chrome, then a `tick` ALONE and an `attach` ALONE each leave ONE Chrome whose parent is the daemon, a new port, the old lease env `Connection refused`, the next `/resolve` env answering over the new port (`tab_gone` → `tab new` → `open` + `get title`); control: a keeper copy (scripts/mutant-copy.mjs) with no heal ⇒ 0 Chromes, `Connection refused`).
- 不变量=a profile browser the product itself cannot relaunch is a dead lease — heal where the absence is seen, from the one process that can launch, and never over a directory someone else now holds.
- **r5 correction (2026-09-25).** The heal above had no memory: a browser that kept dying was relaunched on every tick forever, and one that died before its recapture was recorded a success with its evidence wiped (the dead lease again). It is now evidence-bound and budgeted — the section "A HEAL THAT REMEMBERS NOTHING IS A LOOP" above; a view heals only a leased profile.

## OWNERSHIP OF A PROCESS IS PROVEN BY A MARK WE PUT ON ITS COMMAND LINE, NEVER BY THE DIRECTORY IT SITS IN (lane H verify r4, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** r3 replaced the scrubbed namespace witness with "its `--user-data-dir` IS a directory the keeper minted (`~/.agent-browser/vs-<id>`) and no live daemon parents it". That is a property of the DIRECTORY, not of the launch: a Chrome the HUMAN opened on that folder (to look at what the agent logged into) met it exactly, and the keeper ended it on three paths — (A) the profile stopped, the human opens it, the AGENT's next start SIGTERMed the human's window ("ended its own orphaned browser … before launching"); (B) the daemon alive, its Chrome dead, the human opens the folder, the daemon SIGKILLed ⇒ the tick ended it; (C) the same, then `stop(idle)`. The owner's law is that a used session is reported, never killed. The real Chrome's environ is scrubbed to one variable, so nothing about the launcher survives on the process — except its command line.
- **Reproduced before the fix.** The verifier's p2-human.mjs (real keeper + 0.38.1 + `/opt/google/chrome/chrome` launched by hand, no daemon, no `--remote-debugging-port`): the human's Chrome ended on A, B and C (`exit 0`). In the suites on 29795c01: test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (c2) — A: the start ran and the human's chrome was gone; B: the tick after the SIGKILL ended it; C: `stop(idle)` ended it; the PURE row "minted, no mark" answered `own-orphan`; test-browser-mediation-chrome ④: a real Chrome launched by hand on the minted directory ended by the start ("no refusal").
- **FIX.** THE LAUNCH MARK. Every browser the keeper launches runs with a config whose `args` carry `--vibespace-keeper=<profile id>` (a named profile, `machine-<id>.json`) or `=<browser key>` (an ephemeral: `machine-ephemeral-<key>.json`, or rung D's generated `<key>.json` / a child's `<key>.<n>.json` written by browser-env) — measured on the real 0.38.1: the config's `args` reach the Chrome's title-rewritten command line and Chrome runs normally with the unknown switch. PURE `profileLockVerdict`: `own-orphan` = the recorded identity (pid + starttime) OR the holder carries THIS record's mark (`keeperMarksOf`: exact on a NUL-separated argv, words on a title-rewritten one; any directory — only the keeper writes it: `RAW_ARG_RE` drops `--vibespace-keeper` from every user and project file) OR, for a launch that predates the mark (the upgrade window), a minted directory and the CLI's own `--remote-debugging-port=0` with no mark at all — each only while no live browser daemon is its parent or grandparent. A holder with ANOTHER record's mark is VibeSpace's but not this record's (`foreign`, "another VibeSpace browser", never "the user's"). A holder with no mark is `foreign`, `user:true`: left ALIVE, reported once in the journal ("… is held by pid N, which is left running"), and a start refused `profile_locked … is open in a browser VibeSpace did not start (pid N) — it may be your own browser — close it first`. Because a config whose `args` differ makes the daemon's next verb relaunch its Chrome (measured), a record keeps the config it was LAUNCHED with for every later call (`rec.mark`; a record from before the mark keeps the unmarked file) and a lease's own session (it never launches) keeps `machine.json`.
- **Gates.** test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (c2)/(c3) (the fake's chrome now runs the config's args + `--remote-debugging-port=0` like 0.38.1; the keeper's own chrome carries the mark; A refused by name with the human alive, then closed by hand ⇒ the start runs; B the leased tick does not relaunch over the human (0 relaunches), an attach refused, the SIGKILL + tick ⇒ stopped with the holder reported and alive; C `stop(idle)` alive; a pre-mark orphan ended; another record's mark refused, never "the user's"; 11 new PURE rows; control: a runtime neuter restoring "minted alone" ends the human's chrome on A, B and C) · test-browser-mediation-chrome ④ (heavy, a real `/opt/google/chrome/chrome` launched by hand on the minted directory: refused by name, alive, then closed by hand ⇒ one marked Chrome; control: "minted alone" ends it).
- 不变量=ownership of a process is proven by a mark WE put on its command line, never by the directory it sits in — a human's browser on our directory is reported, never ended.

## THE r4 LOWS: A RELAUNCHED EPHEMERAL IN A NEW TEMP DIR, A WRAPPER RECORDED AS THE BROWSER, THE IDLE OF NOW, A RENAMED MACHINE'S LOCK (lane H verify r4, 2026-09-25)

- **LOW 3 (rung N).** A daemon SIGKILLed inside the ≤ 5 s window after an in-place ephemeral relaunch (before any tick / start / view re-captured it) leaked that Chrome and its new temp dir (measured: p3-eph-b). FIX = the mark: `reapOrphan` of an ephemeral also asks `browser-facts.markedBrowsers(<key>)` (an async /proc walk) and ends every browser carrying the conversation's mark with no live daemon above it, whatever its directory. Gate ⑥ (d3) + control (the scan neutered ⇒ it leaks).
- **LOW 4.** `browserOfDaemon` took the shallowest argv match, so a wrapper between the daemon and Chrome that does not `exec` was recorded as the browser; after the daemon's SIGKILL the tick "ended its own orphaned browser" (the wrapper) while the Chrome lived on holding the lock (p4-fake H). FIX = the directory's LOCK names the browser: `lockHolderFacts` reports `ancestors` (parent + grandparent) and a live daemon among them; `captureBrowser` / `recaptureBrowser` prefer the lock's holder when this daemon is its parent or grandparent, and `browserOfDaemon` prefers the lock holder of the directory it found. Gate ⑥ (i) + control (the r3 capture ⇒ the wrapper recorded, the Chrome survives).
- **LOW 5.** An ephemeral was launched with `idleMs()` NOW while the session's commands carry the spawn pairs' frozen `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`; the binary restarts a daemon whose idle differs, so a live change of `browser.idleTimeoutMs` restarted every existing session's browser on its next verb (p5b). FIX = the launch takes the pairs' idle (`pairsIdleMs`). Gate ⑥ (j) + control (the setting NOW ⇒ 300000).
- **LOW 6.** A minted directory whose lock names another hostname answered "that machine's browser must close first" — impossible after a pod restart under a new name with a persistent home. FIX = the refusal names the lock file and both remedies: close it on that machine, or (this machine renamed) remove `<dir>/SingletonLock`. Gate ⑥ PURE.

- **What happened.** r2 recorded the Chrome each launch started and ended it when its daemon was found gone — but measured on the real 0.38.1 (five shapes: with / without a profile × idle 0 / 600000 × the keeper's config), when that Chrome dies (the user closing a headed window, a crash) the DAEMON LIVES and its next verb relaunches Chrome IN PLACE: the same daemon pid, a new Chrome pid, a new `SingletonLock` and `DevToolsActivePort`, and without a profile a NEW temp `--user-data-dir` (the old one deleted). (b) A WITNESS THAT HOLDS ON THE REAL BINARY replaces the scrubbed one: a holder is the keeper's own when its `--user-data-dir` IS a directory the keeper MINTED (`<home>/.agent-browser/vs-<id>`, an ephemeral's own dir, the temp dir recorded for an ephemeral's browser) and no live daemon parents it — `reapOrphan` judges the lock of every minted dir of a record whose daemon is gone, `clearProfileLock` before every launch; a holder on a directory the keeper never minted is `profile_locked` naming the pid, and ONLY that refusal says it may be the user's. - **What happened.** Measured on the real 0.38.1: `kill -9` of a profile browser's daemon (a crash, an OOM kill, and exactly what `keeper.stop()` does after its 3 s close grace) leaves its Chrome alive, reparented to the subreaper, still holding `<dir>/SingletonLock -> <host>-<pid>` and `DevToolsActivePort`. On the real 0.38.1 (test-browser-mediation-chrome ④): the daemon SIGKILLed, its Chrome survives, a relaunch under the keeper's own session dies with exit 21.
- **FIX.** (1) The keeper RECORDS the browser each launch started: `rec.browser = {pid, starttime, dir}` = the daemon's child whose command line carries `--user-data-dir` (browser-facts.browserOfDaemon; the binary's temp dir on rung N), on a start and on an adoption. (2) Wherever the keeper sees a daemon gone — the tick, a view asking for its port, a start, stop() after its SIGKILL, a boot — it ends that browser while it is STILL that process naming that directory (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL; `reapOrphan`, single flight per profile; a launch waits on it). (3) BEFORE EVERY LAUNCH on a directory the lock's holder is judged by the PURE `profileLockVerdict`: `own-orphan` (alive, its cmdline names the dir, it is the recorded browser — pid AND starttime — or its environ names this keeper's namespace, and no live browser daemon is its parent) ⇒ ended; `foreign` (another machine's lock, an unreadable process, a human's Chrome, a live daemon holding it) ⇒ refused `profile_locked` naming the pid, never signalled; a stale lock or a recycled pid that does not name the dir ⇒ `free` (Chrome clears it). (4) Liveness is finer than signalling: `pidLiveness` answers `recycled` for a pid that is alive with ANOTHER starttime, and that counts as gone for "is it running" (tick / judgeEphemeral / a view's port / a start) while stop() still signals only a pid proven `ours`, and a starttime nobody could read (`unknown`) is never guessed gone.
- **Gates.** test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (the named, pre-fix-record, stranger, ephemeral and recycled legs + a 15-row PURE table; controls: a keeper copy with no orphan rule ⇒ the child lives and the relaunch dies on the lock; a keeper copy whose liveness is `gone`-only ⇒ the CLI is asked) · test-browser-mediation-chrome ④ (heavy, the real binary: recorded Chrome, the binary's own exit-21 control, the tick ending it, a NEW DevTools port 33677 → 40379).
- 不变量=a keeper that starts a browser is the one that ends it; a lock it cannot prove its own is a refusal by name, never a raw exit code.
- **r3 correction (2026-09-25).** The second witness above ("its environ names this keeper's namespace") never held on the real binary — 0.38.1 scrubs `AGENT_BROWSER_*` from its Chrome — and the recorded browser went stale at the daemon's first in-place relaunch. Replaced by the re-capture + the minted-directory witness (the section above).

A title-rewritten Chrome (ONE space-joined cmdline, no NUL) is read off the joined string, and a process answers the name rule by argv[0]'s first token OR its `comm` (`/usr/bin/google-chrome` ⇒ `chrome`; never comm alone — the claude CLI's comm is its version). The ownership walk runs to a FIXPOINT: a parent that is itself a victim of this sweep owns nothing. Gates: test-ci-gate §9 (+ four mutant-copy controls). 不变量=a production root is never scratch, whatever lives under it.
- **A failed tap was silent.** A verb inside the 30 s backoff after a failed arming recorded nothing and said nothing. FIX: `browser-trace-status {code:'arm_failed', at, until, error}` once per failure (and `armed` to clear); the tool card's empty row reads "not recorded until <t>: <why>" (PURE `armGapFor`). Gate: test-browser-ephemeral ④ L5 (+ a silent-recorder control). 不变量=an action not recorded is said, with when and why.
- **`close --all` under a lease closed the namespace.** The binary's `close --all` closes every session of the namespace — the keeper's daemon and the one Chrome every lease shares. FIX: an attachment's `close --all` is its session's `close` + its lease dropped, said `[close_all_scoped]`. Gate: test-browser-pin ⑤ (+ a CLI copy passing `--all` ⇒ the keeper's daemon dead). 不变量=an agent's verb on a shared browser reaches only its own session.
- **An agent's detach ended the user's takeover.** `detach` → `dropInputsFor` → a `detach` handback the agent caused, and on the conversation's own browser a retire under the user (whose `<key>|ephemeral` state detach never looked at). FIX: `detach({by})` — an agent's (the default) is refused `browser_paused` while the user drives; the UI route passes `by: 'user'`. Gates: test-browser-takeover ②/⑥ (+ a keeper copy without the refusal ⇒ a `detach` handback), test-browser-ephemeral ④ L8. 不变量=while the user drives, every agent act on that browser is refused by name — a detach is an act.

## THE SCRATCH CLEANER CHECKED A NAME BEFORE THE EVIDENCE: LEAKED BROWSER DAEMONS WERE NEVER CANDIDATES (lane H verify r1, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** `scripts/ci.mjs`'s scratch-orphan reaper runs after every gate suite, and `--reap` runs it by hand. It dropped every process whose executable was not on `REAP_NAMES` (`node`, `dtach`, … + `vibespace-device*` + `chrome*`) BEFORE it looked at where the process was rooted (`if (!named) continue;` ahead of the root lookup). Its roots were only cwd / HOME / VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT / VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT. A leaked `agent-browser-linux-x64` daemon has its cwd in a checkout and its only scratch roots in `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR` / `_PROFILE` / `_CONFIG`. A `headless_shell` has cwd `/` and its only root in `--user-data-dir=`. So both were invisible under a DELETED `/tmp/vs-*` dir, and `--reap` said "no scratch orphans" while that class piled up to 1045 daemons/Chromes (47 GB). Field pids 1451570 / 3481895, `ppid 3557` (systemd --user), roots `/tmp/vs-browser-live-1449844` / `-3481295` gone for 3–4 days.
- **Reproduced before the fix.** Six real processes under `/tmp/vs-zz-reapfix-*` dirs that were then `rm -rf`'d, reparented to systemd --user: 1 of 6 listed (the one whose argv[0] was `node`). Not listed: two `agent-browser-linux-x64`, a `headless_shell` rooted by `--user-data-dir`, an env-only root, and the two field daemons.
- **FIX.** Candidacy is the same evidence for every process: the roots now include the three agent-browser env names and a `--user-data-dir` (both spellings). A GONE root lists every member that nobody alive outside the group owns (`members.filter(orphaned)`), whatever its name. The name allowlist narrows ONLY the weaker rule, an EXISTING dir whose whole group is unowned and stale. `--reap` prints every victim (pid, ppid, argv head, root, rule) and a closing count; `--reap --dry-run` signals nothing. After: 5 of 5 probes + both field daemons listed, the `zsh` owned by a live parent spared.
- **The pin that said the opposite.** test-ci-gate §9 asserted "an unlisted executable is never a candidate even under a gone scratch root", so it pinned the bug. It is flipped into the OWNED-SHELL CONTROL: a `zsh` in a deleted scratch dir whose parent is a live terminal outside the group is never listed. An orphaned `sleep` under a gone root now IS.
- Gates: test-ci-gate §9 (+ mutant copies: the name gate restored, the pre-fix four roots, `--user-data-dir` ignored, the gone rule listing every member; each goes red).
- 不变量=a reaper's candidacy is evidence, never a name. A name may narrow a rule whose evidence is weaker; it never gates the evidence.

The recorder taps `EPHEMERAL_REF`, never the default pane, and only a holder. A second shape beside the list (`ephemerals`, `ephemeral: {...}`) is invisible to every reader written against the list. (2) Recording never depends on somebody watching: the tap is armed by the holder, not by a viewer. (3) The event that makes a browser usable is awaited, bounded, before the command it enables runs. (4) A view never starts what the keeper does not hold. (5) A suite's "environmental" skip is a claim. Re-derive it when the same leg can be made to run.
- Gates: test-browser-profiles ㉒ · test-browser-ephemeral ④ (+ a mutant-copy keeper whose holder rows drop the ephemeral ⇒ no row, no `browserLive`, no tap) · test-browser-live ③b (heavy: the shipped CLI's first `open` ⇒ within 5 s a split live view beside the chat, the entry on disk, the card thumbnail, both chips, grey on stop / reconnect on the next verb; the same world with that keeper copy ⇒ no window, no trace, no chip) + ④ (real binary).

The agent cursor overlay goes through the same `getBoundingClientRect` basis (`toLocal`), not a second `offsetLeft/clientWidth` basis. The ephemeral read's `cdp_url` mirror pair is never relayed. FIX: `pinAnswer` notices only a MOVED pin, `noteChange` drops X → X, the ticked row asks nothing.
