- 不变量=the pointer map uses the drawn image's own rect and the frame's real size; the overlay and the pointer share one basis.

## A HAND-ROLLED LOCK WITH A BREAK RULE IS A RACE: TWO STARTS STILL RAN TWO xpra INSTALLS (desktop apps lane C, verify r4, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** r3 made "one install per machine" a lock DIRECTORY beside the state dir: `mkdir` to claim, then an `owner` file ("<pid> <starttime>", tmp + `mv`), a lock whose owner was proven dead broken under a keyed mutex, and a lock with NO owner waited on 2 s and then broken. But every claim leaves the lock ownerless for a moment — between the winner's `mkdir` and its owner rename — and the empty-owner break key was the same for every breaker (`B="$K.break--"`, `gone "" ""` true). A breaker could `rm -rf` the lock in that moment; the winner's `mv` then failed (`mv: cannot stat '…/owner.<pid>'`) and it ran `mine=1; break` anyway while the breaker re-claimed — two runners, two apt-gets. Measured on the r3 launcher: 1–4 in 150 starts over an empty dir at natural speed (the suite itself flaked 1 run in 10), 12/20 trials multi-runner with the rename slowed 30 ms, 17/20 at 50 ms (up to 4 runners, a lock left behind 12 times). Each patch to the scheme (check the owner write stuck, key the wait on the lock's mtime) cut the rate without closing it.
- **FIX.** No lock we manage by hand at all. The launcher opens a lock FILE on LOCAL storage (`/run/user/<uid>` when it is a writable directory this user owns, else `/tmp/vibespace-<uid>` created 0700 — named by the uid since verify r5, never `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`; the file named by the sha1 of the state dir's realpath — the state dir may be on NFS / FUSE where flock is not dependable) as fd 9 and takes `flock -n 9` before it spawns; the detached runner shell inherits fd 9 and so does apt-get (apt-get closes inherited descriptors for the children it forks — APT::Keep-Fds — so dpkg never holds it; a dpkg outliving both is fenced by dpkg's own lock), the launcher closes its own copy — the lock is held by the running install itself and the kernel releases it the instant the last holder exits or is killed. A start that finds it held follows the running install (its pidfile, ≤ 20 s for it to appear); one that later gets the lock answers the recorded exit of the install it waited on (written before the lock freed, dated after this start — in nanoseconds since verify r5), else runs. The runner re-asserts the lock on its inherited descriptor before it records itself. Nothing is ever broken, nothing is stale, no owner file, no 2 s wait; a lock that cannot be taken is a named refusal (exit 125), never a fallback to a racy scheme.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) Mutual exclusion is a thing the KERNEL holds for the holder's lifetime — `flock` on an inherited descriptor — never a file we create, read back, judge stale and break: every "is the owner gone?" answer is stale the moment it is read, and a break rule turns a claim-in-progress into a victim. (2) The lock lives on LOCAL storage (a network filesystem's flock is emulated or absent) and is never deleted (a removed lock file lets two holders lock two different inodes). (3) The lock's lifetime is the WORK's lifetime: the process that does the work (and its children) holds it, not the process that started the work — a starter that dies never frees a running install, a SIGKILLed install never leaves a stale lock. (4) A ~2 % race is never gated by one trial — the pin runs the concurrent starts 40× at natural speed and 20× with the windows widened, with a control that removes the lock.
- Gates: test-desktop-serve §10 (40 natural + 20 widened trials of five concurrent starts, a killed install's lock released at once, a killed launcher's runner still holding it, a held lock waited on then taken, the lock path on local storage, the runner's re-assertion, no flock ⇒ 125 naming util-linux; CONTROL = `flock -n 9` → `true` ⇒ 5 runners per five starts), test-desktop-remote §8 (the device's `installing.lock` under the daemon's runtime dir, held). Measured with /tmp/vibespace-lanes/c5/flock-harness.mjs: 300/300 + 200/200 + 200/200 empty-dir trials, 100/100 + 100/100 killed-install trials, 20/20 runner-only kills — one runner every time.
- **Verify r5 (four lows, 2026-09-25).** L1 "dated after this start" was whole seconds (`-ge`): a start in the SAME second as an earlier install's exit, while a child that install left behind still held the lock, answered the stale exit (6/6) — the exit instant is `date +%s%N`, compared strictly (`-gt`). L2 the lock's holders are the runner shell and apt-get (above), never dpkg. L3 the directory came from `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` — two spawners with different environments named two locks for one state dir, and the `/tmp` name was predictable — it is named by the uid, refused by name when the per-uid `/tmp` dir is not this user's. L4 a runner started without fd 9 refuses (by design) and was reported only after the launcher's full 10 s pidfile wait — the wait ends with the runner's life. Invariant: "the one I waited on" is decided at the resolution of the race it arbitrates, and a shared name is derived from what both parties share (the uid), never from what each happens to inherit (the environment). Gates: test-desktop-serve §10 (each with a control), test-desktop-remote §8.
- 不变量=a mutual exclusion the kernel releases when the holder dies, on local storage, never broken by hand.

## A LEASE REVOKED WHILE ITS CLIENT WAITED ON THE UPSTREAM BECAME A CONNECTION NOTHING COULD CLOSE (desktop apps lane C, verify r3 M3, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** `src/server/cdp-mediator.js` onUpgrade parks the client's socket while it dials the upstream CDP websocket (up to 8 s) — the r2 fix made that park survive a client RESET. But the grant the client came for could MOVE during the park: `up.once('open')` checked only whether the client was still there, never whether its grant was. MEASURED (fake CDP upstream with a 300 ms handshake, the grant revoked at 100 ms): the client was upgraded (101), its `Browser.getVersion` answered by the upstream, `med.list()` already empty — and the connection was in NO grant's `conns`, so revoke's 1008 `lease_gone`, `closeTargetsOf` and `shutdown()` never saw it: after shutdown the upstream was still open (1 opened / 0 closed), and tabs it opened were admitted into a dead grant's scope. A repoint at 100 ms wired the client to the OLD browser (old 1 message, new 0). A shutdown at 100 ms threw on the nulled `wss` (uncaught TypeError — unreachable through server.js, which exits synchronously, but the same hole).
- **FIX.** The park belongs to the grant: `g.pendingUps` holds each dial until its open / error, and `closeConns` — the one place revoke, repoint and shutdown end a grant's connections — also TERMINATES the parked upstreams, the client answered `503 <why>` by the same reason its live siblings get (Lease Gone / Browser Restarting / Browser Stopped / Server Shutting Down). Belt at the open: the mediator not `closed`, the grant still granted, an upstream, and the url dialed still the target's CURRENT one — else close the upstream and refuse 503. Each layer alone refuses (pinned); a retry through the same url reaches the current browser.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) Whatever authorizes a connection must still hold at the moment the connection is WIRED, not only when it was asked for — re-check the grant after every await. (2) An in-flight resource (a dial, a forward, a handshake) opened on behalf of a lease is registered WITH that lease, so the lease's end reaches it; a resource in no owner's set outlives every revoke and shutdown. (3) The refusal a parked client gets says the same thing its live siblings are told (the close reason), never a transport error.
- Gate: test-browser-mediation ③c (revoke / repoint / shutdown 100 ms into a 300 ms handshake; the pre-fix copy through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs as the CONTROL: 101 + the upstream left open, wired to the old browser, the TypeError).
- 不变量=a grant that moves while its client is parked refuses that client — the park is the grant's, re-checked when it opens.

## A VIEWER'S RESET DURING THE PAIRED-MACHINE FORWARD WAS AN UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION THAT ENDED THE HUB (desktop apps lane C, verify r2 F1, 2026-09-25)

- **What happened.** `src/server/desktop-stream.js` handleUpgrade's REMOTE branch parks the accepted socket on a promise while the hub-side forward to the paired machine opens (`ep.then(...)`, 4–600 ms). Node's http server removes its own socket 'error' listener at 'upgrade', and ws attaches one only inside `wss.handleUpgrade` — which this path reaches AFTER the forward. So for that window the socket had NO error listener: a viewer whose TCP connection RESET (a phone switching networks, a killed browser, ETIMEDOUT / EHOSTUNREACH) emitted an unhandled 'error' ⇒ server.js's `uncaughtException` handler ⇒ `process.exit(1)` — the whole instance, every client and agent link cut until systemd's restart. MEASURED (real http server + the bridge, a forward resolving in 300 ms, a raw client sending the upgrade and `resetAndDestroy()` at 60 ms): remote path `listenerCount('error') = 0`, uncaught `ECONNRESET`; local path 1 listener, none; remote path with a FIN, none. The fix's own gate had half-close and destroy legs — both a FIN — never a reset, so it was green.
- **The same shape, second site.** `src/server/cdp-mediator.js` onUpgrade parks the client socket while the upstream CDP websocket opens (up to 8 s): a reset there was the same uncaught `ECONNRESET` (measured), and a client that left first left the upstream connection OPEN (a CDP socket to the browser nobody reads; measured 1 opened / 0 closed). browser-stream.js and path-mounts.js do not park (browser-stream upgrades synchronously; path-mounts listens on both sockets).
- **FIX.** Both sites attach a socket 'error' listener BEFORE the park (it destroys the socket; the socket's 'close' — or the destroyed check at the resolve — releases the forward reference, exactly once) and hand it to ws's own at the upgrade (`removeListener` right before `wss.handleUpgrade`, which attaches its listener synchronously), so the live socket carries exactly what a local one does. The mediator also closes the upstream when its client is gone (closed, or half-closed at the open).
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A socket PARKED ON A PROMISE has no error listener unless you give it one — node removed the server's at 'upgrade', ws adds one only when it takes the socket; an RST in that window is an uncaughtException, and in this server an uncaughtException is the process's exit. (2) A connection gate's legs include a RESET, never only a FIN — `end()` and `destroy()` both close gracefully from the peer's side. (3) A resource opened on behalf of a parked socket (a forward reference, an upstream socket) is released on the socket's own end, not only on the handoff's callback.
- Gates: test-desktop-serve §8 (`racing(S, 'rst')` over a real http upgrade with a process-level uncaughtException trap: none, refs 1 / releases 1; CONTROL = the bridge copy without the parked listener ⇒ uncaught ECONNRESET) + test-browser-mediation ③b (a reset and a half-close during the upstream open: no uncaught error, no upstream left open; CONTROL = the pre-fix mediator copy ⇒ ECONNRESET, the upstream left open). Both controls through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs.
- 不变量=a socket parked on a promise has no error listener — an RST there is an uncaughtException, i.e. the hub's exit.

## A RELEASE OVER A PANE THE PAGE CANNOT HEAR (2.369.200, lane-drag-release — userW's inc-muq7uk0f-e59s + inc-muq7wwfq-rruz; the lane M class, SECOND STRIKE)

- **What happened.** UserW (Mac, DPR 2.2, UI scale 0.9, a PDF `viewer` window over a Desktop window), twice in two minutes: a PDF viewer dropped onto the cell of the Desktop window did not fit — "highlight 不消失并且这个viewer停留在原地"; a resize released over that window kept going when the pointer came back — "松开鼠标之后，仍然像是抓着这个缩放的角落"; and the viewer could grow but not shrink — "能放大，不能缩小".
- **Mechanism (reproduced in chrome on b924041f first — scripts/test-window-drag-ui.mjs).** The title-bar drag and the resize ended on a document-level `mouseup`. A release hit-tested on ANOTHER window's iframe never reaches this document (the embedded page gets every event — the Web view, and the PDF viewer's own page is an iframe); noVNC's canvas `stopEvent`s its mouse events. So a drop or a resize released over a Web view / Desktop pane was never heard: the drag stayed armed, the snap highlight stayed, the next pointermove dragged / resized on. And an inward resize over the viewer's OWN page lost every move the same way — it grew, it would not shrink. The .199 `.window.dragging .window-content {pointer-events:none}` shielded the DRAGGED window's own content, never the target's. (lane M, 2.369.182, hit this class for the outside-press closer and for window activation, 2.369.177 — the same cancelled/stopped press.) The live-view picture and the xpra pane do NOT stop a mouse release (measured, printed) — the Web view and the Desktop are the provable swallowers.
- **FIX.** POINTER CAPTURE at every drag's door: the title bar and each resize handle take a POINTER press and `setPointerCapture` the pointer on that element; the drag is fed from it (capture delivers every pointer event there whatever the cursor crosses). ONE end door — PURE `src/lib/drag-end.js` `dragEndVerdict` — pointerup / pointercancel / lostpointercapture / blur / page-hidden / a move with no button held, ended ONCE (the highlight cleared there, the drop applied where the pointer last was). A DRAG SHIELD `body.wm-dragging` while a drag or resize is in flight ⇒ every window's content (iframe / canvas / img by name) pointer-events:none, the hit test the workspace's. A press with no pointerId or capture refused falls to a document feed with every end rule still applied; the seamless hand-over carries the press's pointerId and captures it. The viewer shrinks because the moves are now delivered and `clampToMin` holds the window at the `.window` floor (no `viewer`/`editor`/`browser` window feeds a minimum — `setMinSize`'s only caller is the desktop-app window), the delta read in layout px (viewport ÷ the UI scale).
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A drag and a resize are fed from the element that captured the pointer, never the document's mouse events — a surface that swallows or stops a press (an iframe, a canvas) is then irrelevant; a release over it still ends the gesture. (2) ONE end door per gesture: every way it ends comes through the PURE verdict, once. (3) While any window is dragged or resized, no window's content takes the pointer (the shield). (4) This is the lane M class a SECOND time — pointer capture at the door is the structural close.
- Gate: test-window-drag (fast; the PURE table + the real WindowManager over a fake DOM that models pointer capture, a swallowing iframe and a stopping pane: the incident, every end kind, the occupied cell, the D5 shrink table; controls = a drag-end copy per rule + the pre-capture feed) + test-window-drag-ui (heavy, the reproduction on a Web view / noVNC Desktop / agent-browser live / xpra app grid; the control bundle = today's drag-feed.js / window.js / tab-group.js with the pre-fix feed patched in, the same on every machine — lane mirror-green r2). test-window-minsize + test-desktop-seamless moved to the pointer door.
- **VERIFY r1 (2026-10-01) — the doors the lane missed, and the hold it broke.** The lane moved TWO of the four drag doors; the TAB TEAR-OFF and the ICON-merge drag (tab-group.js) still ended on the document's `mouseup` — reproduced in chrome: a torn-off tab released over the Web view / Desktop pane stayed armed with its highlight; an icon drag released there left the source window `visibility:hidden` with its ghost (the window VANISHED). And the xpra hand-over's hold waited for a pointerup alone, so a drag the new door ended on blur left the pane deaf and the X button down until the next click. FIX = ONE feed module `src/lib/drag-feed.js` every door attaches (window.js ×2, tab-group.js ×2 — the tab drag captures on the strip's TITLE BAR, the element the tear-off's re-render keeps), and the hold asks the same verdict. 不变量 (5) a drag door is a census, not a list: every `pointerdown` that starts a gesture attaches THE feed, and a document mouse listener that ends a drag is red (test-window-drag §4); (6) whoever holds a pointer on the window manager's behalf ends with the window manager's verdict, never with its own subset of it; (7) a release the page never saw arrives as `lostpointercapture` FIRST (measured, mouse and pen) — the verdict's first rule, the `buttons === 0` move its belt.
- **VERIFY r2 (2026-10-02) — the end the feed could not hear, the shield two drags shared, and the census.** (1) HIGH, reproduced in chrome: a window CLOSED mid-drag (another client's close record, the app exiting, a kill) — `closeWindow` aborts `win._listenerCtl` FIRST, the feed's listeners died with it, no end door ran: `body.wm-dragging` stayed up, every window's content (the Web view iframe) `pointer-events:none`, the grid overlay + highlight stayed, the icon's ghost stayed — until some OTHER drag completed. FIX = the feed hands the door ONE `owner-gone` end when its owner's signal aborts (drag-feed.js; PURE drag-end.js names the kind) and every door CANCELS — nothing is dropped for a window that is leaving (the title drag's cancel path, the resize op's cancel, the icon drag's no-merge, the tab drag's chrome-only cleanup, its feed joined to the dragged window's controller too). (2) LOW: a mouse title drag + a touch title drag at once — the shield was a boolean, the first end lowered it for the second (capture still carried the release — a belt gap). FIX = `setDragShield(on, key)`, a SET of holders. (3) THE CENSUS (T1): twelve more pointer drags still ended on the document's `mouseup` / a bare pointerup — the sidebar + Ctrl+G editor Resizer, the theme editor ×2, the minimap scrub, the top-bar scale + taskbar height handles, an explorer column, the viewer's pan + pptx sidebar, customize-mode's move, the split divider (captured, but no blur / hidden / released-unseen end), the queue reorder (no capture) — each moved onto ONE call, `startPointerDrag`. 不变量 (6) a drag door is a CENSUS: test-window-drag §5 grep-derives every document/window move-or-end listener in src/lib (each named with its reason or red) and the feed doors per file (16 in 10 files), with three planted controls; (7) a feed whose OWNER aborts ends the drag it fed — a silent teardown leaves the chrome and the shield behind; (8) a shared chrome state two gestures can hold is a SET of holders, never a boolean. Refuted (evidence in the lane dir): the 3-tab HOST tear-off (the host changes) and the active-guest tear-off both end and fit the pane's cell (the title bar survives the detach — the fake DOM's new REMOVAL RULE shows what a replacement would do); the xpra hold's `visibilitychange` / no-button ends are the WM's own (a pen in contact has buttons ≠ 0; another pointer's hover never matches the hold's pointerId); the binding-model pin's widening is benign for its own sequence and the branch's statements are pinned exactly in §4 now.

## A CLICK INTO A DESKTOP APP NEVER ACTIVATED ITS WINDOW (2.369.177, found by round 3 lane B while wiring the seamless Alt reveal)

- **What happened.** Every VibeSpace window becomes the active one through its element's `mousedown` listener (window.js `createWindow`). The xpra picture pane calls `preventDefault()` on its `pointerdown` (it must — the press is the app's), and a cancelled pointerdown makes the browser send NO compatibility mouse events for that press (Pointer Events: mousedown / mousemove / mouseup are suppressed until pointerup). So a click into an app's picture never focused its window: another window stayed `.window-active`, keyboard shortcuts and the window-scoped Alt reveal went to the wrong window. MEASURED on the real rung before the fix (a probe window focused, a trusted click into the calculator's picture: `activeWindowId` unchanged — "NOT ACTIVATED"); after it: "ACTIVATED".
- **FIX.** desktop-app-window.js adds a capture-phase `pointerdown` on the window element (bound to `winInfo._listenerCtl.signal`) that focuses the window when it is not already active — it sees the press before the pane cancels it, and it covers both picture views (xpra and RFB).
- **The same cancelled pointerdown is why the seamless drag is POINTER-fed.** WindowManager.beginDragFromPointer / beginResizeFromPointer listen to `pointermove` / `pointerup` on a per-drag AbortController — the `mousemove` / `mouseup` the title-bar drag relies on never arrive for a press that started in the pane.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A surface that cancels `pointerdown` owns the consequences: every mouse-event listener above it (focus, drag, hover-intent) is blind for that press — give them a pointer-event path or a capture-phase hook. (2) A window activates on ANY press inside it, never only on presses its chrome sees.
- Gate: test-desktop-xpra-window §12 (6) (a probe window focused, a trusted click into the calculator's picture ⇒ the calculator's window is active); the drag feed: test-desktop-seamless §4.
- 不变量=a cancelled pointerdown silences every mouse listener above it; a window activates on any press inside it.

## A DRAG OFF A MAXIMIZED WINDOW UN-MAXIMIZED IT SILENTLY (2.369.177, lane B verifier r1 — latent in window.js, visible once a seamless app's header bar mirrors the state)

- **What happened.** `_setupDrag`'s `processMove` un-maximizes a maximized window at the drag threshold (`win.isMaximized = false`, the prevBounds size applied) and nothing else — while every other un-maximize (restore, toggleMaximize, the snap paths) calls `win.onResize`. For most windows a ResizeObserver hid it; a seamless desktop app learns its maximize state ONLY through `winInfo.onResize` (→ `setAppState({maximized})`), so after a drag off a maximized calculator — from its own header bar or from our title bar — X kept `maximized: true`: the app's button kept its restore glyph and its first click was dead (reproduced on the real rung, xpra 6.5.3 + GNOME Calculator).
- **FIX.** The drag's un-maximize branch calls `win.onResize` (once, at the moment the size changes), and `_cancelPointerDrag` calls it again when its restore re-maximizes the window.
- **不变量 / invariants.** A state change is said through the SAME hook on every path that makes it — a new path that flips `isMaximized` (or any size) and skips the hook is a silent fork for every consumer that mirrors the state elsewhere.
- Gate: test-desktop-seamless §4 (e) (the real WindowManager over a fake DOM + a mutant-copy CONTROL of window.js without the two calls) + test-desktop-xpra-window §12 (3b) (real rung, a live muted-onResize control).

## A FORK LANDED IN NO TASK GROUP (2.369.173, owner 2026-09-25: "fork的会话不会自动分配到和fork之前的会话相同的group里")

- **What happened.** `_doForkSession` (src/lib/session-lifecycle.js) built its `createSession({…, fork: true})` with no `taskId`. Every other group-aware spawn carries one — the New Session dialog's group, and `resumeSession`'s `contextTask` (the first explicit group rides every resume) — so a fork of a conversation that sat in a Task Group was spawned into none: no server-side `_initialGroupId` (so `groupsForSession` — the task context the agent reads over its session token — named no group until a bind landed) and no explicit tag once its id appeared. Only a membership that came from an auto-include FOLDER carried over (same cwd); every explicit tag was lost and the owner re-bound forks by hand.
- **A second defect under the first.** The client's pending-bind queue held ONE group per webuiId (a second registration replaced the first), and it bound on the FIRST backend id the live row showed. A claude fork resumes the parent's id (`--fork-session`) and a codex fork its parent's thread id; ws-create seeds `backendSessionId`/`claudeSessionId` with that id until the harness announces the fork's own. Simply adding `taskId` to the fork would therefore have bound the PARENT (a no-op — already a member) and consumed the entry: the fork itself would still have ended up untagged.
- **FIX.** PURE src/lib/fork-groups.js: `forkGroupPlan(sourceGroups)` (the source's explicit groups off the sidebar store → the first live one rides the spawn as `taskId`, the rest as `extraTaskBinds`; archived, duplicate and non-`T-…` ids dropped) and `pendingBindVerdict(entry, live)` (wait while the row is unlisted / id-less / still carrying `notId`, the fork source's id; then bind EVERY id to the fork's own key). `_pendingTaskBinds` became Map<webuiId, {taskIds[], notId}>; the `created` handler registers `[taskId, ...extraTaskBinds]` with `notId` on a fork. One implementation for every entry point — the card's Fork…, fork-at-message and the terminal-mode fork all funnel into `_doForkSession`, and the suite's census fails a second client `createSession({…})` naming a `fork` key. Binds go through the ordinary `_taskBind` write-through (the store's `bind()` notifies ⇒ tasks-updated to every client). The star is not inherited (not asked for).
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A spawn that CONTINUES a conversation (resume, fork) carries the conversation's group context the same way a fresh create in a group does. (2) A deferred write keyed on "the session's id has appeared" must name the id it is NOT waiting for when the spawn starts under a borrowed one — a fork's first id is its parent's.
- Gates: test-fork-groups (fast, 140 after the fix rounds below — 96 at round 2: the plan + verdict tables, the REAL `_doForkSession` and pending-bind methods driven from source across the parent-id → fork-id transition for the card / terminal / fork-at-message shapes, the one-fork-create census, and two mutant-copy controls — the pre-fix create without the plan, and the verdict without the fork-source guard — each RED).
- 不变量=a fork inherits its source's explicit Task Groups at the spawn, and a pending bind waits past the id the fork borrowed from its parent.

## THE TERMINAL-MODE FORK NEVER LEARNED ITS OWN ID, AND A FORK'S BORROWED ID STOLE ITS PARENT'S LOCK (2.369.173 fix round, lane-fork-group verifier 2026-09-25)

- **What the verifier saw.** A scratch server from the lane head, a fake `claude` that writes `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` like the CLI and announces its OWN id, headless chrome driving the real card menu. ① A terminal-mode card in two groups → Fork…: the plan rode the create (spawn group = the first), but 25 s later the fork's row still carried the parent's id, no group's `sessions` held `claude:<the fork's real id>`, and the client queue sat on `fork-source-id` for good. ws-create seeds a fork's row with the parent's id (`--resume <parent> --fork-session`); in chat the stream parser adopts the fork's own, in terminal mode nothing did — the only terminal-mode id capture (the lock scan) was gated on an EMPTY id. The suite's terminal leg had asserted only the createSession arguments. ② A fork created within ~2 s of its parent (harness speed): the parent's lock capture, scheduled at create while its id was still null, ran AFTER the stream parser had named it and after the fork row appeared; its claim set counted the fork's SEEDED id — the parent's own — so it skipped its own lock and adopted the fork's; the parent's conversation was then tracked by nobody and the next same-cwd terminal session adopted it.
- **Also wrong in the first round's text:** the fork-groups header, the essay above, kb-file-structure and the CHANGELOG said the first group "rides the spawn as VIBESPACE_TASK_ID". That env var has had no producer since the Task refactor P2 (1dda5ec7, `git log -S`); the fork's environ has none on any path. What carries the group is `taskId` → ws-create's `_initialGroupId` → `groupsForSession` over the session token. The suite pinned the stale comment text.
- **FIX.** ONE local lock capture, src/claude-lock-capture.js, used by ws-create's create chain AND boot-restore's re-arm: `lockCaptureWanted` also answers yes for a pending (`_forkRequested`) non-chat fork (any mode since round 3) and is re-asked on EVERY attempt (a session the stream parser already named stops); `claimedLockIds` skips a pending fork's borrowed id; `pickClaudeLock` excludes the fork seed and picked the first lock to start at/after the session's creation (readdir order used to decide) — **that clock rule was itself wrong and is gone: round 2 below**; `adoptCapturedId` records `forkedFrom`, disarms, persists `forkRequested:false`. The client queue drops an entry whose session was listed and then left the live list (a fork that died before its own id) instead of waiting for the >20 cap. Every VIBESPACE_TASK_ID claim reworded to `_initialGroupId`; the suite pins the create message's `taskId` → `_initialGroupId` and that no text claims the env var. Left as stated, not fixed: a REMOTE terminal claude fork has no adopter (no stream, no local lock) — it keeps its parent's key.
- **Gates.** test-fork-groups ⑥ drives the whole chain over real modules — the real `_doForkSession` on a terminal card → a real TaskGroupManager in a scratch data dir → the real capture over real lock files → the real client queue — and judges `groupsForSession` by the conversation's REAL id (the row's id "has" both groups through the parent's key, exactly what fooled the first round); the parent race (round 1 claimed "both readdir orders" — on tmpfs readdir is name-sorted, so its two file-backed legs were ONE order; round 2 feeds the pure pick both orders and names the fork's lock to sort first). ⑦ controls: the shipped empty-id gate (terminal fork never bound) and the seed-as-claim set (parent takes the fork's lock), each RED.
- 不变量=a session's id is adopted by whatever channel its MODE has (stream in chat, the lock in terminal), a borrowed id is never a claim, and a suite judges membership by the conversation's real id, never by the id a row borrowed.

## A LOCK WAS PICKED BY THE CLOCK: SIBLINGS SWAPPED IDS, STRAY LOCKS WERE ADOPTED, A SLOW FORK KEPT ITS PARENT'S ID (2.369.173 fix round 2, lane-fork-group verifier 2026-09-25)

- **What the verifier saw** (a scratch server from the lane copy, a fake `claude` that sleeps `--fake-plan {delay}` then writes `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` in the CLI's shape, driven over the REAL ws `create` path, read back from `active-sessions`). ① Two forks of one parent 25 ms apart, the first with a slow CLI (2.4 s), the second fast: `sess-2 tracks sess-3's lock, sess-3 tracks sess-2's` — both rows persisted the sibling's id for life (status/config/star/transcript link and the fork-group binds on the wrong conversation). Deterministic: the earlier-created session took whichever same-cwd lock landed first; a plain new session beside a fork swapped the same way. ② A dead CLI's leftover lock started 1 s before a slow session's creation was adopted (`readClaudeLocks`/`pickClaudeLock` never asked whether the pid lived); after a SIGKILL + restart, a restored pending fork adopted an external live same-cwd claude's lock started 3 s before the fork and cleared `forkRequested` on that guess — its own lock, landing later, was orphaned for good. ③ A fork whose CLI took 19 s kept its parent's id with no restart (the create chain was `2 s + 15 × 1 s`, the boot re-arm ran only at boot). ④ The fast-tier test-fixture-isolation was RED on the lane since the build commit: test-fork-groups mints `fixtureSid()` without re-homing its process. ⑤ `claimedLockIds` trusted `_forkRequested`, restored verbatim from meta — and the stream parser's fork adoption write never re-listed `forkRequested`, so after any restart an adopted CHAT fork's OWN id claimed nothing. ⑥ Two claims the suite never proved: dropping `excludeId` and picking by directory order both left every behaviour leg green (tmpfs readdir is name-sorted; the parent's id was already claimed or excluded in every leg).
- **Root cause.** Every rule was a GUESS from time and cwd, while the server already knew the answer: it spawned the CLI. §4 discovery verifies a lock by its PROCESS (alive, is claude); the capture never did.
- **FIX.** src/claude-lock-capture.js: a lock is a session's iff its pid is alive and DESCENDS from that session's wrapper (the wrapper writes its own pid into its sidecar before spawning the CLI; `wrapperDepthOf` walks `/proc` ppids through src/cli-identity.js `readPpid`, ≤ 8 hops, a shim is depth 2); the nearest descendant wins, a tie or no witness is refused; the start floor = the session's creation (no pre-creation slack — it drops a file that PREDATES the session and is NOT the pid-reuse guard: a stale lock under a re-used pid name that starts inside the window passed it until round 3's writer witness); no cwd, no clock order. `armLockCapture` has no attempt cap (2 s, 1 s × 14, 5 s × 30, then 30 s) and ends on adoption / exit / not-wanted, one chain per session; ws-create and boot-restore (`armRestoredCapture`, dtach AND R6 pipe sessions) both use it. `restoredForkPending(meta)` restores the flag only while the record still names its source, and the stream parser's adoption write re-lists `forkRequested: false`. test-fork-groups re-homes its own process (scratch HOME + os.homedir, signal cleanup, a closing `fixtureLitter` census). Verified end to end on a scratch server with the fake CLI: the swap (both orders), N+F, the dead lock, the 19 s fork and the SIGKILL-restart-with-external-lock scenario all track their own ids. Still stated, not fixed: a REMOTE terminal claude fork has no adopter (no stream, no local lock) and keeps its parent's key.
- **Gates.** test-fork-groups (96): the pure pick with the locks in both orders, the parent race file-backed with the fork's lock named to sort first, two sessions created together (both kinds, both orders), stray locks (external / dead / stale pid name / the seed / a nested claude / a tie / no witness), the armed chain adopting at the 40th attempt, REAL process trees over the real `/proc` (a shim at depth 2, a dead pid, a live external pid), the restored flag; nine mutant-copy controls (the empty-id gate, the seed as a claim, the witness removed, excludeId removed, the start floor removed, the 15-attempt cap put back, the flag restored verbatim, …) each RED. test-fixture-isolation green again.
- 不变量=an id is adopted from the file the session's OWN process wrote (the pid witness), never from what a clock or a cwd suggests; a capture stays armed while its reason holds; a one-shot flag is re-listed by the write that consumes it; a suite's "both orders" is constructed, not hoped for from readdir.

- **What the verifiers saw** (scratch servers booted from the lane AND from master with a fake `claude` on PATH, scratch HOME, SIGKILL + reboot; master → lane in the same worktree for the upgrade). ① **The boot dedup SIGTERMed and unlinked the PARENT of every pending fork**: `⤫ Duplicate of <A> — retiring stale cw-1-…` for a live terminal parent beside its pending terminal fork, the same for two chat parents; their dtach masters were killed, socket/buffer/meta unlinked, their CLIs dead (`fake CLIs alive: 4` of 7). `dedupWebuiSockets` keys on `backend:host:claudeSessionId`; a pending fork's meta carries its SOURCE's id (ws-create seeds it); `claudeAlive` is false for both (a live claude never holds its JSONL — the essay's own measurement), so the NEWER (the fork) wins and the parent is "stale". Master shares it — and on master a TERMINAL fork keeps its parent's id FOR LIFE, so **the update boot itself retired every such parent**. ② **A live descendant is not the CLI**: a stale lock named after a pid the kernel had handed to a `sleep` the CLI ran (depth 2, started inside the window, `procStart: '1'` vs the live pid's stat field 22 `63501416`, comm `sleep`) was adopted — by a fresh session, and by a restored pending fork, which cleared its flag on it. The CLI-written `procStart` and cli-identity were never consulted; the suite's `stale` leg only covered a file that predated the session. ③ **A restored pending CHAT fork never adopted its id**: (i) its init landed while the server was down — nobody replays it, and `lockCaptureWanted` refused chat mode although the fork's own lock sat on disk with a live pid under its wrapper; (ii) when the init arrived after the reboot, dtach's re-attach preamble `\e[H\e[J` was glued to the FIRST line the chat consumer saw (`\u001b[H\u001b[J{"type":"system","subtype":"init",…`) and the bare `catch {}` dropped it — whichever line came first after a chat re-attach was lost (a race: an `_stdin_ack` sometimes took the hit instead). The terminal branch has swallowed that preamble since 2.2xx; the chat consumer never did. ④ **Two proofs that proved nothing**: with `if (!wrapperPid) return null;` inverted the suite stayed green (its no-sidecar leg passed by a TIE of two locks), and commenting out boot-restore's R6 re-open `armRestoredCapture(id, session);` left the substring pin satisfied (`/armRestoredCapture\(id, session\);/` matches the comment — the 2.369.134 lesson).

- **What the verifiers saw.** ① `readClaudeLocks` skipped an unreadable file silently (`try { JSON.parse } catch {}`), so while the session's CLI rewrote its own lock (8 of 12 live locks on this box had an mtime past `startedAt`, up to ~7 days later; the chain re-reads every 1–30 s while a capture is wanted) the nested claude's depth-3 lock was the only witnessed one and became "the nearest": `pickClaudeLock({locks:[own, nested]})` = null but `pickClaudeLock({locks:[nested]})` = the nested id — round 4's nearest-first rule fell through by another door. ② Reverting ONLY round 4's JSON-prefix `LOOKS_LIKE_RECORD` left test-fork-groups 140/140: the consumer leg fed only `[EOF - dtach terminating]` and `[detached]`, which the named `DTACH_BANNER` list ALSO excluded, and control (r) reverted both at once. Under the prefix test the list was dead code. The separating inputs were real: dtach's binary carries five banners — `[got signal %d - dying]` (captured from a real attach client on SIGTERM: `\e[999H\r\n[got signal 15 - dying]\r\n\e[?25h`, `\e[999H` on its OWN line), `[read returned an error]`, `[select failed]` — and with the regex reverted they were reported as dropped records.

A torn deeper lock does not hide a readable nearest one; a torn lock beside a readable one at the same depth is a tie. ② The JSON-prefix test IS the whole record rule — a `[` followed by a letter is never JSON, so every dtach banner is raw output by construction; `DTACH_BANNER` is removed.

Controls: (r) = the regex ALONE reverted ⇒ the five banners counted (#2…#6); (u) = the round-4 reader (torn file skipped) ⇒ the real-tree fork adopts the NESTED id; (v) = the pick skipping placeholders ⇒ the nested lock under a torn nearest is adopted. The pick's explicit placeholder refusal is also implied by the start floor (a placeholder has no `startedAt`) — stated, not given a control of its own.
- 不变量=a witness that cannot be read is still a witness — "I could not read the nearest" means "no answer yet", never "the nearest is the next one"; a rule a second rule shadows is proven by a control that reverts IT ALONE, else it is removed.

(2) A classification a list depends on is ONE rule run on every transport (local listing, daemon snapshot, ssh script) — the remote twin gets a parity leg the day the local one exists.
