不变量=a filter choice that hides most of a list is never silently persisted, and the classification it filters on is one rule on every transport with a parity leg.

## THREE SESSIONS DIED IN 40 ms AND THE JOURNAL COULD NOT SAY WHO KILLED THEM (B-3052, 2026-09-24 08:11:33 UTC)

- **What happened.** Three ACTIVE chat sessions on this instance ended in one 40 ms window. The server journal held three lines of the shape `[session] exited <id> "<name>" mode=chat backend=claude` — no code, no signal, no reason. The actor was never identified: the exit path itself destroyed the evidence.
- **Why the record was empty — four gaps, each on its own layer.** (1) `data/bin/chat-wrapper.js` handled `child.on('exit', (exitCode) => …)` and dropped node's second argument: a CLI killed by a signal is `code null` and ONLY the signal says which; `pty-wrapper.js` read only node-pty's `exitCode`, which is **0** for a signal death (the signal rides a separate number) — a killed CLI read as a clean exit. (2) Neither wrapper handled SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT, so a signalled WRAPPER died by the default action: no log line, no `childExitCode` in its meta — and the server line then printed no code at all (`code=` is only printed when one was recorded). (3) The teardown kept a 64 KB buffer tail under `data/exit-tombs/<id>.tail` (2.206.1) but UNLINKED `data/session-buffers/<id>.json`, the one file that would have said whether the wrapper finalized. (4) The line did not say whether the dtach socket was still on disk.
- **FIX.** (1) Both wrappers record `childExitSignal` beside `childExitCode` and log `Child exited with code <c> signal <s>` (pty-wrapper names node-pty's number via `os.constants.signals`). (2) Both install a SYNCHRONOUS record-then-die handler for SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT: write `{wrapperSignal, wrapperSignalAt}` into the meta, persist a pending buffer, log `wrapper received <SIG> (child pid <p>, childDead=<b>)` (that order since r4; r1–r3 logged first), `process.exit(128 + signo)` — the child is handed nothing new and the wrapper still dies. (r3: `codex-chat-wrapper.js`, the THIRD wrapper, got the same record — see r3 below.) (3) The teardown writes `data/exit-tombs/<id>.meta.json` (the meta + `{exitedAt, socketFate, wrapperFate}`) beside the `.tail`, same 7-day sweep. (4) ONE PURE reader `src/exit-facts.js` builds the line's new tail ` [signal=<SIG>] wrapper=<signal:SIG|finalized|unfinalized> socket=<present|gone|none>`, the `session-exited` event and the tomb. Pre-change exit statuses kept and pinned: a signal-killed child ⇒ wrapper exit 0 on both wrappers.
- **What the next incident's line will say.** `signal=SIGTERM wrapper=finalized` = the CLI was killed and the wrapper outlived it; `wrapper=signal:SIGHUP` = the dtach master went first (pty hangup) — true for that order only since r4, when the teardown stopped reading the meta before the wrapper could write it; `wrapper=signal:SIGTERM` = the wrapper itself was signalled; `wrapper=running` = no record and the wrapper was still alive 300 ms after its socket died; `wrapper=unfinalized` = SIGKILL (OOM killer / `kill -9`) — read dmesg and the tomb. On a real teardown `socket=gone` is normal (dtach unlinks its socket on exit; a socket still present takes the re-attach branch instead), so the actor-separating field is `wrapper=`.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) Every process in the session chain records HOW it ended before it ends, whenever the end is catchable — an exit path that can say nothing is the one path an incident always takes. (2) A post-mortem file is kept WITH the tail it explains, never unlinked at the moment it becomes evidence. (3) A record handler never changes the outcome: same death, same status, same child.
- **r2 — four defects in the r1 fix, each reproduced before its repair.** (a) **The record re-created the files the kill path had just removed.** ws-handler's kill case SIGTERMs the dtach master and unlinks `<id>.json`/`<id>.buf` in one tick; the wrapper is SIGHUP'd a few ms LATER by the pty hangup, and the r1 handler's `writeFileSync`/`persistMeta()` wrote both back — an orphan pair per Terminate (5/5 on both wrappers under real dtach, 0/5 on master, whose wrappers died silently). FIX: the record opens only an existing file (`'r+'`), creates a buffer only while the meta exists, and says in the log when it skipped. (b) **"The child is untouched" was measured by a race**: the pty child dies of the kernel's SIGHUP within ~20 ms of ANY wrapper's death, so a liveness sample at the wrapper's exit proved nothing. The suite now pins what the child RECEIVED against the handler-less baseline, with a forwarding copy as the control. (c) **The sentinel paths recorded a kill as a clean exit**: the keeper and the daemon's pipe-session waiter wrote `code ?? 0` and dropped node's signal, and chat-wrapper nulled the signal on that branch — `code=0 wrapper=finalized` for a CLI SIGTERMed on the host. FIX: both writers ADD `signal` (code unchanged), chat-wrapper records it. (d) Two claimed behaviours had no leg (the tomb + sweep without a `.buf`; the reconnect-window record) — both driven now, each with a control.
- **r3 — five more, each reproduced before its repair.** (a) **The third wrapper was left out.** `data/bin/codex-chat-wrapper.js` (codex chat, local and — through the SAME keeper — remote) had `child.on('exit', (code) => …)`, a `_remote_exit` branch that read only `code`, a `finalizeExit` that wrote no exit field, and no signal handler: every codex exit read `code=null wrapper=unfinalized`, the fate the reader reserves for SIGKILL/a crash/a gone meta, and a codex app-server killed on a host read as a clean end. FIX: the same record as chat-wrapper — `(code, signal)`, `childExitCode`/`childExitSignal` in `finalizeExit` (exit status unchanged, `code ?? 0`), the sentinel's `signal` recorded (null from an older writer, never the transport's), the same `overwriteIfPresent` record-then-die handler (143/129/130). (b) **"A chat child receives nothing and outlives the wrapper" was false in production.** It held only in the suite's pipe-only shape (no controlling terminal). Under dtach the wrapper is the session leader on a pty and a chat/codex child shares that controlling terminal: when the wrapper exits (the kill path's pty hangup, or a pkill of the wrapper itself) the kernel SIGHUPs the foreground process group and the child dies of it — the SAME under the handler-less build (20/20 kill, 4/4 pkill, both builds, measured by the verifier; the suite's §2c now pins lane == baseline == `["SIGHUP"]` for all three kinds in both shapes). A chat CLI does not outlive its wrapper. (c) **The forwarding control could not see a forwarded SIGHUP**: the fake CLI died on the FIRST signal, so a SIGHUP the wrapper forwarded and the kernel's pty SIGHUP were one line either way (a SIGHUP-forwarding copy left the pty/SIGHUP row green). The fixture now COUNTS (dies of the first signal 300 ms later) and the forward control runs per signal: pty/SIGHUP forwarded = `["SIGHUP","SIGHUP"]` vs `["SIGHUP"]`, red. (d) **The real-keeper leg had no control** on the claim that none was possible: a copy re-spawns ITSELF only if its `__filename` is its own — mutant-copy's default rebinding pointed it back at the real file. `mutantCopies().write(…, {selfPath: true})` now rebinds only `require`; the r1-shaped keeper copy (waiter drops node's signal) goes red through both chat wrappers. (e) The essays quoted the line's facts in reverse order (`wrapper=… signal=…`); fixed, and the suite greps both essays for the reversed spelling. **Residual, stated:** a wrapper's ordinary persist timers (codex meta 200 ms, chat meta 500 ms / buffer 2 s) are steady-state writers that can re-create an unlinked file if one fires in the kill path's few-ms unlink-to-SIGHUP gap — pre-existing on every wrapper; the handler adds at most the rest of the current event-loop turn (a due timer runs before a signal is dispatched). Not changed: an age-swept idle meta is re-created by exactly those writers. A wrapper process started before this build (dtach sessions survive the update) writes no record and reads `unfinalized` until it is restarted.
- **r4 — the incident's own order was never driven, and there the record lost.** When the dtach MASTER dies first (the 2026-09-24 shape), its death EOFs the server's `dtach -a` attach client AND SIGHUPs the wrapper — two consequences of one event. node-pty delivers `onExit` 2–4 ms after the EOF (measured, node-pty 1.1.0); the wrapper's record landed 1–2 ms after the EOF on tmpfs and later on the production storage class (the workspace is `fuse.bindfs`: an `appendFileSync` of the log line ≈ 3.5 ms, and the handler logged FIRST; an 800 KB buffer flush up to ~200 ms). The r1–r3 teardown read the meta ONCE at `onExit`: a read at EOF+0 missed the record 30/30, at +2 ms on bindfs 29/30, and at +3 ms 12/30 reads PARSED A TORN META (the `'r+'` record was `ftruncate` then `write`, two syscalls a reader could fall between) — the line said `wrapper=unfinalized` and the tomb `{metaMissing:true}`, the whole meta lost. The suite could not see it: every leg fed the teardown only after the wrapper had exited. FIX, both halves: (a) SERVER — `settleWrapperMeta` reads once, synchronously, as before, unless the meta names a wrapper that is still running (identity: `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` carries the meta path, so a recycled pid or a zombie answers no) without a FINALIZED record (PURE `awaitsWrapper`: no record, or a `wrapperSignal` record whose buffer may still be flushing), or the read does not parse — then it re-reads every 20 ms for at most 300 ms (`WRAPPER_SETTLE_MS`), and the rest of the teardown runs after, re-checking that the session is still its own (a Terminate during the wait owns the teardown). Past the bound with the wrapper alive and unrecorded the fate is the new `wrapper=running`, never the SIGKILL fate; a never-parsing meta tombs as `{metaUnreadable:true}`; the tomb carries `settleMs`. (b) WRAPPERS — the record is the handler's FIRST write (before the buffer flush and the log line) and a meta is overwritten in ONE write at offset 0, space-padded to the old length and never truncated (JSON.parse ignores trailing whitespace; a buffer, which may shrink, keeps the truncating form); still `'r+'`, still creating nothing. Measured after: the real teardown at EOF+0 with the wrapper files ON bindfs read `wrapper=signal:SIGHUP` 36/36 (chat, pty, codex; the longest wait 146 ms, the codex buffer flush); the wrapper half alone moved the verifier's +2/+3 ms reads on bindfs from 1/30 and 13/30 (12 torn) to 29/30 and 30/30 (0 torn).
- Gates: test-exit-forensics (fast, 285: the REAL three wrappers against a fake CLI — child SIGTERM, wrapper SIGTERM/SIGHUP with the child's received signals vs the default action in the pipe shape AND under real dtach (kill path + pkill), wrapper SIGKILL, the kill sequence, the reconnect window, the sentinel through the REAL keeper with the r1-keeper control — fed into the REAL setupSessionPty teardown; the tomb pair + the 7-day sweep with and without a `.buf`; r4 §2d the REAL teardown fed AT the socket EOF under real dtach, the master alone killed (lane + a 40 ms production-latency wrapper copy; a no-wait server copy is the control) + the wait's edges (bound → `running`, a recycled pid read at once, a torn meta → `metaUnreadable`, a Terminate during the wait) with pid-identity and ownership controls, §2e a preloaded fs spy: the record is the first write and no syscall instant leaves the meta unparseable, the on-disk meta first inflated LONGER than the record (for pty an UNPARSEABLE inflation — its handler re-reads the file, so a parseable one would ride into a longer record and leave the pad unexercised; r4 verifier) (r3-write, no-pad and log-first controls, every kind); a patched-copy control per change) + test-agentd-session (the daemon's pipe-session sentinel names a SIGTERM).

不变量=a session's exit writes down who ended what (child code AND signal on every path that carries it, the wrapper's own signal, the socket's fate) before the evidence is unlinked — on EVERY wrapper (census the siblings: chat, pty, codex); a signal handler that records must still die the same death, hand its child nothing new, and never create a file somebody else already removed; a claim about what a child receives is measured in the production shape (under dtach), and a fixture that cannot distinguish two deliveries cannot pin "nothing new". A reader woken by the same event as the writer it reads (the socket EOF and the wrapper's SIGHUP) waits, bounded, for that writer to be gone — and a gate drives the two together, in the order the incident had.


**r1 (2.369.172, the Actions mirror):** the handler's own last act bit a suite — test-codex-p2-client killed the wrapper and `rmSync`'d its scratch dir in the same tick; on the 2-vCPU runner the wrapper's log append (which CREATES the log file) landed between rmSync's listing and its rmdir ⇒ `ENOTEMPTY`. Four fast suites had the kill-then-rm shape with no exit wait. Fix = ONE idiom, scripts/scratch.mjs `stopWrapper(child, {dir})` (kill → await exit, SIGKILL after a grace → rmSync with retries) + test-architecture §55 (a suite that spawns a wrapper and removes a dir imports it or waits on `exit`; planted control). 不变量=a process that writes on its way out is waited for before its directory goes.

## A RESOURCE GUARD KILLED THE OWNER'S CHROME THREE SECONDS AFTER IT OPENED, DELETED ITS PROFILE AND PARKED IT FOR AN HOUR (2026-09-25 00:03 UTC; the owner's ruling 00:12 UTC; 2.369.171)

- **What happened.** The owner launched Google Chrome as a desktop app (B-bfe6, the xpra rung). Journal, verbatim: `00:03:06 [desktop] da-mug766wd-blaz ready: Google Chrome on :4 via xpra/xpra (xpra-seamless)` → `00:03:09 [desktop] RUNAWAY — da-mug766wd-blaz (Google Chrome, 25 process(es) in its sessions) stopped: RSS 2.0 GB (limit 2.0 GB); not launching chromium again for 60 min` → `00:03:10 … removed Google Chrome's profile …/data/desktop-apps/da-mug766wd-blaz/profile (stopped (runaway))`. Three seconds of use; the window gone, the profile gone, and every Chrome launch refused `runaway-parked` for an hour.
- **Why the number lied.** The guard (three verbatim copies — src/desktop-apps.js, src/browser-profiles.js, inline in src/opencode-serve.js) SUMMED VmRSS over the session's process set. VmRSS counts every page a process maps, INCLUDING the pages it shares with its siblings (the binary, the libraries, the zygote's copy-on-write heap), so a sum over a multi-process app counts each shared page once per process. Measured on this box the same hour: 891 chrome pids — ΣVmRSS **94.67 GB**, ΣPss **15.09 GB**, ΣRssAnon **21.74 GB** (ΣRssShmem 1.06 GB); one large chrome process Rss 240 MB vs Pss 73 MB. The browser keeper's chromium threshold (3 GiB) had itself been MEASURED in PSS ("420–667 MB PSS per idle browser") and then compared with an RSS sum. The 2 GiB number came from the 2.369.42 OpenCode incident — ONE process, where RSS was the footprint.
- **Why an honest number was not the fix.** The owner (verbatim): "不是就算是单一内存2G也不好啊，chrome这么吃内存，完全可能超过这个量吧。这个keeper到底是干啥的，没必要别乱加会影响使用的feature". Chrome legitimately passes any fixed ceiling; a memory ceiling on an app a PERSON is using is wrong whatever the metric. The keepers exist for lifecycle (launch / adopt / stop on request / app exit), one active viewer, the launch-time ceiling (a refusal naming the holders — never a kill), idle-out, and — from 2.369.42, a HEADLESS serve nobody watched (209 CPU-min, 5 GB RSS, 30k inotify watches, 3.6 GB/s page-cache reads) — the runaway stop. The stop belongs to that kind of process only.
- **FIX.** (1) ONE verdict, PURE `src/runaway-guard.js` `resourceVerdict` → `over` (null or the sentence naming the metric); the three copies deleted. (2) HONEST MEASUREMENT kept as facts: `cli-identity.procSample({memory})` reads smaps_rollup `Pss` (≈**1.1 ms per pid** sync on this box — 891 pids = 954 ms vs 8.7 ms for their status files; a 25-process app ≈ **27 ms per 60 s tick**, read through `procSampleAsync` on the libuv pool), fallback RssAnon+RssShmem; `setMemory` sums the STRONGEST metric EVERY member provides (never a mix) and names it (`memMetric` pss|anon|rss; r2 adds anon-sum); VmRSS kept as `rssBytes` (deprecated). A 'rss' set is NOT judged on memory. (3) TWO OUTCOMES: the OpenCode serve stops + parks on `over` (its `why` names the metric); the desktop-app and browser keepers REPORT ONLY — the live row (`memBytes`, `memMetric`, `over`, `since`), a server notice when a crossing begins ("Google Chrome is using 6.2 GB (PSS) — Stop it from the Desktop panel if that is not what you expect"; `reportTransition`, in memory, no persisted cooldown — r2 below), telemetry `desktop-app-resource` / `browser-resource` (MB). No stop, no park map, no `runaway-parked` refusal, no `runaway` state transition. (4) A desktop-app browser profile goes only by a PERSON's ending (`profileRetireVerdict`: Stop / relaunch / the app's own exit / no app ever ran) — an idle-out keeps it. (5) Migration `2026-09-runaway-parks-void` removes both park maps and rewrites every `stopped as a runaway: RSS …` lastError to name the retired guard and its metric, THROUGH the live keepers (`reshapeStore`) — the desktop keeper loads at construction and would overwrite a file edit (the suite's control proves it). (6) `GUARD_RSS_BYTES` → `GUARD_MEM_BYTES` (the same 2 GiB: the serve's stop threshold, the apps'/browsers' reporting threshold).
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A resource guard's OUTCOME is decided by the kind of process: a headless service the product runs for itself may be stopped; a session a person or an agent is using is reported, never stopped, parked, refused or stripped of its profile. (2) A memory number over a process SET is a footprint (ΣPss; RssAnon+RssShmem only for ONE process), one metric for every member, named where it is shown — a sum of VmRSS is a fact to display at most, never a threshold's input. (3) A keeper-decided ending (idle, a guard) never deletes a person's data; only a person's own ending does.
- Gates: test-runaway-guard (new, fast, 45: the verdict, the incident fixture through the real set rule, the multi-pid anon fixture, the report level incl. r2's oscillation / floor / delivery legs, the words; controls — an `rssBytes` comparison calls the incident OVER, a copy without the summed-RSS skip judges it, a copy without hysteresis fires 1010101010, a copy that latches an undelivered notice never re-sends) · test-desktop-display §8 (a fake /proc root in the incident shape: ΣVmRSS 2.34 GB > 2 GiB, ΣPss 450 MB; parity, the mixed-metric rule, the no-smaps fallback, a zombie member) · test-desktop-app-keeper §5 (heavy: a burner and a 6.2 GB PSS sampler REPORTED on real sessions, still running, one notice; a stop-on-over keeper COPY ends the session = the control) + §18(c2) (an idle-out keeps the profile) · test-browser-pin ③/③a + test-browser-ephemeral ③ · test-opencode-serve ④ (the serve IS stopped on a PSS footprint, not on a summed RSS) · test-architecture §54 (the comparison lives only in runaway-guard.js; no keeper but opencode-serve stops or parks for a resource; planted controls) · test-migrations (2026-09-runaway-parks-void: file path, missing files, through the live keeper, the file-only control).
- **r2 (the review of the fix, each finding reproduced before its fix).** ① THE REPORT LEVEL HAD NO HYSTERESIS: it re-armed after ONE normal sample, and each crossing got a NEW notice key (`…-resource:<id>:<n>`) so server.js's per-boot key dedupe never applied — a reading alternating 2.05 / 1.95 GiB around the 2 GiB line fired `1010101010` (5 notices in 10 one-minute ticks; the real desktop keeper with a 6.2 / 0.9 GB PSS sampler filed `:1…:5`), a warn toast on every client every ~2 min, and live Chrome PSS moves enough between samples to sit on a fixed line. FIX: PURE `reportTransition(state, verdict, {now, limits})` re-arms only after REPORT_REARM_SAMPLES (3) samples IN A ROW read `clear` (under REPORT_REARM_FRACTION 0.9 × the threshold, CPU not hot — the verdict's new `clear`), and never within REPORT_NOTICE_FLOOR_MS (1 h) of the previous notice of the session; the same fixture now fires `1000000000`, and on the real keeper 10 alternating samples file ONE notice. ② A CROSSING NOBODY SAW WAS LOST: server.js latches a key only when a client received it (returns the count, the r5 rule) but the keeper latched `reported` regardless and discarded the answer — after a restart with no browser connected the toast was gone until the reading went normal AND crossed again. FIX: `notify` + `reportDelivery(state, delivered)`: exactly 0 ⇒ `pending`, the next sample still over re-sends the SAME key (no second log / telemetry); a reading back under drops it. ③ THE 'anon' FALLBACK WAS ITSELF A PER-PROCESS SUM over a set: RssAnon counts a CoW page once per sharer, RssShmem shared memory once per mapper — read-only scan of this uid's chrome: 889 pids, ΣVmRSS 94.74 GB, ΣPss 15.15 GB, ΣRssAnon 21.81 GB + ΣRssShmem 1.06 GB = 22.87 GB (+51 % over ΣPss; ΣPss_Shmem 0.65 GB), and it was labelled "private". FIX: `setMemory` names a multi-process anon set `anon-sum` (recorded, never judged); one process keeps `anon`, labelled "anon+shm". ④ THE §54b CENSUS WAS A DENY-LIST: `stop(id, { why: v.over })`, `why: 'over-limit'`, a bare `stop(id)`, `store.resourceHoldUntil[..] =` (and `why: 'user'`, `parkedUntil.set`) all passed it. FIX: structural — the sampled block (the whole scope of the block-scoped verdict) may write only `g.…` / `dirty` / its `let` locals / the guard + live maps and call no stop / retire / kill / fs; every `stop(` names a why from a CLOSED list; the verdict's facts are read nowhere else; all those spellings planted as controls, inside and outside the block. ⑤ kb-api still documented `live{cpuPct,rssBytes,…}` and `parkedUntil`; fixed with the payload.

不变量=一个人或 agent 正在用的会话, 资源守卫只报告不处置 (只有产品自己跑的无头服务可被停); 进程集合的内存是足迹 (ΣPss, 同一口径) 而非 VmRSS 之和; 用户数据只随用户自己的结束动作删除; 报告电平要有回滞与下限且按投递结果锁存 (一个在阈值上摆动的读数只能产生一条通知, 没人收到的通知要重发); 对"不许停"这类法则的普查要按结构 (块内能写什么、stop 的理由是闭集) 而不是按拼写黑名单.

## THE BAND-0 NOTCH: A TALL WINDOW'S FIRST WHEEL-UP LOADED HISTORY AND WENT NOWHERE (2.369.167 r1b; the r1 verifier's reproduction, byte-identical on 3207e03b — pre-existing, adjacent to r1)

- **What happened.** Band 0 = a list TALLER than its rendered window (no scroll range: sh = ch) — the common shape of a tall or maximized window over a fold-dominated agent session, whose attach slab folds to a few hundred px. A wheel-up at scrollTop 0 carries the whole notch (roomUp 0) and starts `_extendTop`; the grow loop's first passes add history that still fits under the list's height, so their anchored landing CLAMPS at scrollTop 0 — no room above the reader. `_applyWheelCarry` consumed the carry unconditionally ("consumed either way"), so the notch was spent at a pass that could apply none of it (`wheelTop{carry:120} extendTop:done{st:0,sh:565}` and no `wheelCarry` trace anywhere in the notch); the later passes landed at the very BOTTOM (each anchored restore keeps a view that started at the bottom there), and the landing's own scroll — dispatched after `_extendingTop` dropped in the finally — re-pinned the view the wheel had just unpinned (`extendTop:grown{st:761,sh:1327,ch:565} repin{structAge:4}`). The r1 essay's "the landing's carried notch moves the reader out of the band" was false for this shape. The height law (sh ≥ 2 viewports) cannot see it (1327/565 = 2.3): the loss is in scrollTop. A second notch lost part of its carry the same way (49 of 120 px applied).
- **FIX.** A grow loop's pass calls `_applyWheelCarry(dir, by, { keepRest: true })` (both `_extendTop` and `_extendBottom`): it consumes only the px it APPLIED, the rest rides into the loop's next pass, and the loop's finally drops what no pass could apply (`_dropWheelCarry` → `wheelCarry:drop` — history exhausted, the pass cap, a pin; never left to inflate the next notch). Single-landing callers (both gap slabs) still consume either way. Measured on the fold transcript (list 565 px over a 445 px slab): unfixed `761/1327/565` pinned, no `wheelCarry`; fixed `642/1327/565` unpinned, `wheelCarry` 34 + 86 = 120 px (the first pass room-less, the second 34 px of room, the third the rest); the verifier's maximized shape (ch 715): `855/1570` pinned → `735/1570` unpinned; the second notch now delivers 49 + 71 = 120 px.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A carried notch is spent only by a landing that APPLIES it — a pass with no room to scroll into is not a landing for the carry. (2) A landing that can only clamp (band 0: no scroll range) is not "where the reader asked to go": the gesture is delivered where room first appears. (3) A notch smaller than the 50 px pin band lands inside it and re-pins — the tail's own hysteresis (a 30 px scroll up from any tail stays pinned), not this defect. (4) Every shape a gate constructs is named with its neighbours: band 25 (a pinned window 25 px short) hid band 0 (a pinned window with slack).
- Gates: test-chat-trim-guard 205 → 214 (⑨: the REAL `_extendTop` loop with the REAL add/apply/drop accounting over a fake list 120 px taller than its 445 px window, the anchor restore clamped as a browser clamps it — Σ wheelCarry 24 + 96 = 120, lands 120 px above the bottom; NEGATIVE CONTROL ⑨ keepRest stripped on the instance: carried none, 0 px from the bottom; five `keepRest`/`_dropWheelCarry` units; the loops' keepRest + finally-drop pins; the assignment census 3 → 4), test-chat-paging §4b BAND 0 (`FOLD_RUN(…, {tall: 120})`: the list sized to the slab + 120 px, asserted with a room-less first pass; the whole notch Σ wheelCarry = 120, the first notch `st ≤ (sh − ch) − 120`, no repin, not pinned; NEGATIVE CONTROL band 0 = keepRest stripped on the instance: Σ 0, at the bottom, re-pinned — red on the unfixed product: 3 legs, control green).

## THE MIRROR'S TWO REDS: A WHEEL-UP'S OWN SCROLL RE-PINNED THE VIEW IT HAD JUST UNPINNED, AND A STALL NOBODY BUILT (2.369.167 r1; the Actions mirror on 3207e03b — test-chat-paging and test-reconnect-storm red on both attempts, green here)

- **What happened — §4b, a product defect behind a font.** The fold-dominated window opens at the WM's 700×500 default; its attach slab rendered 67 px taller than its 386 px list here (`system-ui` = Noto Sans) and 48 px taller on the runner (DejaVu Sans) — inside the 50 px pin band, where a window whose rendered window ends at the live tail is "at the tail" at EVERY scrollTop. The wheel handler unpinned the view and started `_extendTop`; the scroll that the same wheel produced reached the scroll handler during the first fetch, which re-pinned it (`atTail && !this._pinned`); the grow loop read the pin as "the live tail owns this view", stopped after ONE 50-record slab (48 px) and re-tailed (`wheelTop repin(we 1539/1539) trimSkipPinned pinnedRetail`). Forcing DejaVu Sans on this box with the new gate neutered reproduces the mirror's `481/1179 1087/629 1391/79 807/0` byte for byte; the reader loses the first notch of every short window (and lands back at the bottom) — a window within 50 px of its viewport is the common shape right after a fold-dominated attach.
- **What happened — §4f, a lane claim read off one box.** "≥ 2 viewports, no rescue" was measured on this box's fonts AND this box's fixture: the §1c generator counted REAL bytes and every record carries the suite's scratch cwd, whose pid is 5 digits on a fresh runner and 7 here — so where the loop stopped, where the dense tail began and what the tail held moved with the pid's digit count. The runner paged 3,795 records with an image-free 68 KB tail(50) (text window 55 records, 1.58 viewports); this box 3,785 with a 571 KB image in its tail(50) (117 records, 2.14). The product never promised a height: the slab is chosen by TEXT.
- **What happened — (j), a stall hoped for.** The lagged leg throttled the page with `Network.emulateNetworkConditions` and fell back to a 15 s busy-wait only after 20 s without a cut. The runner's chrome does not throttle websocket reads, so its page drained the 25.6 MB burst at 0 queue, and the busy-wait froze a page whose burst was over (ws-lagged 0, cut "seen" at 40 s). The leg was green HERE by the page's natural lag, not by the throttle: measured, this box's page does not drain the UNPACED burst even unfrozen (the server emits faster than the renderer paints 400 KB cards — cut at full CPU and under `taskset -c 0`).
- **FIX.** PRODUCT: `_repinVerdict(atTail)` → `'repin'` | `'skip'` | null — the scroll handler never re-pins while an upward page is in flight (`_extendingTop`, raised with `_loading` by `_extendTop`, dropped in its finally; the skip traced `repinSkipPageUp`); the landing's carried notch moves the reader out of the band and a later scroll re-pins honestly — in band 0 (a list TALLER than its window) only since r1b (the essay above): there the carry was consumed at a room-less first pass and the landing's own scroll re-pinned. HARNESS: §4b CONSTRUCTS the band (the window resized until the list is 25 px shorter than the rendered attach slab, asserted and printed) and the ORDER (each fetch held three frames on the instance, so the wheel's own scroll is decided while the first slab is in flight — the defect is a race between that scroll's frame and the fetch, and a loopback fetch on an idle box can win it), waits for each notch's own landing (the loading span ended, twice), and a same-band control with `_extendingTop` neutered on the INSTANCE must re-pin after one slab. §4f asserts THE RESCUE LAW (no rescue ⇔ the first paint filled its viewport; a short one gets exactly one autoFill traced at sh ≤ ch) and that the text window renders at least as tall as tail(50), never a viewport multiple. The fixture counts every record as if its cwd were `CANON_CWD` (29 bytes): the same records on every machine, byte-identical to this box's former test-chat-paging fixture. (j) PAUSES the page (CDP `Debugger.pause`, confirmed by `Debugger.paused`) BEFORE a burst that is paced (one 400 KB frame per 0.15 s) and bounded by the cut (the stub stops at the harness's STOP file the moment the server's journal line appears, ≤ 160 frames — whatever the machine's socket buffers absorb, the queue reaches the limit), resumes after the cut; a CONTROL leg first sends the same paced burst with no freeze and must never be cut (the page socket's own queue: a preload column for op-seq-capable sockets).
- **Measured.** (j), three full runs + one under `taskset -c 0`: control 64 × 400 KB in 11.0–11.8 s, the page socket's queue 0 B, 0 ws-lagged; freeze: paused 8–20 ms after the request, cut 3.1–3.2 s into the burst after 21 frames at 4,410,829 B (limit + one 400 KB frame), exactly one lagged, the window equal to the server 861–917 ms after the resume (a held replay; 2,455 ms on one CPU). §4b fixed, DejaVu Sans, default geometry: 4 passes per notch, `1040/679 1344/129 854/0`, `repinSkipPageUp` on the first. §4f canonical fixture: 117 records / 17 text / 2.14 viewports here.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A scroll the reader's own gesture produced is never evidence against that gesture: while the page-up it started is in flight, the pin does not re-engage. (2) A stall or an ordering a gate needs is CONSTRUCTED (a paused renderer, a burst ended by the event it waits for, a fetch held past the frame that decides) beside a control that shows its absence — a throttle, a timeout or a machine's slowness is never the construction. (3) A geometric expectation is constructed (resize to the shape) or derived from the product's own law and measured heights — never a viewport multiple read off one box's fonts. (4) A fixture's shape is independent of the paths it embeds. (5) A mirror-only red is reproduced locally by forcing the runner's inputs (its fallback font, its pid length, its drain rate) before anything is changed.
- Gates: test-chat-trim-guard ⑧ (fast: the verdict table, the source pins, the REAL `_extendTop` loop in the band + its neutered control), test-chat-paging §4b/§4f (`VS_PAGING_UI_FONT` = a debugging aid that forces the runner's font), test-reconnect-storm (j).

## THE TEXT WINDOW MADE EVERY MANY-WINDOW SHAPE SLOWER, AND THE RESUME WATERMARK COUNTED OPS IT NEVER APPLIED (2.369.167 perf r1 — the verifier's round on the chat pipeline perf lane)

- **What happened.** Perf 1 shipped a bigger attach slab (a text window, ≤ 2 MiB) to EVERY attach and measured it on ONE window. The verifier's 19-window probe on the 6 MB §1c fixture: a cold open 12.3 → 29.8 MB, first paint ×2.7, server CPU +78 %; after a restart the 14 hidden windows paid for slabs nobody looked at; same-epoch reconnects grew 50–60 ms style/layout stalls (19 views holding 208-record windows each appending a "Disconnected"/"Reconnected" marker — no JS function in them, found with a per-method profiler). Separately perf 4's `_lastSeq` was stamped before an op ran, so one renderer exception inside a held replay lost a card for the life of the epoch.
- **FIX.** The window is bounded by what it ADDS past the floor (128 KiB; a heavy record ends the walk), and the attach ASKS for its slab (`slab:'floor'` for a suspended view and every attach of a burst after its first — PURE `attachSlab`, ONE server mapping `attachWindowOpts`). The watermark advances only after the op ran; a throw poisons it ⇒ the next attach asks no seq and a same-epoch full reply rebuilds from the slab.
- **不变量 / invariants.** (1) A change that grows what an attach ships is measured on the MANY-window shapes (cold open of 19, the restart storm, the drop storm) against MASTER — never one window, never a control that already carries the change. (2) A slab goes only to a view that will paint it now. (3) A resume watermark means "everything up to here is on screen": advanced after application, poisoned by a failure, healed from the authority (the slab), never from a position derived after the failure (`_windowEnd`). (4) CPU "per phase" is read over a FIXED window when the phases differ in length (a stagger stretches the until-painted window and charges idle time to the fix).
- Gates: test-text-window (46), test-hidden-view-suspend §7/§8 (102), test-chat-paging §4f, test-transcript-parity, test-reconnect-storm.

## THE PAGING GATE'S FLAKY RED WAS ITS OWN JUDGE — AND A DOWNWARD SLAB RE-LOCKED ITS ON-SCREEN CARDS (B-1192, 2.369.164 batch 9; test-chat-paging red on the first attempt of both 2.369.160 heavy runs, green on every retry)

**The red.** Every recorded instance was `down-mid-1` ("the card at the top of the viewport before the gesture … is gone from the DOM"), and 2.369.155's essay already carried a local `down-mid-2` of the same shape. The §4c plan's `mid` cadence is 6 notches × 120 px = **720 px**; the fixture's list is **714 px**; the trim's keep zone is ONE viewport above the viewport (`TRIM_KEEP_VIEWPORTS`). A downward wheel of `d` px leaves the reader's card (whose bottom sat `b` px below the viewport top) inside the zone only while `b > d − ch` = 6 px — compact rows are 14–22 px, so a fraction of those gestures (the ones whose trim lands after the whole wheel) trim the card BY THE RULE. The judge (`scripts/paging-gesture-rules.mjs`) excused a vanished card only for `|wheel| ≥ 2 × ch` — a flat bound written for the upward case — and called the rule's own trim a jump. The .160-run red's numbers are consistent with exactly that (inferred from its row, the witness did not exist yet): st 666 before, 74 cards trimmed, st 725 after = a trim at ≈ 1386 (zone top ≈ 672) removing ≈ 661 px. **Fix:** downward, a vanished card is excused when `|wheel| ≥ KEEP_ZONE_VIEWPORTS × ch + (topOff + topH)` (the snapshot gained `topH`); upward — the card must cross the viewport AND the zone below it — and on a snapshot without the height, 2 viewports stays. test-chat-trim-guard pins the rules' `KEEP_ZONE_VIEWPORTS` to the product's `TRIM_KEEP_VIEWPORTS`. **Evidence for the next red:** the suite's TRIM WITNESS wraps `_trimEdge` (suite-side, read-only) and records before each trim the reader card's offsetTop/height, the span `_cardPositions` gives it, the zone, its inline content-visibility and the zero-height run above it — printed only with a "gone from the DOM" violation.

**The residual the .160 agent named — real, and not this red.** A paging slab's fresh cards are inserted `content-visibility: visible` and never rendered under `auto`, so they have NO remembered size; the frame the two-frame release drops the override lays them out at the lock size (measured on the §1c fixture, a per-rAF logger reading after EVERY rAF callback: a 407 px slab read 10 px and scrollTop swung 562 → 168 → 562 inside one page-up landing; a 312 px card read 232 px in that frame with `auto 312px`, `312px` or no pin alike — **pinning `contain-intrinsic-size` does not fix the release frame**). Upward the slab lands above the viewport and scroll anchoring absorbs it; DOWNWARD it lands at the DOM's bottom, on screen: under a 3-frame stall a card at the viewport's bottom edge read 0 px. **Fix:** a slab holds the override on its cards within half a viewport of the viewport (`CV_HOLD_SLAB_NEAR`, chosen in the FIRST frame's callback — that frame lays the slab out anyway), released by a per-view IntersectionObserver once they leave that band; the rest release on the old schedule; a live card keeps its 600 px hold. **A gap card is never held**: five held gap cards (small, in view) raised test-ax-budget ④c's non-ignored platform nodes 652 → 1,311 after the first gap slab, releasing exactly those five restored 652 — the mechanism inside Chrome's accessibility serialiser was NOT identified; the rule is empirical and pinned by ④c. Variants measured and rejected: the whole slab to the observer at 125 % / 50 % / 0 margins, with and without the pin (④c 1,311 each; the observer also released off-screen cards later than two frames).

**The other first-attempt red was the harness too.** `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'viewSession')` (run 1 of the .160 integration, master alike): the suite waited a fixed 10 s for a scratch server and a fixed 24 s for the page, then evaluated `window.app.viewSession` whatever the page was — under 4 busy loops the §4d control's freshly started server answered late, the page stayed on Chrome's connection-refused page and the eval threw. **Fix:** deadline waits (`serverUp`, `pageReady` re-navigating every 30 s) and a named failing check when the app never boots.

**Invariants.** ① A gate's judge encodes the product's GEOMETRY, never a round number near it: a wheel within a few px of the zone makes the rule's own trim look like a jump. ② A harness wait is a deadline on the condition, never a fixed count that falls through into the next step. ③ A red a retry cannot reproduce gets a witness that prints the decision's inputs on the failure path before anyone theorises. ④ A hold on content-visibility costs accessibility-tree nodes — any new hold is measured by test-ax-budget before it ships. Gates: test-chat-paging §4e (6 up + 5 down landings, 45 ms × 3 stall, 0 on-screen off-height reads; the pre-fix release on the same view: 5 of 11 landings), test-chat-trim-guard 189, test-ax-budget ④c.

## THE CALIBRATION METRIC REPORTED ON EVERY TICK, AND THE AUTO-CLI LOG PRINTED A 100-POINT DRIFT AGAINST A CLOSED WINDOW (B-a5c0, 2.369.164 batch 8)

Telemetry held 118k rows of the estimator's error metric in two days, nearly all 0 and none naming an account (33k in the backlog's own 2-day count, mean 0.01, median 0, `detail=None`): the sweep computed the calibration for every identity group on every 60 s tick, before and regardless of whether a new reading had arrived, and emitted it through a hook that could not carry a detail. The 2.368.13 switch to the delta-relative metric hid the common case (a re-seen snapshot has actΔ 0 ⇒ rel null) but not the rule: an identity group whose freshest cache is OLDER than the anchor (a sibling file) still compared against it on every tick — pred Δ 0 vs act Δ −5 pt = a 100 % "error", once a minute, forever. Separately, the auto-cli loop compared `est.utilization` with a raw bucket whose `resetsAt` was already past: the estimator had re-based the rolled window at 0 while the reading still said the old window's number, so `[auto-cli] quota refresh … (drift 100pt)` described old window vs new window, not the estimator.

**FIX** = `sweepAnchorGroup` (src/usage-estimator.js, the engine's sweep delegates to it): a reading is NEW only when it is newer than the last anchor; otherwise nothing — no ledger walk, no calibration, no metric; the metric fires only after `maybeRecord` accepted the anchor, once per moved bucket, `detail: account=<id> bucket=<key>`. `cliRefreshDrift` reports the logged drift over CONTROLLED buckets only (a past `resetsAt` = no control; all stale ⇒ the log says so) while the scheduler keeps its inputs (`triggerDrift`, `moved`): a reading from a closed window IS stale and refreshing it was right — the backlog's own finding — so the vendor-facing spawn cadence does not change.

**不变量** = a measurement is emitted by the arrival of the thing it measures, never by the clock that polls for it, and carries the identity of what it measured; a comparison whose control has expired is "no control", said as such, never a number.

**Gate** = test-usage-estimator (+18, red first — the unfixed tree has no step to drive): four ticks against the REAL UsageAnchors store (first reading ⇒ nothing; a new reading ⇒ exactly one attributed row, value 80 %; the same snapshot ⇒ nothing and no ledger walk; an older sibling ⇒ nothing), a patched-copy control of the pre-fix every-tick shape that floods on the older sibling, the drift legs (stale skipped, scheduler inputs unchanged, all-stale null, live window kept, resetsAt-less kept) and wiring pins on the engine and the auto-cli loop; test-readings-attribution's §16c source pin follows the step into usage-estimator.

## AN OLD WRAPPER QUEUED EVERY BACKGROUND WORK NOTIFICATION AS A BILLED TURN (B-d963, 2.369.164 batch 7; the owner's screenshot, two queued)

A codex chat wrapper runs inside dtach and outlives every update. sess-13's had started on 2026-09-07 07:06Z, before the notification steer and the verb table (both 2.369.63): its sidecar advertised `{peerMessage, frameFile, threadScoped, inputQueue, responseStyle}` and no `queueVerbs`. The server's ladder read the HARNESS row (`notificationDelivery(capsOf('codex')) === 'steer'`), tagged the frame `kind:'notification'` and predicted a free steer; the old process ignored the tag and did `thread/queue/add` — each Background Work event became its own billed turn after the running one, and the strip showed them as ordinary queued rows with nothing saying why or what to do. Same class as the 2.361.1 / 2.364.1 WRAPPER VERSION SKEW: a static capability trusted for a long-lived process.

**FIX** = the process's OWN advert decides, on both ends. `wrapperCaps().notificationSteer` is true only for a sidecar that names an explicit verb table with `steer` (the table and the steer shipped together, so the table is the proof — never a version number). ① The ladder (src/server/conversation-deliver.js rung 1.5) checks it BEFORE the write: a notification to a BUSY wrapper without it is the typed miss `refused:'wrapper-no-steer'` (the hold released in the one `finally`), which every producer already stashes — jobs as `held.kind:'wrapper-no-steer'` — and the next prompt's injection delivers it with its chat card. ② The attach payload carries `queueNotifSteer` (`notificationSteerOf`: sidecar, else the remote wrapper's in-band publication, else null), chat-view derives `notifSteerMissing` (fact false AND the harness lane `steer`), and the strip draws "Restart this session to receive notifications without a billed turn" and marks each queued notification's ✕ as the suggested action — the old wrapper hands a removed peer item back for a re-stash. A notification row is recognised by its sender (PURE src/notification-senders.js), the only carrier an old wrapper keeps; a census pins every `kind:'notification'` producer to a listed sender.

**不变量** = a capability a long-lived child process may LACK is read from that process's own advert at the moment it matters, and a missing advert changes the LANE before the act, not just the words after it; the legacy DEFAULT a reader fills in for an old process (the three queue verbs) is not evidence of what that process can do.

**Gate** = test-peer-delivery (+17, red first: the sess-13 caps verbatim — busy notification refused and not written, hold returned, never charged; a person's message still queues, an idle old wrapper still gets its turn, a new wrapper still steers, no sidecar is not a steer; `heldKind` + the panel sentence; the sender census with a negative control) + test-queue-steer (+22, red first: the strip hint/marks and their controls, the view's fact from both carriers and its three negative controls, the lifted attach advert executed over real sidecars) + test-spend-paths (the rpc fixtures carry the current wrapper's caps).

## THE CLI PATH RESOLVED ONCE AT BOOT STAYED DEAD UNTIL THE NEXT RESTART (B-a18e, 2.369.164 batch 4; a fleet instance, 2026-08-11)

An Update restart landed inside the CLI installer's window — the old version deleted, the new one not yet placed — so the boot-time `resolveCmd('claude')` answered a path (or a bare name) that no longer ran, and that answer was the only one the process ever asked for: every new session and every resume failed ("not installed" in the UI) until somebody restarted the server again. The spawned CLI runs INSIDE the wrapper under dtach (`env … <cmd> …`), so its ENOENT never reaches the server — there was no failure to react to, only a dead session.

**FIX** = `src/server/cli-cmd.js`: ONE resolver (the sync boot spelling + its async twin, one directory list), and `cliCmds.forSpawn(backend, cmd)` called ONCE in `src/ws-create.js` right before the ONE local argv (`r6Argv` — the pty terminal, the chat wrapper and the daemon pipe all run it): the boot-resolved path still executable ⇒ untouched (one `access`, no process); gone ⇒ `resolveCmd` runs once more, the new path is handed to the adapter (`config.claudeCmd` / `codexCmd` / the ACP `command`, + codex-thread-read) so later spawns are born right, and ONE journal line names the old and the new path; nothing found ⇒ the spawn goes ahead exactly as before and fails the old way (plus one line saying the re-resolve found nothing). Only the registered, boot-resolved command is ever re-resolved: a spec override, `ssh`, node and a login shell pass through; remote spawns are untouched (they already replaced the command).

**不变量** = a fact resolved once at boot about something an installer can move is re-checked where it is USED, and a stale answer is re-asked, never trusted until the next restart. When the failure happens inside a child we cannot see (a wrapper under dtach), the check before the spawn IS the retry.

**Gate** = scripts/test-cli-cmd-refresh.mjs (fast, 31): the helper over injected facts; wiring pins (server.js has no resolver of its own, cli-env registers claude + codex + every ACP harness, ONE `forSpawn` before the ONE `r6Argv`); a scratch server whose fake `claude` is renamed A → B → A between spawns — each spawn runs it where it NOW is with no restart (RED on the pre-fix tree: spawn 2 ran nothing), and gone everywhere ⇒ nothing runs + the "found nothing" line. Not covered (out of scope, captured at construction): the usage `/usage` probe, account login and backend-status still read the boot value.

## A REAL-CLI LEG JUDGED BEFORE THE CHILD'S TERMINAL SIGNAL (B-5f0b, 2.369.164 batch 3; the 2.369.69 gate red)

The real `codex app-server` leg of test-queue-steer asserted "the turn the server drained by itself died unauthenticated" while that turn's 401 was still in flight — green on an idle box, red under a loaded gate (fixed in 5cb57f16 by a bounded wait). The audit of every real-binary leg found the same shape twice more: the wire probe (scripts/probe-claude-stdout.mjs) reported `ok:true` for a capture that ended before the turn's `result` (budget expiry / mid-turn death), and test-stdout-registry judged it — a tool_use with no tool_result reads as "no tool ran", a missing trailing record as "the CLI stopped sending it"; and test-vendor-whitelist counted INET connects in a strace trace the 60 s timeout had cut short, where a zero is vacuous. Deterministic controls: the fake CLI's `FAKE_CLI_NO_RESULT` cut (test-stdout-registry) and a 400 ms strace budget over a 1.5 s-delayed loopback connect (test-vendor-whitelist), both RED on the unfixed code.

## THE LAUNCHER RE-BOUGHT A HEAVY VERDICT ALREADY ON DISK (B-3ccf, 2.369.164 batch 2; 2.369.102: a 35-min same-sha re-run holding the machine lock)

**What happened.** The owner (or an agent) ran `npm run ci:heavy` before pushing, earning `data/ci-heavy/<sha>.green`. The pre-push hook then called `ci.mjs --heavy-launch <sha>` for the very same sha, and the launcher — which only refused a TWIN IN FLIGHT (`already running`) — detached the whole tier again: 35 minutes of a verdict nobody needed, holding the one machine lock every other checkout's heavy tier queues on. On 4af276f8 the builder killed the duplicate by pid by hand (exit 4, no verdict, the existing green kept).

**Fix.** `heavyLaunch` asks PURE `heavyAlreadyGreen({markers, sha, full, commitTimeMs, scope, range})` right before it would spawn (after supersession: an ancestor's in-flight run is still stopped — this sha's green subsumes it). It skips only on EVIDENCE: a GREEN for exactly this sha (a short sha matched through its resolved full sha), not PARTIAL, whose file mtime is strictly newer than the sha's committer time, and whose scope covers the launch — a FULL green covers any launch, an AFFECTED green only an affected launch over the SAME range (never a launch the 24 h net turned FULL). It prints `heavy already GREEN for <sha> (<age>), not relaunching` and exits 0 without a child. A RED (or a red at least as new as the green), a partial, a stale or a narrower green relaunches; a missing commit time never skips.

**Gate.** test-ci-heavy-launch §8 (fast), RED on the unfixed launcher first: a stub repo carrying the real module; a fresh full green ⇒ exit 0, the message, NO pid file, NO log, the marker byte-identical; a green an hour older than the commit, a fresh red, a fresh partial green ⇒ each launches a real child (waited out, killed if still alive); 13 pure arms. dbg-ci-mutations carries the mutant (`if (g.skip)` → `if (false)`).

**Invariants.** **A verdict already on disk for exactly the commit is not re-bought** — the launcher asks the markers before it spends the machine. **A marker is evidence only when it is provably ABOUT that commit and at least as wide as what would run**: older than the commit ⇒ not written by a run of it; a slice ⇒ not the tier; an affected set over another range ⇒ not this push's set. **A red never short-circuits**: re-pushing the same sha is how a flaky or environmental red gets its second run.

## A SUITE'S PATCHED COPIES TURNED A NEIGHBOUR SUITE RED (B-0220, 2.369.164 batch 1; a 2026-09-22 integration ran test-new-member-wake and test-auto-resume-loop at once: 3 red, green alone)

**What happened.** test-new-member-wake's negative controls load patched copies of product modules (the pool engine, the account-usage routes, the usage routes, master's auto-resume). They were written as SIBLINGS of the real module — `src/server/vs-wake-mut-<pid>-<n>.js`, `src/vs-wake-mut-…` — because a copy elsewhere could not resolve its relative requires, and they were gitignored so the tree looked clean. test-auto-resume-loop §5 DERIVES its `noteRecovered` census by walking `src/`; running at the same time it met the mutant engine's call sites and reported three unlisted callers. Alone, the copies were gone before anyone walked.

**Fix.** ONE loader, `loadCopy(origRel, src)` in test-new-member-wake: the copy is written to the process's `scratch('wake-mut')` dir as `.cjs`, and on its line 1 (after `'use strict';`, so every line number stays the original's) `var require = require('node:module').createRequire(<the real module's absolute path>);` — `./x` and `../x` resolve to the very files and require-cache entries a sibling reached, so the control differs from the product in its named edit and nothing else. The gitignore lines for the old names are deleted (nothing may write there; a stray copy is now VISIBLE); a legacy sweep removes what a pre-fix run stranded, dead PIDs only.

**Gates, each red on the pre-fix placement first.** test-new-member-wake §10 takes git's view of `src/` INCLUDING ignored files while every copy still exists (the exit handlers remove them — a census after exit passes on the old code) plus the helper's own ledger, every path outside the checkout. test-auto-resume-loop runs a HELD child of test-new-member-wake (`VS_WAKE_HOLD=<path>`: `.ready` carries the copy paths, `.go` releases, a dead parent or 5 min releases too) and runs its whole self — the §5 AUDIT included — inside the hold; with the old placement it reproduces the incident's exact 3 reds.

**Invariants.** **A suite never writes into the checkout.** A patched copy lives in the suite's scratch dir and borrows the real module's resolution through `createRequire`, never through being its sibling. **An ignore rule is not isolation**: it hides litter from `git status` and from nobody else — every suite that walks the tree still reads it. **A cleanliness census is taken while the thing it judges still exists**, and reads ignored files too. **A concurrency failure is reproduced by HOLDING the window open, not by racing for it.** (Other suites still write sibling copies — vs-spend-mut, vs-aredge-mut, vs-readattr-mut, vs-qmr* — the same class, not yet moved.)

## …AND TWENTY-SIX OTHER SUITES STILL DID IT (B-59b8 r1 / B-0220 generalized, 2.369.164 batch r1; found by the batch verifier: test-spend-paths §4b added two more in-tree copies the day after B-0220)

**What happened.** B-0220 fixed ONE suite. The idiom it retired — a patched copy written as a SIBLING in `src/` so its relative requires resolve, "made safe" by a `.gitignore` row + an exit unlink + a PID sweep — was the house style of nineteen more suites behind 17 gitignored families, and seven suites had never even ignored theirs (their runs left the tree DIRTY mid-run, the state the release gate refuses on). Each one was the B-0220 hazard: a SIGKILL strands the copy, and every suite that walks `src/` while it exists (a census, a bundle-freshness check, a fork-site classifier) reads it as product code. Two suites had already bent their own censuses around it by NAME (`!/^vs-fable-mut-/`, `!/vs-[a-z]+-mut-/`) — a patch no OTHER scanner knew to make.

**Fix.** ONE helper, scripts/mutant-copy.mjs (kb-file-structure): copies go to the process's scratch dir with their module resolution re-bound to the real path (CJS: `require`/`__filename`/`__dirname` on the first-statement line; ESM: relative specifiers + `import.meta.url` rewritten to file URLs), a closed world of copies wired by absolute path, a per-suite census leg, a legacy sweep. All 26 suites ported (+ test-new-member-wake's loader delegates), every in-tree `.gitignore` row deleted, the by-name census exclusions dropped, the "is the copy gitignored" legs replaced by the census.

**Gates, each red first.** Per suite: the census leg run against the pre-fix placement (git's view of `src/` incl. ignored files, taken while the copies exist) — RED — then GREEN on the port. Globally: test-architecture §51, RED on the half-ported tree naming the 8 suites still writing into `src/`, with a negative control over the three sibling shapes (`path.dirname(rel)`, an in-tree directory variable, a direct join) and the exceptions that must pass (a mutant-copy write, a scratch-root `src`, the build-version stand-in); plus "no wildcard `.js` ignore under `src/`" and the helper's own CJS/ESM contract.

**Invariants.** **A fix to one instance of an idiom is a census of the idiom** — B-0220 fixed its suite and the next day's control reintroduced the shape; the rule became real only as §51. **An exclusion by name inside a census is a symptom**: the census was right, the tree was wrong. **A copy's module resolution is borrowed, never earned by placement**: `createRequire(<real path>)` / file-URL imports give it a sibling's graph from anywhere. **A copy installed into ANOTHER checkout carries its raw text**, never the rebound copy (whose resolution points at this one).

## EVERY SCRATCH SERVER RAN THE BOOT `git pull` — THE HEAVY GATE WENT RED ON A NETWORK ROUND TRIP (2.369.163 integration, heavy RED on 5c941bf0, 2026-09-24)

**Symptom.** The impact-scoped heavy run for the quota lane (merged onto 2.369.162) ended `HEAVY GATE RED — failed: test-incident` (ECONNREFUSED on its first POST, twice) with five more suites failing once and passing on retry: test-chat-paging and test-ax-budget (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'viewSession' / 'wm')`), test-toolbar-resize (`no app after 20s`), test-attach-rescue (`Inspected target navigated or closed`), test-permission-rules (ENOENT on `src/server/session-stdout.__prefix_control.js`). The same suites were green on the previous heavy run of the same lane seven hours earlier; the product code under test had not changed.

**Mechanism ① (five suites).** server.js has run a SYNCHRONOUS `git -C <root> pull --ff-only` (15 s timeout) before `listen` since the first releases. Every suite's scratch server is a `git worktree add` of the developer checkout, so every scratch boot did a network fetch from `origin` into the SHARED `.git` (moving the developer checkout's remote-tracking refs) and then failed on the detached HEAD. Measured on a scratch worktree of 2.369.162 with an empty data/: **0.5–0.9 s to the first `/api/home` with `NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, 2.5–15.5 s without** — the whole difference is that pull (the traced boot sat 14 s between the `[env]` line and `[auto-update] skipped: Command failed: git … pull --ff-only`). Eighteen scratch suites wait 40 × 250 ms = 10 s for the server and then FALL THROUGH silently, so a slow network turned into ECONNREFUSED or a page with no `window.app`.

**Mechanism ② (test-permission-rules).** Its standing mk()-ref sweep walked every `.js` under `src/` with readdir + readFile, while test-restore-liveness (another heavy lane) writes and unlinks a gitignored PRE-FIX copy of session-stdout.js beside the real one: the walk listed it, then it vanished. The same walk could equally read the pre-fix copy while it existed and report its retired spelling as an offender.

**Fix.** ① A server whose code lives under the OS temp dir (the `hookRegistrationSafe` rule, spelled inline at the top of server.js because it runs before any module is wired) never runs the boot auto-update and says so (`[auto-update] skipped: throwaway/temp server root`). A production install is never under /tmp; `NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` still turns it off anywhere. test-incident now pins it: the boot log carries that line and no `pull --ff-only`, the wait is 60 s with a loud failure that prints the boot log, and it prints the measured boot time (789 ms after the fix). Negative control: the same suite over 2.369.162's server.js fails the new check with `[auto-update] skipped: Command failed: git -C /tmp/vs-incident-smoke-… pull --ff-only`. ② The sweep's scope is the set a commit of the tree would contain (`git ls-files` tracked + untracked-not-ignored, via scripts/git-env.mjs), so gitignored patched copies are never read. Control: a planted gitignored `session-stdout.__probe_control.js` carrying the retired `ref?.()` call turns the pre-fix suite red on exactly that line and leaves the fixed one green.

**INVARIANTS.** (a) A throwaway server does nothing at boot that reaches the network or writes state it shares with the developer checkout: hooks, CLI config, and now `git pull`. (b) A boot window in a suite ends in a loud failure naming what the server printed, never a silent fall-through into the next step. (c) A sweep that derives its file set from the tree reads the commit's set, never a directory walk: suites write gitignored patched copies beside real modules.

## inc-mudv05ja-n5rv THE PINNED CHAT WINDOWS FLICKERED — A FRESH CARD PAINTS AT ITS CONTENT-VISIBILITY PLACEHOLDER, A SWAP DROPPED ITS FOLD, THE PINNED FOLLOW CHASED BOTH, AND THE LIVE WORKFLOW CARD WAS RE-CREATED ON EVERY task_progress (2.369.160, the owner's "不知道是不是workflow的问题，界面有点异常闪烁", five pinned compact chat windows at 120 Hz; + two side bugs in the incident machinery)

**Symptom (owner rings).** Whole-list JUMPS inside pinned compact chat windows: the list displaced by up to 1.5 viewports for 1–3 frames (8–25 ms — every pop/unpop pair in the rings is 8–10 ms apart = the 120 Hz panel) and snapped back, on every tool completion, every workflow heartbeat, every live append. The workflow session's window was the loudest: TEN identical +678 px pop/unpop pairs in 37 s (resting geometry byte-identical for 45 s) plus a 12-write pin shake in 197 ms (±678–836 px) during a 15-frame burst of its msgs; a non-workflow window showed an editReplace followed at +186/+208/+216 ms by `sh 2204→3144→2414` (+940 px then −730 px, exactly the 180 ms fold debounce). The live Workflow card blinked on every progress record; the View Workflow window re-drew every 2.5 s. No JS errors, no freeze, no layout-sync storm.

**Mechanisms (one class: the view painted a card at a transient WRONG height or re-created it, and the pin chased it):**
- ① **A fresh `.chat-msg` enters `content-visibility:auto` LOCKED** (chat.css `.chat-msg`, `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 80px`) until its first relevance check — measured 0 px in a compact window. Every `_swapMessageEl` (tool completion `editReplace`, `_rerenderToolCard`, the live Workflow card's per-`task_progress` re-render) and every live append painted the card collapsed for 1–2 frames (repro: `swap h=80, raf1 80, raf2 140` on EVERY heartbeat; control `.chat-no-content-visibility` = 0 jumps). Dropping a reservation's `content-visibility: visible` override on screen re-locks the card as a NEW lock for one frame (measured `197 → 0 → 197`).
- ② **A swap is not a tail append.** A swap handed the list a card WITHOUT the four run classes, and the runs observer folded before the next paint only for `records.every(tailAppend)` — a `replaceWith` record (one out, one in) and an append at the trim cap (tail append + first-child removals) went to the 180 ms debounce, so a folded member painted UNFOLDED for ~11 frames.
- ③ **The pinned follow chased every transient.** `_forceScrollToBottom` rewrote `scrollTop = scrollHeight` for ten frames whatever happened; while cards resolved and re-locked, scrollHeight alternated and the write re-followed it each frame (repro: 83 A-B-A frames / 481 in 8 s; control = 0).
- ④ **The live Workflow card was re-created on every `task_progress`.** A multi-agent Workflow emits one per agent tool use (several a second); message-manager turns each into `edit {taskInfo}`, and chat-view's taskInfo branch (2.369.118) re-rendered the WHOLE card through `_swapMessageEl`: the label, the View Workflow button, both `<details>` (a Script the reader had opened snapped shut), the `.chat-wf-live` tree and every agent chip — a running chip's `.chat-wf-dot` carries chat.css's infinite `chat-wf-pulse`, which restarts on a new element. The View Workflow window (workflow-detail.js) did `root.innerHTML = ''` on every 2.5 s poll (its status chip's pulse restarted, its View Log buttons were re-created under the pointer).
- ⑤ **The pulse never ran in production anyway.** The CLI's words for a working agent are `start` / `progress` — 8 production buffers: 161 progress, 26 start, 253 done, 56 error, ZERO `running` — and the card's CSS selector and tally compared against the fixture's word.

**FIX.** `_swapMessageEl` is geometry- and fold-NEUTRAL: the run classes ride the swap and every run record (`members`, `inline`) is re-pointed to the new element; a RENDERED card is reserved (`_reserveFreshHeights`) so it lays out at its real height in its first frame; live appends reserve too; a LIVE reservation (`{live: true}` — swap + live append; paging slabs keep their tuned two-frame release) keeps its override until the card has LEFT the screen (one IntersectionObserver per view, ±600 px, `contain-intrinsic-size` pinned to its last height). The observer classifies through the PURE `foldPassMode(records)` (chat-run-summary.js): tail append / 1:1 replace / tail append + head trim ⇒ fold in the next rAF; bulk / non-tail / head-trim-only ⇒ debounce. The pin writes only when `scrollHeight − scrollTop − clientHeight > 1` and the chain ends when scrollHeight held still for two frames OR swung back to its value of two frames ago (A-B-A = a card re-locking, not growth); B-9702's epoch/mute untouched. The live Workflow card is PATCHED IN PLACE (`_scheduleWorkflowPatch` → `_patchWorkflowCard`, one pass per frame and at most one per 150 ms per view): status chip (same node), phases and agent chips keyed by `data-phase` / `data-agent-key` (`_morphWorkflowLive`; the dot node never re-created), the ✓ line — `<details>` and the View Workflow button untouched; the renderer exposes `renderTaskChip` / `renderWorkflowLive` so card and patch share one spelling, `drawsWorkflowCard(msg)` gates the patch (a pending tool_call or an error result draws nothing from taskInfo — the r2 patcher had put a ⟳ chip on the pending card and could overwrite an error card's ✗ line; caught by the parallel lane's legs), and PURE `workflowAgentState` maps start / progress / running to `running` for the chip AND the tally. The View Workflow window renders only a CHANGED run (JSON digest), keeps its head/status chip node, keys rows by agentId and keeps expander open state; state dots `aria-hidden`.

**Measured.** The card (headless Chrome, a stub `claude` emitting task_progress at 3/s, before = 2.369.159, after = the shipped patcher; the parallel lane's harness gave the same numbers on its own patcher): whole-card replacements per 10 s 30 → 0; agent-chip re-creations 120 → 0; the steady running chip's pulse restarted 9 times in 3 s (its `currentTime` never passed ~330 ms) → 0 (monotonic 11.6 s → 14.5 s); the real-word `progress` chip: no animation → pulses; an opened Script: shut within 3 s → stays open; tally "0/4 · 1 running" → "0/4 · 4 running". The window (test-fold-ux chrome legs, in-page pre-fix controls): folded replacement unfolded 6/6 frames → 0; a visible swap at the placeholder 2 frames → 0; scrollTop writes while already at the bottom over 6 s of appends 72 → 0.

**Limits (stated, not hidden).** A live reservation is held until off-screen, not released after two frames; paging slabs still release after two frames, so a layout read in that frame can still see 0 px there. The owner's ±678/940 px amplitudes were not reproduced (the scene's cards are shorter — ~200 px jumps); every mechanism was, with a control. Not done: the judge's optional C (status bar `tasks` chip removed/re-added when the task set empties), D (`setTitleMeta` without a no-op guard on the 5 s sidebar merge), F (`_onSubagentMessage` rebuilding the status line + View Log button per frame), E (the window-waiting blink — a product question), and recording the real rAF interval in the incident snapshot.

**Side bugs (found while mining the report).**
- **A tab return is not a jank storm.** The auto-filed "jank storm — 13.3s" had one piece of evidence: a 13 288 ms rAF interval logged 1 ms after a `visibility: visible` event that ended a 254 s hidden period. `installCompositorStallWatch`'s rAF loop pushed a frame gap when `gap >= 300 && !document.hidden` — at a return `document.hidden` is already false, so the interval spanning the hidden period entered the ring; `jankStormVerdict` counted it as 13.3 s of slow-frame coverage ⇒ an auto incident + a whole scene freeze (63 conversations copied) on every long tab hide. FIX = PURE `frameGapIsReturn` at the ring AND `jankStormVerdict(…, {visibleSince})` skipping any interval that straddles the return. The 2.369.141 self-gap rule already excused the same return's tick lag — the frame-ring twin had been missed.
- **The freeze truncated session-meta as bytes.** `incident.js` copied session-meta (and wrapper-meta) through `copyCapped(…, 64 KiB)`, which keeps the TAIL bytes; since 2.369.140 a meta carries `taskRecords` (the owner's own: 96 877 B), so both bundles held a 65 536-byte unparseable fragment — for exactly the sessions with workflows. FIX = `copyJsonWhole`: whole up to 2 MiB; above it valid JSON trimmed as data (`_frozenTrimmed` names the fields, the counts, the original size); an unparseable file becomes `{_frozenTrimmed, rawTail}`.

**Invariants.** A swap carries EVERY fact the old element carried — incl. fold state and measured height; the fold guarantee is decided by a pure classifier, not by `every(tailAppend)`; the pin never writes when already at the bottom and never re-follows an A-B-A height; a live update of a card is a keyed in-place patch, never a re-creation — an infinite animation's element must survive every update, and a patched card draws exactly what a fresh render draws (a card that draws nothing from the update is left alone). A consumer of a producer's state vocabulary is tested against the producer's REAL words. A frame that spans a hidden period is a return, not a frame. A frozen file is truncated as DATA, never as bytes. Gates: test-task-lifecycle (the live-card legs over the real normalizer/ChatView + the pre-fix negative control), test-fold-ux (heavy chrome legs with in-page pre-fix controls), test-chat-trim-guard (the pin chain's unit table), test-freeze-probe, test-incident.

## THE COLLAB COUNTER LOST ITS SHARED LABEL ELEMENT (2.369.150 → fixed 2.369.154, heavy gate red twice on bbd87d56 and ce5f415e)

**What went red.** scripts/test-collab-live-counter.mjs, one leg of 77: "✗ the read-only stream line carries the same label element (a ticking age is a text write there too)". Green on 2.369.149 (694b52fb, 122/122 heavy), red from 2.369.150 (2368bd72, the lean accessibility-tree fix) on every run, the retry included.

**Root cause — a pin on a spelling, not a fact.** The leg was a SOURCE regex over src/lib/chat-view.js that required the literal `<span class="chat-spinner"></span> <span class="chat-stream-label">${escHtml(label)}</span>`. 2368bd72 marked every spinner creation site paint-only at the source (test-ax-paint ③'s census), and the read-only fallback of `_showTyping` changed by exactly that attribute:

```
-    this._streamStatus.innerHTML = `<span class="chat-spinner"></span> <span class="chat-stream-label">${escHtml(label)}</span>`;
+    this._streamStatus.innerHTML = `<span class="chat-spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span> <span class="chat-stream-label">${escHtml(label)}</span>`;
```

(the ChatInput line and the button-less pending line got the same attribute in the same commit). The label element, the `roLabel` text-write branch and `_roTypingLabel` are byte-identical before and after; the leg's second clause (the `if (roLabel && …)` branch) still matched. **The product invariant never broke** — proven, not argued: the leg is now also a BEHAVIOURAL one (below), green on the 2.369.150+ product, and red (3 legs) on a patched copy whose read-only branch rebuilds the line on every call. Reverting the attribute instead would have reddened test-ax-paint ③ and put a paint-only node back into the reader's tree.

**Fix (suite only; no product change).** ① The static pin became a TWIN-PARITY pin: the spinner+label template is extracted from BOTH chat-view.js and chat-input.js with a regex that tolerates the paint-only spinner's attributes (`<span class="chat-spinner"[^>]*></span>` — those belong to test-ax-paint) and the two must be EQUAL, plus the `roLabel` text-write branch. Controls (node, on the strings): the read-only spinner alone losing `aria-hidden` (twin drift) → red; the read-only label inlined without its own element → red; the 694b52fb pair → green. ② ⑤b, new: on the REAL read-only view the suite already opens, the REAL bundled `_showTyping` is driven through three ticks under a MutationObserver — the `.chat-stream-label` and `.chat-spinner` nodes are the same across ticks, a changed label is exactly ONE mutation record inside the label element, an unchanged label is ZERO records, and `_hideTyping` restores the stopped view.

**Invariants.** (1) A pin on a behaviour names the behaviour's own facts (the label is its own element in both twins; the tick is a text write), never the incidental markup of a NEIGHBOUR another lane owns — a paint-only spinner's attribute list is test-ax-paint's, not this suite's. (2) When two lines are twins, pin their PARITY (extract both, compare), so a change to one alone is red and a change to both is green. (3) A source pin on a DOM behaviour is backed by a behavioural leg on the real bundle with a negative control — a source regex went red on a harmless attribute here, and the same regex would have stayed green on a real regression that kept the spelling.

## SPEND NOTICES LIVED FOREVER AS ACTIONS (2.369.152, measured on the owner's instance 2026-09-22)

**What the owner saw.** The "For you" inbox held 33 open items; 15 were from Spending, and 13 of those sat in the ACTION list, colouring the red badge, 137–288 h old: "X has used 10 of its 12 unattended turns this hour (83%)", "… 48 of 60 today (80%)", "VibeSpace refused the Stop bookkeeping mini-turn in …" — warnings about hour and day windows that had closed weeks earlier. Only the two newest were in the Notices section.

**Three faults, one symptom.** ① *Filed as actions before the lane existed:* spend-guard's `fileInbox` only started declaring `kind: 'notice'` in 2.369.118; every item filed before that has no `kind`, which the client reads as an action. ② *Never migrated:* 2.369.118 added the lane to the store and changed the producer, but left what the store already held where it was — so the fix was invisible on exactly the instance that asked for it. ③ *Never expiring:* nothing in the store could retire an item by time; a notice about "this hour" lived until a human clicked it, however long ago the hour ended.

**Fix.** ① + ③ at the producer and the store: `UserTodoManager.add()` takes a validated `expiresAt` (a future ms epoch, anything else ignored; a merge into an open item keeps the LATER end; a lasting item stays lasting), `expireDue()` resolves due OPEN items `done`/`expired` (one save, one broadcast, never an item without `expiresAt`), run at load and on an unref'd 5-min timer; spend-guard stamps each item by what it is about — the hour warning +60 min, the day/instance warning +24 h, the refusal +6 h (its own re-file cadence). ② one-shot migration `2026-09-spend-notices-expire` through the LIVE store (`reshapeItems`, handed to migrations.js by server.js): every Spending item (`sessionName 'Spending'` in the `accounts` row — the name the one producer freezes on every item; on the real store it selects the same 19 records as the text rule) becomes a notice; an open one gets the end of the window its own detail names (`Scope: hour` +1 h, a refusal +6 h, else +24 h, via spend-guard's `noticeExpiry`) — past ⇒ resolved `expired` with `resolvedAt` = that end (kept, never deleted, sorting as old history), ahead ⇒ stamped; the live store is flushed before the ledger row is written. The counts ride the ledger (`reports[id]`, a new optional return of the shared runner). Panel: a notice row says `expires in {n} min / h`; a resolved row says `expired`.

**Invariants.** (1) A notice about a WINDOW carries the window's end and dies with it — expiry is the PRODUCER's declaration (`expiresAt`), never inferred by the store from age or text. (2) A lane added to a store comes WITH the migration of what is already in it; a producer-only fix is a fix for the future, and the user is looking at the past. (3) A migration that reshapes a store a live manager holds in memory goes THROUGH that manager (a second writer beside it is overwritten by the manager's next save) and FLUSHES it before returning (a debounced save lets the ledger row land before the data). (4) A retirement is dated when the item should have died, never when the migration noticed. Gates: test-user-todos-expiry (38, every leg beside a patched-copy control) + test-migrations (the leg on a fixture shaped like the real store; controls = the registry without the row keeps 14 badge actions, a patched copy without the live-path flush leaves the file unchanged behind a written ledger row) + test-spend-paths + test-user-todos-layout unchanged.

## THE STATUS BAR KEPT THE OLD MODEL AFTER /model SINCE CLI 2.1.257 (2.369.151, noticed on 2.1.280 by the read-only research pass 2026-09-22)

The CLI wraps the model token of its `/model` confirmation echo in backticks: ``<local-command-stdout>Set model to `opus[1m] (claude-opus-5-5[1m])`</local-command-stdout>`` where it used to write `Set model to fable[1m] (claude-fable-5)`. **Since when is DATED BY EACH ROW'S OWN `version`, not by the build it was noticed on:** a read-only census of the local transcript corpus (334 user rows containing `Set model to`) puts the first backticked `alias (id)` echo at **CLI 2.1.257 (2026-09-02)** — 6 rows @2.1.257, 4 @2.1.263, 3 @2.1.267, 1 @2.1.274, 2 @2.1.280; the backticked bare id is one row @2.1.263 — while the LAST plain `alias (id)` echo is @2.1.226 (8 rows) and the last plain bare token @2.1.239. So the vendor switched the spelling between 2.1.239 and 2.1.257, and **the status bar was wrong on every `/model` on this instance for about three weeks**; 2.1.280 is only the build on which the miss was noticed (the first draft of this essay and of the suite dated the change to 2.1.280 and labelled the control "≤2.1.274", which the corpus refutes — 2.1.274 already backticked). The echo is the ONLY authoritative confirmation of a model switch, and three readers each spelled their own regex: the status bar's (chat-view, end-anchored `(\S+?)(?: \(([^)]+)\))?</local-command-stdout>`) stopped matching, so after a switch the bar kept the previous model until the next assistant row happened to carry one; the command card (chat-renderers) printed the raw backticks; the server's model-lock upgrade (claude-stream-json) kept working only because its regex was not end-anchored — a coincidence, not a tolerance. Earlier transcripts already held two further spellings nobody parsed on purpose (a backticked bare id, and the TUI picker's ANSI-bold DISPLAY name "Fable 5 … and saved as your default", which is not a model id at all). FIX = ONE PURE parser, src/model-echo.js (`parseSetModelEcho` + `stripSetModelBackticks`), consumed by all three readers; scripts/test-model-echo.mjs carries the vendor's verbatim lines (the backticked echo as the case, the plain echo — last seen @2.1.226 — as the control, ANSI and display-name forms), drives the REAL renderer for the label, pins the three call sites and censuses src/ for any inline `Set model to` matcher (negative control: the pre-fix regex is flagged and really misses the backticked line).
