The WebSocket itself takes one packet + header per message (`maxPayload`; the ws default buffered 100 MiB before any sieve looked). Measured at the bridge: the 2 GiB-declared viewer closed in its first chunk with arrayBuffers +0 MiB; the uncapped control stayed open holding +97 MiB after 97 MiB. (B) A WATCH VIEWER COULD CHANGE THE KEYMAP THE HOLDER TYPES THROUGH: `keyboard-config` / `keymap-changed` were watch types and xpra 6.5.3 applies a client's keymap to X (set_all_keycodes) whenever no other keyboard client is connected — measured, a Watch viewer's packet put ydiaeresis on keycode 250 within 2 s. FIX: they left the allowlist (`XPRA_KEYMAP_TYPES`); the picture never needed them (measured: a draw ~100 ms after map-window with no keymap packet sent; xpra delays the hello's own keymap). The fence ALONE broke the takeover — the shipped client sends its keymap once, after the hello, so a pane that connected watching and then took over typed `" \x1bOP"` for "abc" — so the last fenced keymap packet is HELD per viewer (≤ 64 KiB) and relayed first the moment that viewer may type.

**Invariants (r7).** ⑤ A relay that buffers a peer's partial message on the peer's say-so is a memory grant to that peer: cap the DECLARED size where the header is read (not after the bytes arrive), with the downstream's own limit as the number, and release on the close. ⑥ "Changes nothing but this viewer's view" is a claim about the SERVER's semantics, verified per packet — a keymap is per-client in the protocol and global in X. ⑦ A packet cut from a refused party that the SAME party needs once it is allowed is held, not dropped: a fence that forgets breaks the legitimate transition (watch → takeover) it sits in front of — measure the transition, not just the refusal.

**Gate (r7).** test-desktop-apps §8 (the fence + hold + replay and both caps on crafted packets, xpra's 16 MiB read from the installed package; CONTROLS = the r6 allowlist and the caps patched to Infinity); test-desktop-stream-keepalive §5 (the bridge close, bounded memory, the other viewer's picture, the ws-layer cap, the rfb cut text; CONTROL = the uncapped bridge); test-desktop-app-keeper §2 + §15 (the real xpra: X's keymap untouched by a Watch viewer, the replay landing at takeover, "abc" typed into a real xterm after watching; CONTROLS = the r6 allowlist reprograms X, the fence without the replay types garbage).

**r8 — round 3 of the P8-2 verify (2.369.156, reproduced first on the real rung through the product keeper).** A WATCH VIEWER COULD RESIZE THE HOLDER'S DISPLAY — the un-fenced sibling of r7's keymap: `display-configure` / `configure-display` / `desktop_size` were still watch types ("the pane's fit needs them") and xpra 6.5.3 `_process_display_configure` calls set_screen_size for whichever client sent it. Measured: a holder's pane sized the display 900x600; a Watch viewer's `display-configure` 1x1 shrank the shared virtual display to 1x1 (the holder's app collapsed) and it STAYED 1x1 after the watcher closed — a connected browser holder re-asserts only on its own pane resize, an agent-only holder never. Reachable by the shipped client in normal use: two people viewing one app, the watcher resizing their own browser window. FIX: `XPRA_DISPLAY_TYPES` left the allowlist — a refused viewer's are cut, the LAST one HELD (≤ 16 KiB) and replayed at its takeover after the held keymap (one table `XPRA_HELD_KINDS`, the log line naming what it replays), so the pane that takes over still gets its own fit. The RFB TWIN in the same file: a refused viewer's SetDesktopSize is cut and not reported (Xvnc `-AcceptSetDesktopSize` resizes the shared display for whoever asks; the shipped noVNC never asks while viewOnly, so nothing is held). OPEN, measured: a Watch viewer's `configure-window` still resizes the holder's app WINDOW (898x589 ⇒ 478x355, it stays) — fencing it needs a view decision (scale or crop a Watch pane smaller than the holder's window), design §9-11.

**Invariants (r8).** ⑧ When one packet of a class is fenced, fence the class: the r7 rationale ("shared state the holder acts through") named the keymap and applied verbatim to the display geometry one line below it — enumerate every packet whose server handler writes state outside the sender's own view, per transport (the rfb SetDesktopSize is the same act on the other rung). ⑨ "The pane's fit needs it" is a reason to HOLD a packet for the moment the pane may act, never to relay it while it may not.

**Gate (r8).** test-desktop-apps §7 + §8 (the three display spellings the client builds are fenced, hold + replay order keymap-then-display, the rfb SetDesktopSize cut + unreported + split + per-message; CONTROLS = the r7 allowlist, the fence without the replay, the x4 rfb strip); test-desktop-app-keeper §13 (b2) (the real Xvnc: a Watch viewer's 640x480 leaves 1024x700; CONTROL = the x4 strip resizes) + §16 (the real xpra: the holder's 900x600 stands through a watcher's 1x1 / 480x360 / 320x240 and after it leaves, the takeover lands its held 700x500; CONTROLS = the r7 allowlist leaves the display 1x1, the fence without the replay leaves 900x600).

**x5 — the r3 open item CLOSED: A WATCH VIEWER'S `configure-window` (2.369.156, 2026-09-22; design-desktop-apps §7.5).** r8 left one hole, measured and named: `configure-window` stayed a watch type, and through the real bridge a watcher's 480x360 took the holder's xterm from 898x589 to 478x355 (xpra 6.5.3 seamless.py `do_process_window_configure` applies the geometry of ANY client that is not read-only; `_process_window_unmap` unmaps for every client, the same class). Fencing it needed a VIEW decision (a Watch pane smaller than the holder's window must scale or crop), and the owner ruled beyond it: "直接block掉非active客户端的app界面，因为多客户端同时操作鼠标感觉也会有问题" + "仿照terminal…可以手动take over" — the terminal's size-override made the default. **The fix:** ONE ACTIVE human viewer per app window (PURE src/desktop-viewers.js; the keeper's election; the bridge's `viewerSeats`): a non-active viewer is BLOCKED with no upstream at all (an overlay, no picture, 0 packets either way; its hello + held kinds replayed when it resumes), Resume here swaps (the old active CUT: upstream closed + 4001), the most recently active remaining viewer takes over when the active one leaves; while an agent drives every viewer is Watch — `configure-window` (HELD, replayed at a takeover) and `unmap-window` left `XPRA_WATCH_TYPES`, the client sends no geometry in Watch (`resize()` a no-op) and the view fit-scales the stage instead. **Measured:** B's 818×493 pane left X at A's 694×433 for 2.5 s; Resume here ⇒ X 814×485 in 648 ms; Watch on a 518×313 pane ⇒ stage scale 0.723, the canvas inside the pane; the pre-x5 server copy (no seats) ⇒ X followed B within 3 s.

**Invariants (x5).** ⑩ A shared display has ONE geometry owner at a time — never "whoever sent the last size": the owner is an election with a manual takeover, and every other viewer sends nothing that can change the display (the bridge enforces it; the client only mirrors it). ⑪ A viewer that must not act gets NO upstream rather than a filtered one: a socket that sends nothing upstream cannot leak a packet class nobody thought to fence (r6 → r7 → r8 → x5 each found one more). ⑫ A protocol session bound to an upstream is ended when the upstream is — a cut is a named close (4001), and the pane reconnects at once to stay seated for re-election. ⑬ The broadcast names PANES (public keys), never the per-socket secret the bridge binds.

**Gate (x5).** test-desktop-viewers (fast: the PURE rule + the keeper's election + the bridge over fake xpra/rfb upstreams + the route + wiring pins; CONTROLS = the pre-x5 bridge as a patched copy, a naive most-recently-joined re-election); test-xpra-client §5 (Watch sends no geometry, dormant outlives its hello timeout, a held hello re-sizes; CONTROLS = the client without the Watch guards, the non-dormant client); test-vnc-view §7; test-desktop-app-keeper §2 (configure-window held and replayed) + §17 (the Xvfb-for-Xpra evidence sweep with two controls); test-desktop-xpra-window §5 (heavy, two chrome pages on a real xpra + an agent lease from a live fake-claude session; CONTROL = a pre-x5 server copy); test-desktop-app-window (the vnc-display second client blocked → Resume here → handed back).

## THE FABLE-CAP POOL STORM — PLACEMENT FOLLOWED A FALLBACK, ONE REJECTION MARKED TWO BUCKETS, AND A HEALTHY MEMBER WAS REPORTED DEAD (2026-09-13 04:58-05:01Z, production forensics)

**THE REPORT.** "有账号有 Fable 额度但总是提示没有了" — and, in the journal, the owner's main conversation being thrown around a five-member pool for three minutes.

**THE TIMELINE**, from `journalctl --user -u vibespace`, `data/usage-anchors`, `data/usage-cache` and the frozen transcript in `data/incidents/inc-mtzcj5sl-lzmw` (all read-only):

- 04:38Z the server is OOM-restarted.
- 04:42:45Z the CLI's safety classifier reroutes the owner's session: an assistant record carrying `{"type":"fallback","from":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1"},"to":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8"}}`, and at 04:43:36Z a `system/model_refusal_fallback` with `originalModel: claude-fable-5-1`, `fallbackModel: claude-opus-4-8`, `trigger: refusal`, **`scope: "session"`**. After that record the session's **next 18 assistant records carry `claude-opus-4-8` and NO marker at all** — no `fallback` block, not even the `usage.iterations[].type: "fallback_message"` the announcing record had.
- 04:58:03Z `[pool] per-session switch …: sub-000000000001 → sub-000000000002 (fam=opus, from 66.95%)` + `Pool "全部": conversation "VibeSpace 主开发" moved to Member F (its opus quota was at 67%)`. The session's spawn model is `fable[1m]`.
- 04:58:33Z the CLI answers `You've reached your Fable limit.` — it had asked for **Fable**, and Member F's Fable cap read **100 % used** in its own 04:31Z panel reading.
- 04:58:33Z `[wall] demoted Member F 7d …` **and** `[wall] demoted Member F fable …` — two buckets, one rejection.
- 04:58:33 → 05:00:42Z the same three lines repeat for **Member W** and **Member Q**, auto-resume continuing the conversation onto each one (`pool switched to Member W — continued automatically` → rejected → armed → …), and the two OPUS conversations linked to the same members (`米哈游监控`, `Proxmox和Docker管理`) are dragged along on every hop, each notice reading "its opus quota was at 0%".
- 04:39:40Z, 04:58:00Z and 05:00:11Z, in between: `[notice] Pool "全部": no member can serve it — out of quota (still available: 5h 100%, 7d 69%, Fable 45%).`
- 05:01Z the owner kills and resumes the session with `model=fable[1m]` explicitly, `spawnModel` is persisted, the family reads `fable`, it lands back on Member P and has run fine since.

**THREE INDEPENDENT DEFECTS.**

**① PLACEMENT FOLLOWED A FALLBACK-SERVED MODEL.** `sessionModelFor` is `picked (newest) > served > spawn`, and the CLI's safety reroute is announced ONCE and then silent (`scope:"session"`), so the eighteen unmarked opus records made the answer `claude-opus-4-8` while the session kept REQUESTING Fable. `familyOfModel` said `opus`, `projectCacheForFamily` dropped the Fable scoped bucket — the binding constraint — and `decidePoolSwitch`'s proactive EDF tier then picked Member F on its soonest weekly deadline (11.8 h out), a member whose plan week read 83 % and whose **Fable cap read 100 %**, over Member P (plan 34 %, Fable 60 %), **the only member with Fable left**.

**② A MODEL-CAP REJECTION MARKED THE PLAN LANE.** The wire form of that rejection on the installed claude 2.1.267 is `rate_limit_event {rateLimitType:'seven_day', status:'rejected', resetsAt}`. The binary's whole type vocabulary is `{five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_overage_included, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_opus, seven_day_oauth_apps}` — **there is no `seven_day_fable`**, so a Fable model-cap rejection is emitted on the UNSCOPED weekly lane and the only thing that names the model is the banner text, which `parseLimitBanner` reads as `{kind:'scoped', name:'Fable'}`. The wall machine got two signals for ONE rejection and wrote both: the event marked the PLAN week `utilization: 1, status: 'limited'`, the banner marked the Fable cap. Three members' plan lanes were falsely marked exhausted with resets 11.8 / 44.8 / 59.8 h out, and the OPUS conversations — for which the Fable cap is invisible but the plan lane is not — were evicted on every hop.

**③ A HEALTHY CURRENT MEMBER WAS REPORTED AS "NO MEMBER CAN SERVE IT".** On a HOT pool `decidePoolSwitch` runs the candidate ranking PROACTIVELY, and the `!pool.length` branch claimed `no-members` **before anything asked whether the current member was exhausted**. Member P was healthy on every bucket (THRESH weekly hard=3/hot=5 against 45 % Fable remaining) — the "still available" numbers in that notice are ITS OWN. The same verdict fed `noteNoPoolTarget`, i.e. auto-resume's "no usable member left". The owner read the sentence exactly as written.

**THE FIXES.**

**① PLACEMENT FOLLOWS THE REQUEST MODEL, NEVER A FALLBACK-SERVED ONE.** New session fact `_servedViaFallback {from,to,at}`, stamped from a `fallback` content block or a `model_refusal_fallback` system record **on the MAIN thread** (a sidechain's reroute says nothing about what the main thread requests), and retired the moment any other model answers. `sessionModelFor`'s ladder becomes **picked (newest) > spawn > served-IF-NOT-A-FALLBACK**: a served model that IS the standing fallback target cannot define the session. NULL-persisted like `_servedModel` itself — it is a statement about a RUNNING CLI's current reroute, and boot-restore's ladder falls to the picked/spawn model, which is the REQUEST model this field exists to protect. **Unknown stays `null` and `null` is the conservative answer**: no projection, so every bucket of every member counts — a member whose Fable cap is spent is a wall for an unknown session too. Both stdout feeds (the parse and `claudeSideEffects`) write it through ONE engine consumer pair (`noteServedModel` / `noteModelFallback`) rather than assigning `_servedModel` inline, because an inline twin is the drift the CS rules ban.

**② A MODEL-CAP REJECTION MARKS THE MODEL'S CAP.** A REJECTED, UNSCOPED weekly `rate_limit_event` on a claude session is **PROVISIONAL**: the wall SIGNAL is raised at once (the session is blocked whoever owns the bucket, the turn still classifies as walled, `maybePoolAutoSwitch` still runs in the same tick) but the BUCKET MARK waits for the lane, stashed on `session._turnLaneDefer` the way `_turnWallRefile` already stashes a per-turn fact. The lane is decided by, in order: the same turn's banner naming a MODEL (`kind:'scoped'` ⇒ fold the event into `scoped:<model>`, its `resetsAt` riding along — the banner deliberately states no time); the banner saying "weekly usage limit" (`kind:'sevenDay'` ⇒ the plan lane, confirmed); or, with no banner by turn end, EVIDENCE — if the slot's own cache shows the plan week clearly alive (remaining > 10, i.e. under 90 % used) **and** a scoped cap for the session's REQUEST-model family at ≥ 99 %, it is the cap; otherwise the plan, which is today's behaviour. Every outcome journals which rule decided, with the numbers it read. A 5-hour banner decides nothing about WHICH weekly lane and leaves the deferral pending. **The rule never mentions a model NAME**: a future `seven_day_fable` parses to `kind:'scoped'` through rate-limit-capture's existing regex and is never deferred, and `seven_day_overage_included` is the weekly lane's own accounting (the 2.361.2 monthly-cap incident) and is likewise never deferred. THE COST, STATED: the immediate write is what makes the pool act in the same tick, so a turn KILLED between the rejection and its `result` now leaves no bucket mark at all (today it would leave a wrong one) — the window is milliseconds, the incident's own rejection and its turn end share a second, and the pool still moves on the provisional signal.

**③ A HEALTHY CURRENT MEMBER IS NEVER "NO MEMBER CAN SERVE IT".** The `!pool.length` branch may claim `no-members` / `all-rejected` / `all-logins-expired` **only when the current member is exhausted (soft or hard)**; otherwise it returns the new named reason `no-better` with `noBetter: true`, which no surface renders and which `noteNoPoolTarget` is not fed. The three refusals are otherwise UNCHANGED — this narrows WHEN they may be claimed, never WHAT they say. And the sentence itself: `poolBlockedNotice` now prints the live list only BESIDE a dead one, because "out of quota (still available: 5h 100%, 7d 69%, Fable 45%)" is a contradiction about one member and it is verbatim what the storm printed.

**THE DATA — MEASURED, NO MIGRATION OWED.** The three false plan-7d marks carried resets 12-60 h out, but a wall mark does NOT outrank a fresh enumerating reading: `carryUnmeasuredLimits` hands back a previous limit only when the CLAIM is unchanged, and a re-measured 7-day window is a different claim. Measured on this instance's own store (read-only, 05:50Z): **Member F 1.00 @ 04:58:33 (wall) → 0.84 @ 05:35:58 (on-demand); Member W 1.00 @ 04:59:48 → 0.66 @ 05:39:58; Member Q 1.00 @ 05:00:42 → 0.70 @ 05:41:58** — i.e. 37 / 40 / 41 minutes of false exhaustion each, healed by the auto-cli loop's ordinary idle-rung panel read, not 12-60 h. That is now a pinned PROPERTY (§4) rather than a note, driven end to end: the false mark is written by the REAL engine (the pre-fix copy, because only it produces one) and cleared by the REAL `refreshViaCliPanel` with a fake `claude` on `CLAUDE_CMD`.

**WHAT COULD NOT BE REPRODUCED, STATED.** The incident's own `rate_limit_event` records are not recoverable — stdout is a head-dropped ring and that session was killed at 05:01Z — so the rejection's payload in the regression is the CLI's documented shape plus the `unifiedWindows` block measured on this instance's surviving buffers, not the incident's own bytes. Separately: those `unifiedWindows` state the SIBLING windows' utilization on every event (the one rejected sample here reads `five_hour 1.01` beside `seven_day 0.13`), which is strictly better evidence than the cache the turn-end rule consults — `parseRateLimitEvent` ignores it today, and wiring it is an OPEN follow-up, deliberately not taken in this change.

**INVARIANTS.**
- **A served model that the vendor SUBSTITUTED for ours is not this session's model.** The reroute is announced once and `scope:"session"`, so the fact must live on the SESSION and be retired by evidence, never re-derived per record.
- **`null` is the conservative answer to "which model".** No projection means every bucket counts; guessing a family hides exactly the bucket that refuses the turn.
- **A rejection whose LANE the vendor cannot spell must not be written on the lane it arrived on.** Defer the WRITE, never the SIGNAL: the session is blocked whoever owns the bucket.
- **Decide the lane by evidence that exists, and say which rule decided.** The banner outranks the cache; the cache outranks a guess; no model ⇒ the plan lane, named.
- **A rule about a model cap may not mention a model NAME** — it must fall out of the type vocabulary and the parse.
- **An empty candidate list on a PROACTIVE scan is not a wall.** A refusal that feeds a user notice and a spend breaker may only be claimed once the member the conversation is actually on has been asked.
- **A notice may not contradict itself about one member**: "out of quota" and "still available: …" are the same member's buckets, and the live list only means something beside a dead one.
- **A suite fixture that pins a CALENDAR DATE is a time bomb.** The codex prose-reset leg in test-auto-resume pinned `"try again at Sep 13th, 2026 8:36 PM"`, which was six days out when written; on 2026-09-13 it became ~14 h out, the arm stopped being a WATCH, and two asserts went red in the MANDATORY pre-push tier with nothing about the product changed (measured identically on master at d2065aa2). The fixture now reproduces the prose SHAPE and derives the instant six days out.
- **A hand-written stub of a live module drifts, and it fails far from the cause.** The three suites that model the engine for `session-stdout` destructure by name from a plain object, so a new dep is `undefined` and the first record that reaches it throws mid-consumer — surfacing four sections later as "the message never rendered". test-stdout-registry now DERIVES the required dep set from the consumers' own `const {…} = engine;` statements.

**ROUND 2 — TWO DEFECTS THIS BRANCH ITSELF SHIPPED, both reproduced against the round-1 commit before anything was changed.**

**r2① THE PROJECTION FAMILY IS NOT THE STATED MODEL — fix ① traded the incident's blind spot for its MIRROR.** `projectCacheForFamily(cache, fam)` DROPS every model-scoped cap of another known family, so whatever family reaches it decides which walls the pool and the verdict may SEE. Fix ① made `sessionModelFor` answer the REQUEST model while a classifier reroute stands, and then handed THAT straight to the projection — so the cap of the model that is actually ANSWERING is thrown away. The spend really is the substituted model's: this instance's own anchor for the incident (`data/usage-anchors/anchors-org_1567dcbc-….ndjson`, 04:58:47Z) reads `costSince.byFamily {opus: 21.3957, fable: 0}` over 24 requests. MEASURED through the REAL engine + REAL pool + real credential symlinks, one variable — current member healthy on everything, the EDF-preferred member with Fable 10 % used but **Opus 100 %** and a sooner weekly deadline: round 1 logs `[pool] per-session switch …: … (fam=fable, from 80%)`, links the conversation to that member and tells the owner "moved to Member F (its fable quota was at 80%)", and `quotaVerdictFor` answers `usable: true` about it — which is the thing that AUTHORISES an unattended continue; master moves nothing and answers `Member P: Opus 0% < 5%`. **Reachability, stated honestly:** an Opus scoped bucket is producible today by BOTH shipped producers — `parseRateLimitEvent({rateLimitType:'seven_day_opus'})` → `{kind:'scoped', scopedName:'opus'}` (that type IS in ②'s measured vocabulary) and `markLimitBanner` on "You've reached your Opus limit." → a `{name:'Opus', utilization:1, status:'limited'}` row — and `familyOfScopedBucket('Opus') === 'opus'`, which `projectCacheForFamily(cache,'fable')` filters out. No claude cache file on this instance carries an Opus bucket TODAY, but one (`__global__.json`) carries a SECOND model cap (`Nimbus Quill` beside `Fable`), so the multi-cap shape is the vendor's, not a hypothetical; the reroute half is routine (6 fallback records across 2 sessions in the frozen capture alone). FIX: **a STANDING reroute makes the family AMBIGUOUS — both the model we ask for and the model we are given can refuse the turn** (the incident proves the first: its rejection was "You've reached your Fable limit" while opus was answering; the ledger proves the second is what gets billed) — so the answer is round 1's own doctrine, written three lines above its own code and not applied here: **UNKNOWN STAYS `null`, and `null` means NO projection, so every bucket counts.** `projectionFamilyFor(session, model)` is the ONE rule, asked at BOTH projection sites (the per-session pass and `quotaVerdictFor` — because the verdict is the site that authorises money, and fixing only the placement site would have left the billed continue): a reroute to another or to an unnameable family ⇒ null; a reroute WITHIN the same family (fable-5-1 → fable-4) is one cap and keeps its projection; **with no session it is exactly `familyOfModel(model)`, so every session-less caller is byte-identical**. A stamp left standing by an idle session therefore costs CONSERVATISM, never money — the same answer an unknown-model session already gets. `sessionModelFor` is unchanged: it still answers the REQUEST model for the notice text, `_wallScope`, `fireIdentityFor`, the model lock and `laneByEvidence`, which asks which cap a REJECTION was about and the CLI rejects the REQUEST.

**r2② A BLOCKED POOL WITH NO NUMBER IN THE SENTENCE.** A HOT pool's `exhausted` is the SOFT (hot-raised) bar while `deadBuckets` is filtered on the HARD one, so fix ③'s `rest = dead && live` dropped the live clause whenever nothing was under the hard floor — and that is exactly the band a hot pool exists for (提前切). Driven through the real `decidePoolSwitch` + real `poolBlockedNotice` (hot, proactive, current member 7d 96 % used = 4 % remaining, which is ≥ `THRESH.weekly.hard` 3 and < `.hot` 5, every other member quota-dead): `reason 'no-members'`, `deadBuckets []`, `liveBuckets ["5h 90%","7d 4%","Fable 80%"]` ⇒ `Pool "P": no member can serve it — out of quota. Conversations on it will hit a limit until a window resets, …` — the binding number is the only actionable content and it is gone, on a pool that really IS blocked. (Master is wrong a DIFFERENT way on the same state: it prints `out of quota (still available: 5h 90%, 7d 4%, Fable 80%)`, i.e. the §3 contradiction, listing the blocking bucket as available.) FIX: **THREE BANDS, NOT TWO** — `deadBuckets` (< hard), `lowBuckets` (≥ hard, under the hot bar) and `liveBuckets` (≥ the soft bar) — and the sentence names every band that is holding the decision back: `spent: 7d 1%; nearly spent: 5h 7%`, `nearly spent: 7d 4% (still available: 5h 90%, Fable 80%)`. **Cold decisions are byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION** (`soft === hard` ⇒ `lowBuckets` always empty, `liveBuckets` the old split), and that is MEASURED over a shape matrix against a master copy rather than read off the diff: three rows identical, three changed, and the three that changed are the hot-band ones.

**r2 INVARIANTS.**
- **The family you PROJECT by is a different question from the model a session STATES.** One asks "which model is this conversation about", the other "which quota buckets can refuse its next turn" — and while the vendor is substituting a model, the honest answer to the second is "more than one, so project by nothing".
- **A fix is scoped to the QUESTION, not to the line the verifier found it on.** The same projection defect sat at the placement site AND at `quotaVerdictFor`, which is the site that authorises a billed continue; the verifier saw one, and fixing only that one would have left the money path open. (Third instance of this rule in this file.)
- **A negative control must be the thing it names.** §1's control reverts `sessionModelFor` AND the projection sites, because "master" is both; on §1's own fixture either revert reproduces (master's ladder makes the stated and substituted families coincide, so the new rule keeps the projection), but on §5's fixture they differ — and the suite asserts that difference so the control cannot quietly decay into a control for something else.
- **A pool that refuses must name the numbers that made it refuse, in the band they are actually in.** "Still available" and "out of quota" argue with each other; "nearly spent" does not, and it is the sentence the 3-5 % band deserves.
- **A band split that is invisible on one setting is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is a measurement.** `soft === hard` on a cold pool is the reason, and a shape matrix against a master copy is the proof.
- **A census reads CODE.** The rule's own doc comment names `projectCacheForFamily(cache, fam)`; the site census blanks comments before counting, or it counts its own prose.

### r3 — THE LOCK, THE RESTART, THE TEARDOWN, AND THE WIRING THAT WAS NEVER THERE (2026-09-13)

Four more, each reproduced against the r2 commit (e3cc388e) on the real engine + real pool + real credential symlinks + the REAL stdout consumer **before** anything changed.

**(A) THE MODEL LOCK IS THE REQUEST MODEL** — the owner's correction. The incident's conversation was **LOCKED**: its frozen meta (`data/incidents/inc-mtzcj5sl-lzmw/frozen/session-meta/cw-6-1788859480777.json`) reads `modelLocked: true, lockedModel: "fable[1m]", pickedModel: "fable[1m]", spawnModel: "fable[1m]"`, and `maybeRepinLockedModel` re-sends `/model` at every turn end where the served model drifted — i.e. the server KNEW the request model the whole time and was actively re-asserting it. Yet "newest wins" let a fallback-served `claude-opus-4-8` record outrank both the lock and the pick. MEASURED with those exact fields: **one** main-thread opus record after a restart ⇒ `sessionModelFor` `'claude-opus-4-8'`, `projectionFamilyFor` `'opus'`, the conversation moved personal → fish (Fable 100 % spent), the notice said *"its opus quota was at 66%"*, and `quotaVerdictFor` — the site that authorises an unattended continue — answered `usable: true` about it.

FIX: the ladder is **LOCKED > picked > spawn > served-IF-NOT-A-FALLBACK**. The lock sits above the pick because the two *cannot disagree on the path that exists* — picking while locked RE-TARGETS the lock on both sides (`chat-status-bar` sends `lockModel` with the pick; ws-handler's `set-model` rewrites `_lockedModel`), and both halves are pinned as source facts rather than assumed. And because the lock is ALREADY persisted and restored, **a locked conversation is right immediately after a restart** — before any stamp, pick or served model has been re-learned, which is the incident's own shape. A lock whose served model DISAGREES is r2's ambiguity one rung lower: `projectionFamilyFor` answers `null`, so both caps count (the belt for a stamp we never saw — an older build's meta, a feed that was down). The CLI-side `/model` control is kept intact (unlocked + served changed with no fallback on record still defines the session), and the rung is deliberately NOT extended to a plain pick: a `set-model` writes `/model` on the same tick, so a served model older than a pick is stale BY CONSTRUCTION and treating that as ambiguity would suppress the projection for one turn after every ordinary model switch.

**(B) THE REROUTE STAMP SURVIVES A RESTART** (round-2 verifier). `_servedViaFallback` was `persisted: null` on the argument that *boot-restore's ladder falls back to picked/spawn = the REQUEST model* — true of the **LADDER**, false of everything else. A restored UNLOCKED conversation whose reroute was announced BEFORE the restart gets ONE main-thread opus record; nothing on the session refutes it, `servedDefinesModel` says yes, and the identical cascade runs (link → the Fable-100 % member, verdict usable via it) — the incident verbatim, one restart later. The reroute is announced ONCE and `scope:"session"`, so it can never be re-learned from the stream; only the file can carry it.

FIX: persisted in session-meta by the two **granular consumers** (never at their call sites — that is the twin the §1b census bans), through a LAZY meta-store dep because session-stdout is constructed after the engine in boot order, following the ws-handler `set-model` idiom (spread what is on disk, re-list only what changed). **ONE write per reroute, not one per record** — the incident announced the same reroute twice and a meta write re-runs the ledger's account-by-time attribution, so restating a standing reroute also leaves `at` alone (it dates when THIS reroute began). Restored at **all three** boot-restore sites through ONE expression, enforced by a DERIVED census so a fourth restore path goes red instead of silently dropping the fact. The retirement clears it **on disk** too, and a stale restored stamp costs only CONSERVATISM: `projectionFamilyFor` answers null and the REQUEST model wins.

**(C) A LANE DEFERRAL IS SETTLED ON TEARDOWN** (round-2 verifier). `settleTurnLane` is reachable only from `noteTurnEnd`, i.e. claude's `result` record — and a turn can end by the **wrapper dying**. MEASURED: a rejected unscoped `seven_day` event followed by a pty exit (no result, no banner) left **NO bucket mark at all**, where MASTER's immediate write left one — asserted as its own control, so the drop is a REGRESSION against master rather than a pre-existing gap. A dropped wall is the money direction: the member reads healthy to every OTHER conversation. FIX: the consumer binds `_settleTurnLane` and session-stdout's teardown calls it, exactly as `_retireCompaction` does for the compaction claim — the claim's OWN named function, never a reach into engine state. Scope kept tight: only the MARK lands, because the demotion still belongs to the turn-classification rule. And the `LANE_DEFER_MAX` early return, which drops a wall in SILENCE, now warns with the member's name and emits `rate-limit-lane-dropped` — with its reachability **stated honestly beside the constant** (a turn's rejections share one key by construction, so the cap binds only through a mid-turn `wallRecordTarget` re-file, and five such keys in one turn has NOT been measured end to end).

**(D) ROUND 1's CONSUMERS WERE NEVER WIRED** — found while wiring (B), reproduced against e3cc388e. server.js hands session-stdout and session-brain **hand-picked `engine:` object literals**, and round 1's own `noteServedModel` / `noteModelFallback` were in NEITHER — nor in the engine's top-level destructure. So the call at `claude-stream-json.js:609` was a `TypeError` inside the **per-LINE try**, whose catch treats the record as "non-JSON noise": MEASURED by building that exact literal and feeding an ordinary assistant record through the REAL consumer — broadcast frames `["output"]` (the JSON line painted into the chat as raw terminal output), normalizer ops `[]` (**the message never rendered**) and `_servedModel` undefined. The whole round-1 fix was dead in production AND every claude chat session was broken, while three suites stayed green because every one of them passes the WHOLE engine. FIX: exported and passed at both literals, and the census DERIVES both halves — the consumer set from the registry, the required names from each consumer's own `const {…} = engine;`, the wired names from server.js's own literals.

**r3 INVARIANTS.**
- **A lock the server RE-ASSERTS to the CLI is the request model, and it outranks any served record however new.** The product was already writing `/model` at every drifted turn end; the ladder just had to believe its own instruction.
- **A fact the CLI announces ONCE cannot be re-learned from the stream, so it belongs in the file.** "Boot-restore's ladder falls back to the right thing" was true of the LADDER and said nothing about `servedDefinesModel`, `projectionFamilyFor`, or any other reader — **an argument that is true of one reader is not true of the field**.
- **A turn-lifecycle claim owes EVERY exit, including the one no record describes.** Second instance of this rule in this file (the compaction claim was the first) — and the second time the missing exit was the teardown.
- **A bound nobody can prove unreachable may not discard a wall in silence** — and the reachability argument belongs beside the constant, stating what was NOT measured.
- **A consumer's dependency list and the literal that satisfies it must be DERIVED from each other.** r2 added a derived census for the *test stubs* and left the *production* literal hand-written; the hole that census was built for was already open in server.js. A hand-written list is the tool this class has already defeated.
- **A mutant must go RED, not crash.** Mutant (B) first killed the run with a `TypeError` 140 asserts early, because a leg read the stamp the assert above had just decided on — a precondition deserves a loud red per leg.
- **Methodology, paid for in lost work:** *never mutation-test with `git checkout` against an UNCOMMITTED tree.* The battery's restore step wiped every product edit in this branch and they had to be redone from scratch; commit first, then mutate.

**r3 GATES.** test-fable-cap-pool-storm (**178**: §7/§7b/§7c the lock — the frozen meta's own fields, the truth table off a real engine, both `set-model` re-target source pins, a control proving the ladder rung and the projection rung are different defects, and the lock-drift rung's own harm on an Opus-spent member; §8/§8b the stamp through the REAL session-meta store and boot-restore's OWN hydration expression, plus the derived site census with its negative control; §9/§9b the teardown through the REAL consumer with a pre-fix patched copy, a MASTER control proving the regression, and the cap's counter with three controls; §10/§10b the derived wiring census and the CONSEQUENCE driven over server.js's own sliced literal) + test-stdout-registry (255) + test-pool-auto (83) + test-account-verdicts (45) + test-account-pool (33) + test-readings-attribution (446) + test-quota-model (299) + test-login-expiry (257) + test-auto-resume (222) + test-auto-resume-loop (205) + test-new-member-wake (119) + test-spend-paths (261) + test-session-schema + test-harness-contract (316) + test-ws-contract + test-architecture (140; server.js back inside the 2100-line ratchet). **Seven product mutations each verified RED in exactly the asserts whose job it is** — lock rung 9, projection lock-drift rung 6, `persistFallbackStamp` 8, boot-restore hydration 1 (the census, naming the two sites that dropped it), teardown settle 3, drop counter 3, server.js wiring 4 (including the raw-output consequence) — and test-stdout-registry stays GREEN under the last of those, which is the stated boundary: that suite censuses its own STUB, §10 censuses the production literal.

### r3-r2 — THE LOCK LATCHED THE MODEL THE CLASSIFIER SUBSTITUTED (2026-09-13)

Two findings from the round-3 adversarial verifier, each reproduced against the r3 commit (89048055) on the **real engine + real pool + real credential symlinks + the REAL stdout consumer** (`session-stdout.create()` → the registry → `claude-stream-json`) on a fake pty, before anything changed.

**(A) THE TARGET-LESS LOCK LATCH MADE THE SUBSTITUTE AUTHORITATIVE FOR PLACEMENT — a REGRESSION against r2.** r3(A) put the LOCK at the top of `sessionModelFor`'s ladder. But `src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js` has latched a **target-less** lock since long before this branch — `if (session._modelLocked && !session._lockedModel) session._lockedModel = session._servedModel;`, in master, where it only ever fed `maybeRepinLockedModel` — and that latch hands the new rung **whatever answered**. While a classifier reroute is standing, that is the SUBSTITUTE.

MEASURED (session `{_spawnModel:'claude-fable-5-1[1m]', _modelLocked:true, _lockedModel:null}` on `personal`, the only Fable-alive member; two real records fed to the real consumer — `{type:'system', subtype:'model_refusal_fallback', original_model:'claude-fable-5-1', fallback_model:'claude-opus-4-8', scope:'session'}` then one main-thread `{type:'assistant', message:{model:'claude-opus-4-8'}}`):

| | r2 (e3cc388e) | r3 (89048055) | r3-r2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_lockedModel` | `claude-opus-4-8` (latched, and **written to session-meta**) | `claude-opus-4-8` (same) | **`null`** — nothing written |
| `sessionModelFor` | `claude-fable-5-1[1m]` | **`claude-opus-4-8`** | `claude-fable-5-1[1m]` |
| `projectionFamilyFor` | `null` | **`opus`** | `null` |
| link | `personal` | **`fish`** (Fable 1.00) | `personal` |
| notice | none | `Pool "all": conversation "sess-lockless" moved to Member F (its opus quota was at 66%)` | none |
| `quotaVerdictFor` | via `personal` | **`usable:true` via Member F** | via `personal` |

The meta write is what makes it permanent, and it **defeats r3(B)**: a session hydrated exactly as `src/server/boot-restore.js` does (`_modelLocked:true, _lockedModel:null, _servedViaFallback` restored from meta) gets one opus record after boot and the latch overrides the very stamp that exists to make a restored conversation right — same measured outcome, one restart later.

Neither existing guard could catch it: after the latch `familyOfModel('claude-opus-4-8') === 'opus'`, so r2's `fb.to` rung and r3's lock-drift rung both compare opus against opus and pass, while the lock rung sits ABOVE `servedDefinesModel` in the ladder. **Reachable by construction, not by luck** — `src/ws-create.js` creates this exact state (`_lockedModel: data.modelLock ? (data.lockModel || data.model || null) : null`, whose own comment says *"No target => the server latches the first main-thread served model instead"*), boot-restore hydrates it from meta at both sites, and `src/lib/session-lifecycle.js` carries `modelLock` and `lockModel` as SEPARATE saved-config keys, so any config predating the review-added `lockModel` resumes locked-with-no-target. r3's own suite built this session as a STATIC object and asserted the ladder falls through — it stopped one record short of driving the latch that fills the field.

**FIX, TWO LAYERS, EACH WITH ITS OWN CONTROL.** ① **The latch asks the engine's own predicate**: `servedDefinesModel(session)` is added to the consumer's `} = engine;` destructure and to server.js's session-stdout `engine:` literal (so §10's derived census enforces the wiring), and the latch runs only when it says yes. It is asked AFTER `noteServedModel` on purpose — a record served by anything but the reroute target has already RETIRED the stamp and may latch — and a refused latch loses nothing, because the repin no-ops with the substitute latched anyway (`modelsMatch(served, locked)`). ② **The rung itself refuses a target that IS the standing reroute** (`!(s._servedViaFallback?.to && modelsMatch(s._lockedModel, s._servedViaFallback.to))`). That is not decoration: `src/ws-handler.js`'s `set-model {lock:true}` with no `lockModel` ALSO adopts `session._servedModel` — the UI row it serves says *"Lock to this model"* about the model on screen, so the user's words are left alone and the RUNG refuses instead — and a session-meta written by any build with an ungated latch carries the substitute for ever. Falling through invents nothing: `servedDefinesModel` refuses that same served model one line below, so the answer is the pick, else the spawn model — the REQUEST — measured byte-for-byte identical to r2's answer for both writers' shapes. The `_lockedModel` writer set is now a PRINTED, source-derived census (7 sites, each classified with a reason) because that field decides placement, and an unclassified writer or a dead row goes red.

**(B) WHAT A STALE REROUTE STAMP ACTUALLY COSTS** (the verifier's LOW finding — a CLAIM defect, not a code one). r3's `_servedViaFallback` row promised a stale stamp "costs only CONSERVATISM". Measured on the real engine + real pool (current member `cur` 5h 1.00 / 7d 0.40 / Fable 0.30; escape `esc` 5h 0.05 / Fable 0.10 but **Opus 1.00**): with no stamp the session projects fable and escapes (`link cur → esc`, usable true); with a stale stamp `projectionFamilyFor` answers null, EVERY bucket counts, `esc` is disqualified by an Opus cap the session is not using, and the conversation **stays on the member whose 5-hour window is 100 % spent** (`usable:false`, notice `no member can serve it — spent: 5h 0% (still available: 7d 60%, Fable 70%, Opus 70%)`). It can never authorise a move ONTO a spent cap — that is the direction that costs money — and it self-heals at the first main-thread record served by anything else (measured: `link cur → esc` on the next tick). **r2 strands on the identical fixture**, so r3(B) introduced nothing; persisting the stamp only makes the state survive a restart instead of being cleared by one. **THE FIX IS THE ORDER, NOT A THIRD GUARD.** `rerouteAnnouncedBy(msg)` (engine-side, one implementation both feeds ask, main-thread-only INSIDE the function so neither call site can get it wrong) extracts the reroute THIS record announces, and the two consumers stamp it through `noteModelFallback` **before** `noteServedModel` and before the latch. **AND THE VERIFIER'S OWN CLAUSE RIDES ALONG AS A BELT**: `!announced` on the latch — a record that ANNOUNCES a reroute never latches, whatever any stamp says. Today **either alone refuses this record**, and that is the point: the ORDER is a property of one function's statement order (one refactor away from being lost), the BELT is a property of the RECORD. Each has its own single-mechanism control, and only reverting BOTH reproduces the shipped shape.

**r4 INVARIANTS.**

When a fact has more than one producer, drive the FIXTURE from the frozen evidence, not from the shape the last round happened to build.
- **A guard that is only correct because of statement order owes a second guard that is correct about the record** — and each owes a control that fails alone, or "defence in depth" is one mechanism with two spellings.
- **A permanent write outlives the transient state that justified it.** The belt made the latch harmless *while the reroute stood*; the harm surfaced when the reroute retired. Ask what a stored value means after the condition that produced it is gone.
