### A PARKED BACKLOG ITEM VANISHED AT THE 200-ITEM CAP (2.369.150, 2026-09-22)
A peer session reported `vibespace-task backlog-add` answering `parked as [B-a5b0]` for three different items and storing none. The group's backlog held exactly 200 items (150 done + 48 open + 2 dropped) = `CAPS.backlogItems`; `update()` sliced the incoming array to the cap, cutting the NEWEST item off; the route then echoed `updated.backlog[actedIdx]` (a position past the end ⇒ nothing) and the CLI printed `backlog[backlog.length - 1]` — the last SURVIVING stranger's id. Three faults in one symptom: a cap applied to a WRITE, an acknowledgement read by POSITION, and a CLI that trusted the list instead of the server's item. Owner ruling: no cap — the store keeps everything; a bound belongs to a READ (what an injection or listing SELECTS by ownership + priority within its budget). FIX = the slice is gone (all three sites: update, the TASK.md re-parse, the import); the route finds the added item by identity (addedAt + addedBy + text) and answers 500 by name when it is not found stored; claim/unclaim echo by id; the CLI reads `r.item` and exits 1 without one. **The CLI outlives the server it talks to (2.369.151):** a server built before 2.369.150 — still running on every instance that has not updated — stores the item and answers with only the open `backlog`, so an `r.item`-only CLI said "not stored" for a stored item; the CLI reads `r.item` FIRST and, only when it is absent, accepts the OPEN row whose text equals the (trimmed, as the old route stored it) argument — an identity by content, never a position; neither ⇒ exit 1 as before. 不变量 = a write is acknowledged only by the stored record, found by identity; a cap that could drop a write is a bug, a cap on a read is a selection that names what it left out; a shipped CLI's acknowledgement rule accepts the proof an older server can give. Gate: test-backlog-no-truncation (24, counted — the old literal said 20 over 19 checks): incl. the REAL CLI against a stub answering the old shape (the item mid-list, not last; a truncated store refused; a closed exact-text row refused) with the `r.item`-only CLI as the CONTROL.

### AN @ IN AN AGENT GROUP WAS WORDS: NO CHIP, NO ID, AND A MEMBER WHO LEFT WAS ITS ID (B-ff04, lane group-chat-ui, 2026-10-02)
The owner's screenshot of 「VibeSpace 车道群」: "@车道 · window-targets-residuals 建设 (Opus)" read as body text, the words could not be selected or copied, and the system line said "VibeSpace 主开发 移出了 3eeda0d9". Reproduced on the base (b924041f): the group window drew a body as ONE text node; the app root's `user-select: none` reached every message; the kick line named `raw.member` through the member list, which no longer held it, so the id's head was all it had. Production 2.369.202 logged `[ws] heartbeat round tainted (… longest loop gap 6–15s)` every one to two minutes; the owner's Design-window comment sat on "Sending…" through a 15 s stall. A 240 s CPU profile of the live process (SIGUSR1 → the V8 inspector, 1 ms sampling, inspector closed after) caught a 16.9 s stall: `readFileUtf8` self time 13.4 s, 10.1 s of it under the auto-cli loop's 60 s `tick` → `projectionRereadFor` (once per claude account, 13) → every live pooled conversation (25) → `sessionBillingMember` → `validateBillingSlot` → `accounts.poolMembers(pool)`, which reads EVERY member's login (`parseClaudeAuth`: .credentials.json + .claude.json, 13 members) only to ask whether ONE id is among them — ~9 K synchronous reads a tick. The data dir is bindfs over NFS (a 2 KB `readFileSync` measured 100–180 µs, far more under load), so the stall is reads × NFS latency and swings with the machine's load: the same code ran 0.5–3.6 s max lag on 2.369.201 (one 9.2 s), 1.3–1.7 s for 2.369.202's first quarter hour, 6–15 s from 04:18 on — the hot functions are byte-identical in both releases. FIX = the work, not a timeout. `accounts.isPoolMember(pool, id)`: the same roster filter and login reader as `poolMembers(pool).some(id)`, ONE login read (a miss resolves the harness dir as poolMembers' first read would, so a pool on an unregistered harness throws identically). `projectionBillingIndex()`: who-bills-where in ONE pass over activeSessions; the tick builds it on the first account that asks and drops it with the tick (no await runs before the tick's list is complete, so nothing it indexed can change under it); `projectionRereadFor(member, now, index)` reads its sessions from it (absent ⇒ builds one, exactly the old per-call loop). `accounts.poolsWithMember(id)`: memberPoolsOf's answer for the projection's hot line, read LIVE with one login per pool (a tick-long snapshot of pool rows was tried first and read a mid-tick sign-out differently — §3 caught it). server.js `resolveAccount` reads the record (`accounts.get`) with list()'s row defaults. Per tick at production's shape: 11 514 → 498 synchronous fs calls; at 150 µs a call the tick's synchronous segment 1.8 s → 82 ms.
不变量 = a periodic pass over conversations × accounts never reads a login file per pair: a membership question reads the one member it asks about, and a per-tick resolution is made once per tick and dies with it — never across ticks, so no decision reads a stale login. Every money decision is unchanged: test-auto-cli-tick-reads holds the fixed engine/loop against a patched copy with the fix reverted (sessionBillingMember, fireIdentityFor, projectionRereadFor per call and through the index, maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool's moves, one tick's asked projections and spent refreshes — across logins wiped / expired / unreadable / missing / a directory, hot and held pools, and logins changing MID-tick), plus the WORK leg (linear in conversations and in members, the reverted copy ×3.7 per ×2 members) and the LOOP leg (150 µs per fs call: < 250 ms, the reverted copy > 1 s).

不变量 = the owner reaches every profile he owns through one of his own doors — start, look, delete — wherever it lives; a paired machine's folder is removed only by that machine from an id (never a path from the hub) and anything left is said; "no browser there" is a named fact with the one command for that machine's platform, never a generic failure. Gate: test-remote-profile-start (fake win32 / darwin / linux daemons over the real op table, client gate, keeper and routes; a patched-copy control per fix).

### A HALF-OPEN RELAY KEPT A CLOSED WINDOW'S SESSION ON THE MACHINE (lane desktop-vnc-native, design 014 D1, 2026-10-03)
The picture forward (`src/server/desktop-access.js forwardPort`) listens with `allowHalfOpen: true`; the bridge DESTROYS its upstream when a browser leaves, but the hub-side socket only saw `end` — never `close` — so the agent's channel to the machine stayed open until the LAST viewer of that machine left (measured with a fake VNC server behind a fake tcpForward: closing one of two windows closed nothing on the server). ### THE SLACK CONSENT LANDING NEEDED THE VIBESPACE LOGIN (lane slack-landing-nologin, userW on a Clerk-SSO pod at 2.369.212, 2026-10-05)

A fleet user connected the cluster-preset Slack app (design 018 `public` mode). Their Slack account is a different identity from their VibeSpace SSO login and lives in another browser profile; they pressed Allow there, Slack (via the relay page) sent that browser to `GET /api/channels/oauth/cb/slack?code&state` — and `src/auth.js middleware()` saw a GET with text/html and no cookie and answered `302 /login`. The code + state address was replaced, the flow never finished, and logging the SSO identity into the Slack profile is exactly what they could not do. The route's comment said "behind the instance's own cookie (SameSite=Lax rides the redirect)": design 018 assumed one browser profile.
Fix: the gate exempts exactly `GET /api/channels/oauth/cb/<kind>` (no other verb, no sibling path; `POST /oauth/callback`, `/oauth/status` and every other route keep the cookie). The STATE is the landing's credential — this boot's HMAC + age first (`SlackManifest.stateVerdict`), then a running `public` flow found by the whole state, the code exchanged once — and a per-address door limit (30 / minute, the 31st is 429 in the page's own refused words, judged before the state). The landing only moves a pending flow to done; the RECORD is still made by the owner's cookied tab (`connect {flowId}`), and the owner's finish line now names who landed ("✓ Connected as {user}") so a stranger's identity is visible before Connect. The page says "Done here — go back to the VibeSpace window where you pressed Connect". Pinned by scripts/test-slack-landing-nologin.mjs (password + stubbed Clerk over the real middleware, two patched-copy controls).
不变量 = a vendor redirect lands without a session (another browser profile is the normal case); the commit that creates anything needs one.
